# @motifx-community/ui

> UI components for MotifJS (@motifx/core) on the MotifJS design system. Version 0.1.0-beta.5: a preview, its API may still change before 1.0.

Built on MotifJS (`@motifx/core`): a component is an object, made in JSX or with `new`, whose every prop takes a value or a function (`Bind<T>`); `x-model` binds a value two-way. The look is the design system’s (`@motifx-community/design-system`): five design languages (`data-design-language`), light and dark themes, density.

## Start

- [Getting started](docs/getting-started.md): install, set up Vite, styles, design languages, the kit’s languages

# Getting started

> `@motifx-community/ui` is a **preview** (`beta`): it is complete enough to build with, and its API may still change
> before 1.0. Install it with the `beta` tag; `@motifx/core` and its compiler with `next`.

## Install

```sh
npm i @motifx/core@next @motifx-community/ui@beta @motifx-community/design-system@beta @motifx-community/data@beta @motifx-community/i18n@beta
npm i -D @motifx/compiler@next vite typescript
```

`exceljs` (the grid's Excel export, `@motifx-community/ui/excel`) and `jspdf` (`@motifx-community/ui/pdf`) are optional: install
them only when you import those entries.

## Set up Vite and TypeScript

```ts
// vite.config.ts
import compiler from '@motifx/compiler';
import { defineConfig } from 'vite';

export default defineConfig({
  plugins: [compiler()],
  resolve: { extensions: ['.tsx', '.ts', '.jsx', '.js'], dedupe: ['@motifx/core'] },
  // The kit's styles use :dir(), :has() and relative colours: build CSS for the browsers it supports.
  build: { cssTarget: ['chrome120', 'edge120', 'firefox128', 'safari18'] },
});
```

```jsonc
// tsconfig.json (the keys that matter)
{ "compilerOptions": { "jsx": "preserve", "target": "ES2021", "module": "esnext", "moduleResolution": "bundler", "useDefineForClassFields": true, "strict": true } }
```

## Styles, design languages, themes

```ts
// main.tsx
import '@motifx-community/ui/styles.css'; // the design system first, then the kit
import { Application } from '@motifx/core';
import { App } from './App';

Application.CreateBuilder().build().run('#app', new App());
```

The look comes from the design system. Choose a design language and a theme on `<html>` (or on any element, for that
part of the page):

```html
<html data-design-language="material" data-theme="dark" data-density="compact">
```

- `data-design-language`: `tactile` (the default, without the attribute), `lounge`, `material`, `fluent`, `lilac`.
- `data-theme`: `light`, `dark`, `high-contrast`; without it the system's preference.
- `data-density`: `compact`; without it the regular one.

Restyle by overriding design-system tokens (`--mx-*`) after the kit's stylesheet, e.g. `:root { --mx-color-accent-solid: #8764b8; }`.

## The kit's language

The texts the components write themselves (buttons, messages, screen-reader names) and their numbers and dates follow
`uiLocale`. English and Turkish ship with the kit; `uiLocale.use('tr')` loads the Turkish pack and every component
draws again, live.

```ts
import { uiLocale } from '@motifx-community/ui';
await uiLocale.use('tr');
uiLocale.add('de', { ok: 'OK', cancel: 'Abbrechen' /* … */ });
```

With `@motifx-community/i18n` for the app's own texts, `connectI18n(i18n)` keeps the kit on the app's language.

## How the components work

- A component is an object: write it in JSX (`<Button text="Save" />`) or make it with `new Button({ text: 'Save' })`, add it
  anywhere (`this.controls.add(button)`), change it later (`button.text = 'Saved'`).
- Every prop and property takes a value or a function (`Bind<T>`): `disabled={() => this.model.busy}` follows the state.
- `x-model` binds a value two-way: `<TextBox label="Name" x-model={() => this.form.name} />`.
- Events are `onX` props or properties that take a listener: `onValueChanged={(e) => …}`, `grid.onRowClick((e) => …)`;
  `e.byUser` tells a user's change from one made by code.
- A component added to another is its child and goes with it when it is disposed; add components with `controls.add`,
  never by putting their element into the page yourself.
- Your data is used as given: items, rows and values are not wrapped or copied.

```tsx
import { Component, reactive } from '@motifx/core';
import { Button, Stack, TextBox } from '@motifx-community/ui';

export class App extends Component<HTMLDivElement> {
  state = reactive({ name: '', saved: false });

  view() {
    return (
      <Stack gap="md">
        <TextBox label="&Name" x-model={() => this.state.name} required />
        <Button text="&Save" tone="accent" disabled={() => !this.state.name} onclick={() => (this.state.saved = true)} />
      </Stack>
    );
  }
}
```

Each component's page in `docs/` lists its props, properties, methods, events, keyboard, accessibility and design
tokens, with examples.

# @motifx-community/ui

> Get started · @motifx-community/ui 0.1.0-beta.5

Components for MotifJS: objects you create when you need them, show anywhere and dispose when you are done, drawn from the MotifJS design system's tokens.

## Install

```tsx
npm i @motifx/core @motifx-community/ui
```

```tsx
import { Button, Control, FocusContainer, addShortcut } from '@motifx-community/ui';
```

## Component model

- Every component is an object. Declare it in JSX and bind it to state, or instantiate it with `new` and add it to the component tree at runtime. Both approaches expose the same API.

- Lifetime follows ownership: disposing a component also disposes the components it owns.

- Every component supports keyboard navigation, focus management and the WAI-ARIA roles and states of its pattern.

## Components

The library includes more than fifty components built on a shared base. Each one provides keyboard and focus support, accessible roles and names, English and Turkish strings that can be switched at runtime, right-to-left layout, and component tokens for the five design languages of the design system: Tactile, Lounge, Material, Fluent and Lilac. Every component has a reference page with live examples and its full API.

| Layout | [`Stack`](layout.md), [`Grid`](layout.md), [`DockPanel`](layout.md), [`Panel`](layout.md), [`GroupBox`](layout.md), [`SplitContainer`](layout.md), [`Splitter`](splitter.md), [`Resizable`](resizable.md), [`Draggable`](draggable.md), [`FormLayout`](formlayout.md), [`ScrollView`](scrollview.md) (pull to refresh, load more), [`Sortable`](sortable.md) |
| Data | [`DataGrid`](datagrid.md) (virtual or paged, editing, filters, grouping, master-detail, export), [`TreeView`](treeview.md), [`FilterBuilder`](filterbuilder.md), [`Scheduler`](scheduler.md) (day to timeline, recurrence, resources, iCalendar), [`TabDocumentManager`](tabdocs.md) (tabs, split, dock, new windows); lists and grids read `@motifx-community/data` sources |
| Base | [`Control`](control.md), [`FocusContainer`](keyboard.md) and [`addShortcut`](keyboard.md), [`uiLocale`](language.md), [the component tokens](tokens.md); `Popup` and `MenuList`, the shared parts a menu or a drop-down opens on |

## Design system

Visual styling comes from `@motifx-community/design-system`, which provides design tokens, three themes, density settings, fonts and user-preference overrides. `styles.css` imports it first, then the `mx.components` layer adds the [component tokens](tokens.md) and the components. Components define no colors or sizes of their own.

- Themes: light, dark and high contrast, selected with `data-theme`. The default follows the operating system preference. The design system build verifies every text and background pair against WCAG AA, and against AAA in high contrast.

- Density: `data-density="compact"` reduces the size of every control, bar and title bar.

- Right-to-left layout: components are built on CSS logical properties.

```tsx
<html data-theme="dark" data-density="compact">
```

```tsx
/* your accent, after styles.css: a design-system override restyles every component */
:root {
  --mx-color-accent-solid: #8764b8;
  --mx-color-accent-solid-hover: #9373c0;
  --mx-color-accent-solid-pressed: #7e5aaf;
  --mx-color-accent-fg: #5c2e91;
}
```

# Showcase: an order screen

> Get started · @motifx-community/ui 0.1.0-beta.5

An order entry screen built with the kit, structured the way a MotifJS application is normally built: state and operations live in a model (`OrderModel`), and the page binds to it. The customer list is a data source of 5,000 rows that responds like a server.

# Design tokens

> Get started · @motifx-community/ui 0.1.0-beta.5

The token system has five layers. The first four (primitives, design language scales, semantic tokens per theme, and density) come from `@motifx-community/design-system` and are listed here for reference. The fifth layer, component tokens, belongs to this kit: each component has its own tokens, written in `@layer mx.components`, and each one references a design system token. Every design language provides its own value for each component token.

## Component ({componentDocs.length})

Source: `tokens/schema/*.json` for names and types, and `tokens/languages/<language>/*.json` for values (Tactile values are listed here). Override a component token after `styles.css` to restyle every instance of that component, or override the design system token it references to restyle everything that uses it.

## Using token names in TypeScript

```tsx
import { cssVar } from '@motifx-community/ui/tokens';

cssVar('color.accent.solid');  // 'var(--mx-color-accent-solid)' — a design-system token
// component tokens join as components bring them; names are typo-checked,
// and apps that need only the design system import cssVar from there
```

# Control

> Foundations · @motifx-community/ui 0.1.0-beta.5

`Control` is the base class of every control in the package. It provides the same `text`, `enabled`, `visible` and `tabStop` properties and the same focus methods, whether a control is declared in JSX and bound to state or created with `new` and changed programmatically.

## Import

```tsx
import { Control, type ControlProps } from '@motifx-community/ui';
```

Every component in the package ([Button](button.md), …) derives from it. Derive from it for your own controls as well.

## Declarative and programmatic

Both approaches are fully supported, so the choice is up to you.

```tsx
// JSX, bound to state
<Badge text="Unread" enabled={() => !this.state.busy} />

// code: create, add anywhere, change later
const unread = new Badge({ text: 'Unread' });
this.toolbar.controls.add(unread);
unread.enabled = false;
unread.text = 'Unread mail';
unread.text = () => `Unread (${this.mail.count})`; // a function is followed
```

`Badge` is the control built in [Writing a control](#own).

```tsx
import { Button, Stack } from '@motifx-community/ui';

/** Buttons created with `new`, added to a container, and their text changed programmatically on a click. */
export default function AddProgrammatically() {
  let added = 0;
  let target: Stack | null = null;

  const addProgrammatic = () => {
    const b = new Button({ text: `Button ${++added}` });
    b.motif.on('click', () => (b.text = `${b.text} ✓`));
    target?.controls.add(b);
  };

  return (
    <>
      <Button text="Add a button programmatically" onclick={addProgrammatic} />
      <Stack orientation="horizontal" wrap align="center" ref={(c: Stack) => (target = c)} />
    </>
  );
}
```

## How a property gets its value

- A prop accepts a value or a function. A function that reads a reactive object (`enabled={() => !state.busy}`) keeps the property in sync with that object. This is how MotifJS keeps a prop live.

- The control uses your data exactly as you provide it. It never makes the data reactive, and it never copies or modifies it. With plain data, the function is read again when you call `reState()` on the control or on one of its ancestors, so you decide which kind of data to use.

- With `x-model`, the model always reflects the state of the control. Changes made by the user, by your code (`ctrl.value = …`, `select()`, `show()`) or by a rule you set (`decimals`, a mask, `min` / `max`) are all written back to the model.

- Setting a property programmatically works the same way. A function (`ctrl.enabled = () => !state.busy`) replaces the existing binding and is tracked. A value (`ctrl.enabled = false`) removes the binding, and your code owns the property from then on.

- Every property is reactive when read. `{() => ctrl.text}` in JSX or a `bindings.watch` tracks it no matter how it changes.

- `x-wait` and `x-display` remain one-way: they show and hide the element based on state, and nothing is written back. If state must change when the control is removed, do it in `onDisposed`.

## Enabled

Disabling a control disables everything inside it, including child controls and plain elements, just as a disabled `<fieldset>` does for form fields. Enabling it restores every element to its previous state. An element that was disabled on its own stays disabled, and content added while the control is disabled is disabled too. Any change the application makes in the meantime, such as a bound `disabled`, is what gets restored. Disabled containers can be nested: an element stays disabled as long as any container, or its own value, says so.

| Item | Result |
| --- | --- |
| `Native controls` | `button`, `input`, `select`, `textarea`, `fieldset`, `optgroup` and `option` receive `disabled`, so the browser blocks them and announces the state. |
| `Other focusable elements` | Links, `[tabindex]`, `contenteditable`, `summary` and `iframe` receive `tabindex="-1"` and `aria-disabled="true"`. |
| `Pointer input` | `pointerdown`, `mousedown`, `click`, `dblclick`, `auxclick` and `contextmenu` events are suppressed inside the disabled control before they reach any handler. |
| `The control itself` | The control receives `data-disabled` for styling. |
| `Windows inside` | A `<dialog>` window opened inside a disabled control is not disabled. Owned windows remain usable. |

If focus was inside the control, it moves to the next usable element in the same window, or to the previous one, instead of falling to `<body>`.

```tsx
import { Button, Panel, Stack } from '@motifx-community/ui';

/** A panel disabled and enabled programmatically: everything inside follows, and the inner button keeps its own `enabled`. */
export default function EnabledPanel() {
  let panel: Panel | null = null;
  let inner: Button | null = null;

  return (
    <>
      <Button text="Toggle panel enabled" onclick={() => (panel!.enabled = !panel!.enabled)} />
      <Panel variant="outline" padding="md" class="ctl-panel" ref={(p: Panel) => (panel = p)}>
        <Stack orientation="horizontal" wrap align="center">
          <label>
            Name <input name="panel-name" />
          </label>
          <Button text="Inner button" ref={(b: Button) => (inner = b)} />
          <a href="#enabled">A link</a>
        </Stack>
      </Panel>
      <output>{() => (inner ? `Inner button: enabled ${inner.enabled}, isEnabled ${inner.isEnabled}` : '')}</output>
    </>
  );
}
```

## Visible and TabStop

`visible` uses the core `hide()` and `show()` methods. A hidden control leaves the page and later returns to the same place with its state intact. If focus was inside, it moves elsewhere first. `tabStop = false` only removes the control from the Tab sequence.

## Focus

```tsx
if (!nameBox.focus()) saveButton.focus();
nameBox.canFocus;      // enabled, on the page, focusable
panel.focusWithin;   // focus is somewhere inside
```

A control never causes focus to fall to `<body>`. Disabling, hiding, removing or disposing the focused part moves focus to the next usable element. Focus rings appear only during keyboard use (`:focus-visible`). For Tab order, access keys and shortcuts, see [Keyboard and focus](keyboard.md).

## FocusContainer

A control that tracks which of its children is active and acts as a scope for Tab. The package's windows, tab pages and document views use it. The outermost container of a page or window also applies the `tabIndex` order (see [Keyboard and focus](keyboard.md)).

```tsx
class CustomerEditor extends FocusContainer<HTMLDivElement> { … }

editor.activeControl;           // the control holding focus inside, reactive
editor.activeControl = nameBox; // focuses it
editor.restoreFocus();          // back to where focus was when it was last active
```

| Member | Type | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `activeControl` | `Control \| null` | read/write, reactive | The child control that has focus, or last had it. It works like `document.activeElement` does for the page, and a nested container counts as one control. Setting it moves focus to that control. |
| `restoreFocus()` | `boolean` | method | Returns focus to where it was the last time the container was active. If that is not possible, it moves to the active control, and then to the first control in Tab order. |
| `cyclesTab` | `boolean` | protected getter | `true` keeps Tab inside the container. The default is `false`, and a modal window returns `true`. |

## Writing a control

Derive from `Control`, set the root element, and render `text` and your own properties with `observeProperty`. No effect is created, and the callback runs on every change.

```tsx
interface BadgeProps extends ControlProps {
  count?: Bind<number>;
}

class Badge extends Control<HTMLSpanElement, BadgeProps> {
  static override elementTag = 'span';

  constructor(props?: IBaseProp<BadgeProps>) {
    super(props);
    if (this.props.count !== undefined) this.bindProperty('count', this.props.count);
  }

  get count(): number { return this.getProperty<number>('count') ?? 0; }
  set count(value: number) { this.setProperty('count', value); }

  override onConfigured() {
    this.class.add('my-badge');
    this.observeProperty<string>('text', (t) => this.element.setAttribute('aria-label', t));
    this.observeProperty<number>('count', (n) => (this.element.textContent = String(n ?? 0)));
  }
}
```

| Member | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `static elementTag` | The root element. It is a `div` unless the subclass specifies another element (`button` for a button). |
| `focusElement` | Getter for the element that receives focus, which is the root by default. Composite controls override it. It runs from the constructor, so derive it from `this.element`. |
| `observeProperty(name, apply)` | Renders a property without an effect. `apply` runs immediately and on every change, whether the change comes from a getter prop or from code. |
| `getProperty(name) / setProperty(name, value)` | The storage behind the shared properties, available for your own: a tracked read, and a programmatic set that replaces any bound getter. |
| `bindProperty(name, prop)` | Binds one of your own props. A getter is read immediately and tracked by a binding on the control, so `reState()` reads it again. A value is stored once. Call it from your constructor. |
| `applyProperty(name, value) / peekProperty(name)` | Renders your own properties without an effect. Override `applyProperty` and call `super`, and read the current value without tracking through `peekProperty`. This method can run from the constructor, so touch only `this.element`. |
| `setAccessKey(key)` | Declares the access key parsed from `&Text` (`parseAccessKey`). It is written to `aria-keyshortcuts` as `Alt+K`, which is how Alt+K finds the control. |

## Performance

The base class adds no per-control listeners, and you pay only for what you use.

| Case | Cost |
| --- | --- |
| `A property nobody set, bound or read` | No cost: no storage, no DOM write and no binding. |
| `A plain value (`enabled={false}`, `new Badge({ text })`)` | Stored and written to the DOM once. |
| `A getter (`enabled={() => !state.busy}`)` | One binding for the property, stopped when the control is disposed or another value or function is set. |
| `Reading a property` | A small change counter, created the first time the property is read. |
| `Setting programmatically` | A direct DOM write. Readers are notified through the counter. |
| ``enabled = false`` | One pass over the control's subtree, plus one shared observer while anything is disabled. The observer is removed when nothing is disabled. |

## API reference

### Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `text` | `Bind<string>` | `''` | The text of the control. Where it appears depends on the control, for example a button's caption or a form's title. |
| `enabled` | `Bind<boolean>` | `true` | `false` disables the control and everything inside it. See "Enabled". |
| `disabled` | `Bind<boolean>` | `false` | The HTML-style inverse of `enabled`, provided for familiarity: `disabled={() => state.busy}`. It is ignored when `enabled` is set. |
| `visible` | `Bind<boolean>` | `true` | `false` hides the control with the core `hide()` method. `true` shows it again with `show()`. |
| `tabStop` | `Bind<boolean>` | `true` | `false` removes the control from the Tab order. A click or `focus()` still gives it focus. |
| `tabIndex` | `Bind<number>` | `0` | The order among controls in the same container. Tab visits them in ascending order, and ties follow document order. Leave it unset where you can, because document order is also the reading order for screen readers. See Keyboard and focus. |

### Properties

| Property | Type | Access | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `text` | `string` | read/write, reactive | Set programmatically with a value or a function, the same as the prop (see "How a property gets its value"). |
| `enabled` | `boolean` | read/write, reactive | The control's own value, as set or bound. This matches the HTML `disabled` attribute. |
| `isEnabled` | `boolean` | read-only, reactive | Indicates whether the control can be used now, meaning that it and all its ancestors are enabled. This matches CSS `:enabled`. Windows shown inside it do not inherit the state. |
| `visible` | `boolean` | read/write, reactive | The control's own value. A hidden parent does not change it. |
| `disabled` | `boolean` | read/write, reactive | `!enabled`. |
| `tabIndex` | `number` | read/write, reactive | The position in its container's Tab order. |
| `tabStop` | `boolean` | read/write, reactive | Writes `tabindex="-1"` on the focus element while `false`, and restores the element's own `tabindex` afterward. |
| `parentControl` | `Control \| null` | read-only | The nearest ancestor that is a `Control`, without crossing a window. |
| `canFocus` | `boolean` | read-only | Indicates that the control is enabled, on the page and focusable right now. |
| `focused` | `boolean` | read-only | Indicates that the focus element has focus. This is a DOM query and is not reactive. |
| `focusWithin` | `boolean` | read-only | Indicates that focus is on the control or inside it. This is a DOM query and is not reactive. |

### Methods

| Method | Returns | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `focus()` | `boolean` | Sets focus on the control. Returns `false` if it cannot receive focus (`canFocus`). |
| `onAccessKey()` | `boolean` | Defines what the access key does (`&Save` → Alt+S, or Control+Option+S on Apple platforms). By default it sets focus, and a button also clicks. Override it in your own control. |
| `addShortcut(chord, handler, options?)` | `() => void` | A shortcut that is active while focus is inside this control and is removed when the control is disposed. See Keyboard and focus. |

## Not yet available

- Arrow key navigation inside composite controls (one Tab stop with arrow keys inside) arrives with the first composite control.

# Keyboard and focus

> Foundations · @motifx-community/ui 0.1.0-beta.5

Every control follows the same rules for Tab order, the active control of a container, focus handling, `&File` access keys and application-wide shortcuts.

## Validation rules

| Rule | Details |
| --- | --- |
| `Tab navigation` | Every control is a Tab stop unless `tabStop = false`. `tabIndex` sets the order of the controls in a container. |
| `Active control` | Containers (`FocusContainer`) track `activeControl` and restore focus with `restoreFocus()` when they become active again. |
| `Composite controls` | One Tab stop with arrow keys inside, using a roving tabindex or `aria-activedescendant`. This arrives with the first composite control. |
| `Focus never on <body>` | When the focused part of a control is disabled, hidden, removed or disposed, focus moves to the next usable element. |
| `Focus ring` | Shown only during keyboard use (`:focus-visible`), with the design system's double ring. |
| `Access keys` | `&Save` in a control's text assigns Alt+S. The letter is underlined while Alt is held. |
| `Shortcuts` | `addShortcut('Ctrl+S', …)` registers a shortcut for the whole application or for one control. |

## Tab order

Give controls a `tabIndex`, and the outermost container of the page or window visits them in ascending order at each level of the control tree. Equal indexes and plain elements (index 0) follow document order. Until a control sets a `tabIndex`, Tab is handled by the browser. A modal window keeps Tab inside itself, and only one radio button per group is a Tab stop, as in browsers.

```tsx
import { Button, FocusContainer, Panel, Stack } from '@motifx-community/ui';

/** A custom container: it manages the Tab order of its controls and remembers the active one. */
class CustomerEditor extends FocusContainer<HTMLDivElement> {}

/** Tab visits the buttons by `tabIndex`; the container reports its `activeControl` and puts focus back with `restoreFocus()`. */
export default function TabOrder() {
  let editor: CustomerEditor | null = null;
  return (
    <>
      <CustomerEditor ref={(c: CustomerEditor) => (editor = c)}>
        <Panel variant="outline" padding="md">
          <Stack orientation="horizontal" wrap align="center">
            <Button text="Third" tabIndex={3} />
            <Button text="First" tabIndex={1} />
            <Button text="Second" tabIndex={2} />
          </Stack>
        </Panel>
      </CustomerEditor>
      <span>
        activeControl: <output class="active-name">{() => editor?.activeControl?.text ?? '—'}</output>
      </span>
      <Button text="restoreFocus()" onclick={() => editor?.restoreFocus()} />
    </>
  );
}
```

## Active control

A `FocusContainer` knows which child control holds focus (`activeControl`, reactive) and returns focus to it with `restoreFocus()`. For example, when a window comes to the front or the user returns to a tab page.

## Access keys

```tsx
<Button text="&Save" onclick={save} />    // Alt+S
<Button text="Save &as…" onclick={saveAs} /> // Alt+A
<Button text="Tom && Jerry" />             // a literal &
<input aria-keyshortcuts="Alt+N" />        // plain elements too
```

| Topic | Behavior |
| --- | --- |
| `Marker` | Put `&` before a letter: `&Save`, `Save &as…`. `&&` produces a literal ampersand. Only the first marker counts. |
| `Keys` | Alt plus the key. On Apple platforms, use Control + Option plus the key, because Option alone types characters there. Browsers use the same keys for HTML `accesskey`. |
| `Description` | The key activates the control. A button receives focus and is clicked, as with HTML `accesskey`. Any other control receives focus (`onAccessKey()`). |
| `Several with the same key` | Each press moves focus to the next match without activating it. |
| `Where` | The modal window if one is open, otherwise the window that has focus, otherwise the page outside any window. Disabled and hidden controls are skipped. |
| `AltGr` | AltGr (Ctrl+Alt on Windows) is ignored, because it types characters such as `@` on a Turkish keyboard. |
| `Underline` | Shown while Alt is held (Control + Option on Apple platforms). Tapping Alt keeps the underlines visible until Alt is tapped again, another key is pressed or the pointer is used. While the page has access keys, that tap is not passed to the browser, which would otherwise move keyboard focus to its menu bar. Set `data-mx-access-keys="always"` on `<html>` to show them all the time. |
| `Accessibility` | The accessible name is the plain text, and the control receives `aria-keyshortcuts="Alt+S"` (`"Control+Alt+S"` on Apple platforms). |
| `Plain elements` | Any element with `aria-keyshortcuts="Alt+N"` takes part. A button-like element is clicked, an input receives focus, and a `<label>` moves focus to its field. |

```tsx
import { reactive } from '@motifx/core';
import { Button } from '@motifx-community/ui';

/** `&` in a button text: Alt+S saves, Alt+O opens, Alt+P exports. */
export default function AccessKeys() {
  const s = reactive({ saves: 0, opens: 0, exports: 0 });
  return (
    <>
      <Button text="&Save" onclick={() => s.saves++} />
      <Button text="&Open" onclick={() => s.opens++} />
      <Button text="Ex&port" onclick={() => s.exports++} />
      <span>
        Saved <output class="saves">{() => s.saves}</output> · opened <output class="opens">{() => s.opens}</output> · exported{' '}
        <output>{() => s.exports}</output>
      </span>
    </>
  );
}
```

Browsers reserve some Alt combinations for their own menus, and these vary by browser and language. Test the keys you choose.

## Shortcuts

```tsx
import { addShortcut } from '@motifx-community/ui';

const remove = addShortcut('Mod+S', () => model.save()); // app-wide
grid.addShortcut('Delete', () => grid.deleteSelected()); // while focus is in the grid
addShortcut('F2', () => rename(), { scope: tree });
```

### Key combinations

| Part | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `Ctrl / Control` | The Ctrl key. |
| `Alt / Option` | The Alt key (Option on a Mac). |
| `Shift` | The Shift key. |
| `Meta / Cmd / Win` | The Windows key, or Cmd on a Mac. |
| `Mod` | Cmd on Apple platforms and Ctrl elsewhere, so `Mod+S` saves on every platform. |
| `keys` | A character (`S`, `1`, `/`) or a `KeyboardEvent.key` name: `Enter`, `Escape` (`Esc`), `Delete` (`Del`), `F2`, `ArrowUp` (`Up`), `Space`, `Plus`… Case does not matter. `Ctrl++` means Ctrl and plus. |

### Shortcut precedence

| Rule | Behavior |
| --- | --- |
| `Most specific first` | Shortcuts scoped to the controls that hold focus run first, starting with the innermost. Application-wide shortcuts run last. A handler that returns `false` passes the key on. |
| `Modal windows` | While a modal window is open, only shortcuts scoped inside it run. Application-wide shortcuts are suppressed. |
| `Windows` | Application-wide shortcuts without Ctrl, Alt or Meta (Delete, Escape, a letter) do not run while focus is in a window, because those keys belong to the window. Combinations with a modifier and function keys still run. |
| `Text fields` | A combination without Ctrl, Alt or Meta does not fire in text fields, so that Delete deletes text, unless you set `inEditable: true`. Function keys and combinations with a modifier work everywhere. |
| `Disabled scope` | A shortcut scoped to a disabled control does not run. |
| `Handled` | The key receives `preventDefault()` and goes no further. Shortcuts run before access keys, so an explicit combination takes priority over an implicit key. |

```tsx
import { Component, reactive } from '@motifx/core';
import { addShortcut } from '@motifx-community/ui';

/** An app-wide shortcut, Mod+K, registered for as long as this component lives. */
export default class Shortcut extends Component {
  private readonly s = reactive({ palette: 0 });

  override onConfigured(): void {
    this.motif.setDisposable(addShortcut('Mod+K', () => void this.s.palette++));
  }

  override view() {
    return (
      <span>
        This page registers <kbd>Mod+K</kbd> (Ctrl+K, Cmd+K on a Mac). Pressed <output class="palette">{() => this.s.palette}</output> times.
      </span>
    );
  }
}
```

## Focus never lands on &lt;body&gt;

When the focused part of a control is disabled, hidden, removed (a list row, a tree branch) or disposed, focus moves to the next usable element from that position in the same window, or to the previous one. Clicking an empty area still clears focus as usual, and route changes are left to the router.

```tsx
import { reactive } from '@motifx/core';
import { Button, Stack } from '@motifx-community/ui';

/** Removing the row that holds focus moves focus to the next row, not to `<body>`. */
export default function FocusGuard() {
  const s = reactive({ items: [{ id: 1 }, { id: 2 }, { id: 3 }, { id: 4 }] });
  return (
    <>
      {s.items.map((item) => (
        <Stack key={item.id} orientation="horizontal" wrap align="center">
          <span>Row {item.id}</span>
          <Button text={`Remove row ${item.id}`} onclick={() => s.items.splice(s.items.indexOf(item), 1)} />
        </Stack>
      ))}
    </>
  );
}
```

## API reference

| Member | Return value / type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `addShortcut(chord, handler, options?)` | `() => void` | Registers a shortcut and returns a function that removes it. `options.scope` limits it to a component, and `options.inEditable` also enables it in text fields. |
| `control.addShortcut(chord, handler, options?)` | `() => void` | Registers a shortcut scoped to the control and removes it when the control is disposed. |
| `parseAccessKey(text)` | `{ text, key, index }` | Parses `&Text` for your own controls. Render the result with the `mx-access-key` class and call `setAccessKey(key)`. |
| `tabIndex` | prop / property | The order inside the container. The default is 0. |
| `activeControl / restoreFocus()` | FocusContainer | See the Control page. |

For `tabStop`, `tabIndex`, `focus()`, `onAccessKey()` and `FocusContainer`, see the `Control` page.

# Language

> Foundations · @motifx-community/ui 0.1.0-beta.5

`uiLocale` controls the strings that controls display, the locale used for dates and numbers, and the text direction. The kit has one `uiLocale`, and each language pack is loaded on demand.

## Import

```tsx
import { uiLocale, connectI18n } from '@motifx-community/ui';
```

## Changing the language

`uiLocale.use('tr')` loads the Turkish pack the first time it is requested. Every control on the page then redraws its strings and formats. The Language menu in the header of these docs does the same thing.

```tsx
import { reactive } from '@motifx/core';
import { Button, DateBox, NumberBox, Pagination, Stack, uiLocale } from '@motifx-community/ui';
import { kitTexts } from '../../../shared/kit-texts';

/** The kit's language switched live: the pack is loaded first, then every control draws its texts and formats again. */
export default function Switch() {
    const s = reactive({ price: 1234.5, when: new Date(2026, 2, 18) as Date | null });
    return (
        <Stack gap="md">
            <Stack orientation="horizontal" wrap align="center">
                <Button text="English" variant="outline" onclick={() => void uiLocale.use('en')} />
                <Button text="Türkçe" variant="outline" onclick={() => void uiLocale.use('tr')} />
                <span>
                    In use: <output class="lang-locale">{() => kitTexts.locale}</output>
                </span>
            </Stack>
            <Stack orientation="horizontal" wrap align="center">
                <NumberBox label="Price" x-model={() => s.price} format={{ style: 'currency', currency: 'EUR' }} />
                <DateBox label="When" x-model={() => s.when} clearButton />
            </Stack>
            <Pagination total={95} pageSizes={[10, 20, 50]} label="Orders" />
        </Stack>
    );
}
```

## Validation rules

| Rule | Details |
| --- | --- |
| `Start` | The initial language comes from the page's `<html lang>` attribute, or from the browser language if it is not set. Set `lang` before creating the first control. `uiLocale.ready` resolves once that language has loaded. |
| `Texts` | Every string a control displays on its own, such as a button name, a message or “No items”, comes from the active language pack. English is used for anything the pack does not include. |
| `Formats` | Dates, numbers, the first day of the week and the 12 or 24-hour clock follow `uiLocale.locale`. A control's own `locale` prop takes precedence for that control. |
| `Direction` | `uiLocale.dir` is `rtl` for Arabic, Hebrew, Persian, Urdu and similar languages. Controls lay themselves out based on `<html dir>`, which `@motifx-community/i18n` keeps in sync. |
| `Nothing follows` | A language change raises a single event, `onChanged`. Controls redraw in response, and your own strings can do the same. No binding reads `uiLocale`. |
| `Plurals` | A string with a count is an ICU message, such as `{count, plural, one {# record} other {# records}}`. Each pack writes it according to the plural rules of its language. |

## Language packs

| Pack | Source |
| --- | --- |
| `English` | Built in. Anything a pack does not include appears in English. |
| `Turkish` | `uiLocale.use('tr')` loads it on first use as a chunk of the package. |
| `@motifx-community/ui/locales/<language>.json` | The same packs as files, for applications that bundle or serve them separately: `uiLocale.add('tr', pack)`. |
| `uiLocale.loader` | Sets where the kit requests packs it does not have: `(language) => fetch(`/i18n/ui/${language}.json`).then((r) => r.json())`. A language without a pack keeps the English strings. |

A custom pack is a plain object of kit strings. `uiLocale.add` registers strings for a language, and `use` switches to it. You can start with a few strings. The rest stay in English until the pack includes them.

```tsx
import { Button, DropDown, Stack, uiLocale } from '@motifx-community/ui';

// A few German strings. Anything omitted stays in English.
uiLocale.add('de', {
    close: 'Schließen',
    clear: 'Leeren',
    search: 'Suchen',
    noItems: 'Keine Einträge',
    loading: 'Wird geladen…',
    ok: 'OK',
    cancel: 'Abbrechen',
});

/** A custom pack: `uiLocale.add` registers strings for a language, and `use` switches to it. */
export default function OwnPack() {
    return (
        <Stack gap="md">
            <Stack orientation="horizontal" wrap align="center">
                <Button text="Deutsch" variant="outline" onclick={() => void uiLocale.use('de')} />
                <Button text="English" variant="outline" onclick={() => void uiLocale.use('en')} />
            </Stack>
            <DropDown label="Empty list" items={[]} placeholder="Open me" />
        </Stack>
    );
}
```

## Using your application's translations

An application translated with `@motifx-community/i18n` already has a locale. `connectI18n(i18n)` makes the kit follow it: when the application switches language, the kit loads its own pack and switches too. Call the function it returns to disconnect.

```tsx
import { Component } from '@motifx/core';
import { createI18n } from '@motifx-community/i18n';
import { Button, connectI18n, Stack, TextBox } from '@motifx-community/ui';

// The app's own translations; the kit follows their locale.
const i18n = createI18n({
    locale: 'en',
    messages: {
        en: { greeting: 'Hello {name}', hint: 'The clear button is named by the kit' },
        tr: { greeting: 'Merhaba {name}', hint: 'Temizle düğmesini kit adlandırır' },
    },
    dom: false,
});

/** One locale for the app and the kit: `connectI18n` switches the kit whenever the app's translations switch. */
export default class Connect extends Component<HTMLDivElement> {
    override onBuilt(): void {
        this.motif.setDisposable(connectI18n(i18n));
    }

    override view() {
        return (
            <Stack gap="md">
                <Stack orientation="horizontal" wrap align="center">
                    <Button text="English" variant="outline" onclick={() => void i18n.setLocale('en')} />
                    <Button text="Türkçe" variant="outline" onclick={() => void i18n.setLocale('tr')} />
                </Stack>
                <p class="lang-greeting">{() => i18n.t('greeting', { name: 'Ada' })}</p>
                <TextBox label={() => i18n.t('hint')} value="Clear me" clearButton />
            </Stack>
        );
    }
}
```

## Keeping your own strings in sync

The kit does not track anything for you. A language change is reported once, through `uiLocale.onChanged`. Update your own strings there, and use `uiLocale.text` to fill in kit strings, including plurals.

```tsx
import { Component, reactive } from '@motifx/core';
import { Button, NumberBox, Stack, uiLocale } from '@motifx-community/ui';

const OWN = {
    en: { title: 'Orders', hint: 'Written by the app, kept with the kit’s language' },
    tr: { title: 'Siparişler', hint: 'Uygulama yazar, kitin diliyle birlikte değişir' },
};

/** Your own texts drawn again on `uiLocale.onChanged`, and the kit's plural texts filled with `uiLocale.text`. */
export default class OwnTexts extends Component<HTMLDivElement> {
    s = reactive({ count: 3, title: '', hint: '', records: '' });

    override onBuilt(): void {
        this.motif.register(uiLocale.onChanged(() => this.draw()));
        this.draw();
    }

    draw(): void {
        const own = uiLocale.locale.startsWith('tr') ? OWN.tr : OWN.en;
        this.s.title = own.title;
        this.s.hint = own.hint;
        this.s.records = uiLocale.text('gridRecords', { count: this.s.count });
    }

    override view() {
        return (
            <Stack gap="md">
                <Stack orientation="horizontal" wrap align="center">
                    <Button text="English" variant="outline" onclick={() => void uiLocale.use('en')} />
                    <Button text="Türkçe" variant="outline" onclick={() => void uiLocale.use('tr')} />
                </Stack>
                <p>
                    <strong class="lang-own-title">{this.s.title}</strong>
                </p>
                <p>{this.s.hint}</p>
                <Stack orientation="horizontal" wrap align="center">
                    <NumberBox label="Count" min={0} max={99} x-model={() => this.s.count} onValueChanged={() => this.draw()} />
                    <output class="lang-records">{this.s.records}</output>
                </Stack>
            </Stack>
        );
    }
}
```

## Formats for a single control

Dates and numbers follow the kit locale. A control with its own `locale` uses that locale, regardless of the kit language.

```tsx
import { reactive } from '@motifx/core';
import { DateBox, NumberBox, Stack } from '@motifx-community/ui';

/** A control's own `locale` takes precedence over the kit's: these use German and Japanese regardless of the kit language. */
export default function Formats() {
    const s = reactive({ amount: 98765.43, day: new Date(2026, 2, 18) as Date | null });
    return (
        <Stack orientation="horizontal" wrap align="center">
            <NumberBox label="Betrag" locale="de-DE" format={{ style: 'currency', currency: 'EUR' }} x-model={() => s.amount} />
            <DateBox label="日付" locale="ja-JP" x-model={() => s.day} />
            <NumberBox label="The kit's locale" format={{ style: 'currency', currency: 'EUR' }} x-model={() => s.amount} />
        </Stack>
    );
}
```

## Validating a pack

In the repository, `npm run locales` validates every pack the kit ships, and `npm run locales -- path/to/de.json` validates one of your own. The strings are defined in `src/locales/en.json`, and a pack uses the same keys in another language.

| Check | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `Every text` | A pack includes every string in `en.json`. A missing string appears in English, and the check reports which one. |
| `Only the kit’s texts` | A key that does not exist in `en.json` is a typo. |
| `The same arguments` | A string uses the same `{values}` as the English string, in ICU format. Plural forms follow the language. |
| `The interface` | `UiStrings` and `en.json` declare the same keys. |

## API reference

| Member | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `uiLocale.use(locale)` | `Promise<void>` | Switches to `locale` (`tr`, `tr-TR`). The pack is loaded first if needed, and then every control redraws. A later call takes precedence over one that is still loading. |
| `uiLocale.locale` | `string` | The active locale. |
| `uiLocale.dir` | `'ltr' \| 'rtl'` | The text direction of the active locale. |
| `uiLocale.strings` | `UiStrings` | The active strings. Assigning a set changes the strings and keeps the locale: `uiLocale.strings = { ...uiLocale.strings, close: 'Shut' }`. |
| `uiLocale.text(key, values)` | `string` | Returns a kit string with its values filled in: `uiLocale.text('gridRecords', { count: 3 })`. |
| `uiLocale.add(language, pack)` | `void` | Adds the pack for a language, or adds strings to it. The active language shows them immediately. |
| `uiLocale.loader` | `(language) => Promise<UiPackModule>` | Sets where packs are loaded from. By default, this is the package. |
| `uiLocale.ready` | `Promise<void>` | Resolves once the initial language has loaded. |
| `uiLocale.onChanged` | event | Occurs after the language changes, with `locale` and `previous`. |
| `connectI18n(i18n)` | `() => void` | Keeps the kit language in sync with your application's translations (`@motifx-community/i18n`, or any object with `locale` and `onLocaleChanged`). Returns a function that stops it. |

# Button

> Buttons · @motifx-community/ui 0.1.0-beta.5

A native `<button>` styled with design tokens. It comes in three variants, three tones and three sizes, and supports an icon and an `&` access key. A button can act as a toggle, indicate that work is in progress, and open a menu or any other content, either from the whole button or from an arrow next to it with `split`, so the button keeps its own action.

## Import

```tsx
import { Button, type MenuItem } from '@motifx-community/ui';
```

## Declarative and programmatic

Both approaches are fully supported. Every prop accepts a value or a function, and a function that reads a reactive object keeps the button in sync with it. Setting a property programmatically works the same way.

```tsx
import { reactive } from '@motifx/core';
import { Button, Stack } from '@motifx-community/ui';

/** A button in JSX, and buttons created with `new`, added and bound programmatically. */
export default function Programmatic() {
  let added = 0;
  let toolbar: Stack | null = null;

  const addProgrammatic = () => {
    const n = ++added;
    const state = reactive({ marks: '' });
    const b = new Button({ variant: 'outline' });
    b.text = () => `Button ${n}${state.marks}`; // a function is tracked
    b.motif.on('click', () => (state.marks += ' ✓'));
    toolbar?.controls.add(b);
  };

  return (
    <>
      <Button text="Add a button programmatically" onclick={addProgrammatic} />
      <Stack orientation="horizontal" wrap align="center" ref={(c: Stack) => (toolbar = c)} />
    </>
  );
}
```

## Variants, tones and sizes

`solid` buttons have an opaque fill, a bottom edge, a highlight along the top and a slight movement when pressed. `outline` buttons have a frame, and `ghost` buttons show a background only on hover. The tone sets the colors, and the size sets the height from the density tokens. Turn on Compact above to see the difference.

```tsx
import { reactive } from '@motifx/core';
import { Button, Stack, type ButtonSize, type ButtonTone, type ButtonVariant } from '@motifx-community/ui';

const VARIANTS: ButtonVariant[] = ['solid', 'outline', 'ghost'];
const TONES: ButtonTone[] = ['standard', 'accent', 'danger'];
const SIZES: ButtonSize[] = ['sm', 'md', 'lg'];

/** Every tone in every variant, in the size picked above them. */
export default function VariantsTonesSizes() {
  const s = reactive({ size: 'md' as ButtonSize });
  return (
    <>
      <Stack orientation="horizontal" wrap align="center" role="group" aria-label="Size">
        {SIZES.map((size) => (
          <Button
            key={size}
            text={size}
            size="sm"
            variant={() => (s.size === size ? 'solid' : 'ghost')}
            aria-pressed={() => s.size === size}
            onclick={() => (s.size = size)}
          />
        ))}
      </Stack>
      {TONES.map((tone) => (
        <Stack key={tone} orientation="horizontal" wrap align="center">
          {VARIANTS.map((variant) => (
            <Button key={variant} text={`${tone} ${variant}`} tone={tone} variant={variant} size={() => s.size} />
          ))}
        </Stack>
      ))}
    </>
  );
}
```

## Text, icons and children

`text` sets the caption, and JSX children follow it. `icon` accepts an image address or any element or component, placed before or after the text with `iconPosition`. A button with only an icon needs an accessible name, so give it a `hint`.

```tsx
import { Button } from '@motifx-community/ui';

const SaveIcon = () => (
  <svg viewBox="0 0 16 16" aria-hidden="true">
    <path d="M3 2.5h8l2.5 2.5v8.5h-10.5zM5.5 2.5v3.5h5v-3.5M5 13.5v-4h6v4" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.2" stroke-linejoin="round" />
  </svg>
);

/** An icon from JSX or from an image address, an icon-only button named by its hint, and JSX children. */
export default function IconAndChildren() {
  return (
    <>
      <Button text="Save" icon={() => <SaveIcon />} />
      <Button text="Next" icon="../favicon.svg" iconPosition="end" variant="outline" />
      <Button icon={() => <SaveIcon />} hint="Save" variant="ghost" />
      <Button tone="accent">
        Total <b>42</b>
      </Button>
    </>
  );
}
```

## Toggle buttons

With `toggle`, a click turns `pressed` on and off. `x-model` provides two-way binding.

```tsx
import { reactive } from '@motifx/core';
import { Button } from '@motifx-community/ui';

/** A toggle button bound two-way with x-model. */
export default function Toggle() {
  const s = reactive({ bold: false });
  return (
    <>
      <Button text="Bold" toggle x-model={() => s.bold} />
      <span>
        bold: <output class="bold-state">{() => String(s.bold)}</output>
      </span>
    </>
  );
}
```

## Busy state

While `busy` is set, a spinner appears over the content, clicks are ignored and the size does not change. The text remains available to screen readers, and the button gets `aria-busy`.

```tsx
import { reactive } from '@motifx/core';
import { Button } from '@motifx-community/ui';

/** A button that shows a spinner while its work runs. */
export default function Busy() {
  const s = reactive({ sending: false });

  const send = () => {
    s.sending = true;
    setTimeout(() => (s.sending = false), 1500);
  };

  return <Button text="Send" tone="accent" busy={() => s.sending} onclick={send} />;
}
```

## Disabled state

A disabled button uses the native disabled state, so it leaves the Tab order and cannot be pressed. With `focusableWhenDisabled`, it keeps its place in the Tab order and only gets `aria-disabled`. Keyboard and screen reader users can still reach it, and a hint can explain why it is unavailable.

```tsx
import { reactive } from '@motifx/core';
import { Button } from '@motifx-community/ui';

/** A disabled button leaves the Tab order; with focusableWhenDisabled it keeps its place. */
export default function Disabled() {
  const s = reactive({ enabled: false });
  return (
    <>
      <Button text="Toggle enabled" variant="outline" onclick={() => (s.enabled = !s.enabled)} />
      <Button text="Plain" enabled={() => s.enabled} />
      <Button text="Focusable" enabled={() => s.enabled} focusableWhenDisabled hint="Fill in the form first" />
    </>
  );
}
```

## Menu

With `menu`, the whole button opens a list of commands. Items can have an icon, a check mark or a group separator, and can be disabled or hidden. While the menu is open, each `&` key selects its item. An item field can be a function, and the open menu tracks what it reads.

```tsx
import { reactive } from '@motifx/core';
import { Button, type MenuItem } from '@motifx-community/ui';

const NewIcon = () => (
  <svg viewBox="0 0 16 16" aria-hidden="true">
    <path d="M3 2.5h8l2.5 2.5v8.5h-10.5zM5.5 2.5v3.5h5v-3.5M5 13.5v-4h6v4" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.2" stroke-linejoin="round" />
  </svg>
);

/** A button that opens a menu: an icon, a disabled item, a check mark, group lines and & keys. */
export default function Menu() {
  const s = reactive({ last: '', wrap: true });

  const fileMenu = (): MenuItem[] => [
    { text: '&New', icon: () => <NewIcon />, click: () => (s.last = 'New') },
    { text: '&Open…', click: () => (s.last = 'Open…') },
    { text: 'Open &recent', enabled: false },
    { text: '&Word wrap', checked: () => s.wrap, beginGroup: true, click: () => (s.wrap = !s.wrap) },
    { text: 'E&xit', beginGroup: true, click: () => (s.last = 'Exit') },
  ];

  return (
    <>
      <Button text="&File" menu={fileMenu} variant="outline" />
      <span>
        Last: <output class="menu-log">{() => s.last || '—'}</output>
      </span>
    </>
  );
}
```

## Split button

With `split`, the button keeps its own action (`onclick`) and an arrow next to it opens the menu. The two parts are separate Tab stops, and Alt+Down on the button also opens the menu. You can change `split` at any time, but the menu itself (`split`, `menu` or `dropDown`) must exist when the button is created, because it divides the button into two parts.

```tsx
import { reactive } from '@motifx/core';
import { Button } from '@motifx-community/ui';

/** A split button: its own action, and an arrow that opens the menu. `split` can be switched off. */
export default function Split() {
  const s = reactive({ last: '', split: true });
  return (
    <>
      <Button
        text="Sa&ve"
        tone="accent"
        split={() => s.split}
        onclick={() => (s.last = 'Save')}
        menu={[
          { text: 'Save &as…', click: () => (s.last = 'Save as…') },
          { text: 'Save a&ll', click: () => (s.last = 'Save all') },
        ]}
      />
      <Button text="split" size="sm" variant="ghost" toggle x-model={() => s.split} />
      <span>
        Last: <output class="split-log">{() => s.last || '—'}</output>
      </span>
    </>
  );
}
```

## Any content

`dropDown` opens any component instead of a menu, such as a picker or a small form. Focus moves to its first field, and Escape or a click outside closes it.

```tsx
import { Button, Stack } from '@motifx-community/ui';

/** A button that opens a small form instead of a menu. */
export default function DropDown() {
  return (
    <Button
      text="Filter"
      variant="outline"
      dropDown={
        <Stack orientation="horizontal" wrap align="center" padding="sm">
          <label>
            From <input name="from" type="date" />
          </label>
          <label>
            To <input name="to" type="date" />
          </label>
        </Stack>
      }
    />
  );
}
```

## Keyboard

| Key | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `Enter, Space` | Presses the button. With a menu and no `split`, it opens the menu and moves focus to the first item. |
| `Alt + key (`&Save`)` | Presses the button (Control + Option + key on Apple platforms). |
| `Down / Up` | On a button that opens a menu, or on the arrow of a split button, opens the menu and moves focus to the first or last item. |
| `Alt + Down` | On the main part of a split button, opens the menu. |
| `In the menu: Down / Up` | Moves to the next or previous item, wrapping at the ends. Disabled items are reachable. |
| `In the menu: Home / End` | Moves to the first or last item. |
| `In the menu: a letter` | Selects the item with that `&` key. Otherwise, focus moves to the next item that starts with that letter. |
| `In the menu: Enter, Space` | Selects the focused item. |
| `Escape` | Closes the menu or drop-down, and focus returns to the part that opened it. |
| `Tab` | Closes the menu and moves to the next control. |

## Accessibility

| Topic | Details |
| --- | --- |
| `Element` | A native `<button>` (two with `split`: the button and the arrow), so forms, Enter, Space and screen readers work as expected. |
| `Name` | The text without the `&` marker. An icon-only button is named by its `hint` or by your `aria-label`. The arrow of a split button gets its name from `uiLocale` ("More options"). |
| `Toggle buttons` | `aria-pressed`. |
| `Busy state` | `aria-busy="true"`. The text remains readable under the spinner. |
| `Menu` | `aria-haspopup="menu"` and `aria-expanded` on the part that opens the menu. The list has `role="menu"`, items are `menuitem` or `menuitemcheckbox` with `aria-checked`, disabled items have `aria-disabled`, and group separators are `separator`. |
| `Drop-down` | `aria-haspopup="dialog"`. The popup has `role="dialog"` and is named by the button's text. Focus moves to its first field. |
| `Focus ring` | Shown only during keyboard use, with the design system's double ring. |

## Localization

The only string a button displays on its own is the name of a split button's arrow. It comes from `uiLocale.strings`, which starts from the page's `lang` (English and Turkish are included) and can be set to any `UiStrings`. Every button updates immediately. The set is used as provided, so to change one string, assign a new set: `uiLocale.strings = { ...uiLocale.strings, moreOptions: 'Mehr' }`. Changing a string inside the existing set has no effect.

```tsx
import { reactive } from '@motifx/core';
import { Button, uiLocale } from '@motifx-community/ui';
import { kitTexts } from '../../../shared/kit-texts';

/** The name of a split button's arrow, from uiLocale: an included language or a custom string. */
export default function Localization() {
  const s = reactive({ lang: 'en' });

  const toggle = () => {
    s.lang = s.lang === 'en' ? 'tr' : 'en';
    void uiLocale.use(s.lang);
  };

  return (
    <>
      <Button text={() => (s.lang === 'en' ? 'Language: English' : 'Dil: Türkçe')} variant="outline" onclick={toggle} />
      <Button text="Own text" variant="outline" onclick={() => (uiLocale.strings = { ...uiLocale.strings, moreOptions: 'Mehr' })} />
      <span>
        The arrow above is named <output class="arrow-name">{() => kitTexts.strings.moreOptions}</output>
      </span>
    </>
  );
}
```

## Styling

| Hook | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `.mx-button` | The button, or the group of a button with a menu. `data-variant`, `data-tone`, `data-size`, `data-icon-position`, `data-stretch`, `data-pressed`, `data-busy`, `data-icon`, `data-mode="menu\|split"`. |
| `.mx-button__face` | The pressable part: the button itself, or `.mx-button__main` and `.mx-button__arrow`. |
| `.mx-button__icon, .mx-button__chevron, .mx-button__spinner` | The icon, the arrow glyph of a menu button and the busy spinner. |
| `.mx-popup` | The surface the menu opens on (`data-side="bottom\|top"`). |
| `.mx-menu, .mx-menu__item, .mx-menu__separator` | The menu, its items and its group separators. |

### Component tokens

| Token | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `button.face` | Unit: the pressable part, with its frame (the bottom side is the key edge), its fill and state layer (`image`) and its focus ring (outline and `glow`). Each appearance is a state (`accent`, `danger`, `outline`, `outline-accent`, `ghost`, …), and each appearance has its own states (`hover`, `toggled-hover`, `open`, `pressed`, `focus`, `toggled`, `disabled`: `outline-hover`, `accent-pressed`, …). There are also `icon-only`, `busy`, and the `main` and `arrow` parts of a split button. |
| `button.icon, button.caption, button.chevron, button.spinner, button.divider` | Units: the icon, the text, the menu arrow (`open`), the busy spinner and the split button divider. Each appearance is a state. |
| `button.height.{sm,md,lg}, button.padding.{sm,md,lg}, button.font-size.{sm,md,lg}, button.line-height.{sm,md,lg}` | Sizes are defined by the density tokens. |
| `button.press-offset, button.icon-only-square, button.text-box, button.spinner-duration` | The distance a solid button moves when pressed, the square icon button, the caption line box and the spinner rotation. |
| `popup.surface, menu.*` | The popup surface and the menu items. |

All of these reference design system tokens (see [Tokens](tokens.md)). Override one after `styles.css` to restyle every button.

## API reference

### Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `text` | `Bind<string>` | `''` | The caption. `&` marks the access key (`&Save` → Alt+S), and `&&` produces a literal `&`. JSX children follow it. |
| `variant` | `Bind<ButtonVariant>` | `'solid'` | `solid` (filled and pressable), `outline` (framed) or `ghost` (visible only on hover). |
| `tone` | `Bind<ButtonTone>` | `'standard'` | `standard`, `accent` for the primary action, or `danger` for a destructive action. |
| `size` | `Bind<ButtonSize>` | `'md'` | `sm`, `md` or `lg`, which map to the control heights in the density tokens. |
| `icon` | `Bind<IconSource \| null>` | — | An image address, or any element or component (an `<svg>` in JSX, an icon font tag). It is decorative and hidden from screen readers. |
| `iconPosition` | `Bind<'start' \| 'end'>` | `'start'` | Places the icon before or after the text. |
| `stretch` | `Bind<boolean>` | `false` | Stretches to the full width of its container. |
| `type` | `Bind<'button' \| 'submit' \| 'reset'>` | `'button'` | The native type. The default is `button`, so a button inside a form never submits by accident. |
| `hint` | `Bind<string>` | `''` | A tooltip (`title`). It also provides the name of an icon-only button. |
| `toggle` | `Bind<boolean>` | `false` | Makes it a toggle button. A click turns `pressed` on and off (`aria-pressed`). |
| `pressed` | `Bind<boolean>` | `false` | The state of a toggle button. `x-model` provides two-way binding. |
| `busy` | `Bind<boolean>` | `false` | Indicates that work is in progress. A spinner appears over the content, clicks are ignored, the size is preserved and `aria-busy` is set. |
| `focusableWhenDisabled` | `Bind<boolean>` | `false` | When disabled, the button stays in the Tab order with `aria-disabled`, so a screen reader can find it and announce it as dimmed. |
| `split` | `Bind<boolean>` | `false` | With a menu, the button keeps its own action and an arrow next to it opens the menu. Without `split`, the whole button opens the menu. |
| `menu` | `Bind<readonly MenuItem[]>` | — | The menu commands, read each time the menu opens. |
| `dropDown` | `Bind<ComponentBase \| null>` | — | Any content to open instead of a menu, such as a picker or a small form. |
| `enabled / disabled, visible, tabStop, tabIndex` | see Control |  | Properties shared by all controls. |

### Properties

| Property | Access | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `every prop above` | read/write, reactive | Set programmatically with a value or a function, the same as the prop: `b.tone = () => this.state.tone` is tracked, and `b.tone = 'accent'` replaces it. |
| `value` | read/write | Maps to `pressed` for `x-model`. |
| `opened` | read/write, reactive | Indicates whether the menu or drop-down is open. Set it to open or close it. |
| `hasMenu` | read-only | Indicates whether the button was created with `split`, `menu` or `dropDown`. |

### Methods

| Method | Returns | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `open()` | `boolean` | Opens the menu or drop-down with focus on its first item. Returns `false` if there is nothing to open, or if the button is disabled or busy. |
| `close()` | `void` | Closes it. If focus is inside, it returns to the part that opened it. |
| `refresh()` | `void` | Your menu items can be plain or reactive, and the button reads them as they are. After changing them in place, call `refresh()`. An open menu shows the change immediately. |
| `focus()` | `boolean` | Sets focus on the button, or on its main part if it has a menu. |

### Events

| Event | When |
| --- | --- |
| `onclick` | The DOM click event of the button, which runs its own action. With `split`, the arrow and the menu do not raise it. With a menu and no `split`, the click opens the menu. |
| `onItemClick(e)` | Occurs when a menu item is selected, after the item's own `click`. `e`: `{ item, source, event }`. |

### MenuItem

| Field | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `text` | `Bind<string>` | The label. `&` marks the key that selects it while the menu is open. |
| `icon` | `Bind<IconSource>` | An icon. A function is called each time the item is drawn. |
| `hint` | `Bind<string>` | The tooltip text. |
| `enabled` | `Bind<boolean>` | `false` shows the item dimmed. It stays reachable but cannot be selected. |
| `visible` | `Bind<boolean>` | `false` removes the item. |
| `checked` | `Bind<boolean>` | When set, the item is a `menuitemcheckbox` and shows a check mark when `true`. Change it in `click`. |
| `beginGroup` | `Bind<boolean>` | Draws a separator before the item. |
| `click(e)` | function | Runs when the item is selected, after the menu closes. |
| `data` | `unknown` | A custom application value. |

The menu and the surface it opens on are shared parts, `MenuList` and `Popup`, exported for use in other components.

# ButtonGroup

> Buttons · @motifx-community/ui 0.1.0-beta.5

A set of related buttons, used as a segmented selection of one or more options or as a row of actions. The buttons are standard kit buttons and are attached by default.

## Import

```tsx
import { ButtonGroup } from '@motifx-community/ui';
```

## Declarative and programmatic

Every prop accepts a value or a function, and `x-model` provides two-way binding for the value. When you create the component with `new`, set the same properties programmatically.

```tsx
import { reactive } from '@motifx/core';
import { ButtonGroup, Stack } from '@motifx-community/ui';

/** One choice bound with `x-model`, and a group created with `new` that accepts the same properties programmatically. */
export default function Programmatic() {
  const s = reactive({ view: 'Week' as unknown });
  const coded = new ButtonGroup({ label: 'Density', items: ['Compact', 'Comfortable'], value: 'Compact' });

  return (
    <Stack gap="lg">
      <ButtonGroup label="View" items={['Day', 'Week', 'Month']} x-model={() => s.view} />
      <span>{() => `View: ${s.view}`}</span>
      <span onConfig={(c) => c.controls.add(coded)} />
    </Stack>
  );
}
```

## Multiple selection and action groups

```tsx
import { reactive } from '@motifx/core';
import { ButtonGroup, Stack } from '@motifx-community/ui';

const MARKS = [
  { value: 'bold', text: 'Bold' },
  { value: 'italic', text: 'Italic' },
  { value: 'underline', text: 'Underline' },
];

/** Several on and off (`multiple`), and plain actions (`none`, `onItemClick`). */
export default function Selections() {
  const s = reactive({ marks: ['bold'] as unknown, last: '' });

  return (
    <Stack gap="lg">
      <ButtonGroup label="Text marks" selection="multiple" items={MARKS} x-model={() => s.marks} />
      <span>{() => `Marks: ${(s.marks as string[]).join(', ') || 'none'}`}</span>
      <ButtonGroup label="Clipboard" selection="none" items={['Cut', 'Copy', 'Paste']} onItemClick={(e) => (s.last = String(e.value))} />
      <span>{() => (s.last ? `Pressed: ${s.last}` : 'Nothing pressed yet')}</span>
    </Stack>
  );
}
```

## Sizes and layout

```tsx
import { ButtonGroup, Stack, type ButtonSize } from '@motifx-community/ui';

const SIZES: ButtonSize[] = ['sm', 'md', 'lg'];
const ITEMS = ['One', 'Two', { value: 'Three', enabled: false }, 'Four'];

/** Each size; apart instead of touching; filling the width; and one button disabled. */
export default function Looks() {
  return (
    <Stack gap="lg">
      {SIZES.map((size) => (
        <ButtonGroup key={size} label={`Size ${size}`} size={size} items={ITEMS} value="Two" />
      ))}
      <ButtonGroup label="Apart" attached={false} items={ITEMS} value="One" />
      <ButtonGroup label="Stretched" stretch items={['Left', 'Center', 'Right']} value="Center" />
    </Stack>
  );
}
```

## Keyboard

| Key | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `Tab` | One Tab stop: the button focused last, otherwise the selected one, otherwise the first. |
| `Arrow keys, Home, End` | Moves between the buttons, skipping disabled ones. |
| `Space, Enter` | Presses the button, which selects it, toggles it or runs its action. |

## Accessibility

| Topic | Details |
| --- | --- |
| `Group` | `role="group"` with its label. |
| `Buttons` | Kit buttons. With a selection, each one reports whether it is on (`aria-pressed`). An icon-only button is named by its `hint`. |

## Styling

| Hook | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `.mx-button-group` | The group. `data-attached`, `data-stretch`. |
| `.mx-button-group__item` | Each button (a `.mx-button`). |

### Component tokens

| Token | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `button-group.item.*` | Place: the appearance of each button in a group (`variant`) and of the selected one (`face.*-toggled.*`). |
| `button-group.inner-start.*, button-group.inner-end.*` | Places: the corners where two buttons meet. |
| `button-group.attached, button-group.gap` | Whether buttons are attached by default, and the gap between them when they are not. |

## API reference

### Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `items` | `Bind<readonly (ButtonGroupItem<T> \| T)[]>` | `[]` | The buttons: `ButtonGroupItem` objects (`value`, `text`, `icon`, `hint`, `enabled`, `visible`), plain values that serve as their own text, or objects of any shape. |
| `itemText, itemValue` | `ItemField` | `'text'`, `'value'` | The location of the text and value in a custom object: a property name or a function. |
| `selection` | `Bind<ButtonGroupSelection>` | `'single'` | `single` selects one button, `multiple` toggles each button, and `none` makes them actions only. |
| `value` | `Bind<T \| readonly T[] \| null>` | `null` / `[]` | The selected value, or an array of the values that are on. `x-model` provides two-way binding, and each change produces a new array. |
| `allowEmpty` | `Bind<boolean>` | `false` | With `single`, pressing the selected button again clears the selection. |
| `attached` | `Bind<boolean>` | Set by the design language (`true`) | The buttons are attached and share their edges. |
| `variant` | `Bind<ButtonVariant>` | Set by the design language (`outline`) | The appearance of every button. |
| `size` | `Bind<ButtonSize>` | `'md'` | `sm`, `md`, `lg`. |
| `stretch` | `Bind<boolean>` | `false` | Stretches to the full width, with the buttons sharing it evenly. |
| `label` | `Bind<string>` | `''` | The accessible name of the group (“Text alignment”). |
| `enabled, visible` | see Control |  | Properties shared by all controls. |

### Events, properties and methods

| Member | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `onValueChanged` | event | Occurs when the value changes (`value`), either through user input or programmatically (`byUser`). |
| `onItemClick` | event | Occurs when a button is pressed (`item`, `value`), with any selection mode. |
| `buttons` | read-only | The kit buttons in the group, in item order. |
| `isSelected(value)` | `boolean` | Indicates whether the button for `value` is selected or on. |
| `refresh()` | `void` | Re-reads the items after they have been changed in place. |

# Toolbar

> Buttons · @motifx-community/ui 0.1.0-beta.5

A command bar that holds buttons, toggle buttons, menus and fields, organized in groups with separators. The toolbar is a single Tab stop, and the arrow keys move between its controls. Items that do not fit move into an overflow menu at the end. You can define items as data, as JSX children, or both.

## Import

```tsx
import { Toolbar, ToolbarSeparator, type ToolbarItem } from '@motifx-community/ui';
```

## Declarative and programmatic

`items` defines commands as data, where each field is a value or a function. JSX children of any control type follow them. Programmatically, fill a toolbar as you would any control: `toolbar.controls.add(button)`. Every prop is also a property.

```tsx
/** A small outline icon drawn from one path. */
function icon(d: string) {
  return () => (
    <svg viewBox="0 0 16 16" aria-hidden="true">
      <path d={d} fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.5" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" />
    </svg>
  );
}

export const BoldIcon = icon('M4.5 3h4.25a2.5 2.5 0 0 1 0 5H4.5zM4.5 8h5a2.5 2.5 0 0 1 0 5h-5z');
export const ItalicIcon = icon('M7 3h5M4 13h5M10 3L6 13');
export const UnderlineIcon = icon('M4.5 2.5v5a3.5 3.5 0 0 0 7 0v-5M3.5 14h9');
export const AlignLeftIcon = icon('M2.5 4h11M2.5 8h7M2.5 12h9');
export const AlignCenterIcon = icon('M2.5 4h11M4.5 8h7M3.5 12h9');
export const AlignRightIcon = icon('M2.5 4h11M6.5 8h7M4.5 12h9');
export const UndoIcon = icon('M5.5 3.5L2.5 6.5l3 3M2.5 6.5h7a3.5 3.5 0 0 1 0 7h-2');
export const RedoIcon = icon('M10.5 3.5l3 3-3 3M13.5 6.5h-7a3.5 3.5 0 0 0 0 7h2');
export const LinkIcon = icon('M7 9a2.5 2.5 0 0 0 3.5 0l2-2a2.5 2.5 0 0 0-3.5-3.5l-.75.75M9 7a2.5 2.5 0 0 0-3.5 0l-2 2A2.5 2.5 0 0 0 7 12.5l.75-.75');
export const ImageIcon = icon('M2.5 3.5h11v9h-11zM2.5 10.5l3-3 3 3 2-2 3 3M10 6.25v.1');
```

```tsx
import { reactive, type Component } from '@motifx/core';
import { Button, Toolbar } from '@motifx-community/ui';

/** A toolbar created with `new` and filled with `controls.add`. */
export default function Programmatic() {
  const s = reactive({ log: '' });
  let added = 0;

  const bar = new Toolbar({ label: 'Actions', size: 'sm' });
  bar.controls.add(new Button({ text: 'First', onclick: () => (s.log = 'First pressed') }));

  const addProgrammatic = () => {
    const n = ++added;
    bar.controls.add(new Button({ text: `Button ${n}`, onclick: () => (s.log = `Button ${n} pressed`) }));
  };

  return (
    <>
      <Button text="Add a button programmatically" variant="outline" onclick={addProgrammatic} />
      <div style="inline-size: 100%" ref={(c: Component<HTMLDivElement>) => c.controls.add(bar)} />
      <output>{() => s.log}</output>
    </>
  );
}
```

## Toggle groups and separators

A `toggle` item is a toggle button (`aria-pressed`). When bound to the application with a function, it reflects application state. In the example above, Bold, Italic and Underline are independent toggles, and the alignment buttons form a group where one is pressed. `separator` items, or `<ToolbarSeparator />`, draw the lines between groups.

```tsx
/** A small outline icon drawn from one path. */
function icon(d: string) {
  return () => (
    <svg viewBox="0 0 16 16" aria-hidden="true">
      <path d={d} fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.5" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" />
    </svg>
  );
}

export const BoldIcon = icon('M4.5 3h4.25a2.5 2.5 0 0 1 0 5H4.5zM4.5 8h5a2.5 2.5 0 0 1 0 5h-5z');
export const ItalicIcon = icon('M7 3h5M4 13h5M10 3L6 13');
export const UnderlineIcon = icon('M4.5 2.5v5a3.5 3.5 0 0 0 7 0v-5M3.5 14h9');
export const AlignLeftIcon = icon('M2.5 4h11M2.5 8h7M2.5 12h9');
export const AlignCenterIcon = icon('M2.5 4h11M4.5 8h7M3.5 12h9');
export const AlignRightIcon = icon('M2.5 4h11M6.5 8h7M4.5 12h9');
export const UndoIcon = icon('M5.5 3.5L2.5 6.5l3 3M2.5 6.5h7a3.5 3.5 0 0 1 0 7h-2');
export const RedoIcon = icon('M10.5 3.5l3 3-3 3M13.5 6.5h-7a3.5 3.5 0 0 0 0 7h2');
```
