# LoadPanel

> Feedback · @motifx-community/ui 0.1.0-beta.5

A loading overlay for a container or the whole page. It includes a shade, a panel with the kit spinner and a message, and a Cancel button when the operation can be stopped. The content underneath is unavailable while it is shown, and focus returns afterward.

## Import

```tsx
import { LoadPanel } from '@motifx-community/ui';
```

## Covering a container

`target` specifies the component or element to cover. `value` or `x-model` shows and hides the panel, or you can call `show()` and `hide()`. `delay` keeps it from flashing during quick operations.

```tsx
import { reactive } from '@motifx/core';
import { Button, LoadPanel, Panel, Stack, TextBox } from '@motifx-community/ui';

/** A load panel over a panel while its orders load: bound with x-model, shown after a short delay. */
export default function Container() {
    const s = reactive({ loading: false, result: '' });
    let panel!: Panel;

    // Simulates a server call.
    const load = () => {
        s.loading = true;
        s.result = '';
        setTimeout(() => {
            s.loading = false;
            s.result = 'Orders loaded.';
        }, 1800);
    };

    return (
        <Stack gap="md" style="inline-size: 100%">
            <Panel class="lp-panel" variant="outline" padding="md" style="min-block-size: 10rem" ref={(c: Panel) => (panel = c)}>
                <Stack orientation="horizontal" wrap align="center">
                    <TextBox label="Customer" value="Ada" />
                    <Button text="Load orders" tone="accent" onclick={load} />
                </Stack>
            </Panel>
            <LoadPanel target={() => panel} message="Loading orders" delay={200} x-model={() => s.loading} />
            <output class="lp-result">{() => s.result}</output>
        </Stack>
    );
}
```

## Covering the page, with Cancel

```tsx
import { reactive } from '@motifx/core';
import { Button, LoadPanel, Stack } from '@motifx-community/ui';

/** Over the whole page, with a Cancel button: the work stops when it is pressed (or on Escape). */
export default function Page() {
    const s = reactive({ told: '' });
    let timer: ReturnType<typeof setTimeout> | null = null;
    const panel = new LoadPanel({
        message: 'Building the report…',
        cancelable: true,
        onCancel: () => {
            if (timer) clearTimeout(timer);
            timer = null;
            s.told = 'Cancelled.';
        }
    });
    const start = () => {
        s.told = '';
        panel.show();
        timer = setTimeout(() => {
            timer = null;
            panel.hide();
            s.told = 'The report is ready.';
        }, 4000);
    };
    return (
        <Stack orientation="horizontal" wrap align="center">
            <Button text="Build the report" variant="outline" onclick={start} />
            <span onConfig={c => c.controls.add(panel)} />
            <output class="lp-told">{() => s.told}</output>
        </Stack>
    );
}
```

## Shade, panel and indicator

```tsx
import { reactive } from '@motifx/core';
import { Button, LoadPanel, Panel, Stack } from '@motifx-community/ui';

/** Without the shade, the panel or the indicator. A click on the shade can hide it. */
export default function Options() {
    const s = reactive({ clear: false, bare: false, words: false });
    let clear!: Panel;
    let bare!: Panel;
    let words!: Panel;
    const flash = (key: 'clear' | 'bare' | 'words') => {
        s[key] = true;
        setTimeout(() => (s[key] = false), 2500);
    };
    return (
        <Stack orientation="horizontal" wrap align="center" style="inline-size: 100%">
            <Panel variant="outline" padding="md" style="min-inline-size: 16rem; min-block-size: 9rem" ref={(c: Panel) => (clear = c)}>
                <Button text="No shade" variant="outline" onclick={() => flash('clear')} />
            </Panel>
            <LoadPanel target={() => clear} shade={false} x-model={() => s.clear} closeOnOutside />
            <Panel variant="outline" padding="md" style="min-inline-size: 16rem; min-block-size: 9rem" ref={(c: Panel) => (bare = c)}>
                <Button text="No pane" variant="outline" onclick={() => flash('bare')} />
            </Panel>
            <LoadPanel target={() => bare} showPane={false} x-model={() => s.bare} />
            <Panel variant="outline" padding="md" style="min-inline-size: 16rem; min-block-size: 9rem" ref={(c: Panel) => (words = c)}>
                <Button text="Words only" variant="outline" onclick={() => flash('words')} />
            </Panel>
            <LoadPanel target={() => words} showIndicator={false} message="Please wait" x-model={() => s.words} />
        </Stack>
    );
}
```

## Behavior

| Topic | Details |
| --- | --- |
| `Covering a container` | The panel is placed inside the container, above its content. The container gets `aria-busy`, and the content under the panel is inert, so it cannot be clicked or focused. |
| `Over the page` | Without a `target`, the panel covers the viewport and the rest of the page is inert. |
| `Focus` | Focus moves from the content underneath to the panel (to the Cancel button if there is one) and returns to its original position when the panel hides. |
| `Delay` | Quick operations show nothing. The panel appears after `delay`, and hiding it before then cancels it. |
| `Spinner.cover` | The kit spinner can cover a container with a single call (`Spinner.cover`). LoadPanel is the full component, with the panel, message, delay and button. |

## Accessibility

| Topic | Details |
| --- | --- |
| `Pane` | A `status` region. The message is announced when the panel appears and when it changes. |
| `Indicator` | Decorative. The message describes what is happening. |
| `Under it` | `inert` and `aria-busy`, so screen readers skip the content and it cannot receive clicks or focus. |
| `Cancel` | A kit button named in the kit language. Escape activates it. |

## Styling

| Hook | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `.mx-load-panel` | The layer. `data-shade`, `data-pane`, `data-page`. |
| `.mx-load-panel__pane` | The panel. |
| `.mx-load-panel__indicator, .mx-load-panel__message, .mx-load-panel__cancel` | The spinner, the message and the button. |

### Component tokens

| Token | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `load-panel.shade, .pane, .message` | Units: the layer (`shaded`), the panel (`shown`) and the message. |
| `load-panel.cancel` | Place: the appearance of the Cancel button (`variant`). |
| `load-panel.padding, .gap` | The minimum distance to the edge of the covered area, and the space between the indicator, message and button. |

## API reference

### Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `target` | `Bind<ComponentBase \| HTMLElement \| null>` | `null` | The area to cover, a component or element. `null` covers the whole page. |
| `message` | `Bind<string>` | The kit string “Loading…” | The message below the indicator. This is the same property as `text`. |
| `value` | `Bind<boolean>` | `false` | Indicates whether the panel is shown. `x-model` provides two-way binding. |
| `delay` | `Bind<number>` | `0` | The delay in milliseconds before it appears. Hiding it before then shows nothing. |
| `shade` | `Bind<boolean>` | `true` | Dims the covered area. |
| `showPane` | `Bind<boolean>` | `true` | Shows the box behind the indicator and the message. |
| `showIndicator` | `Bind<boolean>` | `true` | Shows the rotating indicator (the kit spinner). |
| `cancelable` | `Bind<boolean>` | `false` | Shows a Cancel button in the panel. Escape activates it too. |
| `cancelText` | `Bind<string>` | The kit string “Cancel” | The button text. |
| `closeOnOutside` | `Bind<boolean>` | `false` | Clicking the shade hides the panel. |

### Events, properties and methods

| Member | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `onShown, onHidden` | event | Occur when the panel appears (after its delay) and when it is hidden. |
| `onCancel` | event | Occurs when the Cancel button or Escape is pressed. The panel hides afterward. |
| `show(), hide(), cancel()` | `boolean` / `void` | Programmatic control. `show()` returns `false` while the panel is shown or waiting for its delay. |
| `isShown` | read-only | Indicates whether the panel is currently on screen. |
| `spinner, cancelButton` | read-only | The kit spinner and button in the panel. |

## Feedback

# Toast

> Feedback · @motifx-community/ui 0.1.0-beta.5

Brief notifications at the edge of the window, with four tones, an optional action such as Undo, a custom duration or none, six positions and a limit on how many appear at once. Show them programmatically, or place a custom region in JSX.

## Import

```tsx
import { toast, Toast, Toaster, type ToastTone, type ToastPosition } from '@motifx-community/ui';
```

## Programmatic and declarative use

`toast.show()` and its tone shortcuts return a `Toast` object that you can `close()`, `update()` or await. They use `Toaster.default`, which is created in `document.body` on first use. An application can place its own `Toaster` anywhere in JSX and make it the default.

```tsx
import { reactive } from '@motifx/core';
import { Button, toast, type Toast } from '@motifx-community/ui';

/** Toasts shown programmatically. The returned Toast can be closed and awaited. */
export default function Programmatic() {
  const s = reactive({ reason: '' });

  const exportFile = () => {
    const t = toast.show({ title: 'Export', text: 'Preparing the file…', duration: 0 });
    setTimeout(() => t.close(), 2000);
  };

  const watch = async () => {
    s.reason = 'waiting…';
    const t: Toast = toast.show({ text: 'Close me any way you like.', duration: 3000, action: { text: 'Done' } });
    s.reason = `closed by: ${await t.closed}`;
  };

  return (
    <>
      <Button text="Show a toast" tone="accent" onclick={() => toast.success('Your changes are saved.', { title: 'Saved' })} />
      <Button text="Export" variant="outline" onclick={exportFile} />
      <Button text="Watch how it closes" variant="outline" onclick={watch} />
      <output class="toast-reason">{() => s.reason}</output>
    </>
  );
}
```

## Tones

`tone` sets the glyph, its color, and how screen readers announce the toast: politely for `info` and `success`, and immediately for `caution` and `danger`.

```tsx
import { Button, toast, type ToastTone } from '@motifx-community/ui';

const TONES: { tone: ToastTone; text: string }[] = [
  { tone: 'info', text: 'A new version is ready.' },
  { tone: 'success', text: 'Your changes are saved.' },
  { tone: 'caution', text: 'Your session ends in 5 minutes.' },
  { tone: 'danger', text: 'The server did not answer.' },
];

/** A toast in each of the four tones. */
export default function Tones() {
  return (
    <>
      {TONES.map(({ tone, text }) => (
        <Button key={tone} text={tone} variant="outline" onclick={() => toast.show({ tone, text })} />
      ))}
    </>
  );
}
```

## Action and Undo

`action` adds a button that runs `click` and then closes the toast. Offering Undo is usually better than asking for confirmation first.

```tsx
import { reactive } from '@motifx/core';
import { Button, Stack, toast } from '@motifx-community/ui';

/** Archiving a mail at once, with an Undo button in the toast that brings it back. */
export default function Undo() {
  const s = reactive({ mails: ['Invoice #1042', 'Team lunch on Friday', 'Your order shipped'] });

  const archive = () => {
    const mail = s.mails.shift();
    if (!mail) return;
    toast.info(`“${mail}” archived.`, { action: { text: 'Undo', click: () => s.mails.unshift(mail) } });
  };

  return (
    <>
      <p class="toast-mails">{() => (s.mails.length ? `Inbox: ${s.mails.join(' · ')}` : 'The inbox is empty.')}</p>
      <Stack orientation="horizontal" wrap align="center">
        <Button text="Archive the first" variant="outline" enabled={() => s.mails.length > 0} onclick={archive} />
      </Stack>
    </>
  );
}
```

## Duration and updates

`duration` is 5 seconds by default, and `0` keeps the toast open until it is closed. Every option also accepts a function, and `update()` changes a visible toast and restarts its timer.

```tsx
import { reactive } from '@motifx/core';
import { Button, toast } from '@motifx-community/ui';

/** A toast with a live text that stays until the upload ends, then turns into a success; one that stays. */
export default function DurationAndUpdate() {
  const s = reactive({ progress: 0, uploading: false });

  const upload = () => {
    if (s.uploading) return;
    s.uploading = true;
    s.progress = 0;
    const t = toast.show({ title: 'report.pdf', text: () => `Uploading… ${s.progress}%`, duration: 0, closeButton: false });
    const timer = setInterval(() => {
      s.progress = Math.min(100, s.progress + 10);
      if (s.progress < 100) return;
      clearInterval(timer);
      s.uploading = false;
      t.update({ text: 'Uploaded.', tone: 'success', duration: 4000, closeButton: true });
    }, 300);
    void t.closed.then(() => clearInterval(timer));
  };

  return (
    <>
      <Button text="Upload a file" variant="outline" enabled={() => !s.uploading} onclick={upload} />
      <Button text="A toast that stays" variant="outline" onclick={() => toast.caution('This one stays until you close it.', { duration: 0 })} />
      <Button text="Close all" variant="ghost" onclick={() => toast.closeAll()} />
    </>
  );
}
```

## Positions

There are six positions, and start and end follow the reading direction. The newest toast is closest to the edge. A toast's `position` takes precedence over the toaster's.

```tsx
import { Button, toast, type ToastPosition } from '@motifx-community/ui';

const POSITIONS: ToastPosition[] = ['top-start', 'top', 'top-end', 'bottom-start', 'bottom', 'bottom-end'];

/** A toast at each of the six positions. */
export default function Positions() {
  return (
    <>
      {POSITIONS.map((position) => (
        <Button key={position} text={position} size="sm" variant="outline" onclick={() => toast.info(`At ${position}.`, { position })} />
      ))}
    </>
  );
}
```

## Custom toaster and max

A `Toaster` is the region toasts appear in. `max` limits how many appear at once in one position, and the rest wait until others close. This one is placed directly in the page, so Tab reaches its toasts after these buttons.

```tsx
import { reactive } from '@motifx/core';
import { Button, Stack, Toaster } from '@motifx-community/ui';

/** A toaster placed in the page, showing at most `max` toasts at once. */
export default function OwnToaster() {
  const s = reactive({ max: 2, count: 0 });
  let uploads: Toaster | null = null;

  const addFive = () => {
    for (let i = 0; i < 5; i++) uploads?.success(`photo-${++s.count}.jpg is uploaded.`, { duration: 3000 });
  };

  return (
    <>
      <Toaster ref={(t: Toaster) => (uploads = t)} position="top-start" max={() => s.max} text="Demo notifications" />
      <Stack orientation="horizontal" wrap align="center" role="group" aria-label="Max">
        {[1, 2, 3].map((max) => (
          <Button
            key={max}
            text={`max ${max}`}
            size="sm"
            variant={() => (s.max === max ? 'solid' : 'ghost')}
            aria-pressed={() => s.max === max}
            onclick={() => (s.max = max)}
          />
        ))}
      </Stack>
      <Button text="Add five" variant="outline" onclick={addFive} />
    </>
  );
}
```

## Keyboard

| Key | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `F8 (`hotkey`)` | From anywhere on the page, moves focus to the newest toast. Inside a toast, returns focus to where it was. |
| `Tab` | Moves through the toasts and their buttons. The default toaster is the last element on the page, so Tab reaches it after the page content. |
| `Escape` | With focus in a toast, closes it. Focus moves to the next toast, or back to where it came from. |

## Accessibility

| Topic | Details |
| --- | --- |
| `Region` | `<section role="region">` named "Notifications" (`uiLocale`), with `aria-keyshortcuts` for the hotkey. |
| `Read out` | Info and success toasts are announced politely (`role="status"`), and caution and danger toasts immediately (`role="alert"`). `update()` announces the toast again. A live `text` function does not, so a progress number is not read on every change. |
| `Focus` | A toast never takes focus. Each one is a group named by its title and text, and has its own Tab stop, so toasts without buttons can also be reached. |
| `Time` | Timers stop while the pointer or focus is on the toasts and while the page is hidden (WCAG 2.2.1). Use `duration: 0` for anything the user must act on. |
| `Motion` | It slides in and fades out using the motion tokens. When the user prefers reduced motion, it appears without animation. |

## Localization

The names of the region and the close button come from `uiLocale.strings` (`notifications`, `close`) and update immediately.

```tsx
import { reactive } from '@motifx/core';
import { Button, toast, uiLocale } from '@motifx-community/ui';

/** Switches the names of the region and the close button. */
export default function Localization() {
  const s = reactive({ lang: 'en' });

  const toggle = () => {
    s.lang = s.lang === 'en' ? 'tr' : 'en';
    void uiLocale.use(s.lang);
  };

  return (
    <>
      <Button text={() => (s.lang === 'en' ? 'Language: English' : 'Dil: Türkçe')} variant="outline" onclick={toggle} />
      <Button text="Show a toast" variant="outline" onclick={() => toast.info(s.lang === 'en' ? 'Hello.' : 'Merhaba.')} />
    </>
  );
}
```

## Styling

| Hook | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `.mx-toaster` | The region. |
| `.mx-toaster__stack` | A stack at one position. `data-position`. |
| `.mx-toast` | A toast. `data-tone`, `data-state` (`entering`, `shown`, `leaving`). |
| `.mx-toast__icon, .mx-toast__body, .mx-toast__title, .mx-toast__text` | The parts of the component. |
| `.mx-toast__action, .mx-toast__close` | Its buttons (Button, `sm`). |

### Component tokens

| Token | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `toast.width` | The width of a toast, which never exceeds the window. |
| `toast.inset, toast.slide, toast.slide-inline` | The distance to the window edge, and how far the toast slides in from it (at a corner, also from the side). |
| `toast.buttons-align` | The alignment of the action and close buttons. |
| `toast.stack, toast.surface` | Units: the space between toasts, and the toast with its box per tone (`success`, `caution`, `danger`) and for keyboard focus (`focus`). |
| `toast.stripe, toast.timer` | Optional units: a stripe along the start edge, and a line that shrinks with the remaining time, per tone. |
| `toast.icon, toast.plate, toast.mark` | Units: the tone glyph and a plate behind it, per tone, and the tone's own mark. |
| `toast.title, toast.message, toast.action-room, toast.close-room` | Units: the title, the message and the spacing around the buttons. Their appearance comes from the `action` and `close` places. |

## API reference

### Toast options and props

| Option | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `text` | `Bind<string>` | `''` | The message. |
| `title` | `Bind<string>` | `''` | A bold line above the message. |
| `tone` | `Bind<ToastTone>` | `'info'` | `info`, `success`, `caution` or `danger`, which set the glyph, its color and how screen readers announce the toast. |
| `icon` | `Bind<IconSource \| null>` | The tone glyph | A custom icon, or `null` for none. |
| `duration` | `Bind<number>` | `5000` | The time it stays, in milliseconds. `0` keeps it open until it is closed. |
| `action` | `Bind<ToastAction \| null>` | — | `{ text, click }` adds a button to the toast, such as Undo. It runs `click(toast)` and then closes the toast. |
| `closeButton` | `Bind<boolean>` | `true` | Shows a close button named from `uiLocale`. |
| `position` | `Bind<ToastPosition>` | From the toaster | The stacking position: `top-start`, `top`, `top-end`, `bottom-start`, `bottom` or `bottom-end`. |
| `onClosed` | `(reason) => void` | — | See Events. |

### toast and Toast

| Member | Returns | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `toast.show(options \| Toast)` | `Toast` | Shows a toast on `Toaster.default`. |
| `toast.info / success / caution / danger(text, options?)` | `Toast` | Same as `show`, with the tone already set. |
| `toast.closeAll()` | `void` | Closes every toast on `Toaster.default`. |
| `t.close(reason?)` | `void` | Closes the toast. A closed toast is disposed. |
| `t.update(options)` | `void` | Changes any options, restarts the timer and announces the toast again. |
| `t.closed` | `Promise<ToastCloseReason>` | Resolves when the toast closes, with `timeout`, `button`, `escape`, `action` or `code`. |
| `t.onClosed(fn)` | event | The same information as an event. |
| `t.text, t.tone, …` | read/write, reactive | Every option is also a property that accepts a value or a function. |

### Toaster props

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `position` | `Bind<ToastPosition>` | `'bottom-end'` | The stacking position, unless a toast specifies its own. |
| `max` | `Bind<number>` | `3` | The number of toasts shown at once in one position. The rest wait their turn. |
| `hotkey` | `Bind<string>` | `'F8'` | Moves focus to the newest toast and back again. Use `''` for none. |
| `pauseOnHover` | `Bind<boolean>` | `true` | Pauses timers while the pointer is over the toasts. Timers always stop while focus is inside them or the page is hidden. |
| `text` | `Bind<string>` | `uiLocale` strings | The name of the region. |

### Toaster members

| Member | Returns | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `Toaster.default` | static, read/write | The toaster used by `toast`, created in `document.body` on first use, or the one you assign. |
| `show, info, success, caution, danger, closeAll` | methods | Same as on `toast`, for this toaster. |
| `focusNewest()` | `boolean` | Moves focus to the newest toast. |
| `toasts` | read-only | The toasts on screen, followed by the waiting ones. |
| `paused` | read-only | Indicates whether the timers are currently paused. |

`enabled`, `visible` and the other shared control properties work on both.

# QRCode

> Display · @motifx-community/ui 0.1.0-beta.5

A QR code, drawn as vectors so that it stays sharp at any size. It has no dependencies, chooses the smallest version that holds the text, and can carry a logo.

## Import

```tsx
import { QRCode } from '@motifx-community/ui';
```

## A code from a text

`value` is the text of the code, and the code follows it. Change the text to see the code grow.

```tsx
import { reactive } from '@motifx/core';
import { QRCode, Stack, TextBox } from '@motifx-community/ui';

/** A code that follows a text. The smallest version that holds the text is chosen. */
export default function Basic() {
    const s = reactive({ text: 'https://ui.motifjs.com' });
    return (
        <Stack gap="md">
            <TextBox label="Text" x-model={() => s.text} />
            <QRCode class="qr-basic" value={() => s.text} />
        </Stack>
    );
}
```

## Error correction

`level` sets how much of the code can be damaged. A higher level holds less text, so the code grows.

```tsx
import { reactive } from '@motifx/core';
import { ButtonGroup, QRCode, Stack, type QrLevel } from '@motifx-community/ui';

/** A higher level survives more damage, and needs a larger code. */
export default function Levels() {
    const s = reactive({ level: 'M' as QrLevel });
    return (
        <Stack gap="md">
            <ButtonGroup
                label="Error correction"
                x-model={() => s.level}
                items={[
                    { value: 'L', text: 'L' },
                    { value: 'M', text: 'M' },
                    { value: 'Q', text: 'Q' },
                    { value: 'H', text: 'H' }
                ]}
            />
            <QRCode class="qr-level" value="https://ui.motifjs.com/qrcode" level={() => s.level} size={200} />
        </Stack>
    );
}
```

## A logo

`logo` puts an image in the middle, which takes the place of some modules. Level `H` restores what it covers. `logoSize` sets its share, at most `0.3`.

```tsx
import { QRCode } from '@motifx-community/ui';

/** A logo in the middle, which takes the place of some modules. Level H restores what it covers. */
export default function Logo() {
    return <QRCode class="qr-logo" value="https://ui.motifjs.com/qrcode" level="H" logo="/favicon.svg" size={220} />;
}
```

## Creating an image

`toDataURL()` and `toSVG()` give an image, in black on white unless you set other colors. `onEncodeFailed` occurs when a text does not fit in a code.

```tsx
import { reactive } from '@motifx/core';
import { Button, QRCode, Stack } from '@motifx-community/ui';

/** An image of the code, to download or print. */
export default function Export() {
    const s = reactive({ image: '' });
    let code!: QRCode;
    return (
        <Stack gap="md">
            <QRCode ref={(x: QRCode) => (code = x)} class="qr-export" value="Printed with the order" />
            <Button text="Create the image" variant="outline" onclick={() => (s.image = code.toDataURL('image/png', { size: 256 }))} />
            {s.image && <img class="qr-image" alt="The code as an image" src={() => s.image} />}
        </Stack>
    );
}
```

## Programmatic use

`new QRCode(props)` creates the code without JSX. Each prop is also a property.

```tsx
import { Component } from '@motifx/core';
import { Button, QRCode, Stack } from '@motifx-community/ui';

/** A code created programmatically. Each prop is also a property that can be set later. */
export default class Programmatic extends Component<HTMLDivElement> {
    constructor() {
        super('div');
        const code = new QRCode({ value: 'First', size: 140 });
        const next = new Button({ text: 'Change the text', variant: 'outline', onclick: () => (code.value = 'Second') });
        const stack = new Stack({ gap: 'md' });
        stack.controls.add(code, next);
        this.controls.add(stack);
    }
}
```

## API reference

### Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `value` | `Bind<string>` | `''` | The text of the code. It may hold any characters. |
| `level` | `Bind<'L' \| 'M' \| 'Q' \| 'H'>` | `'M'` | How much of the code can be damaged: about 7, 15, 25 or 30 percent. |
| `size` | `Bind<number \| null>` | From the design language | The width and height in pixels. |
| `margin` | `Bind<number>` | `4` | The quiet zone around the code, in modules. Readers need at least `4`. |
| `logo` | `Bind<string \| null>` | `null` | The address of an image in the middle of the code. Use level `H` with it. |
| `logoSize` | `Bind<number>` | `0.2` | The share of the code the logo covers, at most `0.3`. |
| `label` | `Bind<string>` | The kit string “QR code: …” | The accessible name. |

### Properties and methods

| Member | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `isInvalid` | `boolean` | Indicates that the value could not be drawn. |
| `modules` | `number` | The number of modules along a side of the code, without its margin. |
| `toSVG(options?)` | `string` | The code as an SVG document. The logo is not part of it. |
| `toDataURL(type?, options?)` | `string` | The code as a data URL, a PNG by default. The logo is not part of it. |

### Image options

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `size` | `number` | `512` | The width and height in pixels, rounded to whole modules. |
| `color` | `string` | `'#000000'` | The color of the modules. |
| `background` | `string` | `'#ffffff'` | The background. |

### Events

| Event | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `onEncodeFailed` | `{ value, source }` | Occurs when the text does not fit in a code, which then draws nothing. |

### Accessibility

| Topic | Details |
| --- | --- |
| `Name` | The code has the role `img`, and its name holds the text, so a screen reader can read it. |
| `Colors` | A code stays dark on a light sheet in every theme, as readers expect. |
| `Size` | For printing, keep a module at least 0.4 mm wide, and leave the quiet zone in place. |

### Styling hooks

| Hook | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `.mx-qr-code` | The sheet. `data-invalid` says the value could not be drawn. |
| `.mx-qr-code__svg, .mx-qr-code__logo` | The code and the logo. |

### Design tokens

| Token | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `qr-code.size` | The width and height. |
| `qr-code.sheet, .logo` | Units: the sheet, whose `color` is the color of the modules, and the logo. |

# Barcode

> Display · @motifx-community/ui 0.1.0-beta.5

A linear barcode, drawn as vectors: Code 128, Code 39, EAN-13, EAN-8, UPC-A or Interleaved 2 of 5. It has no dependencies, works out check digits and refuses a value the format cannot hold.

## Import

```tsx
import { Barcode } from '@motifx-community/ui';
```

## Formats

`format` sets the kind of barcode, and `value` what it holds.

| Format | Value | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `code128` | Any ASCII text | The default, for labels, shipping and stock. Digits are packed in pairs, so it stays short. |
| `code39` | Capitals, digits and `- . $ / + %` and space | Older industrial labels. Lower-case letters become capitals. |
| `ean13` | 12 or 13 digits | Retail products. The check digit is worked out, and a wrong one is refused. |
| `ean8` | 7 or 8 digits | Small retail products. |
| `upca` | 11 or 12 digits | Retail products in North America. |
| `itf` | Digits | Interleaved 2 of 5, for cartons. An odd number of digits gets a leading zero. |

```tsx
import { Barcode, Stack } from '@motifx-community/ui';

/** Each format, with a value it can hold. */
export default function Formats() {
    return (
        <Stack gap="md">
            <Barcode class="bc-128" format="code128" value="ORDER-2026-118" />
            <Barcode class="bc-39" format="code39" value="PART-77" />
            <Barcode class="bc-13" format="ean13" value="400638133393" />
            <Barcode class="bc-8" format="ean8" value="9638507" />
            <Barcode class="bc-upc" format="upca" value="03600029145" />
            <Barcode class="bc-itf" format="itf" value="1234567890" />
        </Stack>
    );
}
```

## Size and text

`moduleWidth` and `height` set the size of the bars, and `showText` the text under them. Keep the bars wide enough for the distance it is read from.

```tsx
import { Barcode, Stack } from '@motifx-community/ui';

/** The size of the bars, and a code without its text. */
export default function Options() {
    return (
        <Stack gap="md">
            <Barcode class="bc-large" value="LARGE-1" moduleWidth={3} height={96} />
            <Barcode class="bc-plain" value="NO-TEXT" showText={false} />
        </Stack>
    );
}
```

## Values that do not fit

A value the format cannot hold draws nothing and raises `onEncodeFailed`. Change the last digit of this EAN-13 to see it refused.

```tsx
import { reactive } from '@motifx/core';
import { Barcode, Stack, TextBox } from '@motifx-community/ui';

/** A value the format cannot hold draws nothing and raises `onEncodeFailed`. An EAN refuses a wrong check digit. */
export default function Validation() {
    const s = reactive({ value: '4006381333931', told: '' });
    return (
        <Stack gap="md">
            <TextBox label="EAN-13" x-model={() => s.value} />
            <Barcode
                class="bc-valid"
                format="ean13"
                value={() => s.value}
                onEncodeFailed={e => (s.told = `“${e.value}” is not a valid EAN-13.`)}
            />
            <output class="bc-told">{() => s.told}</output>
        </Stack>
    );
}
```

## Creating an image

`toDataURL()` and `toSVG()` give an image with the text under the bars, in black on white unless you set other colors.

```tsx
import { reactive } from '@motifx/core';
import { Barcode, Button, Stack } from '@motifx-community/ui';

/** An image of the code, with its text, to download or print. */
export default function Export() {
    const s = reactive({ image: '' });
    let code!: Barcode;
    return (
        <Stack gap="md">
            <Barcode ref={(x: Barcode) => (code = x)} class="bc-export" value="LABEL-42" />
            <Button text="Create the image" variant="outline" onclick={() => (s.image = code.toDataURL('image/png', { scale: 2 }))} />
            {s.image && <img class="bc-image" alt="The code as an image" src={() => s.image} />}
        </Stack>
    );
}
```

## Programmatic use

`new Barcode(props)` creates the code without JSX. Each prop is also a property.

```tsx
import { Component } from '@motifx/core';
import { Barcode, Button, Stack } from '@motifx-community/ui';

/** A code created programmatically. Each prop is also a property that can be set later. */
export default class Programmatic extends Component<HTMLDivElement> {
    constructor() {
        super('div');
        const code = new Barcode({ value: 'FIRST' });
        const next = new Button({ text: 'Change the value', variant: 'outline', onclick: () => (code.value = 'SECOND') });
        const stack = new Stack({ gap: 'md' });
        stack.controls.add(code, next);
        this.controls.add(stack);
    }
}
```

## API reference

### Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `value` | `Bind<string>` | `''` | The value of the code. |
| `format` | `Bind<BarcodeFormat>` | `'code128'` | The kind of barcode. |
| `checkDigit` | `Bind<boolean>` | `false` | Adds the optional check character of Code 39. |
| `moduleWidth` | `Bind<number>` | `2` | The width of the thinnest bar in pixels. |
| `height` | `Bind<number \| null>` | From the design language | The height of the bars in pixels. |
| `margin` | `Bind<number>` | `10` | The quiet zone at each side, in modules. Readers need it. |
| `showText` | `Bind<boolean>` | `true` | Shows the text under the bars. |
| `label` | `Bind<string>` | The kit string “Barcode: …” | The accessible name. |

### Properties and methods

| Member | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `isInvalid` | `boolean` | Indicates that the value could not be drawn. |
| `codeText` | `string` | The text under the bars, with the check digit where the format has one. |
| `toSVG(options?)` | `string` | The code as an SVG document, with its text. |
| `toDataURL(type?, options?)` | `string` | The code as a data URL, a PNG by default. |

### Image options

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `scale` | `number` | `2` | The width of a module in pixels. |
| `color` | `string` | `'#000000'` | The color of the bars and the text. |
| `background` | `string` | `'#ffffff'` | The background. |

### Events

| Event | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `onEncodeFailed` | `{ value, format, source }` | Occurs when the format cannot hold the value, which then draws nothing. |

### Accessibility

| Topic | Details |
| --- | --- |
| `Name` | The code has the role `img`, and its name holds the value, so a screen reader can read it. |
| `Colors` | A code stays dark on a light sheet in every theme, as readers expect. |
| `Width` | A narrow parent scrolls the code rather than squeezing its bars, which would stop it reading. |

### Styling hooks

| Hook | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `.mx-barcode` | The sheet. `data-invalid` says the value could not be drawn. |
| `.mx-barcode__svg, .mx-barcode__text` | The bars and the text. |

### Design tokens

| Token | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `barcode.height` | The height of the bars. |
| `barcode.sheet, .text` | Units: the sheet, whose `color` is the color of the bars, and the text. |

# Chart

> Display · @motifx-community/ui 0.1.0-beta.5

Displays lines, areas, bars, scatter points and bubbles on a shared value axis. The chart has no dependencies, takes its appearance from the design language, and makes every value available through the keyboard and a table view.

## Import

```tsx
import { Chart } from '@motifx-community/ui';
```

## Binding rows

`data` holds the rows, `xField` sets the position of each row along the axis, and each item of `series` selects a field and how it is drawn. A chart with one series shows no legend, because its title identifies the series.

```tsx
/** Twelve months of made-up figures, shared by the examples. */
export const SALES = [
    { month: 'Jan', online: 4200, stores: 6100, returns: 310 },
    { month: 'Feb', online: 4600, stores: 5800, returns: 280 },
    { month: 'Mar', online: 5900, stores: 6400, returns: 420 },
    { month: 'Apr', online: 6300, stores: 6000, returns: 390 },
    { month: 'May', online: 7100, stores: 6600, returns: 450 },
    { month: 'Jun', online: 7600, stores: 7000, returns: 520 },
    { month: 'Jul', online: 8200, stores: 6800, returns: 610 },
    { month: 'Aug', online: 8000, stores: 6500, returns: 580 },
    { month: 'Sep', online: 8900, stores: 7200, returns: 640 },
    { month: 'Oct', online: 9400, stores: 7600, returns: 700 },
    { month: 'Nov', online: 11200, stores: 8800, returns: 930 },
    { month: 'Dec', online: 12800, stores: 10100, returns: 1100 }
];
```

## Lines

A line is the default series type. `smooth` curves the line without adding a peak that is not in the data, and `labels` shows selected values on the chart. Point to a position to read every series at that position.

```tsx
/** Twelve months of made-up figures, shared by the examples. */
export const SALES = [
    { month: 'Jan', online: 4200, stores: 6100, returns: 310 },
    { month: 'Feb', online: 4600, stores: 5800, returns: 280 },
    { month: 'Mar', online: 5900, stores: 6400, returns: 420 },
    { month: 'Apr', online: 6300, stores: 6000, returns: 390 },
    { month: 'May', online: 7100, stores: 6600, returns: 450 },
    { month: 'Jun', online: 7600, stores: 7000, returns: 520 },
    { month: 'Jul', online: 8200, stores: 6800, returns: 610 },
    { month: 'Aug', online: 8000, stores: 6500, returns: 580 },
    { month: 'Sep', online: 8900, stores: 7200, returns: 640 },
    { month: 'Oct', online: 9400, stores: 7600, returns: 700 },
    { month: 'Nov', online: 11200, stores: 8800, returns: 930 },
    { month: 'Dec', online: 12800, stores: 10100, returns: 1100 }
];
```

## Areas

`stacked` adds the areas together, so that the top line shows the total.

```tsx
/** Twelve months of made-up figures, shared by the examples. */
export const SALES = [
```

## Grouped and stacked bars

Bars are grouped side by side by default. `stacked` places them on top of each other, as values or as percentages. Use `stack` on a series to assign it to a named stack.

```tsx
/** Twelve months of made-up figures, shared by the examples. */
export const SALES = [
    { month: 'Jan', online: 4200, stores: 6100, returns: 310 },
    { month: 'Feb', online: 4600, stores: 5800, returns: 280 },
    { month: 'Mar', online: 5900, stores: 6400, returns: 420 },
    { month: 'Apr', online: 6300, stores: 6000, returns: 390 },
    { month: 'May', online: 7100, stores: 6600, returns: 450 },
    { month: 'Jun', online: 7600, stores: 7000, returns: 520 },
    { month: 'Jul', online: 8200, stores: 6800, returns: 610 },
    { month: 'Aug', online: 8000, stores: 6500, returns: 580 },
    { month: 'Sep', online: 8900, stores: 7200, returns: 640 },
    { month: 'Oct', online: 9400, stores: 7600, returns: 700 },
    { month: 'Nov', online: 11200, stores: 8800, returns: 930 },
    { month: 'Dec', online: 12800, stores: 10100, returns: 1100 }
];
```

## Horizontal charts

`horizontal` suits long category names and rankings. Rows keep the order in which they are provided.

```tsx
import { Chart } from '@motifx-community/ui';

const TEAMS = [
    { team: 'Customer support', tickets: 412 },
    { team: 'Platform engineering', tickets: 318 },
    { team: 'Finance and accounting operations', tickets: 205 },
    { team: 'Sales', tickets: 164 },
    { team: 'Design', tickets: 96 }
];

/** On its side, for long names and a ranking. The labels carry the values. */
export default function Horizontal() {
    return <Chart class="ch-horizontal" horizontal title="Open tickets" data={TEAMS} xField="team" yAxis={{ grid: false, labels: false }} series={[{ type: 'bar', yField: 'tickets', name: 'Tickets', labels: 'all' }]} />;
}
```

## Negative values

Bars extend in both directions from zero. A label that does not fit or that would cover another label is omitted, and its value remains available in the tooltip and the table view.

```tsx
import { Chart } from '@motifx-community/ui';

const QUARTERS = [
    { quarter: 'Q1 2025', profit: 120 },
    { quarter: 'Q2 2025', profit: -45 },
    { quarter: 'Q3 2025', profit: 80 },
    { quarter: 'Q4 2025', profit: -110 },
    { quarter: 'Q1 2026', profit: 160 }
];

/** Bars grow both ways from zero, each rounded at its far end. */
export default function Negative() {
    return <Chart class="ch-negative" title="Quarterly result" data={QUARTERS} xField="quarter" series={[{ type: 'bar', yField: 'profit', name: 'Result', labels: 'all' }]} />;
}
```

## Scatter and bubble charts

`scatter` and `bubble` plot two numeric values. `sizeField` adds a third value to a bubble, represented by its area. The pointer selects the nearest point.

```tsx
import { Chart } from '@motifx-community/ui';

const CARS = [
    { power: 66, weight: 980, price: 16 },
    { power: 90, weight: 1120, price: 21 },
    { power: 110, weight: 1240, price: 27 },
    { power: 130, weight: 1320, price: 31 },
    { power: 150, weight: 1450, price: 38 },
    { power: 170, weight: 1510, price: 44 },
    { power: 190, weight: 1600, price: 52 },
    { power: 230, weight: 1680, price: 71 },
    { power: 260, weight: 1760, price: 86 },
    { power: 300, weight: 1850, price: 112 }
];

/** Two numbers per dot, and a third as its size. The size counts by area. */
export default function Scatter() {
    return (
        <Chart
            class="ch-scatter"
            title="Power, weight and price"
            data={CARS}
            xField="power"
            xAxis={{ title: 'Power (hp)' }}
            yAxis={{ title: 'Weight (kg)', min: 800 }}
            series={[{ type: 'bubble', yField: 'weight', sizeField: 'price', name: 'Cars' }]}
        />
    );
}
```

## Pie and donut

`pie` and `donut` split one whole into its parts. Shares are written inside the slices that have room for them, the legend names every part, and a donut shows the total in its middle. For close values, bars compare more exactly.

```tsx
import { reactive } from '@motifx/core';
import { ButtonGroup, Chart, Stack, type ChartSeriesType } from '@motifx-community/ui';

const TRAFFIC = [
    { source: 'Search', visits: 4820 },
    { source: 'Direct', visits: 2610 },
    { source: 'Social', visits: 1480 },
    { source: 'Email', visits: 920 },
    { source: 'Referral', visits: 540 }
];

/** One whole and its parts. Hide a part in the legend: the others share the whole again, and keep their colors. */
export default function Parts() {
    const s = reactive({ type: 'donut' as ChartSeriesType });
    return (
        <Stack class="docs-wide" gap="md">
            <ButtonGroup
                label="Shape"
                x-model={() => s.type}
                items={[
                    { value: 'donut', text: 'Donut' },
                    { value: 'pie', text: 'Pie' }
                ]}
            />
            <Chart class="ch-parts" title="Visits by source" data={TRAFFIC} xField="source" series={() => [{ type: s.type, yField: 'visits', name: 'Visits' }]} />
        </Stack>
    );
}
```

## Funnel

`funnel` shows stages in the order of the rows, each with the share of the first stage that is left. The stages take one hue, darker towards the first, as they are in order.

```tsx
import { Chart } from '@motifx-community/ui';

const STEPS = [
    { step: 'Visited the shop', people: 12000 },
    { step: 'Viewed a product', people: 7400 },
    { step: 'Added to the cart', people: 2900 },
    { step: 'Started to pay', people: 1650 },
    { step: 'Paid', people: 1180 }
];

/** Stages in order, each with what is left of the first one. */
export default function Funnel() {
    return <Chart class="ch-funnel" title="From visit to order" data={STEPS} xField="step" legend={false} series={[{ type: 'funnel', yField: 'people', name: 'People' }]} />;
}
```

## Radar

`radar` places a spoke for each category around a center and draws a shape for each series.

```tsx
import { Chart } from '@motifx-community/ui';

const SCORES = [
    { skill: 'Speed', a: 82, b: 64 },
    { skill: 'Battery', a: 58, b: 88 },
    { skill: 'Camera', a: 90, b: 72 },
    { skill: 'Screen', a: 76, b: 80 },
    { skill: 'Sound', a: 64, b: 70 },
    { skill: 'Price', a: 48, b: 84 }
];

/** Several measures around a center, one shape for each series. */
export default function Radar() {
    return (
        <Chart
            class="ch-radar"
            title="Two phones compared"
            data={SCORES}
            xField="skill"
            series={[
                { type: 'radar', yField: 'a', name: 'Phone A', markers: true },
                { type: 'radar', yField: 'b', name: 'Phone B', markers: true }
            ]}
        />
    );
}
```

## Heat map

`heatmap` places a cell at each pair of `xField` and `yField`, colored by `valueField` in seven steps of one hue. Values on both sides of zero take two hues that meet in a neutral middle.

```tsx
import { Chart } from '@motifx-community/ui';

const DAYS = ['Mon', 'Tue', 'Wed', 'Thu', 'Fri', 'Sat', 'Sun'];
const HOURS = ['8', '10', '12', '14', '16', '18', '20'];
const LOAD = DAYS.flatMap((day, d) => HOURS.map((hour, h) => ({ day, hour, orders: Math.round(20 + 60 * Math.sin(((h + 1) / 8) * Math.PI) * (d < 5 ? 1 : 0.55) + d * 3) })));

/** A value for each pair, as a color in seven steps. The legend gives each step its values. */
export default function Heatmap() {
    return <Chart class="ch-heat" title="Orders by day and hour" data={LOAD} xField="hour" series={[{ type: 'heatmap', yField: 'day', valueField: 'orders', name: 'Orders', labels: 'all' }]} />;
}
```

## Ranges

`rangeArea` and `rangeBar` draw from `lowField` to `highField`, and other series share the axis.

```tsx
import { Chart } from '@motifx-community/ui';

const WEATHER = [
    { month: 'Jan', low: 2, high: 9, mean: 5 },
    { month: 'Feb', low: 3, high: 11, mean: 7 },
    { month: 'Mar', low: 5, high: 14, mean: 9 },
    { month: 'Apr', low: 8, high: 18, mean: 13 },
    { month: 'May', low: 12, high: 23, mean: 17 },
    { month: 'Jun', low: 16, high: 28, mean: 22 },
    { month: 'Jul', low: 19, high: 31, mean: 25 },
    { month: 'Aug', low: 19, high: 31, mean: 25 },
    { month: 'Sep', low: 15, high: 26, mean: 21 },
    { month: 'Oct', low: 11, high: 21, mean: 16 },
    { month: 'Nov', low: 7, high: 15, mean: 11 },
    { month: 'Dec', low: 4, high: 11, mean: 7 }
];

/** A band from the lowest to the highest value, with a line through it. */
export default function Ranges() {
    return (
        <Chart
            class="ch-range"
            title="Temperature over the year"
            data={WEATHER}
            xField="month"
            yAxis={{ format: { style: 'unit', unit: 'celsius' } }}
            series={[
                { type: 'rangeArea', lowField: 'low', highField: 'high', name: 'Range' },
                { yField: 'mean', name: 'Mean', smooth: true }
            ]}
        />
    );
}
```

## Candles

`candlestick` and `ohlc` show four prices for each position: `openField`, `highField`, `lowField` and `closeField`. Rising and falling take the design language's colors for good and bad, and a rising candle is hollow as well.

```tsx
import { reactive } from '@motifx/core';
import { ButtonGroup, Chart, Stack, type ChartSeriesType } from '@motifx-community/ui';

const PRICES = Array.from({ length: 24 }, (_, i) => {
    const open = 100 + Math.round(Math.sin(i / 3) * 12 + i * 0.8);
    const close = open + Math.round(Math.cos(i * 1.7) * 6);
    return { day: new Date(2026, 9, i + 1), open, close, high: Math.max(open, close) + 2 + (i % 3), low: Math.min(open, close) - 2 - (i % 4) };
});

/** Four prices a day. A rising candle is hollow and a falling one filled, so they read apart without their colors. */
export default function Candles() {
    const s = reactive({ type: 'candlestick' as ChartSeriesType });
    return (
        <Stack class="docs-wide" gap="md">
            <ButtonGroup
                label="Shape"
                x-model={() => s.type}
                items={[
                    { value: 'candlestick', text: 'Candles' },
                    { value: 'ohlc', text: 'OHLC bars' }
                ]}
            />
            <Chart
                class="ch-candles"
                title="Share price in October"
                data={PRICES}
                xField="day"
                xAxis={{ format: { day: 'numeric' } }}
                series={() => [{ type: s.type, openField: 'open', highField: 'high', lowField: 'low', closeField: 'close', name: 'Price' }]}
            />
        </Stack>
    );
}
```

## Waterfall

`waterfall` adds each change to the last one, and a row with `totalField` set shows the total so far. A thin line carries the total from one step to the next.

```tsx
import { Chart } from '@motifx-community/ui';

const BUDGET = [
    { item: 'Start', change: 1200 },
    { item: 'Sales', change: 860 },
    { item: 'Services', change: 340 },
    { item: 'Salaries', change: -690 },
    { item: 'Rent', change: -240 },
    { item: 'Half year', total: true },
    { item: 'Taxes', change: -310 },
    { item: 'End', total: true }
];

/** Each step adds or takes away, and a total row shows where it stands. */
export default function Waterfall() {
    return <Chart class="ch-waterfall" title="Cash over the year" data={BUDGET} xField="item" series={[{ type: 'waterfall', yField: 'change', totalField: 'total', name: 'Cash', labels: 'all' }]} />;
}
```

## Dates

Date values produce a time axis, with marks on round days and months in the language of the page. Long series are reduced to what the width can display, and their peaks are preserved.

```tsx
import { Chart } from '@motifx-community/ui';

const DAY = 24 * 60 * 60 * 1000;
const START = new Date(2026, 0, 1).getTime();
const VISITS = Array.from({ length: 180 }, (_, i) => ({
    day: new Date(START + i * DAY),
    visits: Math.round(900 + i * 6 + Math.sin(i / 6) * 180 + (i % 7 === 0 ? -160 : 0))
}));

/** Dates place themselves on round days and months. */
export default function TimeAxis() {
    return <Chart class="ch-time" title="Daily visits" data={VISITS} xField="day" series={[{ type: 'area', yField: 'visits', name: 'Visits' }]} />;
}
```

## Missing values

A missing value breaks the line, because nothing was measured at that position. `gaps` connects across it or treats it as zero, and `step` draws a stepped line.

```tsx
import { Chart } from '@motifx-community/ui';

const READINGS = [
    { hour: '08:00', room: 19 },
    { hour: '09:00', room: 20 },
    { hour: '10:00', room: null },
    { hour: '11:00', room: 22 },
    { hour: '12:00', room: 23 },
    { hour: '13:00', room: null },
    { hour: '14:00', room: 24 },
    { hour: '15:00', room: null },
    { hour: '16:00', room: 22 }
];

/** An empty value breaks a line, as nothing was measured. `gaps` can join past it instead. */
export default function Gaps() {
    return (
        <Chart
            class="ch-gaps"
            title="Room temperature"
            data={READINGS}
            xField="hour"
            series={[
                { yField: 'room', name: 'Broken', markers: true },
                { yField: (row: { room: number | null }) => (row.room === null ? null : row.room + 4), name: 'Joined', gaps: 'connect', step: 'middle' }
            ]}
        />
    );
}
```

## Reactive data

A function prop follows reactive data. For plain data, call `reState()`, or `refresh()` after an in-place change.

```tsx
import { reactive } from '@motifx/core';
import { Button, Chart, Stack } from '@motifx-community/ui';

/** A function prop follows reactive data. */
export default function Live() {
    const s = reactive({ points: [12, 18, 15, 21, 19].map((value, i) => ({ step: i + 1, value })) });
    const add = () => {
        const last = s.points[s.points.length - 1];
        s.points = [...s.points, { step: last.step + 1, value: Math.max(2, last.value + Math.round(Math.random() * 12 - 6)) }];
    };
    return (
        <Stack class="docs-wide" gap="md">
            <Chart class="ch-live" label="A growing series" data={() => s.points} xField="step" series={[{ yField: 'value', name: 'Value', markers: true }]} />
            <Button text="Add a value" variant="outline" onclick={add} />
        </Stack>
    );
}
```

## Programmatic use

`new Chart(props)` creates the chart without JSX. Each prop is also a property.

```tsx
    { month: 'Mar', online: 5900, stores: 6400, returns: 420 },
    { month: 'Apr', online: 6300, stores: 6000, returns: 390 },
    { month: 'May', online: 7100, stores: 6600, returns: 450 },
    { month: 'Jun', online: 7600, stores: 7000, returns: 520 },
    { month: 'Jul', online: 8200, stores: 6800, returns: 610 },
    { month: 'Aug', online: 8000, stores: 6500, returns: 580 },

```

## API reference

### Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `data` | `Bind<T[] \| null>` | `null` | The rows. The chart reads them and never changes them. After an in-place change, call `refresh()`. |
| `dataSource` | `Bind<DataSource \| null>` | `null` | Rows from a data source of the data layer. The chart follows its changes and its loading state. |
| `xField` | `Bind<string \| (row) => unknown>` | `null` | The field of a row that holds its position along the axis. |
| `series` | `Bind<ChartSeries[]>` | `[]` | The series to draw. See the Series table. |
| `horizontal` | `Bind<boolean>` | `false` | Draws the chart horizontally, with categories down the page and values across it. |
| `stacked` | `Bind<false \| 'normal' \| 'percent'>` | `false` | Stacks bars and areas, as values or as percentages. |
| `title` | `Bind<string>` | `''` | The title above the chart. |
| `subtitle` | `Bind<string>` | `''` | A line under the title. |
| `label` | `Bind<string>` | The title | The accessible name. |
| `xAxis` | `Bind<ChartAxis>` | `{}` | The position axis. See the Axes table. |
| `yAxis` | `Bind<ChartAxis>` | `{}` | The value axis. See the Axes table. |
| `legend` | `Bind<boolean \| ChartLegendOptions>` | On with two series or more | The legend, its `position`, and whether a click hides a series (`toggle`). |
| `tooltip` | `Bind<boolean \| ChartTooltipOptions>` | On | The tooltip, whether it lists every series (`shared`), and custom content (`format`). |
| `crosshair` | `Bind<boolean>` | `true` | A line that follows the pointer on line and area series. |
| `height` | `Bind<number \| null>` | From the design language | The height in pixels, including the title and the legend. |
| `animation` | `Bind<boolean>` | `true` | Animates the marks when they first appear. |
| `tableButton` | `Bind<boolean>` | `true` | Shows a button that switches between the chart and its table view. |
| `mode` | `Bind<'chart' \| 'table'>` | `'chart'` | Shows the chart or its table view. Supports `x-model`. |
| `emptyText` | `Bind<string>` | A kit string | The text shown when there is nothing to draw. |
| `loading` | `Bind<boolean>` | `false` | Keeps the current chart at reduced opacity while new values load. |

### Series

| Field | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `yField` | `string \| (row) => unknown` | Required | The field that holds the value. |
| `type` | `ChartSeriesType` | `'line'` | How the series is drawn: `line`, `area`, `bar`, `scatter`, `bubble`, `rangeArea`, `rangeBar`, `candlestick`, `ohlc`, `waterfall`, `heatmap`, `pie`, `donut`, `funnel` or `radar`. A chart draws the family of its first series. |
| `name` | `string` | `yField` | The name in the legend, the tooltip and the table view. |
| `xField` | `string \| (row) => unknown` | The chart's | The position, for a series with its own values. |
| `sizeField` | `string \| (row) => unknown` |  | The size of a bubble. |
| `lowField, highField` | `string \| (row) => unknown` |  | The ends of a range, and the lowest and highest price of a candle. |
| `openField, closeField` | `string \| (row) => unknown` |  | The first and the last price of a candle. |
| `valueField` | `string \| (row) => unknown` |  | The value a heat map shows as a color. |
| `totalField` | `string \| (row) => unknown` |  | A row of a waterfall that shows the total so far. |
| `innerRadius` | `number` | From the design language | The hole of a donut, as a share of its radius. |
| `startAngle` | `number` | `0` | Where the first slice starts, in degrees from the top, clockwise. |
| `data` | `T[]` | The chart's rows | The rows of this series. |
| `color` | `string` | The color of its position in `series` | A custom color. |
| `stack` | `string \| boolean` | The chart's `stacked` | Series with the same name stack on each other. |
| `visible` | `boolean` | `true` | Draws the series. |
| `legend` | `boolean` | `true` | Lists the series in the legend. |
| `tooltip` | `boolean` | `true` | Lists the series in the tooltip. |
| `smooth` | `boolean` | `false` | Curves the line without passing the values it connects. |
| `step` | `'start' \| 'middle' \| 'end'` |  | Draws a stepped line, and sets where the value changes. |
| `markers` | `boolean` | `false` | Marks each value on a line. |
| `labels` | `'none' \| 'last' \| 'extremes' \| 'all'` | `'none'` | The values that show a label. A label that does not fit is omitted. |
| `gaps` | `'break' \| 'connect' \| 'zero'` | `'break'` | How a line treats a missing value. |
| `format` | `ChartFormat` | The value axis's | How values are displayed: a function, or options of the browser's number format. |

### Axes

| Field | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `kind` | `'auto' \| 'category' \| 'linear' \| 'log' \| 'time'` | `'auto'` | How the axis places its values. |
| `title` | `string` |  | A title along the axis. |
| `min, max` | `number \| Date` | From the values | The first and the last value. |
| `format` | `ChartFormat` | The language of the page | How values are displayed: a function, or options of the browser's formats. |
| `tickCount` | `number` | As many as fit | The approximate number of values it marks. |
| `labelAngle` | `number` | `0` | Rotates the labels by this many degrees, for long labels. |
| `reversed` | `boolean` | `false` | Reverses the direction of the axis. |
| `labels` | `boolean` | `true` | Shows the labels. |
| `grid` | `boolean` | On the value axis | Draws grid lines. |
| `line` | `boolean` | On the category axis | Draws the line of the axis. |
| `visible` | `boolean` | `true` | Shows the axis. |

### Properties and methods

| Member | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `refresh()` | `void` | Redraws the chart from the current rows and series, after an in-place change. |
| `setSeriesVisible(index, visible)` | `void` | Hides or shows a series, by its index in `series`. |
| `isSeriesVisible(index)` | `boolean` | Indicates whether a series is drawn. |
| `toSVG(options?)` | `string` | Returns the chart as an SVG document, with its title and legend. |
| `toDataURL(type?, options?)` | `Promise<string>` | Returns the chart as a data URL, a PNG by default. |

### Image options

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `scale` | `number` | `2` | The pixel scale of a PNG. |
| `background` | `string` | The color behind the chart | The background. |

### Events

| Event | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `onPointClick` | `{ point, originalEvent, source }` | Occurs when a value is clicked, or chosen with Enter or Space. |
| `onPointFocused` | `{ point, originalEvent, source }` | Occurs when the pointer or the keyboard reaches a value. |
| `onSeriesToggled` | `{ series, visible, source }` | Occurs when a series is hidden or shown in the legend. |
| `onModeChanged` | `{ mode, source }` | Occurs when the chart or its table view appears. |
| `onDataError` | `{ error, source }` | Occurs when the data source fails to load. The chart also displays a message. |

### Keyboard

| Key | Action |
| --- | --- |
| `Arrow keys` | Move between positions along the axis, and between the series at a position across it. |
| `Home, End` | Move to the first or the last position. |
| `Enter, Space` | Raise `onPointClick` for the current value. |
| `Escape` | Hides the current value. |

### Accessibility

| Topic | Details |
| --- | --- |
| `Values` | Every value is available without a pointer. The arrow keys move through the chart, and a screen reader announces each value. |
| `Table` | The button in the title row shows the same values in a table. Keep it unless the values also appear on the page. |
| `Color` | Neighboring series stay distinct for color-blind readers, which each build verifies. The legend and its keys also identify the series, so color is never the only cue. |
| `Motion` | The marks appear immediately when the reader prefers reduced motion. |
| `Name` | Provide a `title` or a `label` to name the chart. |

### Styling hooks

| Hook | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `.mx-chart` | The chart. `data-mode` and `data-legend` describe what it shows, and `data-loading` indicates that it is loading. |
| `.mx-chart__head, .mx-chart__title, .mx-chart__subtitle` | The title row. |
| `.mx-chart__plot, .mx-chart__svg` | The plot. |
| `.mx-chart__series` | A series, with `data-type`. `--_mark` holds its color. |
| `.mx-chart__legend, .mx-chart__legend-item` | The legend. `data-off` marks a hidden series. |
| `.mx-chart__tooltip` | The tooltip. |
| `.mx-chart__table` | The table view. |

### Design tokens

| Token | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `chart.height` | The height, including the title and the legend. |
| `chart.series-1 … series-8` | The colors of the series, from `color.chart.*` of the design system. |
| `chart.bar-width, .bar-radius, .bar-gap` | The maximum bar width, its end corners, and the gap between bars. |
| `chart.line-width, .marker-size, .marker-ring` | Lines and markers, and the ring that separates a marker from what it crosses. |
| `chart.area-opacity, .bubble-opacity` | The fill strength of areas and bubbles. |
| `chart.title, .subtitle, .ticks, .grid, .axis` | Units of the title row and the axes. |
| `chart.tooltip, .tooltip-row, .tooltip-value` | Units of the tooltip. |
| `chart.legend-item, .legend-key` | Units of the legend. |

`States.tsx`

```tsx
/** No values, and new values on their way. */
export default function States() {
```

`Export.tsx`

```tsx
import { reactive } from '@motifx/core';
import { Button, Chart, Stack } from '@motifx-community/ui';
import { SALES } from './sales';

/** An image with the title and the legend, to download or to put in a report. */
export default function Export() {
    const s = reactive({ image: '' });
    let chart!: Chart;
    return (
        <Stack class="docs-wide" gap="md">
            <Chart
                ref={(x: Chart) => (chart = x)}
                class="ch-export"
                title="Sales by channel"
                data={SALES}
                xField="month"
                series={[
                    { type: 'bar', yField: 'online', name: 'Online' },
                    { type: 'bar', yField: 'stores', name: 'Stores' }
                ]}
            />
            <Button text="Create the image" variant="outline" onclick={() => chart.toDataURL().then(url => (s.image = url))} />
            {s.image && <img class="ch-image" alt="The chart as an image" src={() => s.image} />}
        </Stack>
    );
}
```

`Programmatic.tsx`

```tsx
import { Component } from '@motifx/core';
import { Button, Chart, Stack } from '@motifx-community/ui';
import { SALES } from './sales';

/** A chart created programmatically. Each prop is also a property that can be set later. */
export default class Programmatic extends Component<HTMLDivElement> {
    constructor() {
        super('div');
        const chart = new Chart({ label: 'Sales', data: SALES, xField: 'month', series: [{ type: 'bar', yField: 'online', name: 'Online' }] });
        const next = new Button({ text: 'Show the stores', variant: 'outline', onclick: () => (chart.series = [{ type: 'bar', yField: 'stores', name: 'Stores' }]) });
        const stack = new Stack({ gap: 'md' });
        stack.controls.add(chart, next);
        this.controls.add(stack);
    }
}
```

# Badge

> Display · @motifx-community/ui 0.1.0-beta.5

A short text, count or dot, shown inline or on the corner of a button, avatar or icon. A count above its maximum displays as “99+”, and a count of zero is hidden.

## Import

```tsx
import { Badge } from '@motifx-community/ui';
```

## Declarative and programmatic

Every prop accepts a value or a function. When you create the component with `new`, set the same properties programmatically.

```tsx
import { reactive } from '@motifx/core';
import { Badge, Button } from '@motifx-community/ui';

/** A badge in JSX tracks its functions, and one created with `new` accepts the same properties programmatically. */
export default function Programmatic() {
  const s = reactive({ unread: 4 });
  const coded = new Badge({ text: 'Beta', tone: 'info', variant: 'subtle' });

  return (
    <>
      <span>
        Inbox <Badge count={() => s.unread} label={() => `${s.unread} unread`} />
      </span>
      <Button text="Add one" variant="outline" onclick={() => s.unread++} />
      <Button text="Read all" variant="outline" onclick={() => (s.unread = 0)} />
      <span onConfig={(c) => c.controls.add(coded)}>Search </span>
    </>
  );
}
```

## Tones and appearance

```tsx
import { Badge, Stack, type BadgeTone, type BadgeVariant } from '@motifx-community/ui';

const TONES: BadgeTone[] = ['standard', 'accent', 'info', 'success', 'caution', 'danger'];
const VARIANTS: BadgeVariant[] = ['solid', 'subtle', 'outline'];

/** Every tone in each appearance. */
export default function Tones() {
  return (
    <Stack>
      {VARIANTS.map((variant) => (
        <Stack key={variant} orientation="horizontal" wrap align="center">
          {TONES.map((tone) => (
            <Badge key={tone} text={tone} tone={tone} variant={variant} />
          ))}
        </Stack>
      ))}
    </Stack>
  );
}
```

## Counts and dots

```tsx
import { reactive } from '@motifx/core';
import { Badge, NumberBox, Stack, Switch } from '@motifx-community/ui';

/** A count up to `max`, and `max+` beyond it. At 0 it is hidden unless `showZero` is set, and a dot indicates only that something is present. */
export default function Counts() {
  const s = reactive({ count: 120, max: 99, showZero: false });

  return (
    <>
      <NumberBox label="Count" min={0} x-model={() => s.count} />
      <NumberBox label="Max" min={1} x-model={() => s.max} />
      <Switch label="Show zero" x-model={() => s.showZero} />
      <Stack orientation="horizontal" align="center">
        <Badge count={() => s.count} max={() => s.max} showZero={() => s.showZero} />
        <Badge count={() => s.count} max={() => s.max} showZero={() => s.showZero} variant="subtle" />
        <Badge count={() => s.count} dot label="Something new" />
      </Stack>
    </>
  );
}
```

## Corner placement

`position` places the badge on a corner of its container. `Badge.attach` does the same programmatically on any component.

```tsx
import { Badge, Button, Stack, type BadgePosition } from '@motifx-community/ui';

const CORNERS: BadgePosition[] = ['top-end', 'top-start', 'bottom-end', 'bottom-start'];

/** On a corner of what it is in: `position` inside a button, or `Badge.attach` on any component (here a `<span>`). */
export default function OnCorner() {
  return (
    <Stack orientation="horizontal" wrap align="center" gap="xl">
      {CORNERS.map((corner) => (
        <Button key={corner} text={corner} variant="outline">
          <Badge count={7} position={corner} />
        </Button>
      ))}
      <span ref={(bell) => Badge.attach(bell, { dot: true, tone: 'danger', label: 'New notifications' })}>Notifications</span>
    </Stack>
  );
}
```

## Sizes

```tsx
import { Badge, Stack, type ControlSize } from '@motifx-community/ui';

const SIZES: ControlSize[] = ['sm', 'md', 'lg'];

/** A badge and a dot in each size. */
export default function Sizes() {
  return (
    <>
      {SIZES.map((size) => (
        <Stack key={size} orientation="horizontal" align="center">
          <Badge text={size} size={size} />
          <Badge count={42} size={size} variant="subtle" />
          <Badge dot size={size} />
        </Stack>
      ))}
    </>
  );
}
```

## Accessibility

| Topic | Details |
| --- | --- |
| `Text` | A badge is read in place, as part of its container. |
| `label` | With a label, the badge is an image with that name (`role="img"`), so a count can describe what it counts. |
| `Dot` | Without a label, a dot is hidden from screen readers (`aria-hidden`). Give it a label when it conveys information. |
| `Colour` | Do not rely on tone alone to convey meaning. Pair it with text or a label. |

## Localization

A count is formatted in the kit language (`uiLocale`) and updates when the language changes: “1,234” in English and “1.234” in Turkish.

## Styling

| Hook | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `.mx-badge` | The badge. `data-tone`, `data-variant`, `data-size`, `data-position`, `data-dot`, `data-empty`. |
| `.mx-badge-anchor` | The element a corner badge is attached to (`position: relative`). |

### Component tokens

| Token | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `badge.badge` | Unit: the badge at rest (solid, standard), in each appearance and tone (`accent` … `danger`, `subtle-*`, `outline-*`) and as a `dot`. |
| `badge.height.*, badge.dot-size.*, badge.font-size.*, badge.padding.*` | The badge and the dot, per size. |
| `badge.offset` | The offset of a corner badge from the corner. |
| `badge.tone, badge.variant` | The default tone and appearance. |

## API reference

### Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `text` | `Bind<string>` | `''` | Short text, shown when there is no `count`. |
| `count` | `Bind<number \| null>` | `null` | A count formatted in the kit language. Above `max`, it shows `max+`. |
| `max` | `Bind<number>` | `99` | The highest count shown in full. |
| `showZero` | `Bind<boolean>` | `false` | Shows a count of 0. Without it, the badge hides at 0. |
| `dot` | `Bind<boolean>` | `false` | Shows a dot only, indicating that something is present. |
| `tone` | `Bind<BadgeTone>` | Set by the design language | `standard`, `accent`, `info`, `success`, `caution` or `danger`. Material uses `danger` for counts, and the other design languages use `accent`. |
| `variant` | `Bind<BadgeVariant>` | Set by the design language (`solid`) | `solid`, `subtle`, `outline`. |
| `size` | `Bind<ControlSize>` | `'md'` | `sm`, `md`, `lg`. |
| `position` | `Bind<BadgePosition \| null>` | `null` | `top-end`, `top-start`, `bottom-end` or `bottom-start`: the corner of the container, which becomes its anchor. `start` and `end` follow the writing direction. |
| `label` | `Bind<string>` | `''` | The text announced by screen readers (“3 unread messages”). Without it, they read the badge text. |
| `visible, tabStop` | see Control |  | Properties shared by all controls. |

### Properties

| Property | Access | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `every prop above` | read/write | Accepts a value or a function, the same as the prop. |
| `shownText` | read-only | The current display text: the formatted count (`99+`), otherwise the text, or `''` for a dot. |

### Methods

| Method | Returns | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `Badge.attach(target, props?)` | `Badge` | Places a badge on a corner of a component (`top-end` unless `props` specifies otherwise). The badge becomes a child of the component and is disposed with it. |
