# Avatar and AvatarGroup

> Display · @motifx-community/ui 0.1.0-beta.5

Represents a person with a picture, initials or an icon, with an optional presence indicator on its corner. A group stacks or spreads avatars and counts the ones it does not show.

## Import

```tsx
import { Avatar, AvatarGroup } from '@motifx-community/ui';
```

## Declarative and programmatic

Every prop accepts a value or a function. When you create the component with `new`, set the same properties programmatically.

```tsx
import { reactive } from '@motifx/core';
import { Avatar, Button, Stack, type AvatarStatus } from '@motifx-community/ui';

const PEOPLE = ['Ada Lovelace', 'Alan Turing', 'Grace Hopper'];
const STATUSES: AvatarStatus[] = ['online', 'away', 'busy', 'offline'];

/** An avatar in JSX tracks its functions, and one created with `new` accepts the same properties programmatically. */
export default function Programmatic() {
  const s = reactive({ person: 0, status: 0 });
  const coded = new Avatar({ name: 'Edsger Dijkstra', tone: 'success', shape: 'square' });

  return (
    <Stack orientation="horizontal" wrap align="center">
      <Avatar name={() => PEOPLE[s.person]} status={() => STATUSES[s.status]} />
      <Button text="Next person" variant="outline" onclick={() => (s.person = (s.person + 1) % PEOPLE.length)} />
      <Button text="Next presence" variant="outline" onclick={() => (s.status = (s.status + 1) % STATUSES.length)} />
      <span onConfig={(c) => c.controls.add(coded)} />
    </Stack>
  );
}
```

## Picture, initials and icon

The picture appears once it has loaded. Until then, or if it fails to load, the initials appear. Without a name, the person icon appears.

```tsx
import { Avatar, Stack } from '@motifx-community/ui';

// An inline SVG sunset, so that the example needs no network access.
const PICTURE = `data:image/svg+xml,${encodeURIComponent(
  '<svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 64 64"><defs><linearGradient id="sky" x2="0" y2="1">' +
    '<stop offset="0" stop-color="#3b5bdb"/><stop offset="1" stop-color="#f08c00"/></linearGradient></defs>' +
    '<rect width="64" height="64" fill="url(#sky)"/><circle cx="32" cy="40" r="12" fill="#ffd43b"/>' +
    '<path d="M0 46h64v18H0z" fill="#2b8a3e"/></svg>',
)}`;

/** A picture; initials when there is none or it cannot load; a person icon without a name. */
export default function Content() {
  return (
    <Stack orientation="horizontal" wrap align="center">
      <Avatar name="Ada Lovelace" src={PICTURE} />
      <Avatar name="Ada Lovelace" />
      <Avatar name="Alan Turing" src="does-not-exist.png" />
      <Avatar initials="QA" label="Quality team" />
      <Avatar />
    </Stack>
  );
}
```

## Tones and shapes

```tsx
import { Avatar, Stack, type AvatarShape, type AvatarTone } from '@motifx-community/ui';

const TONES: AvatarTone[] = ['standard', 'accent', 'info', 'success', 'caution', 'danger'];
const SHAPES: AvatarShape[] = ['circle', 'square'];
const PEOPLE = ['Ada Lovelace', 'Alan Turing', 'Grace Hopper', 'Edsger Dijkstra', 'Barbara Liskov', 'Linus Torvalds'];

/** Every tone in each shape; `auto` takes a tone from the name, the same for the same name. */
export default function Tones() {
  return (
    <Stack>
      {SHAPES.map((shape) => (
        <Stack key={shape} orientation="horizontal" wrap align="center">
          {TONES.map((tone) => (
            <Avatar key={tone} name={tone} tone={tone} shape={shape} label={`${tone}, ${shape}`} />
          ))}
        </Stack>
      ))}
      <Stack orientation="horizontal" wrap align="center">
        {PEOPLE.map((name) => (
          <Avatar key={name} name={name} tone="auto" />
        ))}
      </Stack>
    </Stack>
  );
}
```

## Sizes and presence

```tsx
import { Avatar, Stack, type AvatarSize, type AvatarStatus } from '@motifx-community/ui';

const SIZES: AvatarSize[] = ['xs', 'sm', 'md', 'lg', 'xl'];
const STATUSES: AvatarStatus[] = ['online', 'away', 'busy', 'offline'];

/** Each size, with each presence. */
export default function Sizes() {
  return (
    <Stack>
      {STATUSES.map((status) => (
        <Stack key={status} orientation="horizontal" wrap align="center">
          {SIZES.map((size) => (
            <Avatar key={size} name="Grace Hopper" size={size} status={status} />
          ))}
        </Stack>
      ))}
    </Stack>
  );
}
```

## Groups

`max` sets how many avatars are shown, and the rest are counted in a `+N`. `total` also counts people who are not provided. The group sets the size of all its avatars.

```tsx
import { Avatar, AvatarGroup, Stack } from '@motifx-community/ui';

const TEAM = ['Ada Lovelace', 'Alan Turing', 'Grace Hopper', 'Edsger Dijkstra', 'Barbara Liskov'];

/** Stacked with the rest counted, side by side, and a total larger than the avatars given. */
export default function Groups() {
  return (
    <Stack gap="lg">
      <AvatarGroup max={3} label="Team">
        {TEAM.map((name) => (
          <Avatar key={name} name={name} />
        ))}
      </AvatarGroup>
      <AvatarGroup layout="spread" size="sm" label="Team">
        {TEAM.map((name) => (
          <Avatar key={name} name={name} />
        ))}
      </AvatarGroup>
      <AvatarGroup size="lg" total={42} label="Followers">
        {TEAM.slice(0, 3).map((name) => (
          <Avatar key={name} name={name} />
        ))}
      </AvatarGroup>
    </Stack>
  );
}
```

## Accessibility

| Topic | Details |
| --- | --- |
| `Name` | With a name or label, the avatar is an image with that name (`role="img"`), and the presence follows it (“Ada Lovelace, Away”). |
| `No name` | An avatar with no name, label or presence is hidden from screen readers. |
| `Picture` | The picture has an empty `alt`, because the avatar carries the name. |
| `Group` | `role="group"` with its label. The `+N` states how many people are not shown (“8 more people”). |
| `Colour` | Presence is not conveyed by color alone. It is included in the name screen readers announce, and Fluent draws a mark in the dot. |

## Localization

Initials use the capitalization rules of the kit language (`uiLocale`), so “ilgin” becomes “İ” in Turkish. The presence and `+N` strings are kit strings (`presenceOnline` … `presenceOffline`, `avatarPresence`, `moreItems`, `avatarGroupMore`) and change with the language.

## Styling

| Hook | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `.mx-avatar` | The avatar. `data-size`, `data-shape`, `data-tone`. |
| `.mx-avatar__image` | The picture. `data-pending` until it loads. |
| `.mx-avatar__initials, .mx-avatar__icon` | The initials, and the person icon shown without them. |
| `.mx-avatar__status` | The presence dot. `data-status`. |
| `.mx-avatar-group` | The group. `data-size`, `data-layout`. An avatar that is not shown has `data-beyond`. |
| `.mx-avatar-group__more` | The `+N` avatar. |

### Component tokens

| Token | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `avatar.avatar` | Unit: the avatar at rest (the standard tone) and in each tone. |
| `avatar.icon, avatar.status, avatar.status-icon` | Units: the person icon, the presence dot and its ring per status, and a mark inside the dot per status. |
| `avatar.size.*, avatar.font-size.*, avatar.icon-size.*, avatar.status-size.*, avatar.square-radius.*` | The avatar, its initials, its icon, its dot and its square corners, per size. |
| `avatar.tone, avatar.shape` | The default tone and shape. |
| `avatar-group.stacked` | Unit: the ring that separates a stacked avatar from the one it overlaps. |
| `avatar-group.overlap.*, avatar-group.gap.*, avatar-group.layout` | The overlap of stacked avatars, the gap between spread avatars, and the default layout. |

## API reference

### Avatar props

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `src` | `Bind<string \| null>` | `null` | The picture. Until it loads, or if it fails, the initials appear, or the person icon if there are none. |
| `name` | `Bind<string>` | `''` | The person's name. It is used to create the initials and is announced by screen readers. |
| `initials` | `Bind<string>` | `''` | Custom initials that replace the ones created from `name`. |
| `label` | `Bind<string>` | `''` | The text screen readers announce instead of the name. |
| `size` | `Bind<AvatarSize>` | `'md'` | `xs`, `sm`, `md`, `lg` or `xl`. In a group, the group's size applies. |
| `shape` | `Bind<AvatarShape>` | Set by the design language (`circle`) | `circle` or `square` (using the design language's corner radius for the size). |
| `tone` | `Bind<AvatarTone>` | Set by the design language | `standard`, `accent`, `info`, `success`, `caution`, `danger`, or `auto`, which derives a tone from the name so the same name always has the same tone. Material and Lilac use `accent`, and the others use `standard`. |
| `status` | `Bind<AvatarStatus \| null>` | `null` | `online`, `away`, `busy` or `offline`: a presence dot on the lower end corner. |
| `visible, tabStop` | see Control |  | Properties shared by all controls. |

### Avatar properties

| Property | Access | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `every prop above` | read/write | Accepts a value or a function, the same as the prop. |
| `shownInitials` | read-only | The displayed initials: the ones provided, otherwise the ones created from the name. |
| `showsPicture` | read-only | Indicates whether the picture has loaded and is currently shown. |

### AvatarGroup props

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `size` | `Bind<AvatarSize>` | `'md'` | The size of every avatar in the group. |
| `layout` | `Bind<AvatarGroupLayout>` | Set by the design language (`stack`) | `stack` overlaps each avatar on the previous one, and `spread` places them side by side. |
| `max` | `Bind<number \| null>` | `null` | The maximum number of avatars shown. The others are counted in a `+N` after them. |
| `total` | `Bind<number \| null>` | `null` | The total number of people when only some are provided. The rest are counted in the `+N`. |
| `label` | `Bind<string>` | `''` | The accessible name of the group (“Members”). |

### AvatarGroup properties

| Property | Access | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `every prop above` | read/write | Accepts a value or a function, the same as the prop. |
| `avatars` | read-only | The elements of the provided avatars in order, including those from JSX lists. The `+N` is not included. |
| `hiddenCount` | read-only | The number of people counted in the `+N`, or 0 when it is not shown. |

### Functions

| Function | Returns | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `initialsOf(name, locale)` | `string` | Creates initials from a name: the first letters of the first and last words, using the capitalization rules of the language. |

# Chip and ChipGroup

> Display · @motifx-community/ui 0.1.0-beta.5

A compact element with short text and an optional leading icon or avatar. Use it as a filter, as a choice among a few options, or to represent a selected item that can be removed. A group handles single or multiple selection and arrow key navigation.

## Import

```tsx
import { Chip, ChipGroup } from '@motifx-community/ui';
```

## Declarative and programmatic

Every prop accepts a value or a function. When you create the component with `new`, set the same properties programmatically.

```tsx
import { reactive } from '@motifx/core';
import { Chip, Stack } from '@motifx-community/ui';

/** A chip in JSX tracks its functions, and one created with `new` accepts the same properties programmatically. */
export default function Programmatic() {
  const s = reactive({ vegan: false });
  const coded = new Chip({ text: 'Spicy', selectable: true });

  return (
    <Stack orientation="horizontal" wrap align="center">
      <Chip text="Vegan" selectable selected={() => s.vegan} onSelectedChanged={(e) => (s.vegan = e.selected)} />
      <span>{() => (s.vegan ? 'Vegan only' : 'Everything')}</span>
      <span onConfig={(c) => c.controls.add(coded)} />
    </Stack>
  );
}
```

## Appearance and states

```tsx
import { Chip, Stack, type ChipVariant } from '@motifx-community/ui';

const VARIANTS: ChipVariant[] = ['filled', 'outline'];

// An inline star, so that the example needs no icon set.
const star = () => {
  const svg = document.createElementNS('http://www.w3.org/2000/svg', 'svg');
  svg.setAttribute('viewBox', '0 0 16 16');
  svg.innerHTML = '<path d="M8 1.5l1.9 4.1 4.4.5-3.3 3 .9 4.4L8 11.3l-3.9 2.2.9-4.4-3.3-3 4.4-.5z" fill="currentColor"/>';
  return svg;
};

/** Each appearance: at rest, selected, with an icon, with an avatar, removable and disabled. */
export default function Looks() {
  return (
    <Stack>
      {VARIANTS.map((variant) => (
        <Stack key={variant} orientation="horizontal" wrap align="center">
          <Chip text="Rest" variant={variant} clickable />
          <Chip text="Selected" variant={variant} selectable selected />
          <Chip text="Icon" variant={variant} icon={star()} clickable />
          <Chip text="Ada Lovelace" variant={variant} avatar={{ name: 'Ada Lovelace' }} removable />
          <Chip text="Removable" variant={variant} removable />
          <Chip text="Disabled" variant={variant} selectable disabled />
        </Stack>
      ))}
    </Stack>
  );
}
```

## Tones

```tsx
import { Chip, Stack, type ChipTone, type ChipVariant } from '@motifx-community/ui';

const TONES: ChipTone[] = ['standard', 'accent', 'info', 'success', 'caution', 'danger'];
const VARIANTS: ChipVariant[] = ['filled', 'outline'];

/** Every tone in each appearance. */
export default function Tones() {
  return (
    <Stack>
      {VARIANTS.map((variant) => (
        <Stack key={variant} orientation="horizontal" wrap align="center">
          {TONES.map((tone) => (
            <Chip key={tone} text={tone} tone={tone} variant={variant} />
          ))}
        </Stack>
      ))}
    </Stack>
  );
}
```

## Sizes

```tsx
import { Chip, Stack, type ControlSize } from '@motifx-community/ui';

const SIZES: ControlSize[] = ['sm', 'md', 'lg'];

/** Each size, plain, with an avatar and removable. */
export default function Sizes() {
  return (
    <Stack>
      {SIZES.map((size) => (
        <Stack key={size} orientation="horizontal" wrap align="center">
          <Chip text={size} size={size} selectable />
          <Chip text="Grace Hopper" size={size} avatar={{ name: 'Grace Hopper' }} removable />
        </Stack>
      ))}
    </Stack>
  );
}
```

## Selection in a group

`selection` turns chips into selectable options. `value` holds their values, and `onValueChanged` reports changes.

```tsx
import { reactive } from '@motifx/core';
import { Chip, ChipGroup, Stack } from '@motifx-community/ui';

const DIETS = ['Vegan', 'Vegetarian', 'Gluten free', 'Dairy free'];
const SIZES = ['Small', 'Medium', 'Large'];

/** Several chosen (filters, bound with `x-model`) and one chosen (`value` and `onValueChanged`); the value is the chips' values. */
export default function Groups() {
  const s = reactive({ diets: ['Vegan'] as unknown, size: 'Medium' as unknown });

  return (
    <Stack gap="lg">
      <ChipGroup selection="multiple" label="Diet" x-model={() => s.diets}>
        {DIETS.map((diet) => (
          <Chip key={diet} text={diet} />
        ))}
      </ChipGroup>
      <span>{() => `Diet: ${(s.diets as string[]).join(', ') || 'any'}`}</span>
      <ChipGroup selection="single" label="Size" value={() => s.size} onValueChanged={(e) => (s.size = e.value)}>
        {SIZES.map((size) => (
          <Chip key={size} text={size} />
        ))}
      </ChipGroup>
      <span>{() => `Size: ${s.size ?? 'none'}`}</span>
    </Stack>
  );
}
```

## Removing chips

A removable chip only sends a request. Remove the item from your list in `onRemove`, and the group updates to match.

```tsx
import { reactive } from '@motifx/core';
import { Button, Chip, ChipGroup, Stack } from '@motifx-community/ui';

const PEOPLE = ['Ada Lovelace', 'Alan Turing', 'Grace Hopper', 'Edsger Dijkstra'];

/** Your code performs the removal: `onRemove` removes the person from the list, and the group updates to match. */
export default function Removing() {
  const s = reactive({ people: PEOPLE.map((name) => ({ name })) });

  return (
    <Stack>
      <ChipGroup label="Invited">
        {s.people.map((person) => (
          <Chip
            key={person.name}
            text={person.name}
            avatar={{ name: person.name }}
            removable
            onRemove={() => s.people.splice(s.people.indexOf(person), 1)}
          />
        ))}
      </ChipGroup>
      <Button text="Invite everyone again" variant="outline" onclick={() => s.people.splice(0, s.people.length, ...PEOPLE.map((name) => ({ name })))} />
    </Stack>
  );
}
```

## Keyboard

| Key | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `Enter, Space` | Presses the chip, which toggles a selectable chip or selects one in a group. |
| `Delete, Backspace` | Requests removal of a removable chip. |
| `Arrow keys, Home, End` | In a group, moves between the chips. The group has one Tab stop, on the chip focused last. |

## Accessibility

| Topic | Details |
| --- | --- |
| `Selectable` | A button with `aria-pressed`. |
| `In a group that selects` | The group is a `listbox` (`aria-multiselectable` for multiple selection), and each chip is an `option` with `aria-selected`. |
| `Remove` | The remove button is named “Remove Ada” in the kit language. Keyboard users reach it with Delete on the chip. |
| `Disabled state` | Removed from the Tab order and marked with `aria-disabled`. |

## Localization

The remove button's name is the `removeItem` kit string (“Remove {text}”) and changes with the kit language (`uiLocale`).

## Styling

| Hook | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `.mx-chip` | The chip. `data-size`, `data-variant`, `data-selected`, `data-pressable`, `data-removable`, `data-lead`, `data-check`, `data-disabled`. |
| `.mx-chip__check, .mx-chip__icon, .mx-chip__avatar` | The content before the text. |
| `.mx-chip__text, .mx-chip__remove` | The text and the remove button. |
| `.mx-chip-group` | The group. `data-wrap`. |

### Component tokens

| Token | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `chip.chip` | Unit: the chip, filled at rest, then `outline`, each tone filled and outlined (`accent` … `danger`, `outline-*`), and `selected`, `hover`, `pressed`, `focus` and `disabled`. |
| `chip.icon, chip.remove` | Units: the icon or check mark, and the remove button (`hover`, `pressed`). |
| `chip.height.*, chip.font-size.*, chip.padding.*, chip.icon-inset.*, chip.gap.*` | The chip, its text and its spacing, per size. |
| `chip.icon-size.*, chip.avatar-size.*, chip.remove-size.*` | The content before and after the text, per size. An avatar and the remove button have the same inset from the edge as from the top and bottom. |
| `chip.variant, chip.check` | The default appearance, and whether a selected chip shows a check mark (Material). |
| `chip-group.gap` | The space between chips. |

## API reference

### Chip props

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `text` | `Bind<string>` | `''` | The text. |
| `value` | `Bind<unknown>` | Its text | The value it represents in a group. |
| `icon` | `Bind<IconSource \| null>` | `null` | An icon before the text: an image address, an element or a component. |
| `avatar` | `Bind<AvatarProps \| null>` | `null` | An avatar before the text (its props; the chip sets the size). |
| `selectable` | `Bind<boolean>` | `false` | Pressing the chip toggles it, as a filter. In a group with selection, the group controls it. |
| `selected` | `Bind<boolean>` | `false` | Indicates whether the chip is on. |
| `clickable` | `Bind<boolean>` | `false` | Lets the chip be pressed like a button (`onclick`). |
| `removable` | `Bind<boolean>` | `false` | Adds a remove button after the text. The button, Delete and Backspace raise `onRemove`. |
| `variant` | `Bind<ChipVariant>` | Set by the design language | `filled` or `outline`. Material draws chips outlined, and the other design languages draw them filled. |
| `tone` | `Bind<ChipTone>` | `'standard'` | `standard`, `accent`, `info`, `success`, `caution` or `danger`. A selected chip shows the selection color instead. |
| `size` | `Bind<ControlSize>` | `'md'` | `sm`, `md`, `lg`. |
| `enabled, visible, tabStop` | see Control |  | Properties shared by all controls. |

### Chip events

| Event | Arguments | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `onRemove` | `ChipRemoveEventArgs` | Occurs when the user requests removal (`byKeyboard`). Your code performs the removal. |
| `onSelectedChanged` | `ChipSelectedChangedEventArgs` | Occurs when the chip is turned on or off (`selected`), either by the user or programmatically (`byUser`). |

### Chip properties

| Property | Access | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `every prop above` | read/write | Accepts a value or a function, the same as the prop. |
| `avatarControl` | read-only | The avatar before the text, if there is one. |

### Chip methods

| Method | Returns | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `remove()` | `void` | Requests removal, as the remove button does (raises `onRemove`). |

### ChipGroup props

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `selection` | `Bind<ChipGroupSelection>` | `'none'` | `none`, `single`, `multiple`. |
| `value` | `Bind<unknown>` | `null` / `[]` | The value of the selected chip (`single`), or an array of selected values (`multiple`). A change produces a new array. `x-model` provides two-way binding. |
| `wrap` | `Bind<boolean>` | `true` | `false` keeps the chips on one line that scrolls. |
| `label` | `Bind<string>` | `''` | The accessible name of the group (“Diet”). |

### ChipGroup events, properties and methods

| Member | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `onValueChanged` | event | Occurs when the value changes (`value`), either through user input or programmatically (`byUser`). |
| `chips` | read-only | The chips in order, including those from JSX lists. |
| `isSelected(value)` | `boolean` | Indicates whether the chip for `value` is selected. |

# Card

> Display · @motifx-community/ui 0.1.0-beta.5

A surface for a single subject, with an optional image, a header with an avatar and titles, content and a row of actions. Empty parts are not rendered.

## Import

```tsx
import { Card } from '@motifx-community/ui';
```

## Declarative and programmatic

Every prop accepts a value or a function. When you create the component with `new`, set the same properties programmatically.

```tsx
import { reactive } from '@motifx/core';
import { Button, Card, Stack } from '@motifx-community/ui';

/** A card in JSX tracks its functions, and one created with `new` accepts the same properties programmatically. */
export default function Programmatic() {
  const s = reactive({ following: false });
  const coded = new Card({ title: 'Made in code', subtitle: 'new Card({ … })', variant: 'outline' });

  return (
    <Stack orientation="horizontal" wrap align="start" gap="lg">
      <Card
        title="Ada Lovelace"
        subtitle={() => (s.following ? 'Following' : 'Mathematician')}
        avatar={{ name: 'Ada Lovelace' }}
        footer={<Button text={() => (s.following ? 'Unfollow' : 'Follow')} onclick={() => (s.following = !s.following)} />}
        style="inline-size: 18rem"
      >
        First to publish an algorithm meant to be carried out by a machine.
      </Card>
      <span onConfig={(c) => c.controls.add(coded)} />
    </Stack>
  );
}
```

## Appearance

```tsx
import { Button, Card, Stack, type CardVariant } from '@motifx-community/ui';

const VARIANTS: CardVariant[] = ['elevated', 'filled', 'outline'];

/** Each appearance with a header, content and actions. */
export default function Variants() {
  return (
    <Stack orientation="horizontal" wrap align="start" gap="lg">
      {VARIANTS.map((variant) => (
        <Card
          key={variant}
          variant={variant}
          title={variant}
          subtitle="A card of this look"
          footer={
            <Stack orientation="horizontal" gap="sm">
              <Button text="Cancel" variant="ghost" />
              <Button text="Open" />
            </Stack>
          }
          style="inline-size: 16rem"
        >
          The same header, content and actions in each look.
        </Card>
      ))}
    </Stack>
  );
}
```

## Images

```tsx
import { Button, Card, Stack } from '@motifx-community/ui';

/** A picture above the rest, or at its start (`horizontal`); it runs to the card's edges and takes its corners. */

        media={PICTURE}

      </Card>
```

## Clickable cards

```tsx
import { reactive } from '@motifx/core';
import { Card, Stack } from '@motifx-community/ui';

const PLACES = ['Istanbul', 'Lisbon', 'Kyoto'];

/** The whole card can be pressed: with the mouse, Enter or Space. */
export default function Clickable() {
  const s = reactive({ chosen: '' });

  return (
    <Stack gap="lg">
      <Stack orientation="horizontal" wrap align="start">
        {PLACES.map((place) => (
          <Card key={place} title={place} subtitle="Press to choose" clickable onclick={() => (s.chosen = place)} style="inline-size: 12rem" />
        ))}
      </Stack>
      <span>{() => (s.chosen ? `Chosen: ${s.chosen}` : 'Nothing chosen yet')}</span>
    </Stack>
  );
}
```

## Links and selection

```tsx
import { reactive } from '@motifx/core';
import { Button, Card, Stack } from '@motifx-community/ui';

const PLACES = ['Istanbul', 'Lisbon', 'Kyoto'];

/**
 * A link card: its title is the link, and a click anywhere on the card follows it (`rel="router"` hands it to the router).
 * Its own button stays a button. A selectable card toggles with a click or with its check box.
 */
export default function Links() {
  const s = reactive({ picked: [] as string[] });
  const toggle = (place: string, on: boolean) => {
    s.picked = on ? [...s.picked, place] : s.picked.filter((p) => p !== place);
  };

  return (
    <Stack gap="lg">
      <Stack orientation="horizontal" wrap align="start">
        <Card title="Tokens" subtitle="A link to the tokens page" href="/tokens" rel="router" footer={<Button text="Later" variant="ghost" />} style="inline-size: 14rem" />
        <Card title="Keyboard" subtitle="A link to the keyboard page" href="/keyboard" rel="router" style="inline-size: 14rem" />
      </Stack>
      <Stack orientation="horizontal" wrap align="start">
        {PLACES.map((place) => (
          <Card
            key={place}
            title={place}
            subtitle="Press to pick"
            selectable
            selected={() => s.picked.includes(place)}
            onSelectedChanged={(e) => e.byUser && toggle(place, e.selected)}
            style="inline-size: 12rem"
          />
        ))}
      </Stack>
      <span>{() => `Picked: ${s.picked.join(', ') || 'none'}`}</span>
    </Stack>
  );
}
```

## Sizes

```tsx
import { Card, Stack, type ControlSize } from '@motifx-community/ui';

/** The space in and between the parts, per size. */

  return (
    <Stack orientation="horizontal" wrap align="start" gap="lg">
      {SIZES.map((size) => (
        <Card key={size} size={size} title={`Size ${size}`} subtitle="Grace Hopper" avatar={{ name: 'Grace Hopper' }} style="inline-size: 15rem">
          Content of the card.
        </Card>
      ))}
    </Stack>
  );

```

## Accessibility

| Topic | Details |
| --- | --- |
| `Name` | A `group` named by its title (`aria-labelledby`). |
| `Picture` | Decorative unless `mediaAlt` describes it. |
| `Clickable cards` | A Tab stop that responds to Enter and Space. Buttons inside it remain independent. |
| `Link` | The title is a real link, and the card shows its focus state. The card's own buttons stay above it. |
| `Selectable` | A check box named “Select <title>” in the kit language. The card shows the selection with its frame. |

## Styling

| Hook | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `.mx-card` | The card. `data-variant`, `data-size`, `data-orientation`, `data-pressable`, `data-disabled`. |
| `.mx-card__media` | The image. |
| `.mx-card__body` | The header, content and actions. |
| `.mx-card__header, .mx-card__avatar, .mx-card__heading, .mx-card__title, .mx-card__subtitle, .mx-card__action` | The header and its parts. |
| `.mx-card__content, .mx-card__footer` | The content and the action row. |

### Component tokens

| Token | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `card.card` | Unit: the card at rest, then `elevated`, `filled`, `outline`, `selected`, `hover`, `pressed`, `focus` and `disabled`. |
| `card.title, card.subtitle, card.content` | Units: the title, the subtitle and the content text. |
| `card.padding.*, card.gap.*` | The spacing around and between the parts, per size. |
| `card.header-gap, card.footer-gap, card.media-width` | The spacing in the header and between actions, and the width of an image at the start. |
| `card.variant, card.footer-align` | The default appearance, and the action alignment (start in Fluent, end in the other design languages). |

## API reference

### Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `title` | `Bind<string>` | `''` | The title, which also provides the accessible name of the card. |
| `subtitle` | `Bind<string>` | `''` | Text below the title. |
| `avatar` | `Bind<AvatarProps \| null>` | `null` | An avatar before the titles (its props). |
| `action` | `Bind<ComponentBase \| null>` | `null` | Content at the end of the header, such as a menu button or a badge. |
| `media` | `Bind<IconSource \| null>` | `null` | An image that extends to the card edges: an image address, an element or a component. |
| `mediaAlt` | `Bind<string>` | `''` | Alternative text for the image when `media` is an image address. Without it, the image is decorative. |
| `content` | `Bind<ComponentBase \| null>` | `null` | The content, in addition to JSX children. |
| `footer` | `Bind<ComponentBase \| null>` | `null` | A row of actions below the content. A replaced component is removed from the card and stays under your control. |
| `variant` | `Bind<CardVariant>` | Set by the design language (`elevated`) | `elevated`, `filled`, `outline`. |
| `size` | `Bind<ControlSize>` | `'md'` | The spacing inside and between the parts: `sm`, `md` or `lg`. |
| `orientation` | `Bind<CardOrientation>` | `'vertical'` | `horizontal` places the image at the start. |
| `clickable` | `Bind<boolean>` | `false` | Makes the whole card pressable (`onclick`, Enter, Space). |
| `href` | `Bind<string \| null>` | `null` | Makes the whole card a link. The title is the link, and clicking anywhere on the card follows it. |
| `rel` | `Bind<string>` | `''` | The `rel` of the link. `router` lets the MotifJS router handle it. |
| `selectable` | `Bind<boolean>` | `false` | Adds a check box on the top end corner, and clicking the card toggles it. |
| `selected` | `Bind<boolean>` | `false` | Indicates whether the card is selected. |
| `onSelectedChanged` | `CardSelectedChangedEventArgs` |  | Occurs when the selection changes (`selected`), either by the user or programmatically (`byUser`). |
| `enabled, visible, tabStop` | see Control |  | Properties shared by all controls. |

### Properties

| Property | Access | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `every prop above` | read/write | Accepts a value or a function, the same as the prop. |
| `contentPart` | read-only | The part that holds the content, for adding to it programmatically. |
| `avatarControl` | read-only | The avatar before the titles, if there is one. |

# Gallery

> Display · @motifx-community/ui 0.1.0-beta.5

Displays a horizontal set of slides, one or several at a time. Users navigate with the side buttons, the indicator dots, swipe gestures or the arrow keys, and it can run as an automatic slideshow. A slide can be an image with a caption or any other content.

## Import

```tsx
import { Gallery } from '@motifx-community/ui';
```

## Images with captions

`items` defines the slides. Each one is an address or an item with `image`, `alt`, `text` and `description`. `value` is the visible slide, identified by its `key` or index, and `x-model` provides two-way binding. Users can drag a slide with a finger or the mouse, press an arrow or a dot, or use the keyboard.

```tsx
import { Gallery } from '@motifx-community/ui';
import { scene } from './scenes';

/** Five pictures with captions: the buttons at the sides, the dots under them, a swipe or the arrow keys move them. */
export default function Basic() {
    return (
        <Gallery
            class="ga-trip"
            label="A trip"
            height={300}
            items={[
                { image: scene(205), alt: 'Boats in a harbour', text: 'Harbour', description: 'Early morning' },
                { image: scene(30), alt: 'Market stalls', text: 'Market' },
                { image: scene(120), alt: 'Hills under cloud', text: 'Hills', description: 'After the rain' },
                { image: scene(280), alt: 'The town at night', text: 'Night' },
                { image: scene(345), alt: 'The way home', text: 'Home', description: 'Last day' }
            ]}
        />
    );
}
```

## Looping and slideshow

`loop` wraps around at the ends. The slide on the other side moves next to the outgoing one, so the transition never runs back across the slides in between. `slideInterval` starts a slideshow, which pauses while the pointer is over the gallery, while focus is inside it, while the page is hidden, and when the user prefers reduced motion. The button in the bar pauses it manually. `stretchImages` makes images fill the slides.

```tsx
import { reactive } from '@motifx/core';
import { Gallery, Stack } from '@motifx-community/ui';
import { scene } from './scenes';

/** A slideshow around the ends: it moves on every 2.5 s, waits while the pointer or focus is on it, and its button pauses it. */
export default function Slideshow() {
    const s = reactive({ shown: 0 as string | number | null, told: '' });
    return (
        <Stack gap="sm" style="inline-size: 100%">
            <Gallery
                class="ga-show"
                label="Slideshow"
                height={240}
                loop
                stretchImages
                slideInterval={2500}
                x-model={() => s.shown}
                onSlideChanged={e => (s.told = e.byUser ? 'moved by you' : 'moved by the slideshow')}
                items={[
                    { image: scene(190), alt: 'Dawn over the sea', text: 'Dawn' },
                    { image: scene(50), alt: 'Noon in the square', text: 'Noon' },
                    { image: scene(260), alt: 'Dusk on the hill', text: 'Dusk' }
                ]}
            />
            <output class="ga-show-told">{() => `in view: ${s.shown}${s.told ? `, ${s.told}` : ''}`}</output>
        </Stack>
    );
}
```

## Multiple slides per view

`itemsPerPage` sets how many slides fit in the width, separated by the `gap` token. The buttons and keys move one slide at a time and stop when the last slide is in view. The current slide is the first visible one.

```tsx
import { Gallery } from '@motifx-community/ui';
import { scene } from './scenes';

/** Three panes share the width; next and previous move one pane at a time and stop when the last is in view. */
export default function PerPage() {
    const places = ['Pier', 'Lane', 'Roof', 'Park', 'Bridge', 'Shore', 'Tower'];
    return (
        <Gallery
            class="ga-wide"
            label="Places"
            height={150}
            itemsPerPage={3}
            stretchImages
            items={places.map((place, i) => ({ image: scene(i * 48), alt: `The ${i + 1}. picture of the walk`, text: place }))}
        />
    );
}
```

## Any content

An item's `content` creates the slide content when the slide is created, and it behaves the same as anywhere else. `onItemClick` reports a click on a slide that was not a drag.

```tsx
import { reactive } from '@motifx/core';
import { Button, Gallery, Stack } from '@motifx-community/ui';

const PLANS = [
    { name: 'Starter', price: '€9', line: 'One project, two people' },
    { name: 'Team', price: '€29', line: 'Ten projects, your whole team' },
    { name: 'Company', price: '€79', line: 'No limits, a person to call' }
];

/** Any content in a slide: a plan each, with its own button. A click on the slide itself is also reported. */
export default function Content() {
    const s = reactive({ told: '' });
    const plan = (p: (typeof PLANS)[number]) => (
        <Stack class="ga-plan" gap="xs" align="center" justify="center" style="block-size: 100%">
            <strong>{p.name}</strong>
            <span class="ga-plan-price">{p.price} a month</span>
            <span>{p.line}</span>
            <Button text="Choose" variant="outline" onclick={() => (s.told = `${p.name} chosen`)} />
        </Stack>
    );
    return (
        <Stack gap="sm" style="inline-size: 100%">
            <Gallery class="ga-plans" label="Plans" height={200} swipeEnabled={false} items={PLANS.map(p => ({ key: p.name, content: () => plan(p) }))} onItemClick={e => (s.told = `pane ${e.index + 1} pressed`)} />
            <output class="ga-plans-told">{() => s.told}</output>
        </Stack>
    );
}
```

## Programmatic use

Create the gallery with `new` and navigate with `next()`, `previous()` and `goTo()`. With `showNavButtons` and `showIndicator` off, you can use your own buttons, and `onSlideChanged` reports the position.

```tsx
import { reactive } from '@motifx/core';
import { Button, Gallery, Stack } from '@motifx-community/ui';
import { scene } from './scenes';

/** A gallery created programmatically without its own buttons or dots: custom buttons navigate, and `onSlideChanged` reports the position. */
export default function Programmatic() {
    const s = reactive({ at: 0, told: '' });
    const coded = new Gallery({
        label: 'Rooms',
        height: 200,
        showNavButtons: false,
        showIndicator: false,
        swipeEnabled: false,
        items: [
            { key: 'hall', image: scene(20), alt: 'The hall', text: 'Hall' },
            { key: 'study', image: scene(200), alt: 'The study', text: 'Study' },
            { key: 'garden', image: scene(110), alt: 'The garden', text: 'Garden' }
        ],
        onSlideChanged: e => {
            s.at = e.index;
            s.told = `slide ${e.index + 1} of ${coded.count}`;
        }
    });
    return (
        <Stack gap="sm" style="inline-size: 100%">
            <span class="ga-rooms" onConfig={c => c.controls.add(coded)} />
            <Stack orientation="horizontal" wrap align="center">
                <Button text="Previous" variant="outline" enabled={() => s.at > 0} onclick={() => void coded.previous()} />
                <Button text="Next" variant="outline" enabled={() => s.at < 2} onclick={() => void coded.next()} />
                <Button text="Garden" variant="outline" onclick={() => void coded.goTo('garden')} />
                <output class="ga-rooms-told">{() => s.told}</output>
            </Stack>
        </Stack>
    );
}
```

## Keyboard

| Key | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `Tab` | The slideshow button, the dots (one Tab stop, on the dot of the current slide), the previous button, the slides and the next button, followed by any content in the current slide. |
| `Arrow keys` | On the slides or dots, Left and Right move to the previous and next slide (reversed on right-to-left pages), and Home and End move to the first and last. |
| `Enter, Space` | On a button or dot, activates it. |

## Accessibility

| Topic | Details |
| --- | --- |
| `Landmark` | A `region` with `aria-roledescription="carousel"`, named “Gallery” in the kit language. If a page has several, give each one its own `label`. |
| `A pane` | A `group` with `aria-roledescription="slide"`, named “Slide 2 of 5”. Slides out of view are hidden from assistive technology and the keyboard (`inert`). |
| `Images` | Give each image an `alt`. An empty value marks a decorative image. The caption is read as part of the slide. |
| `Slideshow` | The slides are a live region while stopped (`polite`) and silent while running (`off`), as the carousel pattern requires. The button that stops the slideshow comes first in the Tab order. |
| `Dots and arrows` | Buttons named “Slide 2 of 5”, “Previous slide” and “Next slide”. The dot of the current slide has `aria-current`, and an arrow at an end has `aria-disabled`. |

## Styling

| Hook | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `.mx-gallery` | The gallery. `data-swipe` when dragging is enabled, `data-dragging` during a drag, `data-playing` while the slideshow runs, and `data-stretch`. |
| `.mx-gallery__viewport, .mx-gallery__track` | The frame that clips the slides and the track that moves inside it (`data-dragging`, `data-no-motion`). |
| `.mx-gallery__item, .mx-gallery__figure, .mx-gallery__image` | A slide (`data-current`, `aria-hidden`), its content and the image. |
| `.mx-gallery__caption, .mx-gallery__title, .mx-gallery__description` | The caption band over the bottom of a slide and its two lines. |
| `.mx-gallery__nav, .mx-gallery__arrow` | The previous and next buttons (`data-direction`, `aria-disabled`) and their glyphs. |
| `.mx-gallery__bar, .mx-gallery__indicator, .mx-gallery__dot, .mx-gallery__play, .mx-gallery__play-glyph` | The bar along the bottom, the dots (`aria-current`), the slideshow button and its glyph. |

### Component tokens

| Token | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `gallery.frame, .item, .caption, .title, .description` | Units: the frame (`focus`, `swipeable`, `dragging`), a slide (`current`), the caption and its text. |
| `gallery.nav, .arrow, .dot, .play, .play-glyph, .bar` | Units: the side buttons (`hover`, `pressed`, `focus`, `disabled`), their glyphs (`icon` per direction), the dots (`current`, `hover`, `pressed`, `focus`), the slideshow button and its glyph (`icon` while `playing`), and the bar. |
| `gallery.gap, .nav-inset, .bar-inset, .indicator-gap, .caption-padding` | The gap between side-by-side slides, the offset of overlaid parts from the sides and bottom, the gap between dots, and the caption padding. |

## API reference

### Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `items` | `Bind<readonly (GalleryItem \| string)[]>` | `[]` | The slides in order: `GalleryItem` objects (`image`, `alt`, `text`, `description`, `key`, `content`, `data`) or image addresses. |
| `value` | `Bind<string \| number \| null>` | `0` | The current slide, identified by its `key` or index. `x-model` provides two-way binding. |
| `loop` | `Bind<boolean>` | `false` | The first slide follows the last, and the transition wraps around instead of running back across the slides in between. |
| `showNavButtons` | `Bind<boolean>` | `true` | Shows previous and next buttons over the sides. |
| `showIndicator` | `Bind<boolean>` | `true` | Shows indicator dots below the slides, one per slide. |
| `slideInterval` | `Bind<number>` | `0` | The time each slide stays in a slideshow, in milliseconds. `0` turns it off. The slideshow pauses on hover, while focus is inside, while the page is hidden and when the user prefers reduced motion. |
| `pauseOnHover` | `Bind<boolean>` | `true` | Pauses the slideshow while the pointer is over the gallery. |
| `swipeEnabled` | `Bind<boolean>` | `true` | Lets a finger or pointer drag the slides. A drag that is far or fast enough moves to the next slide. |
| `itemsPerPage` | `Bind<number>` | `1` | The number of slides side by side, with the `gap` token between them. |
| `stretchImages` | `Bind<boolean>` | `false` | Makes an image fill its slide and crops the edges, instead of fitting the whole image inside. |
| `height` | `Bind<string \| number \| null>` | `null` | A CSS length or pixels. Without it, the gallery is as tall as its tallest slide. |
| `label` | `Bind<string>` | The kit string “Gallery” | The accessible name. |

### Events, properties and methods

| Member | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `onSlideChanging` | event | Occurs before the current slide changes (`from`, `to`, `fromItem`, `toItem`, `byUser`). Set `cancel = true` to keep the current slide. |
| `onSlideChanged` | event | Occurs after the current slide changes (`index`, `item`, `previous`, and `byUser` for a click, swipe or key, as opposed to code or the slideshow). |
| `onItemClick` | event | Occurs when a slide is clicked without dragging (`index`, `item`, `event`). |
| `selectedIndex` | read-only | The index of the current slide, or -1 if there is none. |
| `count` | read-only | The number of panes. |
| `isPlaying` | read-only | Indicates that the slideshow is running and nothing is holding it. |
| `next(), previous()` | `Promise<boolean>` | Moves to the next or previous slide. Returns `false` at an end without `loop`, or if the change was canceled. |
| `goTo(pane)` | `Promise<boolean>` | Moves to a slide by index or key. `onSlideChanging` is raised first. |
| `play(), pause()` | `void` | Starts the slideshow again, or stops it until `play()` is called. The button in the bar does the same. |
| `refresh()` | `void` | Re-reads the items after they have been changed in place. |

# TileView

> Display · @motifx-community/ui 0.1.0-beta.5

Arranges tiles of different sizes on a grid of base cells, where each tile spans a set number of cells. Tiles fill the height in columns and scroll horizontally, or fill the width in rows. They can be selected and reordered by dragging.

## Import

```tsx
import { TileView } from '@motifx-community/ui';
```

## Tile grid

`baseItemWidth` and `baseItemHeight` define one cell, and a tile's `widthRatio` and `heightRatio` set how many cells it spans. In the default `horizontal` direction, the view needs a `height` and scrolls horizontally. Tiles are packed so that no cell stays empty where a later tile fits.

```tsx
import { TileView } from '@motifx-community/ui';

/** Tiles of one, two and four base cells packed down the columns; the view scrolls sideways when they do not fit. */
export default function Basic() {
    return (
        <TileView
            class="tv-board"
            label="Board"
            height={330}
            baseItemWidth={120}
            baseItemHeight={100}
            items={[
                { text: 'Sales today', widthRatio: 2 },
                { text: 'Orders' },
                { text: 'Returns' },
                { text: 'Visitors this week', widthRatio: 2, heightRatio: 2 },
                { text: 'Stock' },
                { text: 'Staff on duty', heightRatio: 2 },
                { text: 'Tickets' },
                { text: 'Deliveries', widthRatio: 2 },
                { text: 'Reviews' },
                { text: 'Costs' }
            ]}
        />
    );
}
```

## Selecting tiles

`selectionMode` makes tiles selectable. `single` keeps one selected, and `multiple` allows any number (Ctrl + click or Space adds and removes). `value` is the `key` or index of the selected tile, or a list of them, and `x-model` provides two-way binding. The arrow keys move through the grid based on tile positions.

```tsx
import { reactive } from '@motifx/core';
import { Stack, TileView } from '@motifx-community/ui';

/** Tiles along the rows with any number selected: click, Ctrl + click or Space, and the arrow keys move through the grid. */
export default function Selection() {
    const s = reactive({ chosen: ['tea'] as string | number | null | readonly (string | number)[] });
    return (
        <Stack gap="sm" style="inline-size: 100%">
            <TileView
                class="tv-pick"
                label="Snacks"
                direction="vertical"
                selectionMode="multiple"
                baseItemWidth={110}
                baseItemHeight={70}
                x-model={() => s.chosen}
                items={[
                    { key: 'tea', text: 'Tea' },
                    { key: 'coffee', text: 'Coffee' },
                    { key: 'water', text: 'Water', enabled: false },
                    { key: 'cake', text: 'Cake', widthRatio: 2 },
                    { key: 'fruit', text: 'Fruit' },
                    { key: 'nuts', text: 'Nuts' }
                ]}
            />
            <output class="tv-pick-told">{() => `chosen: ${JSON.stringify(s.chosen)}`}</output>
        </Stack>
    );
}
```

## Reordering

With `allowReorder`, users can drag a tile to a new position (a long press on a touch screen) or move it with Ctrl and an arrow key. The tile moves and `onReordered` reports the indexes. Reorder your data there, as the example does, so the next render matches.

```tsx
import { reactive } from '@motifx/core';
import { Stack, TileView } from '@motifx-community/ui';

/** Drag a tile to another place, or move it with Ctrl and an arrow key; the data is reordered in `onReordered`. */
export default function Reorder() {
    const s = reactive({ tiles: [{ text: 'Plan' }, { text: 'Design', widthRatio: 2 }, { text: 'Build' }, { text: 'Test' }, { text: 'Ship', heightRatio: 2 }, { text: 'Rest' }] });
    return (
        <Stack gap="sm" style="inline-size: 100%">
            <TileView
                class="tv-order"
                label="Steps"
                direction="vertical"
                allowReorder
                baseItemWidth={100}
                baseItemHeight={70}
                items={() => s.tiles}
                onReordered={e => s.tiles.splice(e.toIndex, 0, ...s.tiles.splice(e.fromIndex, 1))}
            />
            <output class="tv-order-told">{() => s.tiles.map(t => t.text).join(', ')}</output>
        </Stack>
    );
}
```

## Any content

An item's `content` creates the tile content when the tile is created, and it behaves the same as anywhere else. A click on a button inside goes to that button. `onItemClick` reports a click on the tile itself.

```tsx
import { reactive } from '@motifx/core';
import { Button, Stack, TileView } from '@motifx-community/ui';

const ROOMS = [
    { name: 'Kitchen', temp: 21 },
    { name: 'Lounge', temp: 23 },
    { name: 'Study', temp: 19 },
    { name: 'Bedroom', temp: 18 }
];

/** Any content on a tile: a room each, with its own button. A click on the tile itself is also reported. */
export default function Content() {
    const s = reactive({ told: '' });
    const room = (r: (typeof ROOMS)[number]) => (
        <Stack class="tv-room" gap="xs" justify="center" style="block-size: 100%">
            <strong>{r.name}</strong>
            <span class="tv-room-temp">{r.temp} °C</span>
            <Button text="Warmer" variant="outline" size="sm" onclick={() => (s.told = `${r.name}: warmer`)} />
        </Stack>
    );
    return (
        <Stack gap="sm" style="inline-size: 100%">
            <TileView class="tv-rooms" label="Rooms" direction="vertical" baseItemWidth={150} baseItemHeight={120} items={ROOMS.map(r => ({ key: r.name, content: () => room(r) }))} onItemClick={e => (s.told = `${(e.item as { key: string }).key} pressed`)} />
            <output class="tv-rooms-told">{() => s.told}</output>
        </Stack>
    );
}
```

## Keyboard

| Key | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `Tab` | One Tab stop: the tile focused last, otherwise the first selected tile, otherwise the first tile. |
| `Arrow keys` | Moves to the nearest tile in that direction, based on tile positions. Home and End move to the first and last tile. |
| `Space` | Selects the tile (`single`), or toggles it (`multiple`). |
| `Enter` | Acts as a click on the tile: raises `onItemClick` and applies the selection. |
| `Ctrl + Arrow keys` | With `allowReorder`, moves the tile one position back or forward. Ctrl + Home and End move it to the ends, and each move is announced. |

## Accessibility

| Topic | Details |
| --- | --- |
| `Roles` | A `list` of `listitem` elements without selection, or a `listbox` of `option` elements with it (`aria-multiselectable` for `multiple`), each with `aria-selected`. |
| `Disabled tiles` | `aria-disabled`. The tile is skipped by the keyboard and cannot be selected with a click. |
| `Dragging` | A copy of the tile follows the pointer, the tile at the drop position is marked, and Escape cancels. On a touch screen, a long press lifts the tile. |

## Styling

| Hook | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `.mx-tile-view` | The view. `data-direction`, `data-reorder`, and `data-dragging` while a tile is dragged. |
| `.mx-tile-view__tile` | A tile. `aria-selected`, `aria-disabled`, `data-dragging` (shown faded in place), and `data-drop="before\|after"` at the drop position. |
| `.mx-tile-view__text, .mx-tile-view__ghost` | The tile text, and the copy that follows the pointer. |

### Component tokens

| Token | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `tile-view.tile, .text, .ghost, .view` | Units: a tile (`hover`, `pressed`, `focus`, `selected`, `disabled`, `dragging`, `target`), its text, the drag copy and the view. |
| `tile-view.gap` | The gap between tiles. |

## API reference

### Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `items` | `Bind<readonly (TileViewItem \| string)[]>` | `[]` | The tiles in order: `TileViewItem` objects (`text`, `widthRatio`, `heightRatio`, `key`, `content`, `enabled`, `data`) or plain text. |
| `baseItemWidth, baseItemHeight` | `Bind<number>` | `100` | The size of a base cell in pixels. A tile spans `widthRatio` × `heightRatio` cells. |
| `direction` | `Bind<TileViewDirection>` | `'horizontal'` | `horizontal` fills the height in columns and scrolls horizontally (set a `height`). `vertical` fills the width in rows. |
| `selectionMode` | `Bind<TileViewSelectionMode>` | `'none'` | `none`, `single` or `multiple`. |
| `value` | `Bind<string \| number \| null \| (string \| number)[]>` | `null` | The selected tile (`single`), identified by its `key` or index, or a list of selected tiles (`multiple`). `x-model` provides two-way binding. |
| `allowReorder` | `Bind<boolean>` | `false` | Lets users reorder tiles by dragging or with Ctrl and an arrow key. |
| `height` | `Bind<string \| number \| null>` | `null` | A CSS length or pixels. |
| `label` | `Bind<string>` | The kit string “Tiles” | The accessible name. |

### Events, properties and methods

| Member | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `onItemClick` | event | Occurs when a tile is clicked without dragging (`index`, `item`, `event`), or when Enter is pressed on a focused tile. |
| `onSelectionChanged` | event | Occurs when the selected tiles change (`indexes`, `items`, `byUser`). |
| `onReordering` | event | Occurs before a tile is dragged or moved with the keyboard (`fromIndex`, `toIndex`). Set `cancel = true` to keep it in place. |
| `onReordered` | event | Occurs after a tile is dropped or moved to a new position (`item`, `fromIndex`, `toIndex`). Your code reorders the data. |
| `selectedIndexes` | read-only | The indexes of the selected tiles, in tile order. |
| `count` | read-only | The number of tiles. |
| `isDragging` | read-only | Indicates that a tile is being dragged. |
| `select(index)` | `void` | Selects a tile programmatically, as the only one (`single`) or in addition to others (`multiple`). |
| `indexOf(value), valueAt(index)` | `number`, `string \| number` | Converts between a value (a key or an index) and a tile index. |
| `refresh()` | `void` | Re-reads the items after they have been changed in place. |

# Timeline

> Display · @motifx-community/ui 0.1.0-beta.5

Displays events in chronological order. In the vertical layout, each event is a card next to a line with a marker. In the horizontal layout, events appear along a line of dates, and selecting a date shows that event's card below the line. Dates are formatted in the kit language. For scheduling by the hour, see [Scheduler](scheduler.md).

## Import

```tsx
import { Timeline } from '@motifx-community/ui';
```

## Vertical layout

`items` defines the events, each with a `date`, a `title`, a `description`, a `tone` for the marker and a `glyph` inside it. `alternate` places the cards on alternating sides of the line, and `collapsible` hides descriptions until a card is clicked. `onItemClick` reports the click.

```tsx
import { reactive } from '@motifx/core';
import { Button, Stack, Timeline } from '@motifx-community/ui';

/** A project shown vertically, with a marker per event colored by its tone. Cards can alternate sides or collapse. */
export default function Vertical() {
    const s = reactive({ alternate: false, collapsible: false, told: '' });
    return (
        <Stack gap="md" style="inline-size: 100%">
            <Stack orientation="horizontal" wrap align="center">
                <Button text="Take turns" variant="outline" toggle x-model={() => s.alternate} />
                <Button text="Fold the cards" variant="outline" toggle x-model={() => s.collapsible} />
                <output class="tl-told">{() => s.told}</output>
            </Stack>
            <Timeline
                class="tl-project"
                label="The project"
                alternate={() => s.alternate}
                collapsible={() => s.collapsible}
                onItemClick={e => (s.told = `pressed: ${(e.item as { title: string }).title}`)}
                items={[
                    { date: '2026-01-12', title: 'Kick-off', description: 'The team met and the scope was agreed.', glyph: 'calendar' },
                    { date: '2026-02-20', title: 'Design signed off', description: 'Five languages, every state measured.', tone: 'info', glyph: 'pencil' },
                    { date: '2026-04-03', title: 'Beta', description: 'The first users came in; two slow screens were found.', tone: 'accent', glyph: 'person' },
                    { date: '2026-05-15', title: 'Slow screens fixed', description: 'The grid draws only what is in view.', tone: 'caution' },
                    { date: '2026-06-30', title: 'Shipped', description: 'Version one, on time.', tone: 'success', glyph: 'check' }
                ]}
            />
        </Stack>
    );
}
```

## Horizontal layout

`orientation='horizontal'` places the dates on a scrollable line with buttons at each end. The selected event (`value`, `x-model`) shows its card below the line. The arrow keys move between dates, and `dateFormat` accepts `Intl.DateTimeFormat` options.

```tsx
import { reactive } from '@motifx/core';
import { Stack, Timeline } from '@motifx-community/ui';

const MONTHS = ['January', 'February', 'March', 'April', 'May', 'June', 'July', 'August', 'September', 'October', 'November', 'December'];

/** Releases along a line of dates. Clicking a date, or using the arrow keys, shows that release below the line, and the buttons scroll the track. */
export default function Horizontal() {
    const s = reactive({ shown: 'r3' as string | number | null });
    const releases = MONTHS.map((month, i) => ({
        key: `r${i + 1}`,
        date: new Date(2026, i, 15),
        title: `Release ${i + 1}`,
        description: `What ${month} brought: ${i % 3 === 0 ? 'new components' : i % 3 === 1 ? 'fixes and speed' : 'the docs and the languages'}.`,
        tone: i % 3 === 0 ? ('accent' as const) : ('default' as const),
        glyph: i % 3 === 0 ? 'star' : ''
    }));
    return (
        <Stack gap="sm" style="inline-size: 100%">
            <Timeline class="tl-releases" label="Releases" orientation="horizontal" dateFormat={{ month: 'short', year: 'numeric' }} items={releases} x-model={() => s.shown} />
            <output class="tl-releases-told">{() => `shown: ${s.shown}`}</output>
        </Stack>
    );
}
```

## Any content

An item's `content` adds custom content to its card, in addition to the text. `icon` places a custom icon in the marker. A date includes the time when `dateFormat` specifies it.

```tsx
import { reactive } from '@motifx/core';
import { Button, Stack, Timeline } from '@motifx-community/ui';

/** Any content in a card: a button that acts on the event, and a custom icon in the marker. */
export default function Content() {
    const s = reactive({ told: '' });
    const act = (what: string) => (
        <Stack orientation="horizontal" gap="sm">
            <Button text={what} variant="outline" size="sm" onclick={() => (s.told = `${what} pressed`)} />
        </Stack>
    );
    return (
        <Stack gap="sm" style="inline-size: 100%">
            <Timeline
                class="tl-orders"
                label="An order"
                items={[
                    { date: '2026-11-02T09:15:00', title: 'Order placed', description: 'Three items, paid by card.', tone: 'info', content: () => act('See the invoice') },
                    { date: '2026-11-03T14:40:00', title: 'Packed', tone: 'accent', glyph: 'columns' },
                    { date: '2026-11-04T08:00:00', title: 'On its way', description: 'Handed to the courier.', content: () => act('Track it') },
                    { date: '2026-11-05T16:25:00', title: 'Delivered', tone: 'success', glyph: 'check', content: () => act('Rate it') }
                ]}
                dateFormat={{ dateStyle: 'medium', timeStyle: 'short' }}
            />
            <output class="tl-orders-told">{() => s.told}</output>
        </Stack>
    );
}
```

## Keyboard

| Key | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `Tab` | In the vertical layout, each collapsible card is a Tab stop. In the horizontal layout, the selected date is one Tab stop, and the track buttons are also Tab stops. |
| `Arrow keys` | In the horizontal layout, Left and Right show the previous or next event (reversed on right-to-left pages), and Home and End show the first and last. |
| `Enter, Space` | On a collapsible card, expands or collapses it. On a date, shows it. |

## Accessibility

| Topic | Details |
| --- | --- |
| `Vertical layout` | A `list` named by `label`, with one item per event. A date is a `time` element with its ISO value, and a collapsible card is a button with `aria-expanded` that controls its description. |
| `Along the line` | The dates are tabs (`tablist`, `tab`, `aria-selected`), and the card below them is the `tabpanel` they control. The buttons at the ends are named “Earlier” and “Later”. |
| `Dots and glyphs` | Decorative. The tone is conveyed only by color, so put important information in the title. |

## Styling

| Hook | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `.mx-timeline` | The timeline. `data-orientation`, `data-alternate`. |
| `.mx-timeline__list, .mx-timeline__item` | The list (the line is its `::before`) and an event (`data-tone`, `data-side`, `data-expanded`, `data-selected`). |
| `.mx-timeline__dot, .mx-timeline__dot-glyph, .mx-timeline__dot-icon` | The marker and its content. |
| `.mx-timeline__card, .mx-timeline__flag, .mx-timeline__detail` | A card in the vertical layout, a date in the horizontal layout, and the card below the line. |
| `.mx-timeline__date, .mx-timeline__title, .mx-timeline__description, .mx-timeline__content` | The text and custom content. |
| `.mx-timeline__track, .mx-timeline__nav, .mx-timeline__nav-glyph` | The scrolling track, its buttons and their arrows. |

### Component tokens

| Token | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `timeline.line, .dot, .dot-glyph, .card, .flag, .date, .title, .description, .detail, .nav, .nav-glyph` | Units: the line, a marker and its glyph (by tone), a card (`pressable`, `hover`, `pressed`, `focus`, `expanded`), a date item (`hover`, `pressed`, `focus`, `selected`), the text, the detail card and the track buttons. |
| `timeline.gap, .dot-gap, .track-gap, .row-gap, .mark-size, .line-thickness` | The gap between events, between a marker and its card, between dates, and between the track and the detail card, plus the marker size and line thickness. |

## API reference

### Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `items` | `Bind<readonly TimelineItem[]>` | `[]` | The events in order: `date` (a `Date`, an ISO string or milliseconds), `title`, `description`, `glyph` or `icon`, `tone`, `content`, `key` and `data`. |
| `orientation` | `Bind<TimelineOrientation>` | `'vertical'` | `vertical` shows a card per event down the page. `horizontal` shows a line of dates with the selected event's card below it. |
| `alternate` | `Bind<boolean>` | `false` | In the vertical layout, places cards on alternating sides of the line. |
| `collapsible` | `Bind<boolean>` | `false` | In the vertical layout, shows a card's description only when clicked. |
| `dateFormat` | `Bind<TimelineDateFormat>` | `'medium'` | `short`, `medium`, `long` or `Intl.DateTimeFormat` options. Dates use the kit language. |
| `value` | `Bind<string \| number \| null>` | `0` | In the horizontal layout, the event whose card is shown, identified by its `key` or index. `x-model` provides two-way binding. |
| `label` | `Bind<string>` | The kit string “Timeline” | The accessible name. |

### Events, properties and methods

| Member | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `onItemClick` | event | Occurs when an event's card or date is clicked (`index`, `item`). |
| `onSelectionChanged` | event | In the horizontal layout, occurs when the selected event changes (`index`, `item`, `previous`, `byUser`). |
| `selectedIndex` | read-only | In the horizontal layout, the index of the selected event, or -1 if there is none. |
| `count` | read-only | The number of events. |
| `goTo(event)` | `boolean` | In the horizontal layout, shows an event by index or key. In the vertical layout, expands its card. |
| `unfold(event, on), isUnfolded(event)` | `void`, `boolean` | In the vertical layout with `collapsible`, expands or collapses a card, or reports whether it is expanded. |
| `formatDate(date)` | `string` | Formats a date the same way the timeline does. |
| `refresh()` | `void` | Re-reads the items after they have been changed in place. |

# Skeleton

> Display · @motifx-community/ui 0.1.0-beta.5

A placeholder that matches the shape of content that is loading, so the page keeps its layout while data arrives. If you provide content, it replaces the placeholder in the same place when loading ends.

## Import

```tsx
import { Skeleton } from '@motifx-community/ui';
```

## Shapes

```tsx
import { Skeleton, Stack } from '@motifx-community/ui';

/** Lines of text (the last of several is shorter), a block, and a circle. Lines and blocks take the width they are given. */
export default function Shapes() {
  return (
    <Stack gap="lg" style="inline-size: 24rem; max-inline-size: 100%">
      <Skeleton lines={3} />
      <Skeleton shape="rect" height={96} />
      <Stack orientation="horizontal" align="center">
        <Skeleton shape="circle" />
        <Skeleton shape="circle" width={24} />
      </Stack>
    </Stack>
  );
}
```

## Showing content after loading

`loading` accepts a value or a function. When it becomes `false`, the JSX children appear instead.

```tsx
import { reactive } from '@motifx/core';
import { Avatar, Button, Card, Skeleton, Stack } from '@motifx-community/ui';

/** While `loading`, the shape of the card shows; then the card itself, in the same place. */
export default function Loading() {
  const s = reactive({ loading: true });

  return (
    <Stack gap="lg" style="inline-size: 22rem; max-inline-size: 100%">
      <Button text={() => (s.loading ? 'Finish loading' : 'Load again')} variant="outline" onclick={() => (s.loading = !s.loading)} />
      <Card>
        <Stack orientation="horizontal" align="center">
          <Skeleton shape="circle" loading={() => s.loading}>
            <Avatar name="Grace Hopper" />
          </Skeleton>
          <Skeleton lines={2} loading={() => s.loading} grow>
            <strong>Grace Hopper</strong>
            <div>Wrote the first compiler.</div>
          </Skeleton>
        </Stack>
      </Card>
    </Stack>
  );
}
```

## Animation

```tsx
import { Skeleton, Stack, type SkeletonAnimation } from '@motifx-community/ui';

const ANIMATIONS: SkeletonAnimation[] = ['wave', 'pulse', 'none'];

/** Each way it moves; reduced motion keeps them all still. */
export default function Animations() {
  return (
    <Stack gap="lg" style="inline-size: 24rem; max-inline-size: 100%">
      {ANIMATIONS.map((animation) => (
        <Stack key={animation} gap="sm">
          <span>{animation}</span>
          <Skeleton lines={2} animation={animation} />
        </Stack>
      ))}
    </Stack>
  );
}
```

## Accessibility

| Topic | Details |
| --- | --- |
| `Loading` | A `progressbar` with `aria-busy` and a name (“Loading…” in the kit language). The shapes are hidden from screen readers. |
| `Loaded` | The role and busy state are removed, and the content is read normally. |
| `Motion` | With reduced motion, the wave and pulse stay still, because their duration follows the motion tokens. |

## Styling

| Hook | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `.mx-skeleton` | The skeleton. `data-shape`, `data-animation`, `data-loading`. |
| `.mx-skeleton__bone` | A shape (a line, a block or a circle). |
| `.mx-skeleton__content` | The content shown after loading. |

### Component tokens

| Token | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `skeleton.bone` | Unit: a shape in `text`, `rect` and `circle`. `color` is the color the wave and pulse blend in. |
| `skeleton.line-height, skeleton.line-gap, skeleton.last-line` | A line of text, the space between lines, and the width of the last line. |
| `skeleton.circle-size, skeleton.rect-height` | The default size of a circle or block. |
| `skeleton.animation, skeleton.duration, skeleton.easing, skeleton.wave-mix, skeleton.pulse-dim` | The default animation, its duration, easing and intensity. |

## API reference

### Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `shape` | `Bind<SkeletonShape>` | `'text'` | `text` for lines, `rect` for a block such as an image or field, or `circle` for an avatar. |
| `lines` | `Bind<number>` | `1` | The number of text lines. The last of several lines is shorter. |
| `width` | `Bind<string \| number \| null>` | The available space | A CSS length, or a number in pixels. Also sets the size of a circle (the default comes from the design language). |
| `height` | `Bind<string \| number \| null>` | One line, or set by the design language | A CSS length, or a number in pixels. |
| `animation` | `Bind<SkeletonAnimation>` | Set by the design language | `wave`, `pulse` or `none`. Tactile, Lounge and Fluent use a wave, and Material and Lilac use a pulse. |
| `loading` | `Bind<boolean>` | `true` | Shows the skeleton while `true`, and then the JSX children. |
| `label` | `Bind<string>` | The kit string “Loading…” | The text announced by screen readers while loading. |
| `visible` | see Control |  | Properties shared by all controls. |

### Properties

| Property | Access | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `every prop above` | read/write | Accepts a value or a function, the same as the prop. |
| `content` | read-only | The part that holds the loaded content, for adding to it programmatically. |

# AppBar

> Navigation · @motifx-community/ui 0.1.0-beta.5

The top bar of an application, with a navigation button, a logo, a title, a control and commands. The commands are a `Toolbar`, so those that do not fit move into a menu.

## Import

```tsx
import { AppBar } from '@motifx-community/ui';
```

## Title and commands

`navigation` adds a button at the start of the bar, and `onNavigationClick` reports it. `actions` takes the same items as `Toolbar.items`. Make the window narrower to see commands move into the menu.

```tsx
import { reactive } from '@motifx/core';
import { AppBar, Stack } from '@motifx-community/ui';

const icon = (name: string) => () => <span class="mx-glyph" data-icon={name} />;

/** A title, a menu button and commands. Commands that do not fit move into the "more" menu. */
export default function Basic() {
    const s = reactive({ told: 'nothing yet' });
    const actions = [
        { icon: icon('search'), hint: 'Search', click: () => (s.told = 'search') },
        { icon: icon('download'), hint: 'Download', click: () => (s.told = 'download') },
        { icon: icon('trash'), hint: 'Delete', click: () => (s.told = 'delete') }
    ];
    return (
        <Stack gap="md" style="inline-size: 100%">
            <AppBar class="ab-basic" position="static" title="Orders" subtitle="This week" navigation="menu" actions={actions} onNavigationClick={() => (s.told = 'the menu')} />
            <output class="ab-told">{() => `Pressed: ${s.told}`}</output>
        </Stack>
    );
}
```

## Title and tone

`titleAlign` centers the title, `tone` gives the bar the accent color, and `prominent` puts a larger title on a row of its own.

```tsx
import { AppBar, Stack } from '@motifx-community/ui';

const icon = (name: string) => () => <span class="mx-glyph" data-icon={name} />;

/** A centered title, the accent tone, and a prominent title on a row of its own. */
export default function Looks() {
    const actions = [{ icon: icon('search'), hint: 'Search' }];
    return (
        <Stack gap="md" style="inline-size: 100%">
            <AppBar class="ab-center" position="static" title="Invoice" navigation="back" titleAlign="center" actions={actions} />
            <AppBar class="ab-accent" position="static" title="Inbox" tone="accent" navigation="menu" actions={actions} />
            <AppBar class="ab-prominent" position="static" title="Reports" prominent navigation="back" actions={actions} />
        </Stack>
    );
}
```

## A control in the bar

JSX children lie between the title and the commands. This is the place for a search box.

```tsx
import { AppBar, TextBox } from '@motifx-community/ui';

/** A control between the title and the commands, written as a JSX child. */
export default function WithContent() {
    return (
        <AppBar class="ab-content" position="static" title="Customers" style="inline-size: 100%">
            <TextBox label="Search" labelMode="hidden" placeholder="Search customers" />
        </AppBar>
    );
}
```

## Scrolling

By default, the bar sticks to the top of what scrolls. `scrollBehavior` raises it over the content or moves it away while scrolling down. Scroll the box to compare them.

```tsx
import { reactive } from '@motifx/core';
import { AppBar, ButtonGroup, Stack } from '@motifx-community/ui';

const ROWS = Array.from({ length: 30 }, (_, i) => `Order ${i + 1}`);

/** The bar sticks to the top of the box that scrolls. `lift` raises it over the content, `hide` moves it away. */
export default function Scrolling() {
    const s = reactive({ behavior: 'lift' as 'none' | 'lift' | 'hide' });
    return (
        <Stack gap="md" style="inline-size: 100%">
            <ButtonGroup
                label="Scroll behavior"
                x-model={() => s.behavior}
                items={[
                    { value: 'none', text: 'None' },
                    { value: 'lift', text: 'Lift' },
                    { value: 'hide', text: 'Hide' }
                ]}
            />
            <div class="ab-scroll" tabindex="0" style="block-size: 260px; overflow: auto; border: 1px solid var(--mx-color-stroke-divider)">
                <AppBar class="ab-scrolling" title="Orders" navigation="menu" scrollBehavior={() => s.behavior} />
                {ROWS.map(row => (
                    <p key={row} style="margin: 0; padding: 12px 16px">
                        {row}
                    </p>
                ))}
            </div>
        </Stack>
    );
}
```

## Programmatic use

`new AppBar(props)` creates the bar without JSX. Each prop is also a property.

```tsx
import { Component } from '@motifx/core';
import { AppBar, Button, Stack } from '@motifx-community/ui';

/** A bar created programmatically. Each prop is also a property that can be set later. */
export default class Programmatic extends Component<HTMLDivElement> {
    constructor() {
        super('div');
        const bar = new AppBar({ title: 'Draft', position: 'static', navigation: 'back' });
        const rename = new Button({ text: 'Rename', variant: 'outline', onclick: () => (bar.title = 'Final') });
        const stack = new Stack({ gap: 'md' });
        stack.controls.add(bar, rename);
        this.controls.add(stack);
    }
}
```

## API reference

### Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `title, subtitle` | `Bind<string>` | `''` | The title, and a smaller line under it. |
| `titleAlign` | `Bind<'start' \| 'center'>` | `'start'` | A centered title stays in the middle of the bar whatever lies beside it. |
| `headingLevel` | `Bind<number \| null>` | `null` | Makes the title a heading of this level. |
| `logo` | `Bind<IconSource \| null>` | `null` | An image address, an element or a component before the title. |
| `navigation` | `Bind<'none' \| 'menu' \| 'back'>` | `'none'` | The button at the start of the bar. |
| `navigationGlyph` | `Bind<string>` | `'menu'`, `'arrow-start'` | The glyph of that button. The back arrow is mirrored in a right-to-left page. |
| `navigationLabel` | `Bind<string>` | A kit string | The accessible name of that button. |
| `actions` | `Bind<readonly ToolbarItem[]>` | `[]` | The commands at the end of the bar, the same items as `Toolbar.items`. |
| `actionsLabel` | `Bind<string>` | The kit string “Actions” | The accessible name of the commands. |
| `overflow` | `Bind<ToolbarOverflow>` | `'menu'` | How commands that do not fit are handled. |
| `content` | `Bind<ComponentBase \| null>` | `null` | A control between the title and the commands, the same as JSX children. |
| `tone` | `Bind<'surface' \| 'accent'>` | `'surface'` | The color of the bar. |
| `prominent` | `Bind<boolean>` | `false` | Puts a larger title on a row of its own under the buttons. |
| `position` | `Bind<'static' \| 'sticky' \| 'fixed'>` | `'sticky'` | How the bar stays on the page. |
| `scrollBehavior` | `Bind<'none' \| 'lift' \| 'hide'>` | `'none'` | `lift` raises the bar over the content that scrolls under it. `hide` also moves it away while scrolling down, and brings it back while scrolling up. |
| `scrollTarget` | `Bind<HTMLElement \| null>` | The nearest ancestor that scrolls | What `scrollBehavior` watches. Without a scrolling ancestor, it is the page. |

### Events

| Event | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `onNavigationClick` | `{ navigation, originalEvent, source }` | Occurs when the button at the start of the bar is pressed. |

### Accessibility

| Topic | Details |
| --- | --- |
| `Landmark` | The bar is a `<header>`, which is a banner landmark when it is not inside a sectioning element. |
| `Heading` | Use `headingLevel` when the title is the heading of the page. |
| `Commands` | The commands are a `Toolbar` with an accessible name: one Tab stop, with the arrow keys, Home and End inside it. |
| `Focus` | A bar moved away by `hide` comes back when focus enters it. |

### Styling hooks

| Hook | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `.mx-app-bar` | The bar. `data-tone`, `data-position`, `data-title-align`, `data-prominent`, `data-lifted` and `data-hidden` describe its state. |
| `.mx-app-bar__row, .mx-app-bar__start, .mx-app-bar__navigation, .mx-app-bar__logo` | The row, the start of the bar, the navigation button and the logo. |
| `.mx-app-bar__titles, .mx-app-bar__title, .mx-app-bar__subtitle` | The titles. |
| `.mx-app-bar__content, .mx-app-bar__actions` | The control and the commands. |

### Design tokens

| Token | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `app-bar.bar, .row, .start, .logo, .titles, .title, .subtitle, .content` | Units: the bar (`lifted`, `accent`), the row (`prominent`), the title (`prominent`, `accent`) and the subtitle (`accent`). |
| `app-bar.title-least` | The room the titles keep before commands move into the menu. |
| `app-bar.toolbar, .button` | Places: the commands, and a button of an accent bar. |
