# ActionSheet

> Navigation · @motifx-community/ui 0.1.0-beta.5

A list of commands that slides up from the bottom of the screen, built from the kit's menu items and sized for touch. It supports a title, a message and a separate Cancel button. A context menu uses it on touch screens.

## Import

```tsx
import { ActionSheet, type ActionSheetProps } from '@motifx-community/ui';
```

## Choosing programmatically

`choose()` opens the sheet and resolves with the selected item, or `null`. An item with `items` opens its submenu in place, with a Back option.

```tsx
import { reactive, type Component } from '@motifx/core';
import { ActionSheet, Button, type MenuItem } from '@motifx-community/ui';

const ITEMS: MenuItem[] = [
  { text: '&Share…' },
  { text: '&Rename…' },
  {
    text: '&Move to',
    items: [{ text: 'Reports' }, { text: 'Archive' }, { text: 'Shared with me' }],
  },
  { text: '&Delete', tone: 'danger', beginGroup: true },
];

/** choose() opens the sheet and resolves with the item chosen, or null; a submenu opens in place, with a way back. */
export default function Choose() {
  const s = reactive({ said: 'Nothing chosen yet.' });
  let host!: Component<HTMLDivElement>;

  const ask = async () => {
    const sheet = new ActionSheet({ title: 'report.pdf', message: 'Changed today at 09:41' });
    const item = await sheet.choose(ITEMS, host);
    s.said = item ? `Chosen: ${String(item.text).replace('&', '')}` : 'Closed without a choice.';
  };

  return (
    <div ref={(c: Component<HTMLDivElement>) => (host = c)} style="display: contents">
      <Button text="Actions…" variant="outline" onclick={ask} />
      <output>{() => s.said}</output>
    </div>
  );
}
```

## Using it in JSX

Bind it with `x-model`. Check and radio items show their marks, and `cancelText` sets the Cancel button text.

```tsx
import { reactive } from '@motifx/core';
import { ActionSheet, Button, type MenuItem } from '@motifx-community/ui';

/** An action sheet in JSX, bound with x-model, with checked items and its own cancel text; onItemClick reports the choice. */
export default function InJsx() {
  const s = reactive({ open: false, sort: 'date', said: '' });

  const sortItem = (value: string, text: string): MenuItem => ({
    text,
    group: 'sort',
    checked: () => s.sort === value,
    click: () => (s.sort = value),
  });

  return (
    <>
      <Button text={() => `Sort by: ${s.sort}`} variant="outline" onclick={() => (s.open = true)} />
      <output>{() => s.said}</output>
      <ActionSheet
        title="Sort by"
        cancelText="Keep as it is"
        items={[sortItem('date', 'Date'), sortItem('name', 'Name'), sortItem('size', 'Size')]}
        x-model={() => s.open}
        onItemClick={(e) => (s.said = `Sorted by ${String(e.item.text).toLowerCase()}.`)}
      />
    </>
  );
}
```

## Context menus on touch screens

`ContextMenu` has a `presentation` prop: `'menu'` (the default), `'sheet'`, or `'auto'`, which opens an action sheet when a finger opened the menu with a long press. The items, `onOpening` and `onItemClick` stay the same.

```tsx
import { reactive, type Component } from '@motifx/core';
import { ContextMenu, RadioGroup, Stack, type ContextMenuPresentation, type MenuItem } from '@motifx-community/ui';

const ROWS = ['Invoice 1042', 'Invoice 1043', 'Invoice 1044'];

/** One ContextMenu, shown as a menu, as an action sheet, or (auto) as a sheet when opened by touch: long press a row on a phone. */
export default function FromContextMenu() {
  const s = reactive({ presentation: 'auto' as ContextMenuPresentation, said: '' });
  let list!: Component<HTMLUListElement>;

  const items = (row: string): MenuItem[] => [
    { text: `&Open ${row}`, click: () => (s.said = `Opened ${row}`) },
    { text: '&Copy number', click: () => (s.said = `Copied ${row}`) },
    { text: '&Delete', tone: 'danger', click: () => (s.said = `Deleted ${row}`) },
  ];

  return (
    <Stack gap="sm">
      <RadioGroup
        label="Presentation"
        orientation="horizontal"
        items={[
          { value: 'menu', text: 'Menu' },
          { value: 'sheet', text: 'Sheet' },
          { value: 'auto', text: 'Auto' },
        ]}
        itemText="text"
        itemValue="value"
        x-model={() => s.presentation}
      />
      <ul ref={(c: Component<HTMLUListElement>) => (list = c)} aria-label="Invoices" style="margin: 0; padding: 0; list-style: none">
        {ROWS.map((row) => (
          <li key={row} tabindex="0" data-row={row} style="padding: var(--mx-space-3); border-block-end: var(--mx-border-width-1) solid var(--mx-color-stroke-divider); user-select: none">
            {row}
          </li>
        ))}
      </ul>
      <output>{() => s.said || 'Right-click or long press a row; the Menu key on a focused row.'}</output>
      <ContextMenu
        label="Invoice"
        target={() => list}
        presentation={() => s.presentation}
        onOpening={(e) => {
          const row = (e.target as Element).closest('[data-row]')?.getAttribute('data-row');
          if (row) e.items = items(row);
          else e.cancel = true;
        }}
      />
    </Stack>
  );
}
```

## Keyboard

| Key | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `Up, Down, Home, End` | Moves between the items, wrapping at the ends. |
| `Enter, Space, an item's `&` letter` | Selects the item, or opens a submenu in place. |
| `A letter` | Moves to the next item that starts with that letter. |
| `Escape` | Closes the sheet without a selection. |
| `Tab` | Moves to the Cancel button and back. |

## Accessibility

| Topic | Details |
| --- | --- |
| `Dialog and menu` | The sheet is a `dialog` named by its title. The items are a `menu` of `menuitem`, `menuitemcheckbox` and `menuitemradio` elements, as in the kit's menus. |
| `Focus` | When opened from the keyboard, focus moves to the first item. When opened by touch or pointer, it moves to the list. Focus returns to where it was when the sheet closes. |
| `Submenus` | Submenus replace the menu in place, with "Back" as the first item. An arrow at the end of an item indicates a submenu. |
| `Touch` | Items are `control.height.lg` tall (`actionsheet.item-height`), which exceeds the 24 pixels required by WCAG 2.2. |

## Localization

Cancel, Back and the default name come from `uiLocale.strings` (`cancel`, `back`, `actionSheetLabel`). `cancelText` sets custom text.

## Styling

| Hook | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `.mx-action-sheet` | Built on the bottom sheet layer (`.mx-bottom-sheet`) and its hooks. |
| `.mx-action-sheet__message` | Text below the title. |
| `.mx-action-sheet__list` | The menu (`.mx-menu`). |
| `.mx-action-sheet__cancel` | The Cancel button row. |
| `.mx-action-sheet__back` | The Back indicator. |

### Component tokens

| Token | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `actionsheet.message, actionsheet.back, actionsheet.cancel` | Units: the message, the Back item indicator (`rtl`), and the strip that holds the Cancel button. |
| `actionsheet.menu.*, actionsheet.cancel-button.*, actionsheet.sheet.*` | Places: touch-sized items, the Cancel button and the sheet content padding. |
| `sheet.*` | The surface, handle and title, as on the bottom sheet. |

## API reference

### Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `items` | `Bind<readonly MenuItem[]>` | `[]` | The commands: kit menu items with icons, check and radio marks, tones, `&` keys, groups and submenus. Shortcuts are not shown. |
| `title` | `Bind<string>` | `''` | A title above the items, which also names the sheet. Otherwise, the name comes from `label`, or is "Actions". |
| `message` | `Bind<string>` | `''` | A line below the title that explains the choice. |
| `showCancel` | `Bind<boolean>` | `true` | Shows a separate Cancel button at the bottom. |
| `cancelText` | `Bind<string>` | `''` | Its text. An empty value uses the `uiLocale` Cancel string. |
| `detents` | `Bind<readonly BottomSheetDetent[]>` | `['fit']` | The height of its items, up to full. Any bottom sheet height works. |
| `onItemClick` | `(e: MenuItemClickEventArgs) => void` | — | Occurs when an item is selected, after the sheet closes and the item's own `click` runs. |
| `every BottomSheet prop` | see BottomSheet |  | Modal behavior, the handle, swipe down, Escape, the scrim and the back button work as on the [BottomSheet page](bottomsheet.md#api). |

### Members

| Member | Returns | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `choose(items?, host?)` | `Promise<MenuItem \| null>` | Opens the sheet with these items and resolves with the selected item, or `null` if it closes without a selection. `host` gives it a place if it has none. |
| `open(byKeyboard?)` | `boolean` | Opens the sheet. `byKeyboard` moves focus to the first item. Otherwise, focus moves to the list, as with a menu opened by the pointer. |
| `chosenItem` | read-only | The item selected the last time the sheet was open. |
| `menu` | read-only | Its `MenuList`. |
| `refresh()` | `void` | Your items can be plain or reactive, and the sheet reads them as they are. After changing them in place, call `refresh()`. The visible level updates. |
| `ContextMenu presentation` | `Bind<'menu' \| 'sheet' \| 'auto'>` | On `ContextMenu`, the default is `'menu'`. `'sheet'` opens its items in an action sheet. `'auto'` does so when a finger opened the menu with a long press, or on a screen with only a coarse pointer unless a key opened it. `onOpening`, `onItemClick` and `onClosed` work the same way, and `actionSheet` is the sheet. |

# Layout

> Navigation · @motifx-community/ui 0.1.0-beta.5

Container controls for arranging other controls: `Stack` (a row or column), `Grid` (rows and columns), `Panel` (a plain box that can scroll), `GroupBox` (a titled frame), `DockPanel` (children docked to its edges) and `SplitContainer` (two panes with a splitter). All of them are controls, so they can disable and hide their content, and they lay out children added at any time.

## Import

```tsx
import { Stack, Grid, Panel, GroupBox, DockPanel, SplitContainer, type LayoutSpace } from '@motifx-community/ui';
```

## Declarative and programmatic

Children can be declared in JSX or added later with `controls.add`, and the container handles both. A child sets its own layout options through its props (`grow`, `row`, `dock`…), whatever type of component it is.

```tsx
import type { Component } from '@motifx/core';
import { Button, Grid, Stack, TextBox } from '@motifx-community/ui';

/** Buttons added to a Stack with `controls.add`, and a Grid built with `new`. */
export default function Programmatic() {
  let added = 0;
  let bar: Stack | null = null;

  const addButton = () => bar?.controls.add(new Button({ text: `Button ${++added}`, variant: 'outline', grow: added % 3 === 0 }));

  const buildProgrammatic = (host: Component<HTMLDivElement>) => {
    const grid = new Grid({ columns: '* *', gap: 'xs' });
    grid.element.classList.add('layout-coded');
    grid.controls.add(
      new TextBox({ label: 'From', stretch: true }),
      new TextBox({ label: 'To', stretch: true }),
      new TextBox({ label: 'Subject', stretch: true, columnSpan: 2 }),
    );
    host.controls.add(grid);
  };

  return (
    <>
      <Stack ref={(c: Stack) => (bar = c)} orientation="horizontal" gap="sm" wrap align="center" style="inline-size: 100%">
        <Button text="Add a button" tone="accent" onclick={addButton} />
      </Stack>
      <div style="inline-size: 100%" ref={(c: Component<HTMLDivElement>) => buildProgrammatic(c)} />
    </>
  );
}
```

## Stack

A row or column with a gap. `align` positions children across the direction, and `justify` positions them along it. `wrap` starts a new line when they do not fit, and a child with `grow` takes the free space.

```tsx
import { reactive } from '@motifx/core';
import { Button, Panel, Stack, TextBox, type LayoutAlign, type StackJustify } from '@motifx-community/ui';

const ALIGNS: LayoutAlign[] = ['start', 'center', 'end', 'stretch', 'baseline'];
const JUSTIFIES: StackJustify[] = ['start', 'center', 'end', 'space-between', 'space-evenly'];
const FRAME = 'border: var(--mx-border-width-1) solid var(--mx-color-stroke-card); border-radius: var(--mx-radius-lg);';

/** A Stack's orientation, align, justify, wrap and reverse, and a child that grows. */
export default function StackOptions() {
  const s = reactive({
    orientation: 'horizontal' as 'horizontal' | 'vertical',
    align: 'center' as LayoutAlign,
    justify: 'start' as StackJustify,
    wrap: false,
    reverse: false,
  });
  return (
    <>
      <Stack orientation="horizontal" wrap align="center" role="group" aria-label="Orientation">
        {(['horizontal', 'vertical'] as const).map((o) => (
          <Button key={o} text={o} size="sm" variant={() => (s.orientation === o ? 'solid' : 'ghost')} aria-pressed={() => s.orientation === o} onclick={() => (s.orientation = o)} />
        ))}
      </Stack>
      <Stack orientation="horizontal" wrap align="center" role="group" aria-label="Align">
        {ALIGNS.map((a) => (
          <Button key={a} text={a} size="sm" variant={() => (s.align === a ? 'solid' : 'ghost')} aria-pressed={() => s.align === a} onclick={() => (s.align = a)} />
        ))}
      </Stack>
      <Stack orientation="horizontal" wrap align="center" role="group" aria-label="Justify">
        {JUSTIFIES.map((j) => (
          <Button key={j} text={j} size="sm" variant={() => (s.justify === j ? 'solid' : 'ghost')} aria-pressed={() => s.justify === j} onclick={() => (s.justify = j)} />
        ))}
      </Stack>
      <Stack orientation="horizontal" wrap align="center">
        <Button text="wrap" size="sm" toggle x-model={() => s.wrap} variant="outline" />
        <Button text="reverse" size="sm" toggle x-model={() => s.reverse} variant="outline" />
      </Stack>
      <Stack
        class="layout-stack-demo"
        orientation={() => s.orientation}
        align={() => s.align}
        justify={() => s.justify}
        wrap={() => s.wrap}
        reverse={() => s.reverse}
        gap="sm"
        padding="sm"
        style={`inline-size: 100%; min-block-size: 10rem; ${FRAME}`}
      >
        <Panel variant="card" padding="sm">One</Panel>
        <Panel variant="card" padding="md">Two, taller</Panel>
        <Panel variant="card" padding="sm">Three</Panel>
        <TextBox label="Grows" labelMode="hidden" placeholder="I grow" grow />
      </Stack>
    </>
  );
}
```

## Spacing

`gap` and `padding` accept a step from the spacing scale, a number of pixels, or any CSS length.

| Value | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `'xxs' … 'xxl'` | A step from the spacing scale: `xxs`, `xs`, `sm`, `md`, `lg`, `xl` or `xxl`, from the `layout.space.*` tokens (the design system `space.1` … `space.12`). Density and themes apply to them. |
| `12` | A number is in pixels. |
| `'1.5rem'` | Any CSS length. |
| `'xs md'` | Padding accepts one to four values, as in CSS (block-start, inline-end, block-end, inline-start), and can mix steps and lengths. The values follow the reading direction. |

```tsx
import { reactive } from '@motifx/core';
import { Button, Grid, Panel, Stack } from '@motifx-community/ui';

const STEPS = ['xxs', 'xs', 'sm', 'md', 'lg', 'xl', 'xxl'] as const;
const FRAME = 'border: var(--mx-border-width-1) solid var(--mx-color-stroke-card); border-radius: var(--mx-radius-lg);';

/** A gap from the spacing steps, a gap in pixels with a two-value padding, and a gap as a CSS length. */
export default function Spacing() {
  const s = reactive({ gap: 'sm' as string });
  return (
    <>
      <Stack orientation="horizontal" wrap align="center" role="group" aria-label="Gap">
        {STEPS.map((step) => (
          <Button key={step} text={step} size="sm" variant={() => (s.gap === step ? 'solid' : 'ghost')} aria-pressed={() => s.gap === step} onclick={() => (s.gap = step)} />
        ))}
      </Stack>
      <Stack class="layout-gap-demo" orientation="horizontal" gap={() => s.gap} padding="xs">
        <Panel variant="card" padding="sm">A</Panel>
        <Panel variant="card" padding="sm">B</Panel>
        <Panel variant="card" padding="sm">C</Panel>
      </Stack>
      <Stack orientation="horizontal" gap={12} padding="xs md" style={FRAME}>
        <Panel variant="card" padding="sm">12 pixels apart</Panel>
        <Panel variant="card" padding="sm">padding xs md</Panel>
      </Stack>
      <Grid columns="* *" gap="1.5rem" style="inline-size: 100%">
        <Panel variant="card" padding="sm">1.5rem apart</Panel>
        <Panel variant="card" padding="sm">in a Grid</Panel>
      </Grid>
    </>
  );
}
```

## Grid

Rows and columns defined in a CSS-like syntax. Children fill the cells in order, or set their position with `row`, `column`, `rowSpan` and `columnSpan`, counted from 1.

| Tracks | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `'auto 1fr 2fr 120'` | CSS grid tracks. A bare number is in pixels. |
| `'* 2*'` | `*` means `1fr`, and `2*` means `2fr`. |
| `'minmax(8rem, 1fr) auto'` | Any CSS track, including functions. |
| `['auto', 120, '*']` | The same tracks as a list. |
| `3` | A number creates that many equal columns or rows. |

```tsx
import { reactive } from '@motifx/core';
import { Button, Grid, Stack, TextBox } from '@motifx-community/ui';

/** A form on a Grid whose column count follows state; Street and the buttons span columns. */
export default function GridForm() {
  const s = reactive({ columns: 2 });
  return (
    <>
      <Stack orientation="horizontal" wrap align="center" role="group" aria-label="Columns">
        {[1, 2, 3].map((n) => (
          <Button key={n} text={`${n} column${n > 1 ? 's' : ''}`} size="sm" variant={() => (s.columns === n ? 'solid' : 'ghost')} aria-pressed={() => s.columns === n} onclick={() => (s.columns = n)} />
        ))}
      </Stack>
      <Grid class="layout-form" columns={() => s.columns} gap="sm" align="end" style="inline-size: 100%">
        <TextBox label="First name" stretch />
        <TextBox label="Last name" stretch />
        <TextBox label="Street" stretch column={1} columnSpan={() => Math.min(2, s.columns)} />
        <TextBox label="City" stretch />
        <TextBox label="Postal code" stretch />
        <Stack orientation="horizontal" justify="end" gap="xs" column="1" columnSpan={() => s.columns}>
          <Button text="Cancel" variant="ghost" />
          <Button text="Save" tone="accent" />
        </Stack>
      </Grid>
    </>
  );
}
```

```tsx
import { Grid, Panel } from '@motifx-community/ui';

/** A fixed column and two flexible ones, a fixed row, and a child placed by row and column. */
export default function GridTracks() {
  return (
    <Grid class="layout-tracks" columns="120 * 2*" rows="auto 4rem" gap="xs" style="inline-size: 100%">
      <Panel variant="card" padding="xs">120px</Panel>
      <Panel variant="card" padding="xs">1fr</Panel>
      <Panel variant="card" padding="xs">2fr</Panel>
      <Panel variant="card" padding="xs" column={2} columnSpan={2}>
        row 2, columns 2–3
      </Panel>
    </Grid>
  );
}
```

## Panel

A plain box with padding, an optional frame and its own scrolling. A scrolling panel is a Tab stop, so it can be scrolled with the keyboard, and `text` provides its name.

```tsx
import { Panel } from '@motifx-community/ui';

/** A named panel that scrolls, a card and an outline. */
export default function Panels() {
  return (
    <>
      <Panel class="layout-scroll" text="Terms" scrollable="vertical" padding="md" variant="outline" style="block-size: 8rem; inline-size: 18rem">
        <p>1. The service is offered as it is.</p>
        <p>2. You keep the rights to what you upload.</p>
        <p>3. We may change these terms with a notice of 30 days.</p>
        <p>4. Either side may end the agreement at any time.</p>
        <p>5. The law of the place you live in applies.</p>
      </Panel>
      <Panel variant="card" padding="md">
        A card
      </Panel>
      <Panel variant="outline" padding="md">
        An outline
      </Panel>
    </>
  );
}
```

## GroupBox

A titled frame around related controls. It is a `<fieldset>`, so screen readers announce the group by its title and disabling it disables its content. The `&` key in the title moves focus to the first control, and `collapsible` lets the title show and hide the content.

```tsx
import { reactive } from '@motifx/core';
import { Button, Grid, GroupBox, TextBox } from '@motifx-community/ui';

/** A group with an access key that is enabled from state, and one that opens and closes. */
export default function GroupBoxes() {
  const s = reactive({ editing: true });
  return (
    <>
      <Button text="Enabled" size="sm" variant="outline" toggle x-model={() => s.editing} />
      <Grid columns="* *" gap="md" style="inline-size: 100%" align="start">
        <GroupBox title="&Address" enabled={() => s.editing}>
          <TextBox label="Street" stretch />
          <TextBox label="City" stretch />
        </GroupBox>
        <GroupBox title="More &options" collapsible collapsed>
          <TextBox label="Coupon" stretch />
          <TextBox label="Gift note" stretch />
        </GroupBox>
      </Grid>
    </>
  );
}
```

## DockPanel

Children dock to the edges in the order they appear: `top`, `bottom`, `start` and `end` (the last two follow the reading direction), and `fill` takes the remaining space. A `float` child sits over the others at its own `left`, `top`, `right` and `bottom`. The layout uses CSS grid, so no code runs when the size changes.

```tsx
import { reactive } from '@motifx/core';
import { Button, DockPanel, Panel, Stack, TextBox, type Dock } from '@motifx-community/ui';

const FOLDERS = ['Inbox', 'Drafts', 'Sent', 'Archive', 'Spam', 'Trash'];
const FRAME = 'border: var(--mx-border-width-1) solid var(--mx-color-stroke-card); border-radius: var(--mx-radius-lg);';
const BAR = 'background: var(--mx-color-bg-bar);';
const LAYER = 'background: var(--mx-color-bg-layer);';

/** A mail app laid out with DockPanel: a header, a sidebar that changes sides, a status bar, a float button and a panel added programmatically. */
export default function AppShell() {
  const s = reactive({ side: 'start' as Dock, messages: 3 });
  let shell: DockPanel | null = null;
  let notes: Panel | null = null;

  const toggleNotes = () => {
    if (notes) {
      shell?.controls.remove(notes);
      notes = null;
      return;
    }
    notes = new Panel({ dock: 'end', padding: 'sm' });
    notes.element.setAttribute('style', `inline-size: 9rem; ${LAYER}`);
    notes.element.classList.add('layout-notes');
    notes.controls.add(<span>Notes, added programmatically.</span>);
    shell?.controls.add(notes);
  };

  return (
    <>
      <Stack orientation="horizontal" wrap align="center">
        <Button text={() => `Sidebar: ${s.side}`} size="sm" variant="outline" onclick={() => (s.side = s.side === 'start' ? 'end' : 'start')} />
        <Button text="Notes panel programmatically" size="sm" variant="outline" onclick={toggleNotes} />
      </Stack>
      <DockPanel class="layout-shell" ref={(c: DockPanel) => (shell = c)} style={`block-size: 22rem; inline-size: 100%; overflow: hidden; ${FRAME}`}>
        <Stack dock="top" orientation="horizontal" align="center" gap="sm" padding="xs sm" style={BAR}>
          <strong>Mail</strong>
          <TextBox label="Search mail" labelMode="hidden" placeholder="Search" grow />
          <Button text="New" tone="accent" onclick={() => s.messages++} />
        </Stack>
        <Panel class="layout-side" dock={() => s.side} scrollable="vertical" padding="xs" text="Mailboxes" style={`inline-size: 11rem; ${LAYER}`}>
          <Stack gap="xxs">
            {FOLDERS.map((f) => (
              <Button key={f} text={f} variant="ghost" stretch />
            ))}
          </Stack>
        </Panel>
        <Stack class="layout-status" dock="bottom" orientation="horizontal" justify="space-between" padding="xxs sm" style={BAR}>
          <span>Ready</span>
          <span>{() => `${s.messages} messages`}</span>
        </Stack>
        <Panel class="layout-content" text="Message" scrollable padding="md">
          <h3 style="margin-block-start: 0">Welcome</h3>
          <p>The header, the folders and the status bar are docked; this panel fills the rest and scrolls on its own.</p>
          <p>Switch the sidebar to the other side, or add a panel programmatically: the layout follows at once.</p>
        </Panel>
        <Button class="layout-help" dock="float" right={16} bottom={48} text="Help" variant="outline" />
      </DockPanel>
    </>
  );
}
```

## SplitContainer

Two panes, `first` and `second`, separated by a splitter that can be dragged or moved with the keyboard. `fixedPanel` preserves the size of one pane when the container is resized, and the minimum sizes are enforced. Enter collapses the first pane and restores it. Split containers can be nested.

```tsx
import { reactive } from '@motifx/core';
import { Button, Panel, SplitContainer, Stack, type SplitPanel, type SplitPosition } from '@motifx-community/ui';

const FOLDERS = ['Inbox', 'Drafts', 'Sent', 'Archive', 'Spam', 'Trash'];
const FRAME = 'border: var(--mx-border-width-1) solid var(--mx-color-stroke-card); border-radius: var(--mx-radius-lg);';
const LAYER = 'background: var(--mx-color-bg-layer);';

/** A split container inside another: a position bound with x-model, minimum sizes, a fixed pane, and hiding a pane programmatically. */
export default function NestedSplit() {
  const s = reactive({ tree: 180 as SplitPosition, fixed: 'first' as SplitPanel, log: '' });
  let outer: SplitContainer | null = null;

  return (
    <>
      <Stack orientation="horizontal" wrap align="center">
        <Button text="Hide folders" size="sm" variant="outline" onclick={() => outer?.collapse('first')} />
        <Button text="Restore" size="sm" variant="outline" onclick={() => outer?.restore()} />
        <Button text={() => `fixedPanel: ${s.fixed}`} size="sm" variant="outline" onclick={() => (s.fixed = s.fixed === 'first' ? 'none' : 'first')} />
        <output class="layout-split-out">{() => `position: ${s.tree}`}</output>
        <output class="layout-split-log">{() => s.log}</output>
      </Stack>
      <SplitContainer
        class="layout-split"
        ref={(c: SplitContainer) => (outer = c)}
        position={180}
        fixedPanel={() => s.fixed}
        firstMinSize={120}
        secondMinSize={200}
        x-model={() => s.tree}
        onSplitterMoved={(e: { position: SplitPosition; byUser: boolean; collapsed: SplitPanel }) => (s.log = `moved${e.byUser ? ' by you' : ''}${e.collapsed !== 'none' ? `, ${e.collapsed} hidden` : ''}`)}
        style={`block-size: 20rem; inline-size: 100%; ${FRAME}`}
      >
        <Panel text="Folders" scrollable padding="sm" style={LAYER}>
          <Stack gap="xxs">
            {FOLDERS.map((f) => (
              <Button key={f} text={f} variant="ghost" stretch />
            ))}
          </Stack>
        </Panel>
        <SplitContainer orientation="vertical" position="65%" secondMinSize={48}>
          <Panel text="Editor" scrollable padding="sm">
            <p>Drag the splitters, or Tab to one and use the arrow keys, Home, End and Enter.</p>
          </Panel>
          <Panel text="Output" scrollable padding="sm" style={LAYER}>
            <code>Build finished in 1.2 s.</code>
          </Panel>
        </SplitContainer>
      </SplitContainer>
    </>
  );
}
```

## Keyboard

| Key | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `Tab` | The splitter is one Tab stop between the panes, and a scrolling `Panel` is its own Tab stop. |
| `Left / Right (side by side), Up / Down (one over the other)` | Moves the splitter by `step`. Left and Right follow the visual direction on right-to-left pages. |
| `Home / End` | Sets the first pane to its smallest or largest size. |
| `Enter` | Collapses the first pane, or restores the splitter to its previous position. |
| `Alt + key (`&Address`)` | Moves focus to the first control in a `GroupBox` (Control + Option + key on Apple platforms). |
| `Arrows, Page Up / Down` | Scrolls a focused scrolling `Panel`, using the browser's default behavior. |

## Accessibility

| Topic | Details |
| --- | --- |
| `Splitter` | `role="separator"`, focusable, with `aria-valuenow` (the share of the first pane, 0 to 100), `aria-valuemin`, `aria-valuemax`, `aria-orientation` and `aria-controls` for the first pane. It is named by `splitterLabel` or `uiLocale`, following the ARIA window splitter pattern. |
| `Hidden pane` | `inert`, so it is out of reach of Tab and screen readers. Focus inside moves to the splitter. |
| `GroupBox` | A native `<fieldset>` named by its `<legend>`. When disabled, it disables the native controls inside. A collapsible group box has a button with `aria-expanded`. |
| `Panel` | With `text`, a region landmark with that name. When scrolling, it is a Tab stop. |
| `Order` | Stack, Grid and DockPanel position children with CSS only. Tab and screen readers follow document order, so write children in reading order. |

## Localization

The only string these containers display is the splitter name, `uiLocale.strings.resize`, unless `splitterLabel` is set.

```tsx
import { reactive } from '@motifx/core';
import { Button, uiLocale } from '@motifx-community/ui';
import { kitTexts } from '../../../shared/kit-texts';

/** Switches the texts of the kit; the splitters on the page take the new name at once. */
export default function Localization() {
  const s = reactive({ lang: 'en' });
  const toggle = () => {
    s.lang = s.lang === 'en' ? 'tr' : 'en';
    void uiLocale.use(s.lang);
  };
  return (
    <>
      <Button text={() => (s.lang === 'en' ? 'Language: English' : 'Dil: Türkçe')} variant="outline" onclick={toggle} />
      <span>
        The splitter is named <output class="layout-resize">{() => kitTexts.strings.resize}</output>
      </span>
    </>
  );
}
```

## Styling

| Hook | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `.mx-stack` | `data-orientation`, `data-align`, `data-justify`, `data-wrap`, `data-reverse`, `data-inline`. A growing child gets `data-mx-grow`. |
| `.mx-grid` | `data-align`, `data-justify`, `data-inline`. Tracks and child positions are inline grid properties. |
| `.mx-panel` | `data-variant`, `data-scroll`. |
| `.mx-group-box` | `data-variant`, `data-collapsible`, `data-collapsed`, `data-disabled`; `.mx-group-box__legend`, `__title`, `__toggle`, `__chevron`. |
| `.mx-dock-panel` | Each child gets `data-mx-dock`. Its position and the `gap`, a margin on the side facing the remaining area, are set inline. |
| `.mx-split-container` | `data-orientation`, `data-collapsed`, `data-resizable`, `data-dragging`; `.mx-split-container__pane` (`data-pane`), `__splitter`. |
| `--_gap, --_row-gap, --_column-gap` | Set inline from `gap`, `rowGap` and `columnGap` (Stack, Grid, GroupBox). |

### Component tokens

| Token | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `layout.space.xxs … xxl` | The spacing steps of `gap` and `padding`. |
| `layout.gap` | The default gap of Stack and Grid. |
| `layout.panel` | Unit: a panel (`outline` for a frame, `card` for a raised surface). |
| `layout.group, layout.group-caption, layout.group-toggle, layout.group-chevron` | Units: a group box (`plain`, `collapsed`), its label, the collapse button and its chevron. |
| `layout.group-box.gap, layout.group-box.legend-float` | The default gap inside a group box, and the position of its label. |
| `layout.splitter-handle, layout.splitter-line, layout.splitter-grip` | Units: the splitter (`focus`), its line and its grip (`active`, `disabled`). |
| `layout.splitter.*` | `size` (the pointer target area), `line-width`, `active-width`, `grip-length`, `grip-thickness`. |

## API reference

Every container also has the properties shared by `Control`: `enabled` and `disabled` (which apply to everything inside), `visible`, `tabStop` and `tabIndex`.

### Stack props

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `orientation` | `Bind<'horizontal' \| 'vertical'>` | `'vertical'` | `horizontal` follows the reading direction. |
| `gap` | `Bind<LayoutSpace>` | `layout.gap` | The space between children. |
| `padding` | `Bind<LayoutSpace>` | — | The space inside the edges. |
| `align` | `Bind<LayoutAlign>` | `'stretch'` | Alignment across the direction: `start`, `center`, `end`, `stretch` or `baseline`. |
| `justify` | `Bind<StackJustify>` | `'start'` | Alignment along the direction: `start`, `center`, `end`, `space-between`, `space-around` or `space-evenly`. |
| `wrap` | `Bind<boolean>` | `false` | Moves children that do not fit to a new line. |
| `reverse` | `Bind<boolean>` | `false` | Lays out children from the opposite end. The Tab order stays in document order. |
| `inline` | `Bind<boolean>` | `false` | Flows within a line of text, as wide as its children. |

### Grid props

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `columns, rows` | `Bind<GridTracks>` | One column | See Tracks. |
| `gap` | `Bind<LayoutSpace>` | `layout.gap` | The gap between rows and columns. |
| `rowGap, columnGap` | `Bind<LayoutSpace>` | `gap` | The gap in one direction only. |
| `padding` | `Bind<LayoutSpace>` | — | The space inside the edges. |
| `autoRows, autoColumns` | `Bind<number \| string>` | `'auto'` | The size of implicit tracks. A number is in pixels. |
| `flow` | `Bind<GridFlow>` | `'row'` | How children without a position fill the grid: `row`, `column`, `row dense` or `column dense`. |
| `align` | `Bind<LayoutAlign>` | `'stretch'` | The vertical alignment of children in their cells. |
| `justify` | `Bind<GridJustify>` | `'stretch'` | The horizontal alignment of children in their cells. |
| `inline` | `Bind<boolean>` | `false` | Flows within a line of text. |

### Panel props

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `scrollable` | `Bind<boolean \| 'vertical' \| 'horizontal' \| 'both'>` | `false` | Scrolls its content. It then becomes a Tab stop, so the keyboard can scroll it. |
| `padding` | `Bind<LayoutSpace>` | — | The space inside the edges. |
| `variant` | `Bind<PanelVariant>` | `'plain'` | `plain`, `outline` (a border) or `card` (a card surface). |
| `text` | `Bind<string>` | `''` | Names the panel, which makes it a region landmark with that name. |

### GroupBox props

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `title` | `Bind<string>` | `''` | The legend. `&Address` makes Alt+A move focus to the first control inside. This is the same property as `text`. |
| `collapsible` | `Bind<boolean>` | `false` | Makes the title a button that shows and hides the content. |
| `collapsed` | `Bind<boolean>` | `false` | Hides the content (with `collapsible`). |
| `padding` | `Bind<LayoutSpace>` | `layout.group-box.padding` | The space inside the frame. |
| `gap` | `Bind<LayoutSpace>` | `layout.group-box.gap` | The space between children, which stack in a column. |
| `variant` | `Bind<GroupBoxVariant>` | `'outline'` | `outline` (a frame with the title on its edge) or `plain` (the title above the content). |

### DockPanel props

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `gap` | `Bind<LayoutSpace>` | — | The space between a docked child and the remaining area. |
| `padding` | `Bind<LayoutSpace>` | — | The space inside the edges. |

### SplitContainer props

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `orientation` | `Bind<'horizontal' \| 'vertical'>` | `'horizontal'` | `horizontal` places the panes side by side, as in Stack, and `vertical` stacks them. |
| `position` | `Bind<SplitPosition>` | `'50%'` | The size of the pane that keeps its size (the first pane with `fixedPanel="none"`), in pixels, as a share, or as a CSS length. `x-model` binds it. |
| `fixedPanel` | `Bind<'none' \| 'first' \| 'second'>` | `'none'` | The pane that keeps its size when the container is resized. With `none`, both grow and the position is kept as a share. |
| `firstMinSize, secondMinSize` | `Bind<number>` | `0` | The minimum size of each pane, in pixels. |
| `collapsed` | `Bind<'none' \| 'first' \| 'second'>` | `'none'` | The collapsed pane. The other pane takes all the space. |
| `resizable` | `Bind<boolean>` | `true` | Lets the pointer and keyboard move the splitter. |
| `collapsible` | `Bind<boolean>` | `true` | Enter and a double-click collapse and restore the first pane. |
| `step` | `Bind<number>` | `10` | The distance an arrow key moves the splitter, in pixels. |
| `splitterLabel` | `Bind<string>` | `uiLocale.strings.resize` | The accessible name of the splitter. |

### Props a child sets for its container

| Prop | Used by | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `grow` | Stack | `Bind<boolean \| number>` | Takes the free space along the direction. Numbers share it proportionally. |
| `row, column` | Grid | `Bind<number \| string>` | The starting line, counted from 1. A string is passed to CSS as is (`-1`). |
| `rowSpan, columnSpan` | Grid | `Bind<number>` | The number of tracks it spans. |
| `dock` | DockPanel | `Bind<Dock>` | `top`, `bottom`, `start`, `end`, `fill` (the default) or `float`. |
| `left, top, right, bottom` | DockPanel | `Bind<number \| string>` | The anchors of a `float` child. A number is in pixels, and `left` plus `right` stretches it. |

### Properties

| Property | Access | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `every prop above` | read/write, reactive | Accepts a value or a function, the same as the prop. |
| `SplitContainer.first, second` | read-only | The two panes, as `Panel` objects: `split.first.controls.add(…)`, `split.second.scrollable = true`. |
| `SplitContainer.splitterElement` | read-only | The `role="separator"` element. |
| `SplitContainer.value` | read/write | Maps to `position` for `x-model`. |
| `GroupBox.legendElement` | read-only | The `<legend>` element. |

### Methods

| Method | Returns | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `Stack.setGrow(child, grow), growOf(child)` | `void`, value | Sets a child's `grow` programmatically, with a value or a function. |
| `Grid.setCell(child, cell), cellOf(child)` | `void`, `GridCell` | Sets a child's `row`, `column`, `rowSpan` and `columnSpan` programmatically. |
| `DockPanel.setDock(child, dock), dockOf(child)` | `void`, `Dock` | Sets a child's `dock` programmatically. |
| `DockPanel.setAnchors(child, anchors)` | `void` | Sets the `left`, `top`, `right` and `bottom` of a `float` child. |
| `SplitContainer.collapse(pane?), restore()` | `void` | Collapses a pane (the first by default), or shows both panes again. |
| `GroupBox.focus()` | `boolean` | Sets focus on the first control inside, expanding a collapsed box if needed. |

### Events

| Event | When |
| --- | --- |
| `SplitContainer.onSplitterMoved(e)` | Occurs when the splitter moves (at the end of a drag), or when a pane is collapsed or restored. `e`: `{ position, collapsed, byUser, source }`. |
| `GroupBox.onToggled(e)` | Occurs when the content is shown or hidden. `e`: `{ collapsed, byUser, source }`. |

`ChildSettings`, which reads a child's settings from its props and tracks children added later, is exported for use in your own containers.

# Splitter

> Navigation · @motifx-community/ui 0.1.0-beta.5

Divides space into any number of resizable panes, arranged side by side or stacked. A handle between each pair of panes can be dragged or moved with the keyboard, and it resizes the two panes next to it. Panes can be collapsed from their handle and can contain another splitter. For two panes where one has a fixed size, see [SplitContainer](layout.md).

## Import

```tsx
import { Splitter, SplitPane } from '@motifx-community/ui';
```

## Pixels, percentages and remaining space

Each `SplitPane` sets its `size`. A pixel value stays fixed when the splitter resizes, a percentage (`'30%'`) divides the space available to percentages, and a pane without a size takes an equal part of what remains. `minSize` and `maxSize` limit the handles. Drag a handle, or focus it and use the arrow keys, Home and End.

```tsx
import { SplitPane, Splitter } from '@motifx-community/ui';

/** Three panes: a fixed one in pixels with a least size, one that takes what is left, and a share. */
export default function Basic() {
    return (
        <Splitter class="sp-basic" style="block-size: 240px">
            <SplitPane size={220} minSize={140} padding="md" text="Folders">
                <p class="sp-note">Folders, 220 px to start, never under 140.</p>
            </SplitPane>
            <SplitPane minSize={120} padding="md" text="Messages">
                <p class="sp-note">Messages take what the others leave.</p>
            </SplitPane>
            <SplitPane size="30%" minSize={100} padding="md" text="Preview">
                <p class="sp-note">Preview, three tenths of the room the shares divide.</p>
            </SplitPane>
        </Splitter>
    );
}
```

## Collapsing panes

A `collapsible` pane gets a button on the adjacent handle. Enter on the handle and a double-click do the same. Adjacent panes take its space, and it returns to its previous size when expanded. `onCollapsing` can cancel the action, and `onCollapsed` reports it.

```tsx
import { reactive } from '@motifx/core';
import { SplitPane, Splitter, Stack } from '@motifx-community/ui';

/** The side panes can be collapsed with a button on the handle, Enter on it, or a double-click. The middle pane cannot. */
export default function Collapsible() {
    const s = reactive({ told: '' });
    return (
        <Stack gap="sm" style="inline-size: 100%">
            <Splitter class="sp-fold" style="block-size: 200px" onCollapsed={e => (s.told = `${e.pane.text} ${e.collapsed ? 'hidden' : 'shown'}`)}>
                <SplitPane size={180} minSize={120} collapsible padding="md" text="Tree">
                    <p class="sp-note">Tree</p>
                </SplitPane>
                <SplitPane minSize={160} padding="md" text="Page">
                    <p class="sp-note">Page</p>
                </SplitPane>
                <SplitPane size={200} minSize={120} collapsible padding="md" text="Properties">
                    <p class="sp-note">Properties</p>
                </SplitPane>
            </Splitter>
            <output class="sp-fold-told">{() => s.told}</output>
        </Stack>
    );
}
```

## Nested splitters

A pane is a `Panel`, so you can place a `Splitter` with the other `orientation` inside it, for example to show an editor above an output panel next to a tree.

```tsx
import { SplitPane, Splitter } from '@motifx-community/ui';

/** A pane may hold another splitter: here the right pane is split the other way. */
export default function Nested() {
    return (
        <Splitter class="sp-nested" style="block-size: 260px">
            <SplitPane size={200} minSize={120} padding="md" text="Navigation">
                <p class="sp-note">Navigation</p>
            </SplitPane>
            <SplitPane minSize={200}>
                <Splitter class="sp-inner" orientation="vertical">
                    <SplitPane minSize={80} padding="md" text="Editor">
                        <p class="sp-note">Editor</p>
                    </SplitPane>
                    <SplitPane size={90} minSize={60} collapsible padding="md" text="Output">
                        <p class="sp-note">Output</p>
                    </SplitPane>
                </Splitter>
            </SplitPane>
        </Splitter>
    );
}
```

## Persisting the layout

After every move, the pane sizes in pixels are written to `x-model`, and `onResized` reports them. Pass them back as `sizes` to restore a layout. `null` returns to the panes' own sizes.

```tsx
import { reactive } from '@motifx/core';
import { Button, SplitPane, Splitter, Stack } from '@motifx-community/ui';

/** The sizes are written to x-model as pixels after every move and can be set back: a layout saved and restored. */
export default function Sizes() {
    const s = reactive({ sizes: null as readonly (number | string | null)[] | null, kept: null as readonly number[] | null, moved: 0 });
    return (
        <Stack gap="sm" style="inline-size: 100%">
            <Splitter class="sp-sizes" style="block-size: 180px" x-model={() => s.sizes} onResized={() => s.moved++}>
                <SplitPane size={160} minSize={80} padding="md" text="Left">
                    <p class="sp-note">Left</p>
                </SplitPane>
                <SplitPane minSize={80} padding="md" text="Middle">
                    <p class="sp-note">Middle</p>
                </SplitPane>
                <SplitPane size={160} minSize={80} padding="md" text="Right">
                    <p class="sp-note">Right</p>
                </SplitPane>
            </Splitter>
            <Stack orientation="horizontal" wrap align="center">
                <Button text="Keep this layout" variant="outline" onclick={() => (s.kept = (s.sizes as number[] | null)?.slice() ?? null)} />
                <Button text="Restore it" variant="outline" enabled={() => !!s.kept} onclick={() => (s.sizes = s.kept)} />
                <Button text="Start again" variant="outline" onclick={() => (s.sizes = null)} />
                <output class="sp-sizes-told">{() => `sizes: ${JSON.stringify(s.sizes)}, moved ${s.moved} times`}</output>
            </Stack>
        </Stack>
    );
}
```

## Keyboard

| Key | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `Tab` | Each handle that can move or collapse a pane is a Tab stop between its panes. |
| `Arrow keys` | Left and Right (Up and Down when stacked) move the handle by `step` pixels, within the panes' minimum and maximum sizes. These are reversed on right-to-left pages. |
| `Home, End` | Sets the pane before the handle to its minimum or maximum size. |
| `Enter` | Collapses the pane before the handle or expands it. If that pane cannot collapse, the pane after it is used. |

## Accessibility

| Topic | Details |
| --- | --- |
| `A handle` | A `separator` named “Resize” in the kit language, with `aria-controls` pointing to the pane before it, `aria-orientation`, and `aria-valuenow` as that pane's share of the two panes next to the handle. |
| `Fold buttons` | Buttons named “Hide the pane” and “Show the pane”, outside the Tab order. Enter on the handle does the same. |
| `A hidden pane` | Hidden and `inert`. Focus inside it moves to the handle. |
| `Panes` | A pane with `text` is a `region` with that name. |

## Styling

| Hook | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `.mx-splitter` | The splitter. `data-orientation`, and `data-dragging` while a handle is dragged. |
| `.mx-splitter__pane` | A pane (a `Panel`). `data-collapsed` while collapsed. |
| `.mx-splitter__handle` | A handle. `data-resizable`, `data-dragging`. |
| `.mx-splitter__grip, .mx-splitter__fold, .mx-splitter__fold-glyph` | The grip in the middle of a handle, the collapse buttons at either end (`data-side`), and their arrows. |

### Component tokens

| Token | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `splitter.handle, .line, .grip, .fold, .fold-glyph, .pane` | Units: the handle (`focus`), the line along it (`active`, `disabled`), the grip (`active`, `disabled`), the collapse buttons (`hover`, `pressed`, `focus`) and their arrows, and a pane (`collapsed`). |
| `splitter.size, .line-width, .active-width, .grip-length, .grip-thickness` | The thickness of the handle and line, the line thickness on hover, and the grip size. |

## API reference

### Splitter props

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `orientation` | `Bind<LayoutOrientation>` | `'horizontal'` | `horizontal` places the panes side by side, and `vertical` stacks them. |
| `resizable` | `Bind<boolean>` | `true` | Lets users drag handles and move them with the keyboard. A pane's own `resizable` takes precedence. |
| `collapsible` | `Bind<boolean>` | `false` | Lets every pane be collapsed from its adjacent handle. A pane's own `collapsible` takes precedence. |
| `step` | `Bind<number>` | `10` | The distance an arrow key moves a handle, in pixels. |
| `sizes` | `Bind<readonly (number \| string \| null)[] \| null>` | `null` | The pane sizes in order (pixels, a percentage or `null`). When set, they replace each pane's own `size`. After a drag or key press, the sizes in pixels are written to `x-model`. |

### SplitPane props

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `size` | `Bind<number \| string \| null>` | `null` | Pixels, a percentage (`'30%'`) of the space divided by percentages, or `null` for an equal share of what remains. |
| `minSize, maxSize` | `Bind<number>`, `Bind<number \| null>` | `0`, `null` | The minimum and maximum size, in pixels. |
| `collapsible` | `Bind<boolean \| undefined>` | `undefined` | Lets the adjacent handles collapse the pane. `undefined` inherits from the splitter. |
| `collapsed` | `Bind<boolean>` | `false` | Indicates that the pane is collapsed, and adjacent panes take its space. |
| `resizable` | `Bind<boolean>` | `true` | Lets the adjacent handles change its size. |
| `key` | `Bind<string>` | `''` | Identifies the pane. The JSX `key` is also read. |
| `content` | `() => ComponentBase \| ComponentBase[]` | — | Content created with the pane, in addition to the JSX children. |
| `padding, scrollable, variant, text` | Same as `Panel` |  | A pane is a `Panel`, with padding, scrolling, a frame and an accessible name (a region). |

### Events, properties and methods

| Member | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `onResizing` | event | Occurs while a handle is dragged (`handle`, `sizes` in pixels). |
| `onResized` | event | Occurs after a drag ends or a key moves a handle (`handle`, `sizes`). |
| `onCollapsing` | event | Occurs before a pane is collapsed or expanded (`pane`, `index`, `collapsed`, `byUser`). Set `cancel = true` to keep the current state. |
| `onCollapsed` | event | Occurs after a pane is collapsed or expanded. |
| `panes` | read-only | The panes in order, including collapsed ones. |
| `currentSizes` | read-only | The current pane sizes in pixels, with 0 for a collapsed pane. |
| `count` | read-only | The number of panes. |
| `add(pane), insert(index, pane)` | `SplitPane` | Adds a pane at the end or at an index. |
| `remove(pane)` | `boolean` | Removes a pane and disposes it. |
| `collapse(pane), expand(pane)` | `boolean` | Collapses or expands a pane, by index or object. `onCollapsing` is raised first. A pane's own `collapse()` and `expand()` do the same. |

# Resizable

> Navigation · @motifx-community/ui 0.1.0-beta.5

A box that users can resize from its edges and corners with the pointer, or with the arrow keys on the grip in its end corner. It respects minimum and maximum sizes, can stay within an area, and can preserve its aspect ratio.

## Import

```tsx
import { Resizable } from '@motifx-community/ui';
```

## Edges, corners and the grip

JSX children are the content. `handles` sets which edges and corners respond to the pointer (`all` by default). The grip in the end corner is the Tab stop, and the arrow keys change the size by `step`. `minWidth`, `minHeight`, `maxWidth` and `maxHeight` set the limits. A box positioned with `absolute` or `fixed` also moves when its start or top edge is dragged, so the opposite edge stays in place. A box in the normal flow only changes size.

```tsx
import { reactive } from '@motifx/core';
import { Panel, Resizable, Stack } from '@motifx-community/ui';

/** A box resized from any side or corner, never under 160 × 80 or over 480 × 240; the grip in the corner takes the keys. */
export default function Basic() {
    const s = reactive({ told: '' });
    return (
        <Stack gap="sm" style="inline-size: 100%">
            <Resizable class="rs-box" width={280} height={140} minWidth={160} minHeight={80} maxWidth={480} maxHeight={240} onResized={e => (s.told = `${e.width} × ${e.height}, from the ${e.edge}`)}>
                <Panel padding="md" variant="outline" text="A note" style="block-size: 100%">
                    <p class="rs-note">Drag a side or a corner, or focus the grip and use the arrow keys.</p>
                </Panel>
            </Resizable>
            <output class="rs-box-told">{() => s.told}</output>
        </Stack>
    );
}
```

## Staying within an area and keeping the aspect ratio

`area` keeps the box inside its parent or a specified element, and `keepAspectRatio` adjusts the other dimension. In this example, only the end edge, the bottom edge and the corner between them resize the image.

```tsx
import { Resizable } from '@motifx-community/ui';
import { scene } from '../../gallery/examples/scenes';

/** A picture that keeps its shape and stays inside the dashed area; only the end side, the bottom and the corner resize it. */
export default function Area() {
    return (
        <div class="rs-area" style="position: relative; inline-size: 100%; block-size: 260px; outline: 2px dashed var(--mx-color-stroke-control-strong); outline-offset: -2px">
            <Resizable class="rs-picture" width={240} height={135} minWidth={120} minHeight={68} area="parent" keepAspectRatio handles={['end', 'bottom', 'bottom-end']} style="position: absolute; left: 16px; top: 16px">
                <img src={scene(200)} alt="A harbour at dawn" style="display: block; inline-size: 100%; block-size: 100%; object-fit: cover" />
            </Resizable>
        </div>
    );
}
```

## Programmatic use

`size` sets the size in pixels, and `x-model` receives it after every resize (`onResized` also reports it). Use this to save and restore a layout, or to set the size from a button.

```tsx
import { reactive } from '@motifx/core';
import { Button, Panel, Resizable, Stack } from '@motifx-community/ui';

/** The size is written to x-model after every resize and can be set back: set, saved and restored programmatically. */
export default function Programmatic() {
    const s = reactive({ size: { width: 240, height: 120 } as { width: number; height: number } | null, kept: null as { width: number; height: number } | null });
    return (
        <Stack gap="sm" style="inline-size: 100%">
            <Resizable class="rs-coded" minWidth={120} minHeight={60} x-model={() => s.size}>
                <Panel padding="md" variant="outline" style="block-size: 100%">
                    <p class="rs-note">Sized by the model.</p>
                </Panel>
            </Resizable>
            <Stack orientation="horizontal" wrap align="center">
                <Button text="Wider" variant="outline" onclick={() => (s.size = { width: (s.size?.width ?? 240) + 40, height: s.size?.height ?? 120 })} />
                <Button text="Keep this size" variant="outline" onclick={() => (s.kept = s.size ? { ...s.size } : null)} />
                <Button text="Restore it" variant="outline" enabled={() => !!s.kept} onclick={() => (s.size = s.kept ? { ...s.kept } : null)} />
                <output class="rs-coded-told">{() => `size: ${JSON.stringify(s.size)}`}</output>
            </Stack>
        </Stack>
    );
}
```

## Keyboard

| Key | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `Tab` | The grip in the end corner is the only Tab stop. |
| `Arrow keys` | On the grip, Left and Right change the width by `step` (reversed on right-to-left pages), and Up and Down change the height, within the limits, the area and the aspect ratio. |

## Accessibility

| Topic | Details |
| --- | --- |
| `The grip` | A button named “Resize” in the kit language. The new size is announced after every change (“Width 320, height 200”). |
| `The handles` | Strips along the edges and corners for pointer use only, hidden from screen readers. The grip provides the same function for the keyboard. |
| `Content` | JSX children are the content and are left unchanged, such as a panel, an image or a form. |

## Styling

| Hook | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `.mx-resizable` | The box. `data-resizing` and `data-edge` while a handle is dragged, and `data-disabled`. |
| `.mx-resizable__frame, .mx-resizable__handle` | The frame over the box and its eight handles (`data-edge`, `data-active` during a drag, and `hidden` when not enabled). |
| `.mx-resizable__grip, .mx-resizable__grip-glyph` | The grip in the end corner and its glyph. |

### Component tokens

| Token | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `resizable.box, .handle, .grip, .grip-glyph` | Units: the box (`resizing`), a handle (`hover`, `active`, `corner`), the grip (`hover`, `pressed`, `focus`) and its glyph (`icon`). |
| `resizable.edge` | The width of the pointer target along an edge. A corner is twice that in each direction. |

## API reference

### Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `handles` | `Bind<ResizeHandles>` | `'all'` | `all`, `edges`, `corners`, or a list of `top`, `bottom`, `start`, `end`, `top-start`, `top-end`, `bottom-start` and `bottom-end`. |
| `minWidth, minHeight` | `Bind<number>` | `30` | The minimum width and height, in pixels. |
| `maxWidth, maxHeight` | `Bind<number \| null>` | `null` | The maximum width and height, in pixels. `null` means no limit. |
| `area` | `Bind<'parent' \| HTMLElement \| null>` | `null` | The area the box stays inside: its parent, or an element that contains it. |
| `keepAspectRatio` | `Bind<boolean>` | `false` | Preserves the ratio of width to height. |
| `step` | `Bind<number>` | `10` | The number of pixels an arrow key changes an edge. |
| `width, height` | `Bind<number \| string \| null>` | `null` | The initial size, as a CSS length or in pixels. Without it, the content determines the size. |
| `size` | `Bind<ResizeSize \| null>` | `null` | The size in pixels. When set, it is applied, and after every resize the new size is written to `x-model`. |

### Events, properties and methods

| Member | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `onResizeStarting` | event | Occurs before a resize starts from a handle (`edge`, `width`, `height`). Set `cancel = true` to keep the size. |
| `onResizing` | event | Occurs while the box is being resized (`edge`, and the current `width` and `height`). |
| `onResized` | event | Occurs when a resize ends, either when the pointer is released or when a key moves an edge. |
| `currentSize` | read-only | The current size in pixels. |
| `gripElement` | read-only | The grip in the end corner, which is the Tab stop for keyboard resizing. |

# Draggable and DropTarget

> Navigation · @motifx-community/ui 0.1.0-beta.5

Makes any content movable with the pointer, touch or the arrow keys, optionally along one axis, inside a boundary, by a handle or as a copy. `DropTarget` defines areas that accept it. To reorder items in a list, see [Sortable](sortable.md).

## Import

```tsx
import { Draggable, DropTarget } from '@motifx-community/ui';
```

## Moving content

JSX children are the movable content. `boundary` keeps it inside its parent or an element, `axis` limits it to one direction, and `handle` sets the only part that responds to the pointer and keyboard. A drag writes the position to `x-model`, `onDragEnded` reports it, and Escape returns the content to its start.

```tsx
import { reactive } from '@motifx/core';
import { Draggable, Panel, Stack } from '@motifx-community/ui';

/** Three notes in a room: one moves anywhere inside it, one only sideways, one only by its grip; the keys move the focused one. */
export default function Free() {
    const s = reactive({ told: '' });
    const note = (text: string, grip = false) => (
        <Panel padding="sm" variant="outline" style="inline-size: 150px">
            {grip && <span class="dg-grip">⋮⋮ </span>}
            <span>{text}</span>
        </Panel>
    );
    return (
        <Stack gap="sm" style="inline-size: 100%">
            <div class="dg-room" style="position: relative; block-size: 220px; outline: 2px dashed var(--mx-color-stroke-control-strong); outline-offset: -2px">
                <Draggable class="dg-free" boundary="parent" style="position: absolute; left: 16px; top: 16px" onDragEnded={e => (s.told = `free: ${e.x}, ${e.y}`)}>
                    {note('Anywhere in the room')}
                </Draggable>
                <Draggable class="dg-axis" axis="x" boundary="parent" style="position: absolute; left: 16px; top: 100px" onDragEnded={e => (s.told = `sideways: ${e.x}, ${e.y}`)}>
                    {note('Only sideways')}
                </Draggable>
                <Draggable class="dg-handle" handle=".dg-grip" boundary="parent" style="position: absolute; left: 300px; top: 16px" onDragEnded={e => (s.told = `by the grip: ${e.x}, ${e.y}`)}>
                    {note('Only by the grip', true)}
                </Draggable>
            </div>
            <output class="dg-free-told">{() => s.told}</output>
        </Stack>
    );
}
```

## Drop targets

A `DropTarget` in the same `group` accepts a draggable dropped on it and receives the draggable's `data` in `onDropped`. `onDragEntering` can reject it. With `clone`, a copy follows the pointer and the original stays, so one item can be dropped many times. Your code decides what a drop does to your data.

```tsx
import { reactive } from '@motifx/core';
import { Draggable, DropTarget, Stack } from '@motifx-community/ui';

const FRUIT = ['Apple', 'Pear', 'Plum'];

/** Copies of the chips go to the bowls of their group; the small bowl refuses a third, and the data moves in `onDropped`. */
export default function Targets() {
    const s = reactive({ big: [] as string[], small: [] as string[], told: '' });
    const bowl = (name: 'big' | 'small', limit: number) => (
        <DropTarget
            class={`dg-bowl dg-bowl-${name}`}
            group="fruit"
            grow
            style="flex-basis: 0; min-block-size: 96px; padding: 12px; border: 1px solid var(--mx-color-stroke-divider); border-radius: var(--mx-radius-md)"
            onDragEntering={e => (e.cancel = s[name].length >= limit)}
            onDropped={e => {
                s[name].push(e.data as string);
                s.told = `${e.data} went to the ${name} bowl`;
            }}
        >
            <strong>{name === 'big' ? 'Big bowl' : 'Small bowl, two at most'}</strong>
            <div class="dg-bowl-list">{() => s[name].join(', ') || 'empty'}</div>
        </DropTarget>
    );
    return (
        <Stack gap="md" style="inline-size: 100%">
            <Stack orientation="horizontal" gap="sm" wrap>
                {FRUIT.map(fruit => (
                    <Draggable class="dg-chip" clone group="fruit" data={fruit} style="padding: 6px 12px; border-radius: var(--mx-radius-full); border: 1px solid var(--mx-color-stroke-control-strong)">
                        {fruit}
                    </Draggable>
                ))}
            </Stack>
            <Stack orientation="horizontal" gap="md">
                {bowl('big', 99)}
                {bowl('small', 2)}
            </Stack>
            <output class="dg-bowls-told">{() => s.told}</output>
        </Stack>
    );
}
```

## Programmatic use

`position` sets the location in pixels from the element's layout position, and `x-model` receives it after every drag or key press, so you can save and restore it.

```tsx
import { reactive } from '@motifx/core';
import { Button, Draggable, Panel, Stack } from '@motifx-community/ui';

/** The position is written to x-model after every drag or key press and can be set back: moved, saved and restored programmatically. */
export default function Programmatic() {
    const s = reactive({ at: { x: 0, y: 0 } as { x: number; y: number } | null, kept: null as { x: number; y: number } | null });
    return (
        <Stack gap="sm" style="inline-size: 100%">
            <div style="position: relative; block-size: 160px">
                <Draggable class="dg-coded" boundary="parent" step={20} x-model={() => s.at} style="position: absolute; left: 0; top: 0">
                    <Panel padding="sm" variant="outline" style="inline-size: 140px">
                        Moved by the model
                    </Panel>
                </Draggable>
            </div>
            <Stack orientation="horizontal" wrap align="center">
                <Button text="Right by 40" variant="outline" onclick={() => (s.at = { x: (s.at?.x ?? 0) + 40, y: s.at?.y ?? 0 })} />
                <Button text="Keep this place" variant="outline" onclick={() => (s.kept = s.at ? { ...s.at } : null)} />
                <Button text="Restore it" variant="outline" enabled={() => !!s.kept} onclick={() => (s.at = s.kept ? { ...s.kept } : null)} />
                <Button text="Back to the start" variant="outline" onclick={() => (s.at = { x: 0, y: 0 })} />
                <output class="dg-coded-told">{() => `at: ${JSON.stringify(s.at)}`}</output>
            </Stack>
        </Stack>
    );
}
```

## Keyboard

| Key | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `Tab` | The draggable, or its handle, is one Tab stop. |
| `Arrow keys` | Moves it by `step` pixels along its axis and inside its boundary, and the new position is announced. |
| `Escape` | During a drag, cancels it and returns the item to where it started. |

## Accessibility

| Topic | Details |
| --- | --- |
| `The draggable` | A `group` with `aria-roledescription="draggable"`, named “Move” in the kit language. With a `handle`, that element is a button with this name instead. |
| `Dragging` | A long press lifts it on a touch screen. During a drag, it lets pointer events pass through so the target underneath can be detected, and a `clone` copy follows the pointer. |
| `Targets` | Marked while a drag from their group is active, while the draggable is over them, and when they reject it. |

## Styling

| Hook | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `.mx-draggable` | The draggable. `data-dragging`, `data-handle`, `data-clone`, `data-axis`. |
| `.mx-draggable__handle, .mx-draggable__ghost` | The handle specified by `handle`, and the copy that follows the pointer. |
| `.mx-drop-target` | A target. `data-drop-active` during a drag from its group, `data-drop-over`, `data-drop-refused`. |

### Component tokens

| Token | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `draggable.box, .handle, .ghost` | Units: the draggable (`draggable`, `dragging`, `focus`), its handle (`hover`, `focus`) and the copy. |
| `drop-target.target` | Unit: a target (`active`, `over`, `refused`). |

## API reference

### Draggable props

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `axis` | `Bind<DragAxis>` | `'both'` | `both`, `x` or `y`. |
| `boundary` | `Bind<'parent' \| HTMLElement \| null>` | `null` | The area it stays inside: its parent, or an element that contains it. |
| `handle` | `Bind<string \| null>` | `null` | A selector inside the draggable. Only this part starts a drag, and it receives the Tab stop and keyboard input. |
| `clone` | `Bind<boolean>` | `false` | A copy follows the pointer and the draggable stays in place, ready to be dropped on a target. |
| `group` | `Bind<string \| null>` | `null` | Drop targets in the same group accept it. |
| `data` | `unknown` | — | Custom data passed to the drop target on drop. |
| `step` | `Bind<number>` | `10` | The number of pixels an arrow key moves it. |
| `position` | `Bind<DragPosition \| null>` | `null` | The position in pixels from its layout position. When set, it is applied, and after every drag or key press the new position is written to `x-model`. |

### DropTarget props and events

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `group` | `Bind<string \| null>` | `null` | Accepts draggables in this group. `null` accepts those without a group. |
| `onDragEntering` | event | Occurs when a draggable enters (`draggable`, `data`). Set `cancel = true` to reject it. |
| `onDragLeaving` | event | Occurs when the draggable leaves. |
| `onDropped` | event | Occurs when a draggable is dropped on it. Your code moves the data. |

### Events, properties and methods

| Member | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `onDragStarting` | event | Occurs before a drag starts. Set `cancel = true` to keep it in place. |
| `onDragging` | event | Occurs during a drag (`x`, `y`, and the `target` under the pointer). |
| `onDragEnding` | event | Occurs when the pointer is released. Set `cancel = true` to return it to where it started. |
| `onDragEnded` | event | Occurs when the drag ends (`x`, `y`, `target`, `dropped`). |
| `currentPosition` | read-only | The current position. |
| `isDragging` | read-only | Indicates that a drag is in progress. |
| `handleElement` | read-only | The element that handles the pointer and keyboard: the handle, or the draggable itself. |

# ScrollView

> Navigation · @motifx-community/ui 0.1.0-beta.5

A scrollable container with configurable scrollbars, pull-to-refresh, and load-on-scroll near the end of the content. You can scroll it programmatically to a position or an element.

## Import

```tsx
import { ScrollView } from '@motifx-community/ui';
```

## Scrollable content

JSX children are the content. `showScrollbar` sets when scrollbars appear. `scrollTo` and `scrollToElement` scroll programmatically, and `onScrolled` reports the position.

```tsx
import { reactive } from '@motifx/core';
import { Button, ScrollView, Stack, type ScrollViewBars } from '@motifx-community/ui';

const LINES = Array.from({ length: 40 }, (_, i) => `Line ${i + 1} of a long text that needs a box of its own to scroll in.`);
const MODES: ScrollViewBars[] = ['onScroll', 'onHover', 'always', 'never'];

/** A scrolling box with configurable scrollbars, moved programmatically to a line and back to the top. */
export default function Bars() {
    const s = reactive({ bars: 'onScroll' as ScrollViewBars, top: 0 });
    let view!: ScrollView;
    return (
        <Stack gap="md" style="inline-size: 100%">
            <Stack orientation="horizontal" wrap align="center">
                {MODES.map(mode => (
                    <Button key={mode} text={mode} size="sm" variant={() => (s.bars === mode ? 'solid' : 'outline')} onclick={() => (s.bars = mode)} />
                ))}
                <Button text="Line 20" variant="outline" size="sm" onclick={() => view.scrollToElement(view.content.element.querySelectorAll('p')[19], true)} />
                <Button text="Top" variant="outline" size="sm" onclick={() => view.scrollTo(0, true)} />
                <output class="sv-top">{() => `scrollTop: ${Math.round(s.top)}`}</output>
            </Stack>
            <ScrollView ref={(v: ScrollView) => (view = v)} label="Long text" class="sv-text" showScrollbar={() => s.bars} style="block-size: 12rem" onScrolled={e => (s.top = e.top)}>
                {LINES.map(line => (
                    <p key={line}>{line}</p>
                ))}
            </ScrollView>
        </Stack>
    );
}
```

## Pull to refresh

With `pullToRefresh`, pulling the content down from the top raises `onPullDown`. Set `promise`, or call `release()`, and the panel closes when the work is finished.

```tsx
import { reactive } from '@motifx/core';
import { Panel, ScrollView, Stack } from '@motifx-community/ui';

/** Pulled down from the top, the list requests new items and shows the panel until the promise settles. */
export default function Pull() {
    const s = reactive({ notes: ['Welcome aboard', 'Your plan was renewed', 'A new comment on "Roadmap"'], count: 0 });
    const reload = () =>
        new Promise<void>(resolve =>
            setTimeout(() => {
                s.count++;
                s.notes = [`Fresh note ${s.count}`, ...s.notes];
                resolve();
            }, 1200)
        );
    return (
        <Stack gap="sm" style="inline-size: 100%">
            <span>Drag the list down from its top (a finger, or the mouse) and let go.</span>
            <ScrollView label="Notes" class="sv-notes" pullToRefresh onPullDown={e => (e.promise = reload())} style="block-size: 12rem">
                {s.notes.map(note => (
                    <Panel key={note} variant="outline" padding="sm">
                        {note}
                    </Panel>
                ))}
            </ScrollView>
        </Stack>
    );
}
```

## Load more

With `loadOnReachBottom`, scrolling within `reachBottomOffset` of the end raises `onReachBottom` once. `release()` allows the next request, and `release(true)` signals that there is no more data. Content that does not fill the view requests more immediately.

```tsx
import { reactive } from '@motifx/core';
import { Panel, ScrollView, Stack } from '@motifx-community/ui';

const TOTAL = 60;
const PAGE = 15;

// A page of rows, as a server would send them.
const fetchRows = (from: number) =>
    new Promise<string[]>(resolve => setTimeout(() => resolve(Array.from({ length: Math.min(PAGE, TOTAL - from) }, (_, i) => `Order #${1000 + from + i}`)), 800));

/** Near the end, the view requests more data. The indicator stays until the rows arrive, and `release(true)` ends it when there is no more. */
export default function More() {
    const s = reactive({ rows: [] as string[] });
    const more = () =>
        fetchRows(s.rows.length).then(rows => {
            s.rows = [...s.rows, ...rows];
            return s.rows.length >= TOTAL;
        });
    return (
        <Stack gap="sm" style="inline-size: 100%">
            <output class="sv-more-told">{() => (s.rows.length >= TOTAL ? `All ${TOTAL} orders are in.` : `${s.rows.length} of ${TOTAL} orders`)}</output>
            <ScrollView label="Orders" class="sv-orders" loadOnReachBottom reachBottomOffset={80} onReachBottom={e => more().then(done => e.release(done))} style="block-size: 14rem">
                {s.rows.map(row => (
                    <Panel key={row} variant="outline" padding="sm">
                        {row}
                    </Panel>
                ))}
            </ScrollView>
        </Stack>
    );
}
```

## Behavior

| Topic | Details |
| --- | --- |
| `Scrolling` | The box scrolls with the mouse wheel, the keyboard when focused, touch, and code. `direction` locks the other axis, and the page behind does not continue scrolling when the content ends. |
| `Scrollbars` | These are the design system scrollbars. With `onScroll`, the thumb appears while the content moves and hides shortly after. With `onHover`, it appears while the pointer is over the view or focus is inside it. `always` keeps it visible, and `never` hides it while the content still scrolls. |
| `Pull to refresh` | From the top, with a finger or the pointer, the content moves down with increasing resistance, and the panel above it prompts the user to pull and then release. Releasing far enough starts a refresh, and the spinner runs until `release()` or the promise. A short pull returns to its position. |
| `Load more` | Within `reachBottomOffset` of the end, `onReachBottom` is raised once, and the panel below the content is shown meanwhile. After release, the next approach raises it again, until `release(true)`. Content that does not fill the box requests more immediately, and again as it grows. |
| `Texts` | The kit strings in the kit language, unless the text props override them. |

## Accessibility

| Topic | Details |
| --- | --- |
| `Region` | A focusable box named by `label`. The arrow keys, Page Up, Page Down, Home and End scroll it, using the browser's default behavior. |
| `Panels` | Live regions announce “Refreshing…” and “Loading…” when they appear. |
| `Spinners` | Decorative. The text describes what is happening. |
| `Motion` | A finger that pulls does not scroll the page, and a finger that scrolls does not pull. |

## Styling

| Hook | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `.mx-scroll-view` | The box. `data-direction`, `data-bars`, `data-scrolling` while the content moves, `data-pull` when pull-to-refresh is on, `data-pulling` during a pull, `data-pull-state` (`pull`, `release`, `refreshing`) and `data-loading`. |
| `.mx-scroll-view__content` | The element that holds the children, which moves down during a pull. |
| `.mx-scroll-view__pull, .mx-scroll-view__pull-text, .mx-scroll-view__pull-spinner` | The panel above the content, its text and the kit spinner. |
| `.mx-scroll-view__bottom, .mx-scroll-view__bottom-text, .mx-scroll-view__bottom-spinner` | The panel below the content while more data loads. |

### Component tokens

| Token | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `scroll-view.box` | Unit: the box (`focus`). |
| `scroll-view.pull, .pull-text, .bottom, .bottom-text` | Units: the two panels (the pull panel has `release` and `refreshing`) and their text. |
| `scroll-view.panel-height, .panel-gap` | The height of the panels, and the space between a panel's spinner and its text. |

## API reference

### Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `direction` | `Bind<ScrollViewDirection>` | `'vertical'` | `vertical`, `horizontal` or `both`: the scroll direction. |
| `showScrollbar` | `Bind<ScrollViewBars>` | `'onScroll'` | When scrollbars appear: `onScroll` while scrolling, `onHover` while the pointer is over the view, `always` or `never`. |
| `pullToRefresh` | `Bind<boolean>` | `false` | Pulling the content down from the top raises `onPullDown`. |
| `loadOnReachBottom` | `Bind<boolean>` | `false` | Scrolling near the end raises `onReachBottom`, as does content that does not reach the end. |
| `reachBottomOffset` | `Bind<number>` | `100` | The distance from the end, in pixels, at which `onReachBottom` is raised. |
| `pullDownText, releaseText, refreshingText` | `Bind<string>` | The kit strings | The pull panel text: while pulling, once far enough, and while refreshing. |
| `reachBottomText` | `Bind<string>` | The kit string “Loading…” | The text below the content while more data loads. |
| `label` | `Bind<string>` | `''` | The accessible name of the scrolling region. |

### Events, properties and methods

| Member | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `onPullDown` | event | Occurs when the content is pulled down and released. Load the new data and call `release()`, or set `promise` and the panel closes when it settles. |
| `onReachBottom` | event | Occurs when the content is scrolled near its end. Load more data and call `release()`. `release(true)` signals that there is no more data, and the view stops requesting. A `promise` also releases it. |
| `onScrolled` | event | Occurs when the position changes: `top`, `left`. |
| `scrollTo(where, smooth?)` | `void` | Scrolls to a top position, or to `{ top, left }`. `smooth` animates the scroll. |
| `scrollBy({ top, left }, smooth?)` | `void` | Scrolls by a distance. |
| `scrollToElement(target, smooth?)` | `void` | Scrolls an element or component of the content into view. |
| `refresh(), release()` | `void` | Starts a refresh as a pull would, or ends it. |
| `loadMore(), update()` | `boolean` / `void` | Requests more data now, or checks the position again after the content changes. |
| `scrollTop, scrollLeft` | read-only | The current scroll position. |
| `isRefreshing, isLoading` | read-only | Indicates that a refresh or a load is in progress. |
| `content` | read-only | The element that holds the children, between the two panels. |
