# TabDocumentManager: Tablet and phone

> TabDocumentManager · @motifx-community/ui 0.1.0-beta.5

On tablets and phones, a layout of groups, splits and dock areas does not fit as designed. The manager keeps the layout and changes how it is presented: the documents, groups, areas and saved JSON stay the same, and content is moved rather than recreated. The presentation depends on the manager's own width rather than the device, and on touch screens its tabs and buttons are larger.

## Import

```tsx
import { TabDocumentManager, type TabPresentation, type TabDockPresentation } from '@motifx-community/ui';
```

## Three presentations of one layout

| Presentation | Displayed content |
| --- | --- |
| `Desktop` | The full layout: groups side by side and one above the other, dock areas around them, floating windows and new browser windows. |
| `Tablet` | Up to two groups side by side, with the first branch of the layout on one side and the rest on the other, each showing its most recently used group. Groups that do not fit collapse as tabs into the strip of the adjacent group. Their tabs keep their own group, and tapping one activates that group there. Dock areas become drawers from their edge, with the bottom area as a sheet, and open from their titles along the edges or by swiping in from the edge. A floating window is a large sheet. |
| `Phone` | One document at full screen. The bar above it shows its title (swipe left or right to move to the adjacent document, or tap to open its commands in an action sheet), its close button, and the number of open documents, which opens the document list. Dock area tools are buttons in a bottom bar. Tapping one opens a sheet (peek, half or full with its handle, and swipe down to close), or a drawer for an area configured to use one. A floating window is a full-screen sheet. New browser windows are disabled, and the tab menu is an action sheet. |

Choose one, and the underlying layout does not change. Save the layout in each presentation, and the JSON is identical.

```tsx
import { reactive } from '@motifx/core';
import { Button, RadioGroup, Stack, TabDocumentManager, type TabPresentation } from '@motifx-community/ui';
import { FILES, fileDocument } from './files';
import { explorer, outline, output, problems, toolDocument } from './tools';

/**
 * One layout shown four ways: two groups (the second split again), the explorer and the outline on
 * the left, problems and output at the bottom, a floating window. Pick a presentation: the layout
 * stays the same (Save shows its JSON does not change), only where things show changes.
 */
export default function Presentations() {
  const s = reactive({ presentation: 'tablet' as TabPresentation, shown: '', saved: '' });
  const docs = new TabDocumentManager({ label: 'Editor shown as on a desktop, a tablet or a phone', presentation: () => s.presentation, minGroupWidth: 120 });
  docs.element.style.cssText = 'block-size: 32rem; inline-size: 100%; max-inline-size: 100%';
  const open = (path: string) => docs.open(docs.findDocument(path) ?? fileDocument(path), { focus: true });
  for (const file of FILES.slice(0, 3)) docs.open(fileDocument(file.path), { index: 99 });
  const right = docs.split(docs.activeGroup!, 'right', docs.findDocument('src/router.ts')!)!;
  right.open(fileDocument('README.md'));
  docs.split(right, 'down', docs.findDocument('README.md')!);
  docs.dock(
    toolDocument('explorer', 'Explorer', () => explorer(open)),
    'left',
  );
  docs.dock(toolDocument('outline', 'Outline', outline), 'left');
  docs.dock(toolDocument('problems', 'Problems', problems), 'bottom');
  docs.dock(toolDocument('output', 'Output', output), 'bottom');
  docs.float(docs.open(fileDocument('package.json'))!, { x: 80, y: 80, width: 360, height: 220 });
  docs.activate(docs.findDocument('src/index.ts')!);
  docs.onPresentationChanged((e) => (s.shown = `${e.from} → ${e.to} (${e.width} px wide)`));
  let first = '';
  const save = () => {
    const json = JSON.stringify(docs.saveLayout());
    first ||= json;
    s.saved = `Saved as ${docs.currentPresentation}: ${json.length} characters, ${json === first ? 'the same as the first save' : 'not the same as the first save'}.`;
  };

  return (
    <>
      <Stack orientation="horizontal" wrap align="center" gap="lg">
        <RadioGroup
          label="Presentation"
          orientation="horizontal"
          items={[
            { value: 'auto', text: 'By its width' },
            { value: 'desktop', text: 'Desktop' },
            { value: 'tablet', text: 'Tablet' },
            { value: 'phone', text: 'Phone' },
          ]}
          itemText="text"
          itemValue="value"
          x-model={() => s.presentation}
        />
        <output class="td-state">{() => (s.shown ? `Shown: ${s.shown}` : `Shown as: ${docs.currentPresentation}`)}</output>
      </Stack>
      {docs}
      <Stack orientation="horizontal" wrap align="center">
        <Button text="Save the layout" variant="outline" onclick={save} />
        <output class="td-state">{() => s.saved || 'The layout saves the same in every presentation.'}</output>
      </Stack>
    </>
  );
}
```

## Based on its own width

With `presentation: 'auto'` (the default), the manager monitors its own width and the device's pointer type. Below `phoneWidth` (560), it uses the phone presentation regardless of the pointer. Phones are typically 360 to 430 pixels wide, so a manager of about 590 pixels next to a page's side column stays in the desktop presentation. Below `tabletWidth` (1024), it uses the tablet presentation on touch screens and stays in the desktop presentation with a mouse (`tabletWhen: 'width'` uses the width alone). An application can change both limits to fit its layout. Drag the corner of the frame in this example, and the text you typed in the note and the scroll position of a file are kept.

```tsx
import { reactive, type Component } from '@motifx/core';
import { Button, Stack, TabDocumentManager } from '@motifx-community/ui';
import { FILES, fileDocument, source } from './files';
import { problems, toolDocument } from './tools';

/**
 * A manager that follows its own width (`presentation: 'auto'`): drag the frame's corner, or pick a
 * width. Under 560 pixels it shows as on a phone; under 1024 as on a tablet when the screen is a touch
 * screen (with a mouse it stays a desktop). A text and a scroll position are kept across every change:
 * the content moves and is never recreated.
 */
export default function FollowsWidth() {
  const s = reactive({ shown: '', typed: '' });
  let frame!: Component<HTMLDivElement>;
  const docs = new TabDocumentManager({ label: 'Editor that follows its width' });
  docs.element.style.cssText = 'block-size: 100%; inline-size: 100%';
  docs.open(
    { id: 'note', title: 'Note', content: () => <textarea aria-label="Note" style="display: block; box-sizing: border-box; inline-size: 100%; block-size: 100%; padding: var(--mx-space-3); font: inherit; border: 0; resize: none" x-model={() => s.typed} /> },
    { index: 99 },
  );
  for (const file of FILES.slice(0, 4)) docs.open(fileDocument(file.path), { index: 99 });
  // A long one: a plain swipe over it scrolls it, on a phone too.
  docs.open({ id: 'log', title: 'Build log', content: () => source(Array.from({ length: 80 }, (_, i) => `${String(i + 1).padStart(3, ' ')}  step ${i + 1} done`).join('\n')) }, { index: 99 });
  docs.split(docs.activeGroup!, 'right', docs.findDocument('src/orders/index.ts')!);
  docs.dock(toolDocument('problems', 'Problems', problems), 'bottom');
  docs.activate(docs.findDocument('note')!);
  docs.onPresentationChanged((e) => (s.shown = `${e.to} at ${e.width} px`));
  const width = (px: string) => (frame.element.style.inlineSize = px);

  return (
    <>
      <Stack orientation="horizontal" wrap align="center">
        <Button text="390 px" variant="outline" onclick={() => width('390px')} />
        <Button text="720 px" variant="outline" onclick={() => width('720px')} />
        <Button text="Full width" variant="outline" onclick={() => width('100%')} />
        <output class="td-state">{() => s.shown || `Shown as: ${docs.currentPresentation}`}</output>
      </Stack>
      <div
        ref={(c: Component<HTMLDivElement>) => (frame = c)}
        class="td-frame"
        style="box-sizing: border-box; inline-size: 100%; max-inline-size: 100%; min-inline-size: 18rem; block-size: 30rem; overflow: hidden; resize: horizontal; border: var(--mx-border-width-1) solid var(--mx-color-stroke-card); border-radius: var(--mx-radius-lg)"
      >
        {docs}
      </div>
    </>
  );
}
```

## Settings and events

Every part is a setting that can change at runtime, including how dock areas appear in each presentation (an area can set its own), swiping from an edge, the Back button, and how tab menus appear. `onPresentationChanging` can refuse a change.

```tsx
import { reactive } from '@motifx/core';
import { RadioGroup, Stack, Switch, TabDocumentManager, type TabDockPresentation, type TabPresentation } from '@motifx-community/ui';
import { FILES, fileDocument } from './files';
import { outline, problems, toolDocument } from './tools';

/**
 * Every part is a setting: how dock areas show on a phone and a tablet (the outline area says its
 * own), the swipe from an edge, the back button. onPresentationChanging can refuse a change: with
 * "Stay a phone" on, the phone does not go back to a tablet.
 */
export default function PresentationEvents() {
  const s = reactive({
    presentation: 'phone' as TabPresentation,
    phoneDock: 'sheet' as TabDockPresentation,
    tabletDock: 'auto' as TabDockPresentation,
    edge: true,
    back: true,
    stay: false,
    log: [] as string[],
  });
  const log = (line: string) => {
    s.log.push(line);
    if (s.log.length > 5) s.log.shift();
  };
  const docs = new TabDocumentManager({
    label: 'Editor with presentation settings',
    presentation: () => s.presentation,
    phoneDockMode: () => s.phoneDock,
    tabletDockMode: () => s.tabletDock,
    edgeSwipe: () => s.edge,
    backButton: () => s.back,
    onPresentationChanging: (e) => {
      log(`changing ${e.from} → ${e.to}`);
      if (s.stay && e.from === 'phone') e.cancel = true;
    },
    onPresentationChanged: (e) => log(`changed to ${e.to}`),
  });
  docs.element.style.cssText = 'block-size: 30rem; inline-size: 100%';
  for (const file of FILES.slice(0, 3)) docs.open(fileDocument(file.path), { index: 99 });
  docs.dock(toolDocument('problems', 'Problems', problems), 'bottom');
  docs.dock(toolDocument('outline', 'Outline', outline), 'right');
  // The outline's area chooses a drawer for itself on a phone.
  docs.dockArea('right')!.phoneDockMode = 'drawer';
  const modes = [
    { value: 'auto', text: 'Auto' },
    { value: 'sheet', text: 'Sheet' },
    { value: 'drawer', text: 'Drawer' },
    { value: 'hidden', text: 'Hidden' },
  ];

  return (
    <>
      <Stack orientation="horizontal" wrap align="center" gap="lg">
        <RadioGroup
          label="Presentation"
          orientation="horizontal"
          items={[
            { value: 'tablet', text: 'Tablet' },
            { value: 'phone', text: 'Phone' },
          ]}
          itemText="text"
          itemValue="value"
          x-model={() => s.presentation}
        />
        <Switch label="Stay a phone" x-model={() => s.stay} />
        <Switch label="Swipe from an edge" x-model={() => s.edge} />
        <Switch label="Back goes back" x-model={() => s.back} />
      </Stack>
      <Stack orientation="horizontal" wrap align="center" gap="lg">
        <RadioGroup label="Dock areas on a phone" orientation="horizontal" items={modes} itemText="text" itemValue="value" x-model={() => s.phoneDock} />
        <RadioGroup label="On a tablet" orientation="horizontal" items={modes} itemText="text" itemValue="value" x-model={() => s.tabletDock} />
      </Stack>
      <output class="td-state">{() => s.log.join(' · ') || 'No changes yet.'}</output>
      {docs}
    </>
  );
}
```

## The document list on phones

| Gesture or key | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `Tap a row` | Shows that document and closes the list. |
| `Swipe a row sideways` | Closes the document, as determined by `onClosing`. A document that can only be hidden is hidden. Releasing early returns it to its place. |
| `Long press, then drag` | Lifts the row. Drag it up or down within its group, or into the section of another group, and release to move the document there (`onMoving`, `onMoved`). |
| `Long press, let go` | Opens the document's commands in an action sheet. |
| `Search` | Filters by title and description. |
| `Up, Down, Home, End; Enter` | Moves between rows, and Enter shows the document. |
| `Delete; Alt+Up, Alt+Down; the Menu key` | Closes it, moves it one position up or down (past an end, into the previous or next group), or opens its commands. |

## The Back button

Android's Back button and the browser's back gesture use the session history. Each sheet, drawer and list holds one entry while it is open and removes it when it closes another way, so no entries are left behind. The manager holds one entry while it can go back through its documents.

| When | Back |
| --- | --- |
| `A sheet or a drawer is open (a tool, a window, the list, an action sheet)` | The Back button closes the topmost one. |
| `Nothing is open, and the manager has gone through documents` | Goes back to the previous document (`goBack`), as long as there is one. |
| `Nothing to go back to` | The browser handles it, and the page goes back. |

## API reference

### Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `presentation` | `Bind<'auto' \| 'desktop' \| 'tablet' \| 'phone'>` | `'auto'` | How the layout is presented: based on the manager's own width, or always the same way. |
| `phoneWidth` | `Bind<number>` | `560` | Below this width (of the manager, not the screen, in pixels), `auto` uses the phone presentation regardless of the pointer type. |
| `tabletWidth` | `Bind<number>` | `1024` | Below this width, `auto` uses the tablet presentation on touch screens (see `tabletWhen`). |
| `tabletWhen` | `Bind<'touch' \| 'width'>` | `'touch'` | With `'touch'`, the tablet presentation applies only when the device's pointer is a finger (`(pointer: coarse)`, tracked live). With a mouse, a narrow manager stays in the desktop presentation until it is below `phoneWidth`. With `'width'`, only the width is considered. |
| `narrowBars` | `Bind<'compact' \| 'documents'>` | `'compact'` | The appearance of the document group bars on a tablet or phone. By default, they use the `compact…` settings (no scroll buttons, shrinking tabs, small buttons, and a single document as a title), like the dock areas. `'documents'` keeps the desktop bar. Change the `compact…` props to adjust this appearance. |
| `phoneDockMode` | `Bind<'auto' \| 'sheet' \| 'drawer' \| 'hidden'>` | `'sheet'` | How dock areas appear on a phone. An area's own `phoneDockMode` takes precedence. |
| `tabletDockMode` | `Bind<'auto' \| 'sheet' \| 'drawer' \| 'hidden'>` | `'auto'` | How dock areas appear on a tablet. `auto` uses a drawer for the sides and top, and a sheet for the bottom. An area's own `tabletDockMode` takes precedence. |
| `edgeSwipe` | `Bind<boolean>` | `true` | On a tablet or phone, swiping in from an edge opens the dock area there as a drawer. |
| `backButton` | `Bind<boolean>` | `true` | On a phone, the browser's back action goes back through the documents once nothing is open on top. |
| `menuPresentation` | `Bind<'menu' \| 'sheet' \| 'auto' \| null>` | `null` | How tab menus appear. `null` uses an action sheet on a phone, a sheet for touch on a tablet, and a menu in the desktop presentation. |
| `onPresentationChanging` | `(e: PresentationChangingEventArgs) => void` | — | `{ from, to, width, cancel }`. If canceled, the presentation stays the same until the width or the setting changes again. |
| `onPresentationChanged` | `(e: PresentationChangedEventArgs) => void` | — | `{ from, to, width }`. |

### Members

| Member | Returns | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `currentPresentation` | read-only, reactive | The current presentation: `'desktop'`, `'tablet'` or `'phone'`. |
| `showDocumentList(), hideDocumentList()` | `boolean` | On a phone, opens or closes the list of open documents. `documentListOpen` is reactive. |
| `showTool(doc), hideTool(area)` | `boolean` | On a tablet or phone, opens a dock area's drawer or sheet with that document shown, or closes it. `activate(doc)` on a tool, or on a document in a floating window, also opens its drawer or sheet. |
| `TabDockArea.phoneDockMode, tabletDockMode` | read/write, reactive | The area's own setting. `null` uses the manager's setting. |
| `split, move, float, dock, saveLayout…` | unchanged | These work as in the desktop presentation and change the layout, which appears as the current presentation allows. `moveToNewWindow` returns `null` on a phone. |

The drawers and sheets are the kit's [Drawer](drawer.md) and [BottomSheet](bottomsheet.md), and the action sheet is its [ActionSheet](actionsheet.md).

# TabDocumentManager: A whole workspace

> TabDocumentManager · @motifx-community/ui 0.1.0-beta.5

A complete screen built from kit components: a menu bar, the manager, a DataGrid with every feature enabled, forms, and a tool docked at the bottom. Each part is the same component documented on its own page, and the manager simply hosts them.

## An order desk

The orders grid supports filtering, grouping, search, summaries, batch editing and row actions, which are also in its context menu. Its tab shows the unsaved mark while edits are waiting to be saved. Open a customer from a row, using its menu or the actions column, and the customer's card opens in the group on the right. Drag a tab to a guide, float it, move it to a new window or use the menus, and the grid keeps its filters, scroll position and unsaved edits wherever it goes.

```tsx
import type { ComponentBase } from '@motifx/core';
import { Button, confirm, DataGrid, FormLayout, type FormItem, type GridColumn } from '@motifx-community/ui';
import { makeOrders, type Order } from './orders';

const columns: GridColumn<Order>[] = [
  { field: 'id', title: 'No', type: 'number', width: 70 },
  { field: 'customer', title: 'Customer', width: 160 },
  { field: 'city', title: 'City', width: 110 },
  { field: 'amount', title: 'Amount', type: 'number', width: 100 },
];

/** A grid of orders that fills its tab. */
export function ordersGrid(count = 60): ComponentBase {
  return <DataGrid rows={makeOrders(count)} rowKey="id" columns={columns} label="Orders" style="block-size: 100%" />;
}

/** The fields a customer is edited with. */
export interface Customer {
  name: string;
  email: string;
  city: string;
}

/** The forms open over each customer: a copy of a document has a form of its own over the same object. */
const formsOf = new WeakMap<Customer, Set<FormLayout<Customer>>>();

/**
 * A form over a customer: what is typed goes straight into it. The form reads the object as it is, so the other forms
 * over the same customer are told to read the field again.
 */
export function customerForm(customer: Customer): ComponentBase {
  const items: FormItem[] = [
    { field: 'name', label: 'Name', required: true },
    { field: 'email', label: 'Email', editor: 'email' },
    { field: 'city', label: 'City' },
  ];
  const forms = formsOf.get(customer) ?? new Set<FormLayout<Customer>>();
  formsOf.set(customer, forms);
  return (
    <div style="padding: var(--mx-space-4); max-inline-size: 32rem">
      <FormLayout<Customer>
        data={customer}
        items={items}
        ref={(form: FormLayout<Customer>) => {
          forms.add(form);
          form.motif.setDisposable(() => forms.delete(form));
        }}
        onFieldChanged={(e) => {
          for (const other of forms) if (other.data === e.data && !other.isDisposed) other.refreshField(e.field);
        }}
      />
    </div>
  );
}

/** A few paragraphs of plain text. */
export function notes(title: string): ComponentBase {
  return (
    <div style="padding: var(--mx-space-4); max-inline-size: 40rem">
      <h3 style="margin-block-start: 0">{title}</h3>
      <p>Any component can be a document: a form, a grid, a chart or plain text like this.</p>
      <p>Drag the line between two groups, or focus it with Tab and use the arrow keys. A double click on it gives the groups the same size.</p>
    </div>
  );
}

const CITIES = ['İstanbul', 'Ankara', 'İzmir', 'London', 'New York'];

/** A customer card: text fields and a city drop-down over a reactive customer, and a button that opens a dialog. */
export function customerCard(customer: Customer): ComponentBase {
  const items: FormItem[] = [
    { field: 'name', label: 'Name', required: true },
    { field: 'email', label: 'Email', editor: 'email' },
    { field: 'city', label: 'City', editor: 'dropdown', editorProps: { items: CITIES } },
  ];
  let card: ComponentBase | null = null;
  // The dialog opens where the card is: in a new window, there.
  const clear = async () => {
    if (await confirm('Clear the customer card?', { title: 'Clear', host: card! })) Object.assign(customer, { name: '', email: '', city: '' });
  };
  return (
    <div ref={(c: ComponentBase) => (card = c)} style="padding: var(--mx-space-4); max-inline-size: 32rem">
      <FormLayout data={customer} items={items} />
      <Button text="Clear…" variant="outline" onclick={clear} />
    </div>
  );
}
```

## Example files

`Workspace.tsx`

```tsx
import { reactive, type ComponentBase } from '@motifx/core';
import { DataGrid, MenuBar, TabDocument, TabDocumentManager, type GridAction, type GridColumn, type GridSummary, type MenuItem } from '@motifx-community/ui';
import type { Order } from '../../datagrid/examples/order';
import { columns, makeOrders } from '../../datagrid/examples/orders';
import { customerCard, type Customer } from './contents';

// Narrow, the grid moves columns into the row's details, the lowest number first; the customer always stays.
const PRIORITY: Partial<Record<keyof Order, number>> = { note: 0, paid: 1, date: 2, city: 3, status: 4, id: 5, amount: 6 };
const deskColumns: GridColumn<Order>[] = columns.map((c) => ({
  ...c,
  sticky: undefined,
  hidingPriority: PRIORITY[c.field as keyof Order],
  width: c.field === 'customer' ? 150 : c.field === 'amount' ? 100 : c.width,
}));

const summary: GridSummary<Order> = {
  totalItems: [
    { column: 'id', summaryType: 'count', showInColumn: 'customer' },
    { column: 'amount', summaryType: 'sum' },
  ],
  groupItems: [{ column: 'amount', summaryType: 'sum', alignByColumn: true }],
};

/**
 * An order desk: a menu bar over the manager, the orders in a full grid (filters, grouping, search,
 * summaries, batch editing, row actions and their context menu, export), a customer card that opens
 * in a tab from a row, and an activity log docked at the bottom.
 */
export default function Workspace() {
  const s = reactive({ orders: makeOrders(500), selected: 0, log: [] as { id: number; text: string }[], gridReady: 0 });
  let grid: DataGrid<Order> | null = null;
  let logId = 0;
  const write = (text: string) => {
    s.log.unshift({ id: ++logId, text });
    s.log.splice(40);
  };

  const docs = new TabDocumentManager({ label: 'Order desk', dockGuides: true, dockAreaSize: { bottom: 160 } });
  docs.element.style.cssText = 'block-size: 36rem; inline-size: 100%';

  const customers = new Map<string, Customer>();
  const openCustomer = (name: string) => {
    const id = `customer:${name}`;
    const open = docs.findDocument(id);
    if (open) return void docs.activate(open, true);
    let customer = customers.get(name);
    if (!customer) {
      customer = reactive({ name, email: `${name.split(' ')[0].toLowerCase()}@example.com`, city: '' });
      customers.set(name, customer);
    }
    const card = customer;
    const doc = new TabDocument({ id, type: 'customer', title: () => card.name || 'New customer', description: 'Customer', content: () => customerCard(card) });
    // Customers open beside the orders: in the group on the right, or in a new one there.
    const side = docs.groups.find((g) => g !== orders.group && !g.dockArea && !g.window && !g.browserWindow);
    if (side) docs.open(doc, { group: side, focus: true });
    else {
      const opened = docs.open(doc, { group: orders.group ?? undefined, focus: true });
      if (opened && orders.group) docs.split(orders.group, 'right', opened);
    }
  };

  const openOrder: GridAction<Order> = { id: 'customer', text: 'Open the customer', onclick: (row) => openCustomer(row.customer) };
  const approve: GridAction<Order> = {
    id: 'approve',
    text: 'Approve',
    tone: 'accent',
    visible: (row) => row.status === 'Draft',
    onclickMany: (rows) => {
      for (const row of rows) row.status = 'Approved';
      write(`${rows.length} orders approved`);
    },
    onclick: (row) => {
      row.status = 'Approved';
      write(`order ${row.id} approved`);
    },
  };

  const ordersGrid = (): ComponentBase => (
    <DataGrid
      style="block-size: 100%"
      rows={() => s.orders}
      rowKey="id"
      columns={deskColumns}
      label="Orders"
      locale="en"
      saveMode="batch"
      summary={summary}
      export={{ formats: ['csv'] }}
      actions={(_row: Order, state) => (state.isRemoved ? ['restore'] : [openOrder, approve, 'edit', 'remove'])}
      settings={{
        editable: true,
        selection: 'multiple',
        filterRow: true,
        headerFilter: true,
        groupPanel: true,
        searchPanel: true,
        columnChooserButton: true,
        exportButton: true,
        totalSummary: true,
        groupSummary: true,
        rowStatus: true,
        striped: true,
        actionsContextMenu: true,
        // Narrow beside a customer: the actions stay one "…" button, and columns that do not fit go into the row's details.
        actionsDisplay: 'menu',
        actionsWidth: 48,
        columnHidingEnabled: true,
      }}
      onSelectionChanged={(e) => (s.selected = e.selection.all ? s.orders.length - e.selection.except.length : e.selection.keys.length)}
      onSaved={() => write('changes saved')}
      ref={(g: DataGrid<Order>) => {
        grid = g;
        s.gridReady++;
      }}
    />
  );
  // The tab shows the unsaved mark while the grid has edits that are not saved.
  const orders = new TabDocument({
    id: 'orders',
    type: 'orders',
    title: 'Orders',
    pinned: true,
    closable: false,
    badge: () => s.orders.length,
    dirty: () => s.gridReady > 0 && !!grid?.hasChanges,
    content: ordersGrid,
  });
  const activity = new TabDocument({
    id: 'activity',
    type: 'tool',
    title: 'Activity',
    closable: false,
    content: () => (
      <ol style="margin: 0; padding: var(--mx-space-2) var(--mx-space-4); font-size: var(--mx-font-size-caption)" aria-label="Activity">
        {s.log.map((line) => (
          <li key={line.id}>{line.text}</li>
        ))}
      </ol>
    ),
  });

  docs.open(orders);
  // The log waits folded at the bottom edge: a click on its title slides it out.
  docs.dock(activity, 'bottom');
  docs.autoHide(docs.dockArea('bottom')!);
  docs.activate(orders);

  docs.onOpened((e) => write(`opened ${e.document.title}`));
  docs.onClosed((e) => write(`closed ${e.document.title}`));
  docs.onMoved((e) => write(`moved ${e.document.title}`));
  docs.onFloated((e) => write(`${e.document?.title ?? 'a group'} floats`));
  docs.onDocked((e) => write(`${e.document?.title ?? 'a group'} docked${e.side ? ` on the ${e.side}` : ''}`));
  docs.onHidden((e) => write(`${e.document.title} hidden`));

  const active = () => docs.activeDocument;
  const menu: MenuItem[] = [
    {
      text: '&File',
      items: [
        { text: 'New customer', click: () => openCustomer(`Customer ${customers.size + 1}`) },
        { text: 'Reopen closed', enabled: () => docs.documents.length > 0, click: () => docs.reopenClosed() },
        { text: 'Close', shortcut: 'Ctrl+Alt+W', beginGroup: true, enabled: () => !!active()?.closable, click: () => active() && docs.close(active()!) },
        { text: 'Close all', click: () => docs.closeAll() },
      ],
    },
    {
      text: '&Orders',
      items: [
        { text: 'Save changes', enabled: () => s.gridReady > 0 && !!grid?.hasChanges, click: () => grid?.saveEditData() },
        { text: 'Undo changes', enabled: () => s.gridReady > 0 && !!grid?.hasChanges, click: () => grid?.cancelEditData() },
        { text: 'Group by city', beginGroup: true, click: () => grid?.groupBy('city') },
        { text: 'Clear grouping', click: () => grid?.clearGrouping() },
        { text: 'Clear filters', click: () => grid?.clearFilters() },
        { text: 'Choose columns…', beginGroup: true, click: () => grid?.showColumnChooser() },
        { text: 'Export to CSV', click: () => grid?.exportCsv({ fileName: 'orders' }) },
      ],
    },
    {
      text: '&View',
      items: [
        { text: 'Split right', click: () => docs.activeGroup && docs.split(docs.activeGroup, 'right') },
        { text: 'Split down', click: () => docs.activeGroup && docs.split(docs.activeGroup, 'down') },
        { text: 'Maximize the group', beginGroup: true, click: () => docs.activeGroup && docs.maximizeGroup(docs.activeGroup) },
        { text: 'Restore the groups', click: () => docs.restoreGroups() },
        { text: 'Same sizes', click: () => docs.evenSizes() },
      ],
    },
    {
      text: '&Window',
      items: [
        { text: 'Float the active tab', enabled: () => !!active() && !active()!.window, click: () => active() && docs.float(active()!) },
        { text: 'Move into a new window', enabled: () => !!active() && !active()!.browserWindow, click: () => active() && docs.moveToNewWindow(active()!) },
        { text: 'Dock back', enabled: () => !!active()?.window, click: () => active() && docs.dock(active()!) },
        {
          text: 'Show the activity',
          beginGroup: true,
          // Its area's close button hides it because it cannot close. When shown again, it returns to its previous place.
          click: () => (activity.isHidden ? docs.show(activity, { focus: true }) : activity.dockArea?.autoHidden ? docs.showAutoHidden(activity) : docs.activate(activity, true)),
        },
      ],
    },
  ];

  return (
    <>
      <MenuBar items={menu} label="Order desk" />
      {docs}
      <output class="td-state">{() => `${s.orders.length} orders · ${s.selected} selected${s.gridReady > 0 && grid?.hasChanges ? ' · unsaved changes' : ''}`}</output>
    </>
  );
}
```

`contents.tsx`

```tsx
import type { ComponentBase } from '@motifx/core';
import { Button, confirm, DataGrid, FormLayout, type FormItem, type GridColumn } from '@motifx-community/ui';
import { makeOrders, type Order } from './orders';

const columns: GridColumn<Order>[] = [
  { field: 'id', title: 'No', type: 'number', width: 70 },
  { field: 'customer', title: 'Customer', width: 160 },
  { field: 'city', title: 'City', width: 110 },
  { field: 'amount', title: 'Amount', type: 'number', width: 100 },
];

/** A grid of orders that fills its tab. */
export function ordersGrid(count = 60): ComponentBase {
  return <DataGrid rows={makeOrders(count)} rowKey="id" columns={columns} label="Orders" style="block-size: 100%" />;
}

/** The fields a customer is edited with. */
export interface Customer {
  name: string;
  email: string;
  city: string;
}

/** The forms open over each customer: a copy of a document has a form of its own over the same object. */
const formsOf = new WeakMap<Customer, Set<FormLayout<Customer>>>();

/**
 * A form over a customer: what is typed goes straight into it. The form reads the object as it is, so the other forms
 * over the same customer are told to read the field again.
 */
export function customerForm(customer: Customer): ComponentBase {
  const items: FormItem[] = [
    { field: 'name', label: 'Name', required: true },
    { field: 'email', label: 'Email', editor: 'email' },
    { field: 'city', label: 'City' },
  ];
  const forms = formsOf.get(customer) ?? new Set<FormLayout<Customer>>();
  formsOf.set(customer, forms);
  return (
    <div style="padding: var(--mx-space-4); max-inline-size: 32rem">
      <FormLayout<Customer>
        data={customer}
        items={items}
        ref={(form: FormLayout<Customer>) => {
          forms.add(form);
          form.motif.setDisposable(() => forms.delete(form));
        }}
        onFieldChanged={(e) => {
          for (const other of forms) if (other.data === e.data && !other.isDisposed) other.refreshField(e.field);
        }}
      />
    </div>
  );
}

/** A few paragraphs of plain text. */
export function notes(title: string): ComponentBase {
  return (
    <div style="padding: var(--mx-space-4); max-inline-size: 40rem">
      <h3 style="margin-block-start: 0">{title}</h3>
      <p>Any component can be a document: a form, a grid, a chart or plain text like this.</p>
      <p>Drag the line between two groups, or focus it with Tab and use the arrow keys. A double click on it gives the groups the same size.</p>
    </div>
  );
}

const CITIES = ['İstanbul', 'Ankara', 'İzmir', 'London', 'New York'];

/** A customer card: text fields and a city drop-down over a reactive customer, and a button that opens a dialog. */
export function customerCard(customer: Customer): ComponentBase {
  const items: FormItem[] = [
    { field: 'name', label: 'Name', required: true },
    { field: 'email', label: 'Email', editor: 'email' },
    { field: 'city', label: 'City', editor: 'dropdown', editorProps: { items: CITIES } },
  ];
  let card: ComponentBase | null = null;
  // The dialog opens where the card is: in a new window, there.
  const clear = async () => {
    if (await confirm('Clear the customer card?', { title: 'Clear', host: card! })) Object.assign(customer, { name: '', email: '', city: '' });
  };
  return (
    <div ref={(c: ComponentBase) => (card = c)} style="padding: var(--mx-space-4); max-inline-size: 32rem">
      <FormLayout data={customer} items={items} />
      <Button text="Clear…" variant="outline" onclick={clear} />
    </div>
  );
}
```

# Scheduler

> Scheduler · @motifx-community/ui 0.1.0-beta.5

A full-featured calendar for appointments across days and hours. It provides day, week, work week and month views, all-day and multi-day bars, side-by-side display of overlapping appointments, and a "+N more" link when a day is full. Appointments can come from an array or a data source, and every setting can change at runtime.

## Import

```tsx
import { Scheduler } from '@motifx-community/ui';
```

## Getting started

Provide the appointments. By default, it reads `startDate`, `endDate`, `text` and `allDay`, and `fields` maps other names. The toolbar moves by the view's step, and the date opens a calendar.

```tsx
import { reactive } from '@motifx/core';

export interface Meeting {
  id: number;
  text: string;
  startDate: Date;
  endDate: Date;
  allDay?: boolean;
  color?: string;
  description?: string;
}

/** A week of appointments around today, so the examples always show something. */
export function sampleAppointments(): Meeting[] {
  const today = new Date();
  const day = (offset: number, hour: number, minute = 0) => new Date(today.getFullYear(), today.getMonth(), today.getDate() + offset, hour, minute);
  return reactive([
```

## Views and settings

`views` lists the built-in types or custom views, each with a name, a caption, an `intervalCount` and settings that override the scheduler's. Every setting accepts a value or a function that is tracked.

```tsx
import { reactive } from '@motifx/core';
import { Scheduler, Switch } from '@motifx-community/ui';
import { sampleAppointments, type Meeting } from './sample-appointments';

/** Views of its own (three days, two weeks) next to the built-in ones, and settings bound to switches. */
export default function Views() {
  const s = reactive({
    allDay: true,
    dim: true,
    cascade: false,
    quarter: false,
    holidays: true,
  });
  // Every Friday is a holiday here, to show the appearance.
  const friday = (date: Date) => date.getDay() === 5;
  return (
    <div class="sched-demo">
      <div class="docs-flow">
        <Switch label="All-day panel" x-model={() => s.allDay} />
        <Switch label="Ended ones quieter" x-model={() => s.dim} />
        <Switch label="Cascade" x-model={() => s.cascade} />
        <Switch label="15-minute cells" x-model={() => s.quarter} />
        <Switch label="Fridays off" x-model={() => s.holidays} />
      </div>
      <Scheduler<Meeting>
        appointments={sampleAppointments()}
        views={[
          'day',
          { type: 'day', name: 'threeDays', text: '3 days', intervalCount: 3 },
          'workWeek',
          { type: 'week', name: 'twoWeeks', text: '2 weeks', intervalCount: 2 },
          'month',
        ]}
        currentView="threeDays"
        startDayHour={8}
        endDayHour={20}
        allDayPanel={() => s.allDay}
        dimPast={() => s.dim}
        overlapMode={() => (s.cascade ? 'cascade' : 'columns')}
        cellDuration={() => (s.quarter ? 15 : 30)}
        isHoliday={() => (s.holidays ? friday : null)}
      />
    </div>
  );
}
```

## From a data source

With a `DataSource` (REST, OData or a service), it requests only the visible days and requests again when the view moves. It shows a loading state, and offers a retry if a request fails.

```tsx
import { data } from '@motifx-community/data';

/** Rows in memory that answer a little later, the way a server does; for the examples. */
export class SlowAdapter<T extends object, K> extends data.ArrayAdapter<T, K> {
  constructor(
    options: data.ArrayAdapterOptions<T>,
    private readonly delayMs = 300,
  ) {
    super(options);
  }

  override async load(options: data.LoadOptions = {}): Promise<data.LoadResult<T>> {
    await new Promise((done) => setTimeout(done, this.delayMs));
    return super.load(options);
  }
}
```

## Templates

`appointmentTemplate` customizes the content of each appointment. The scheduler still positions it, colors it with `color` and provides its accessible name.

```tsx
import { Scheduler, type AppointmentTemplateContext } from '@motifx-community/ui';
import { sampleAppointments, type Meeting } from './sample-appointments';

/** The content of each appointment drawn by a template. The scheduler still positions it, colors it and provides its name. */
export default function Templates() {
  const template = (c: AppointmentTemplateContext<Meeting>) =>
    c.allDay ? (
      <strong>{c.text}</strong>
    ) : (
      <div class="sched-card">
        <strong>{c.text}</strong>
        <span>{c.allDay ? 'All day' : c.time}</span>
        {c.appointment.color ? <span class="sched-tag">{c.appointment.color === '#c62828' ? 'urgent' : 'team'}</span> : <span class="sched-tag">personal</span>}
      </div>
    );
  return (
    <div class="sched-demo">
      <Scheduler<Meeting> appointments={sampleAppointments()} currentView="day" startDayHour={8} endDayHour={18} appointmentTemplate={template} />
    </div>
  );
}
```

## Programmatic use

```tsx
import { reactive } from '@motifx/core';
import { Button, Scheduler, Stack } from '@motifx-community/ui';
import { sampleAppointments, type Meeting } from './sample-appointments';

/** A scheduler created with `new`, added programmatically and controlled through its methods. */
export default function Programmatic() {
  const state = reactive({ said: '' });
  let host: Stack | null = null;
  let scheduler: Scheduler<Meeting> | null = null;

  const make = () => {
    if (scheduler) return;
    scheduler = new Scheduler<Meeting>({
      appointments: sampleAppointments(),
      currentView: 'workWeek',
      locale: 'tr-TR',
      firstDayOfWeek: 1,
    });
    scheduler.onDateChanged(
      (e) => (state.said = `Shows ${e.range.start.toLocaleDateString('tr-TR')} – ${new Date(e.range.end.getTime() - 1).toLocaleDateString('tr-TR')}`),
    );
    scheduler.onSelectionChanged(
      (e) =>
        (state.said = e.selection
          ? `Selected ${e.selection.start.toLocaleString('tr-TR')} – ${e.selection.end.toLocaleTimeString('tr-TR')}`
          : 'Nothing selected'),
    );
    host?.controls.add(scheduler);
  };
  // The work week shows Monday to Friday: the next of those days.
  const nextWorkday = () => {
    const t = new Date();
    let start = new Date(t.getFullYear(), t.getMonth(), t.getDate() + 1, 9);
    while (start.getDay() === 0 || start.getDay() === 6) start = new Date(start.getFullYear(), start.getMonth(), start.getDate() + 1, 9);
    scheduler?.showDate(start);
    scheduler?.selectCells({
      start,
      end: new Date(start.getTime() + 90 * 60_000),
      allDay: false,
    });
    scheduler?.scrollToTime(8);
  };
  return (
    <div class="sched-demo">
      <div class="docs-flow">
        <Button text="Create" variant="outline" onclick={make} />
        <Button text="Previous" variant="outline" onclick={() => scheduler?.previous()} />
        <Button text="Next" variant="outline" onclick={() => scheduler?.next()} />
        <Button text="Select the next workday 9:00–10:30" variant="outline" onclick={nextWorkday} />
        <Button text="Month" variant="outline" onclick={() => scheduler?.showView('month')} />
      </div>
      <p class="sched-log" role="status">
        {() => state.said}
      </p>
      <Stack ref={(c: Stack) => (host = c)} />
    </div>
  );
}
```

## Keyboard

| Key | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `Arrows` | Moves across the cells, mirrored on right-to-left pages. Moving past the first or last day advances the view. Up from the first time moves to the all-day panel, and in the month view Up and Down move by a week. |
| `Shift + arrows` | Extends the selection from the starting cell. |
| `Home / End` | Moves to the first or last day of the row. With Ctrl, moves to the first or last cell. |
| `Page Up / Page Down` | Moves up or down one screen of times. In the month view, moves to the previous or next month. |
| `Enter, Space` | On a cell, equivalent to a double-click and a click. The same applies to an appointment. |
| `Escape` | Clears the selection. |
| `Tab` | The toolbar, the cells (one Tab stop), the all-day panel, and then each appointment. |
| `T, N / J, P / K` | Today, next and previous (the `keys` option, not active in a text field). |
| `D, W, X, M` | Day, week, work week and month view. |

## Accessibility

| Topic | Details |
| --- | --- |
| `Cells` | The time grid is a `grid`, as are the all-day panel and the month, with one Tab stop. Each cell is named by its day and time and has `aria-selected`. |
| `Appointments` | Buttons in their own group after the cells, named by their time, text and day ("continues" when they span days). |
| `Changes` | A new date or view is announced in a polite live region (`announce`). |
| `Loading` | `aria-busy` while the data source loads. A failed load is an alert with Retry. |

## Localization

Dates and times come from `Intl` using `locale` (12 or 24-hour clock, first day of the week). Strings come from `uiLocale` (English, Turkish), and `texts` can override each one.

## Styling

| Hook | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `.mx-scheduler` | `data-view="day\|week\|workWeek\|month"`. |
| `.mx-scheduler__bar, __title, __view-button` | The toolbar. |
| `.mx-scheduler__date, __all-day, __cells, __cell` | The day views: `data-today`, `data-work`, `data-hour-start`, `aria-selected`. |
| `.mx-scheduler__month-cell` | `data-today`, `data-outside`, `data-holiday`. |
| `.mx-scheduler__appointment` | `data-kind="timed\|bar\|chip"`, `data-before`, `data-after`, `data-short`, `data-past`, `data-disabled`. Its color is `--_color`. |
| `.mx-scheduler__more, __more-list, __now` | "+N more", its list, and the current time indicator. |
| `scheduler.scheduler, bar, head, date, day-number, hour, time-row, cell, now, week-row, appointment, tooltip, more, more-item, state, …` | Units: every part in each state (for a cell: `today`, `off`, `holiday`, `month`, `outside`, `weekend`, `past`, `hover`, `selected`, `focus` …). |
| `scheduler.height, slot-height, ruler-width, lane-size, appointment-tint, appointment-*-width, appointment-*-mix, chip-*, …` | Sizes, and the ratios that blend an appointment's color into its fill, text and four edges. |

## API reference

### Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `appointments` | `Bind<readonly T[]>` | `[]` | The in-memory appointments. Your data can be plain or reactive, and the component reads it as it is. After changing it in place, call `refresh()`. Changes made by the component (the form, a drag, the methods) appear immediately. |
| `dataSource` | `Bind<DataSource \| null>` | `null` | Appointments from `@motifx-community/data`, used instead of `appointments`. |
| `remoteFiltering` | `Bind<boolean>` | `true` | Requests only the visible days from the data source, by adding a filter on the start and end fields. |
| `fields` | `Bind<Partial<SchedulerFields>>` | See below | The fields it reads: `key`, `start`, `end`, `text`, `allDay`, `description`, `color`, `disabled` and `visible`. |
| `views` | `Bind<(type \| SchedulerView)[]>` | Day, week, work week, month | The available views. A `SchedulerView` has its own `name`, `text`, `intervalCount`, hours, `cellDuration`, `allDayPanel` and `maxAppointmentsPerCell`. |
| `currentView` | `Bind<string>` | The week view | The current view, by name. |
| `currentDate` | `Bind<Date>` | Today | The date the view shows. |
| `firstDayOfWeek` | `Bind<number \| null>` | From the locale | 0 (Sunday) through 6 (Saturday). |
| `workDays` | `Bind<number[]>` | Monday to Friday | The work week, and the days shaded separately. |
| `workStartHour / workEndHour` | `Bind<number>` | 9 / 17 | The work hours. The rest are shaded. |
| `startDayHour / endDayHour` | `Bind<number>` | 0 / 24 | The hours shown in the day columns. |
| `cellDuration` | `Bind<number>` | 30 | The duration of a cell, in minutes. |
| `allDayPanel` | `Bind<boolean>` | `true` | Shows the all-day and multi-day panel above the hours. |
| `allDayLines` | `Bind<number>` | 3 | The number of lines the all-day panel shows before "+N more". |
| `maxAppointmentsPerCell` | `Bind<number \\| 'auto'>` | `'auto'` | The number of appointments in a month day before "+N more". `auto` shows as many as fit. |
| `overlapMode` | `Bind<'columns' \\| 'cascade'>` | `'columns'` | Shows overlapping appointments side by side, or stacked with a slight offset. |
| `isHoliday` | `Bind<(date) => boolean>` | — | Days marked as holidays. |
| `showCurrentTime` | `Bind<boolean>` | `true` | Shows a line at the current time. |
| `dimPast` | `Bind<boolean>` | `false` | Dims appointments that have ended. |
| `scrollHour` | `Bind<number \| null>` | Work start | The hour the day columns scroll to. By default, this is the work start, or the current time later in the day. |
| `toolbar` | `Bind<boolean>` | `true` | Shows the toolbar with today, previous, next, the date and the views. |
| `locale` | `Bind<string>` | From the page | Dates, times and the week. |
| `appointmentTemplate` | `Bind<(context) => Component>` | — | Customizes an appointment's content: `{ appointment, start, end, text, time, allDay, view }`. |
| `texts` | `Bind<Partial<UiStrings>>` | — | Strings that override `uiLocale`. |
| `keys` | `Bind<Partial<SchedulerKeys>>` | see Keyboard | The key bindings. An empty list disables a binding. |
| `announce` | `Bind<boolean>` | `true` | Announces a new date or view to screen readers. |

### Methods and properties

| Member | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `goToday(), next(), previous()` | Moves the view, raising `onDateChanging`. |
| `showDate(date), showView(name)` | Shows a date or another view. |
| `scrollToTime(hour, minute?)` | Scrolls the day columns to a time of day. |
| `selectCells(cell \| null)` | Selects the cells for a time range in the visible days. |
| `appointmentsIn(start, end), findAppointment(key)` | Returns the appointments in a time range, or one by its key. |
| `refresh()` | Re-reads the appointments and resources. Your data can be plain or reactive, and the component reads it as it is. After changing it in place, call `refresh()`. |
| `refreshAppointment(appointment)` | Re-reads one appointment after it has been changed in place. For an occurrence, this means its series. |
| `refreshResources()` | Re-reads the resources after their items have been changed in place. |
| `visibleRange, resolvedView, selectedCells, shownAppointments, loading` | Reactive state. |
| `textOf(key, values?)` | A string from `uiLocale` or `texts`, with its values filled in. |

### Events

| Event | Arguments |
| --- | --- |
| `onViewChanging / onViewChanged` | `{ from, to, byUser, cancel }`: a view change. Cancel to keep the current view. |
| `onDateChanging / onDateChanged` | `{ from, to, byUser, cancel }` and `{ …, range }`: today, previous, next or a selected date. |
| `onCellClick / onCellDblClick` | `{ cell: { start, end, allDay }, event, cancel }`. Also raised by Space and Enter on a cell. |
| `onAppointmentClick / onAppointmentDblClick` | `{ appointment, start, end, event, cancel }`. Also raised by Space and Enter on an appointment. |
| `onSelectionChanged` | `{ selection }`: the selected cells as one time range, or `null`. |
| `onContentReady` | `{ range, appointments }`: after a load, a new date or view, or new data. |
| `onMoreOpening` | `{ date, appointments, cancel }`: "+N more" was clicked. Cancel to display the day yourself. |

`FromSource.tsx`

```tsx
import { reactive } from '@motifx/core';
import { data } from '@motifx-community/data';
import { Scheduler } from '@motifx-community/ui';
import { SlowAdapter } from '../../../shared/slow-adapter';
import { sampleAppointments, type Meeting } from './sample-appointments';

/** Appointments from a data source that responds with a delay, like a server. Only the displayed days are requested. */
export default function FromSource() {
  const asked = reactive({ text: '' });
  const adapter = new SlowAdapter<Meeting, number>({ data: sampleAppointments(), key: 'id' }, 600);
  const source = new data.DataSource<Meeting, number>({
    adapter,
    // 'all': a view needs every appointment of its days, and the scheduler requests only those days.
    loadMode: 'all',
  });
  source.onChanged((e) => {
    if (e.reason !== 'loading') return;
    const filter = JSON.stringify(source.filter);
    asked.text = `Asked: ${filter.length > 140 ? filter.slice(0, 140) + '…' : filter}`;
  });
  return (
    <div class="sched-demo" onDisposing={() => source.dispose()}>
      <Scheduler<Meeting> dataSource={source} currentView="month" />
      <p class="sched-log">{() => asked.text}</p>
    </div>
  );
}
```

`slow-adapter.ts`

```tsx
import { data } from '@motifx-community/data';

/** Rows in memory that answer a little later, the way a server does; for the examples. */
export class SlowAdapter<T extends object, K> extends data.ArrayAdapter<T, K> {
  constructor(
    options: data.ArrayAdapterOptions<T>,
    private readonly delayMs = 300,
  ) {
    super(options);
  }

  override async load(options: data.LoadOptions = {}): Promise<data.LoadResult<T>> {
    await new Promise((done) => setTimeout(done, this.delayMs));
    return super.load(options);
  }
}
```


---

# Scheduler: Editing

> Scheduler · @motifx-community/ui 0.1.0-beta.5

Users can add, move, resize, copy and delete appointments with the pointer and the keyboard, and you can do the same programmatically. Every change raises its event first, can wait for a server, and is reverted if saving fails.

## Drag, resize and edit

While dragging, the appointment itself moves to the new position, on the `snapMinutes` step, and the view scrolls near the edges. On touch screens, a long press starts a drag.

## Saving to a server

With a data source, changes go through its adapter. While saving, the appointment stays where it was placed and cannot be changed. If saving fails, `onDataError` reports it and the appointment reverts.

```tsx
import { data } from '@motifx-community/data';

/** Rows in memory that answer a little later, the way a server does; for the examples. */
export class SlowAdapter<T extends object, K> extends data.ArrayAdapter<T, K> {
  constructor(
    options: data.ArrayAdapterOptions<T>,
    private readonly delayMs = 300,
  ) {
    super(options);
  }

  override async load(options: data.LoadOptions = {}): Promise<data.LoadResult<T>> {
    await new Promise((done) => setTimeout(done, this.delayMs));
    return super.load(options);
  }
}
```

## The appointment form

`onFormOpening` receives the form's `items` (a `FormLayout`) and its `data`. You can add or remove fields, or cancel and show your own form.

```tsx
import { Scheduler, type FormOpeningEventArgs } from '@motifx-community/ui';
import { sampleAppointments, type Meeting } from './sample-appointments';

type Booking = Meeting & { room?: string };

const rooms = [
  { value: 'blue', text: 'Blue room' },
  { value: 'green', text: 'Green room' },
  { value: 'online', text: 'Online' },
];

/** The form gets a field of its own (a room) and loses the description; the room is written to the appointment's `room` field. */
export default function CustomForm() {
  const opening = (e: FormOpeningEventArgs<Booking>) => {
    e.data.room = e.appointment?.room ?? 'online';
    e.items.splice(
      e.items.findIndex((item) => item.field === 'description'),
      1,
    );
    e.items.push({ field: 'room', label: 'Room', editor: 'dropdown', editorProps: { items: rooms }, colSpan: 'all' });
    e.form.title = e.appointment ? `Edit ${e.appointment.text}` : 'Book a room';
  };
  return (
    <div class="sched-demo">
      <Scheduler<Booking> appointments={sampleAppointments()} currentView="day" startDayHour={8} endDayHour={18} onFormOpening={opening} />
    </div>
  );
}
```

## Validation rules

`onMoving` and `onResizing` control where an appointment can go. When canceled, the drag shows that it cannot drop there. An appointment's own `allowDrag` and `allowResize` can lock it.

```tsx
import { reactive } from '@motifx/core';
import { Scheduler, type DragEventArgs } from '@motifx-community/ui';
import { sampleAppointments, type Meeting } from './sample-appointments';

type Locked = Meeting & { allowDrag?: boolean; allowResize?: boolean };

/** Nothing may go over lunch (12:00–13:00) or onto a weekend: the drag shows it cannot drop there. "Lunch with Ana" is locked in place. */
export default function Rules() {
  const list = sampleAppointments() as Locked[];
  const lunch = list.find((m) => m.text === 'Lunch with Ana');
  if (lunch) {
    lunch.allowDrag = false;
    lunch.allowResize = false;
  }
  const s = reactive({ said: '' });
  const allowed = (e: DragEventArgs<Locked>) => {
    const weekend = [0, 6].includes(e.start.getDay());
    const noon = new Date(e.start.getFullYear(), e.start.getMonth(), e.start.getDate(), 12);
    const overLunch = !e.allDay && e.start < new Date(noon.getTime() + 3_600_000) && e.end > noon;
    e.cancel = weekend || overLunch;
    s.said = weekend ? 'Not on a weekend.' : overLunch ? 'Not over lunch.' : '';
  };
  return (
    <div class="sched-demo">
      <Scheduler<Locked> appointments={list} startDayHour={8} endDayHour={19} onMoving={allowed} onResizing={allowed} />
      <p class="sched-log" role="status">
        {() => s.said}
      </p>
    </div>
  );
}
```

## Programmatic use

```tsx
import { reactive } from '@motifx/core';
import { Button, Scheduler } from '@motifx-community/ui';
import { sampleAppointments, type Meeting } from './sample-appointments';

/** The same changes programmatically: add, move, delete, open the form for a new one. */
export default function EditProgrammatically() {
  const state = reactive({ appointments: sampleAppointments(), said: '' });
  let scheduler: Scheduler<Meeting> | null = null;
  const tomorrow = (hour: number) => {
    const t = new Date();
    return new Date(t.getFullYear(), t.getMonth(), t.getDate() + 1, hour);
  };
  const planning = () => state.appointments.find((m) => m.text === 'Planning');
  const add = async () => {
    const added = await scheduler?.addAppointment({ id: Date.now(), text: 'Planning', startDate: tomorrow(11), endDate: tomorrow(12), color: '#6a1b9a' });
    state.said = added ? `Added ${added.text}` : 'Not added';
  };
  const later = async () => {
    const item = planning();
    if (!item) {
      state.said = 'Add it first';
      return;
    }
    const hour = 3_600_000;
    const ok = await scheduler?.updateAppointment(item, {
      startDate: new Date(item.startDate.getTime() + hour),
      endDate: new Date(item.endDate.getTime() + hour),
    });
    state.said = ok ? 'Moved an hour later' : 'Not moved';
  };
  const remove = async () => {
    const item = planning();
    state.said = item && (await scheduler?.deleteAppointment(item)) ? 'Deleted' : 'Nothing to delete';
  };
  return (
    <div class="sched-demo">
      <div class="docs-flow">
        <Button text="Add tomorrow 11:00" variant="outline" onclick={add} />
        <Button text="An hour later" variant="outline" onclick={later} />
        <Button text="Delete it" variant="outline" onclick={remove} />
        <Button
          text="New in the form"
          variant="outline"
          onclick={() => void scheduler?.showAppointmentForm(null, { start: tomorrow(15), end: tomorrow(16), allDay: false })}
        />
      </div>
      <p class="sched-log" role="status">
        {() => state.said}
      </p>
      <Scheduler<Meeting> appointments={state.appointments} startDayHour={8} endDayHour={19} ref={(c: Scheduler<Meeting>) => (scheduler = c)} />
    </div>
  );
}
```

## Keyboard

| Key | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `Enter on cells` | Opens the form for a new appointment over the selection. |
| `Enter on an appointment` | Opens its form. Space shows its tooltip. |
| `Arrows on an appointment` | Moves it: Up and Down by a step (a week in the month view), Left and Right by a day. Shift + arrow changes its end. Enter saves, and Escape reverts. |
| `Delete` | Deletes the focused appointment, after confirmation. |
| `Ctrl while dragging` | Drops a copy. |
| `Escape while dragging` | Reverts the change. |

## API reference

### Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `editing` | `Bind<boolean \| Partial<SchedulerEditing>>` | `true` | `false` makes the scheduler read-only. You can also set `allowAdding`, `allowUpdating`, `allowDeleting`, `allowDragging`, `allowResizing`, `allowCopying` and `confirmDelete` individually. |
| `fields.allowDrag / allowResize / allowEdit / allowDelete` | `string` | The same names | An appointment's own settings, which override `editing`. |
| `snapMinutes` | `Bind<number>` | The cell duration | The step used by dragging and the keyboard. |
| `minDuration` | `Bind<number>` | `snapMinutes` | The minimum duration when resizing, in minutes. |
| `tooltip` | `Bind<boolean>` | `true` | Clicking an appointment shows its tooltip with Edit and Delete. |

### Methods

| Method | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `addAppointment(values)` | Adds an appointment to the source (the array or, through the data source, the server) and resolves to it. |
| `updateAppointment(appointment, changes)` | Changes its fields. Resolves to `false` if an event canceled it or saving failed. |
| `deleteAppointment(appointment)` | Deletes it. There is no confirmation when called programmatically. |
| `showAppointmentForm(appointment?, cell?)` | Opens the form for an appointment, or for a new one at `cell` (the selection by default). |
| `showTooltip(appointment, anchor?) / hideTooltip()` | Controls its tooltip. |

### Events

| Event | Arguments |
| --- | --- |
| `onAppointmentAdding / Added` | `{ appointment, byUser, cancel, promise? }`. The values can still be changed, and `promise` waits, for example for a server. |
| `onAppointmentUpdating / Updated` | `{ appointment, changes, byUser, cancel, promise? }`. |
| `onAppointmentDeleting / Deleted` | `{ appointment, byUser, cancel, promise? }`, raised after the confirmation if there is one. |
| `onFormOpening` | `{ appointment, data, items, form, cancel }`. Change the fields, or cancel to open your own form. |
| `onMoveStart / onMoving / onMoveEnd` | `{ appointment, start, end, allDay, copy, byKeys, cancel }`. Canceling `moving` marks a position as invalid. |
| `onResizeStart / onResizing / onResizeEnd` | The same, for resizing. |
| `onDataError` | `{ operation, appointment, error }`: saving failed, and the appointment reverted. |

## Example files

`Editing.tsx`

```tsx
import { reactive } from '@motifx/core';
import { Scheduler, Switch } from '@motifx-community/ui';
import { sampleAppointments, type Meeting } from './sample-appointments';

/** Drag an appointment, pull its edges, Ctrl-drag a copy, double-click to edit, click for its tooltip. Every switch is live. */
export default function Editing() {
  const s = reactive({ drag: true, resize: true, copy: true, ask: true, quarter: false, log: [] as string[] });
  const say = (text: string) => {
    s.log.unshift(text);
    if (s.log.length > 6) s.log.pop();
  };
  const time = (d: Date) => d.toLocaleString([], { weekday: 'short', hour: '2-digit', minute: '2-digit' });
  return (
    <div class="sched-demo">
      <div class="docs-flow">
        <Switch label="Drag" x-model={() => s.drag} />
        <Switch label="Resize" x-model={() => s.resize} />
        <Switch label="Ctrl copies" x-model={() => s.copy} />
        <Switch label="Ask before deleting" x-model={() => s.ask} />
        <Switch label="15-minute steps" x-model={() => s.quarter} />
      </div>
      <Scheduler<Meeting>
        appointments={sampleAppointments()}
        startDayHour={8}
        endDayHour={19}
        editing={() => ({ allowDragging: s.drag, allowResizing: s.resize, allowCopying: s.copy, confirmDelete: s.ask })}
        snapMinutes={() => (s.quarter ? 15 : 30)}
        onMoveEnd={(e) => say(`${e.copy ? 'Copied' : 'Moved'} ${e.appointment.text} to ${time(e.start)}${e.byKeys ? ' (keys)' : ''}`)}
        onResizeEnd={(e) => say(`${e.appointment.text} now ${time(e.start)} – ${time(e.end)}`)}
        onAppointmentAdded={(e) => say(`Added ${e.appointment.text}`)}
        onAppointmentUpdated={(e) => say(`Saved ${e.appointment.text}`)}
        onAppointmentDeleted={(e) => say(`Deleted ${e.appointment.text}`)}
      />
      <ol class="sched-events" aria-label="What happened">
        {s.log.map((line, i) => (
          <li key={`${i}-${line}`}>{line}</li>
        ))}
      </ol>
    </div>
  );
}
```


`Saving.tsx`

```tsx
import { reactive } from '@motifx/core';
import { data } from '@motifx-community/data';
import { Scheduler } from '@motifx-community/ui';
import { SlowAdapter } from '../../../shared/slow-adapter';
import { sampleAppointments, type Meeting } from './sample-appointments';

/** A service that saves late and refuses every third change. */
class PickyService extends SlowAdapter<Meeting, number> {
  private changes = 0;

  protected override async updateRow(key: number, changes: Partial<Meeting>): Promise<Partial<Meeting>> {
    await new Promise((done) => setTimeout(done, 700));
    if (++this.changes % 3 === 0) throw new Error('The server said no.');
    return super.updateRow(key, changes);
  }
}

/** Move an appointment: it waits in place while the server saves, and reverts if saving fails. */
export default function Saving() {
  const s = reactive({ said: 'Move an appointment: it waits for the server; every third change fails.' });
  const source = new data.DataSource<Meeting, number>({ adapter: new PickyService({ data: sampleAppointments(), key: 'id' }, 300), loadMode: 'all' });
  return (
    <div class="sched-demo" onDisposing={() => source.dispose()}>
      <Scheduler<Meeting>
        dataSource={source}
        currentView="workWeek"
        startDayHour={8}
        endDayHour={19}
        onAppointmentUpdated={(e) => (s.said = `Saved: ${e.appointment.text}`)}
        onDataError={(e) => (s.said = `Not saved (${(e.error as Error).message}); it is back where it was.`)}
      />
      <p class="sched-log" role="status">
        {() => s.said}
      </p>
    </div>
  );
}
```

`slow-adapter.ts`

```tsx
import { data } from '@motifx-community/data';

/** Rows in memory that answer a little later, the way a server does; for the examples. */
export class SlowAdapter<T extends object, K> extends data.ArrayAdapter<T, K> {
  constructor(
    options: data.ArrayAdapterOptions<T>,
    private readonly delayMs = 300,
  ) {
    super(options);
  }

  override async load(options: data.LoadOptions = {}): Promise<data.LoadResult<T>> {
    await new Promise((done) => setTimeout(done, this.delayMs));
    return super.load(options);
  }
}
```

# Scheduler: Recurrence and time zones

> Scheduler · @motifx-community/ui 0.1.0-beta.5

Recurring appointments based on RFC 5545 rules, with exceptions and individually edited occurrences, a prompt that asks what a change should apply to, a recurrence editor, and time zone support that handles daylight saving time.

## Recurring appointments

An appointment with a `recurrenceRule` is a series, and the scheduler shows its occurrences only in the visible days. `recurrenceException` excludes specific times, and an appointment whose `recurrenceId` references a series replaces one of its occurrences. Supported parts are `FREQ` (daily to yearly), `INTERVAL`, `COUNT`, `UNTIL`, `BYDAY` (`2MO`, `-1FR`), `BYMONTHDAY`, `BYMONTH`, `BYYEARDAY`, `BYWEEKNO`, `BYSETPOS`, `WKST`, `BYHOUR` and `BYMINUTE`.

```tsx
import { reactive } from '@motifx/core';
import { formatRuleDate } from '@motifx-community/ui';

export interface Booking {
  id: number;
  text: string;
  startDate: Date;
  endDate: Date;
  allDay?: boolean;
  color?: string;
  recurrenceRule?: string;
  recurrenceException?: string;
  recurrenceId?: number;
  startDateTimeZone?: string;
  endDateTimeZone?: string;
}

/** Series around this week: a daily standup with one excluded day and one moved, a review every other week, a report on the last Friday, and an all-day Friday. */
export function recurringAppointments(): Booking[] {
  const today = new Date();
  const monday = new Date(today.getFullYear(), today.getMonth(), today.getDate() - ((today.getDay() + 6) % 7));
  const day = (offset: number, hour = 0, minute = 0) => new Date(monday.getFullYear(), monday.getMonth(), monday.getDate() + offset, hour, minute);
  return reactive([
    {
      id: 1,
      text: 'Team standup',
      startDate: day(-21, 9),
      endDate: day(-21, 9, 30),
      recurrenceRule: 'FREQ=WEEKLY;BYDAY=MO,TU,WE,TH,FR',
      // This Tuesday is excluded, and this Wednesday's occurrence is moved (appointment 2).
      recurrenceException: [day(1, 9), day(2, 9)].map((d) => formatRuleDate({ time: d.getTime(), utc: true, dateOnly: false })).join(','),
    },
    { id: 2, text: 'Team standup', startDate: day(2, 11), endDate: day(2, 11, 30), recurrenceId: 1 },
    {
      id: 3,
      text: 'Design review',
      startDate: day(-11, 14),
      endDate: day(-11, 15, 30),
      color: '#7c4dff',
      recurrenceRule: 'FREQ=WEEKLY;INTERVAL=2;BYDAY=TH',
    },
    {
      id: 4,
      text: 'Monthly report',
      startDate: day(-60, 16),
      endDate: day(-60, 17),
      color: '#c62828',
      recurrenceRule: 'FREQ=MONTHLY;BYDAY=-1FR',
    },
    {
      id: 5,
      text: 'Remote day',
      startDate: day(-3),
      endDate: day(-2),
      allDay: true,
      color: '#00838f',
      recurrenceRule: 'FREQ=WEEKLY;BYDAY=FR;COUNT=12',
    },
    { id: 6, text: 'Lunch with Ana', startDate: day(3, 12, 30), endDate: day(3, 13, 30), color: '#2e7d32' },
  ]) as Booking[];
}
```

## Editing a series

Moving, resizing, the form and Delete all ask the same question. **This one**: a new appointment takes its place, referencing its series, and its time is excluded from the series. **This and following**: the series ends before it (with `UNTIL` or a smaller `COUNT`), and a new series continues from it. **The whole series**: every occurrence moves the same way, and moving a weekly series to another day moves its weekdays.

With a data source, each write goes through its adapter in sequence: new rows first, then updates, then deletes. If a later write fails, the earlier ones are rolled back through the adapter. `onDataError` reports what was saved (`saved`, `unsaved`) and whether everything was rolled back (`undone`). An individually edited occurrence is an ordinary row linked to its series through `recurrenceId`, and deleting the series requests those rows from the adapter, whether they are loaded or not. This example uses a data source.

```tsx
import { data } from '@motifx-community/data';

/** Rows in memory that answer a little later, the way a server does; for the examples. */
export class SlowAdapter<T extends object, K> extends data.ArrayAdapter<T, K> {
  constructor(
    options: data.ArrayAdapterOptions<T>,
    private readonly delayMs = 300,
  ) {
    super(options);
  }

  override async load(options: data.LoadOptions = {}): Promise<data.LoadResult<T>> {
    await new Promise((done) => setTimeout(done, this.delayMs));
    return super.load(options);
  }
}
```

## Recurrence editor

The appointment form includes it (`editing.allowRecurrence`). On its own, it is `RecurrenceEditor`, with the repeat list, the interval, the weekdays, a day of the month or a weekday by position, the month and the end. A rule it cannot fully display stays unchanged until a selection is changed.

```tsx
import { reactive } from '@motifx/core';
import { RecurrenceEditor } from '@motifx-community/ui';

/** The standalone editor: it reads and writes the rule text, and describes it in words below. */
export default function RuleEditor() {
  const s = reactive({ rule: 'FREQ=MONTHLY;BYDAY=2TU;COUNT=6' });
  return (
    <div class="sched-demo sched-rule">
      <RecurrenceEditor x-model={() => s.rule} start={new Date()} />
      <p class="sched-log">
        <code>{() => s.rule || '(none)'}</code>
      </p>
    </div>
  );
}
```

```tsx
// In a form of your own:
FormLayout.editors.set('recurrence', (p) => new RecurrenceEditor(p));
// { field: 'rule', label: 'Repeat', editor: 'recurrence' }
```

## Time zones

`timeZone` displays days and hours in a given zone. A series recurs in the zone of its start (`startDateTimeZone`), so 09:00 in New York stays 09:00 there across daylight saving changes. On the night the clocks go forward, the skipped hour is passed, and a time inside it moves forward by the hour. On the night they go back, an appointment's box is as long as the appointment lasts.

With `editing.allowTimeZones`, the form has a time zone picker and a **Separate end time zone** check box. When checked, a second picker sets the end zone, and an appointment with a different end zone opens with it checked. When unchecked, the end follows the start zone again.

```tsx
import { reactive } from '@motifx/core';
import { Scheduler } from '@motifx-community/ui';
import type { Booking } from './recurring-appointments';

/**
 * The same appointments on two clocks. The call repeats at 09:00 in New York, so in Istanbul it moves an hour when America
 * changes its clocks. The flight leaves on Istanbul's clock and lands on New York's: open it, its form has a separate end time zone.
 */
export default function TimeZones() {
  const today = new Date();
  const at = (hour: number) => new Date(Date.UTC(today.getFullYear(), today.getMonth(), today.getDate(), hour));
  const appointments = reactive([
    // 09:00 in New York, every weekday, in New York's time zone.
    { id: 1, text: 'Call with New York', startDate: at(13), endDate: at(14), startDateTimeZone: 'America/New_York', recurrenceRule: 'FREQ=WEEKLY;BYDAY=MO,TU,WE,TH,FR' },
    { id: 2, text: 'Istanbul lunch', startDate: at(9), endDate: at(10), startDateTimeZone: 'Europe/Istanbul' },
    // 08:00 in Istanbul to 16:00 in New York.
    { id: 3, text: 'Flight to New York', startDate: at(5), endDate: at(20), startDateTimeZone: 'Europe/Istanbul', endDateTimeZone: 'America/New_York' },
  ]) as Booking[];
  const views = [{ type: 'day' as const, intervalCount: 3 }];
  return (
    <div class="sched-zones">
      <div class="sched-card">
        <span class="sched-tag">Europe/Istanbul</span>
        <Scheduler<Booking> appointments={appointments} views={views} timeZone="Europe/Istanbul" startDayHour={6} endDayHour={22} editing={{ allowTimeZones: true }} />
      </div>
      <div class="sched-card">
        <span class="sched-tag">America/New_York</span>
        <Scheduler<Booking> appointments={appointments} views={views} timeZone="America/New_York" startDayHour={0} endDayHour={16} editing={{ allowTimeZones: true }} />
      </div>
    </div>
  );
}
```

## Keyboard

| Key | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `Arrows (in the question)` | Chooses this occurrence, this and following, or the whole series. |
| `Enter / Escape` | Confirms, or cancels so that the change is discarded and the appointment reverts. |

## Accessibility

| Topic | Details |
| --- | --- |
| `Occurrences` | An occurrence is named with how its series repeats, and an individually edited one says so. The indicators are decorative (`aria-hidden`). |
| `The question` | A modal form with radio buttons under the question. The first option is selected. |
| `The editor` | A group named "Repeat". The weekdays are toggle buttons (`aria-pressed`) in a group named by its label, and the description is polite live text. |

## Styling

| Hook | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `.mx-scheduler__appointment` | `data-series`, `data-exception`. |
| `scheduler.series-mark, exception-mark` | Units: the indicators (`bar`, `chip`, `open`, `past`, `disabled`). A design language without them omits them. |
| `scheduler.tooltip-repeat` | Unit: the tooltip line that describes the recurrence (`exception`). |
| `.mx-recurrence-editor, __days, __day, __summary` | The editor, its weekday buttons and its description. |
| `recurrence-editor.editor, days-label, days, summary` | Units of the editor. `day-button` is the place for the weekday buttons, plus `row-gap` and `column-gap`. |

## API reference

### Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `timeZone` | `Bind<string \| null>` | `null` uses the browser time zone | The time zone for days and hours, as an IANA name (`Europe/Istanbul`). Conversion uses `Intl` only. |
| `seriesEdit` | `Bind<'ask' \\| 'occurrence' \\| 'following' \\| 'series'>` | `'ask'` | What changing or deleting an occurrence applies to. `ask` prompts the user. Programmatically, it applies to the occurrence unless the call specifies otherwise. |
| `recurrenceMarks` | `Bind<boolean>` | `true` | The indicators of an occurrence and of an individually edited one, where the design language draws them. |
| `editing.allowRecurrence` | `boolean` | `true` | Includes the recurrence editor in the form. |
| `editing.allowTimeZones` | `boolean` | `false` | Includes a time zone picker and a "Separate end time zone" check box in the form (`separateEndZone` in the form `data` and `items`), which shows a picker for the end. When unchecked, the end follows the start zone. It is not available for all-day appointments. |
| `fields.recurrenceRule` | `string` | `'recurrenceRule'` | The recurrence, as an RFC 5545 rule (`FREQ=WEEKLY;BYDAY=MO,WE`). Leave it empty for a single appointment. |
| `fields.recurrenceException` | `string` | `'recurrenceException'` | The excluded times (`EXDATE`), as comma-separated text (`20261104T090000Z,…`) or a list of dates. |
| `fields.recurrenceId` | `string` | `'recurrenceId'` | On an individually edited occurrence, the key of its series. |
| `fields.startTimeZone / endTimeZone` | `string` | `'startDateTimeZone'` / `'endDateTimeZone'` | The time zones of the start (and the series) and the end. Leave them empty to use the scheduler zone for the start and the start zone for the end. |

### Methods

| Method | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `updateAppointment(appointment, changes, scope?)` | For an occurrence, `scope` sets what the change applies to: `occurrence`, `following` or `series`. |
| `deleteAppointment(appointment, scope?)` | The same for a delete. |
| `askSeries(appointment, action?)` | Asks the user what a change (`update`) or a delete (`delete`) applies to. Resolves to the answer, or `null`. |
| `seriesOf(appointment)` | The series of an occurrence or an individually edited one, the series itself, or otherwise `null`. |
| `isOccurrence(appointment), isException(appointment)` | Indicate an occurrence generated from a rule, and an occurrence edited individually from its series. |
| `occurrencesOf(series, start, end)` | The occurrences of a series in a time range. |
| `recurrenceText(appointment)` | Describes the recurrence in plain words in the current locale. |

### Events

| Event | Arguments |
| --- | --- |
| `onSeriesAsking` | `{ appointment, series, action, scopes, scope, cancel }`. Set `scope` to answer without prompting, narrow `scopes`, or cancel the change. |
| `onSeriesAnswered` | `{ appointment, series, action, scope, byUser }`. `scope` is `null` when the prompt was canceled. |
| `onAppointmentUpdating / Updated` | These also include `scope` and `series` (`null` for a non-recurring appointment). `Updated` includes `added`, which is the individually edited occurrence or the continuing series. |
| `onAppointmentDeleting / Deleted` | These also include `scope` and `series`. |
| `onDataError` | This also includes `saved` and `unsaved` (each `{ kind, appointment, changes? }`) and `undone`, which report what a series change wrote before failing and whether it was rolled back. |

### RecurrenceEditor

| Member | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `value` | `Bind<string>` | `''` | The rule as RFC 5545 text, empty when it does not repeat. `x-model` provides two-way binding. |
| `start` | `Bind<Date \| null>` | Now | The start of the series. A rule takes its weekday and day of the month from it, unless the rule specifies them. |
| `allDay` | `Bind<boolean>` | `false` | Writes the last date as a date, instead of the end of that day in UTC. |
| `timeZone` | `Bind<string \| null>` | The browser time zone | The time zone the series recurs in. |
| `frequencies` | `Bind<("never" \\| frequency)[]>` | all five | The options in the repeat list. |
| `firstDayOfWeek, locale, texts, readOnly, summary` | — | — | The first weekday button, names and strings, read-only state, and the description line. |
| `rule, summaryText` | — | — | The rule parsed from `value`, and its description in words. Reactive. |
| `onValueChanged` | `{ value, previousValue, byUser }` | — | Occurs when a selection changes the rule. |

### Utilities

| Part | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `TimeZone.of(name) / TimeZone.local` | A time zone: `wall(moment)`, `moment(wall, later?)`, `offset`, `dayStart`, `addDays`, `sameDay`, `toLocal` and `fromLocal` (for editors), and `TimeZone.names()`. |
| `parseRecurrenceRule(text) / formatRecurrenceRule(rule)` | Converts a rule to an object (`RecurrenceRule`) and back. |
| `recurrenceDates(rule, start, from, to, options?)` | The times a rule occurs in a range, as wall clock times. |
| `describeRecurrence(rule, start, options)` | Describes a rule in plain words. |
| `readRuleDates, addRuleDate, filterRuleDates, parseRuleDate, formatRuleDate` | Exception dates as stored in the field. |
| `rangeFilter(range, fields)` | The data layer filter for a range: it starts before the range ends and either ends at or after the range starts or has a rule. The scheduler's `remoteFiltering` uses it. |
