`PhoneFrame.tsx`

```tsx
import { reactive, type Component } from '@motifx/core';
import { Button, Scheduler, Stack } from '@motifx-community/ui';
import { sampleAppointments, type Meeting } from './sample-appointments';

/**
 * A scheduler that goes by its own width (`presentation: 'auto'`), in a frame the size of a phone:
 * under 560 pixels it shows as on a phone, under 1024 as on a tablet (here by the width alone,
 * `tabletWhen: 'width'`, so a mouse shows it too). Drag the frame's corner, or pick a width.
 */
export default function PhoneFrame() {
  const s = reactive({ shown: '' });
  let frame!: Component<HTMLDivElement>;
  const width = (px: string) => (frame.element.style.inlineSize = px);
  return (
    <div class="sched-demo">
      <Stack orientation="horizontal" wrap align="center">
        <Button text="390 px" variant="outline" onclick={() => width('390px')} />
        <Button text="820 px" variant="outline" onclick={() => width('820px')} />
        <Button text="Full width" variant="outline" onclick={() => width('100%')} />
        <output class="sched-log">{() => s.shown}</output>
      </Stack>
      <div ref={(c: Component<HTMLDivElement>) => (frame = c)} class="sched-phone-frame">
        <Scheduler<Meeting>
          appointments={sampleAppointments()}
          views={['day', 'week', 'month', 'agenda']}
          tabletWhen="width"
          startDayHour={7}
          onPresentationChanged={(e) => (s.shown = `${e.to} at ${e.width} px`)}
        />
      </div>
    </div>
  );
}
```

`Touch.tsx`

```tsx
import { reactive } from '@motifx/core';
import { NumberBox, Scheduler, Stack, Switch } from '@motifx-community/ui';
import { sampleAppointments, type Meeting } from './sample-appointments';

/**
 * A finger: hold an appointment to lift it and drag it; let go and its handles stay, drag one to
 * resize. Swipe sideways for the next or the previous days; pinch to zoom the hours. Tap a free
 * cell, then tap it again for a new appointment.
 */
export default function Touch() {
  const s = reactive({ swipe: true, pinch: true, zoom: 1, said: '' });
  return (
    <div class="sched-demo">
      <Stack orientation="horizontal" wrap align="center" gap="lg">
        <Switch label="Swipe between days" x-model={() => s.swipe} />
        <Switch label="Pinch to zoom" x-model={() => s.pinch} />
        <NumberBox label="Zoom" labelMode="side" min={0.5} max={4} step={0.25} x-model={() => s.zoom} />
        <output class="sched-log">{() => s.said}</output>
      </Stack>
      <Scheduler<Meeting>
        appointments={sampleAppointments()}
        views={['day', 'week', 'timelineDay']}
        currentView="week"
        presentation="tablet"
        swipeNavigation={() => s.swipe}
        pinchZoom={() => s.pinch}
        timeZoom={() => s.zoom}
        onTimeZoomChanged={(e) => {
          s.zoom = e.to;
          s.said = `Zoomed from ${e.from.toFixed(2)} to ${e.to.toFixed(2)}`;
        }}
        onMoveEnd={(e) => (s.said = `${e.appointment.text} moved`)}
        onDateChanged={(e) => (s.said = e.byUser ? `Moved to ${e.to.toDateString()}` : s.said)}
      />
    </div>
  );
}
```


---

# Scheduler: iCalendar and print

> Scheduler · @motifx-community/ui 0.1.0-beta.5

Exports appointments to an iCalendar file (RFC 5545) and imports them back, for use with other calendar applications. The scheduler can also be printed.

## Import

```tsx
import { Scheduler, parseICalendar, writeICalendar } from '@motifx-community/ui';
```

## Export

`exportICalendar()` writes the appointments of the displayed days, or all appointments. A series is exported whole with its rule, so another calendar repeats it the same way.

```tsx
import { reactive } from '@motifx/core';
import { formatRuleDate } from '@motifx-community/ui';

export interface Booking {
  id: number;
  text: string;
  startDate: Date;
  endDate: Date;
  allDay?: boolean;
  color?: string;
  recurrenceRule?: string;
  recurrenceException?: string;
  recurrenceId?: number;
  startDateTimeZone?: string;
  endDateTimeZone?: string;
}

/** Series around this week: a daily standup with one excluded day and one moved, a review every other week, a report on the last Friday, and an all-day Friday. */
export function recurringAppointments(): Booking[] {
  const today = new Date();
  const monday = new Date(today.getFullYear(), today.getMonth(), today.getDate() - ((today.getDay() + 6) % 7));
  const day = (offset: number, hour = 0, minute = 0) => new Date(monday.getFullYear(), monday.getMonth(), monday.getDate() + offset, hour, minute);
  return reactive([
    {
      id: 1,
      text: 'Team standup',
      startDate: day(-21, 9),
      endDate: day(-21, 9, 30),
      recurrenceRule: 'FREQ=WEEKLY;BYDAY=MO,TU,WE,TH,FR',
      // This Tuesday is excluded, and this Wednesday's occurrence is moved (appointment 2).
      recurrenceException: [day(1, 9), day(2, 9)].map((d) => formatRuleDate({ time: d.getTime(), utc: true, dateOnly: false })).join(','),
    },
    { id: 2, text: 'Team standup', startDate: day(2, 11), endDate: day(2, 11, 30), recurrenceId: 1 },
    {
      id: 3,
      text: 'Design review',
      startDate: day(-11, 14),
      endDate: day(-11, 15, 30),
      color: '#7c4dff',
      recurrenceRule: 'FREQ=WEEKLY;INTERVAL=2;BYDAY=TH',
    },
    {
      id: 4,
      text: 'Monthly report',
      startDate: day(-60, 16),
      endDate: day(-60, 17),
      color: '#c62828',
      recurrenceRule: 'FREQ=MONTHLY;BYDAY=-1FR',
    },
    {
      id: 5,
      text: 'Remote day',
      startDate: day(-3),
      endDate: day(-2),
      allDay: true,
      color: '#00838f',
      recurrenceRule: 'FREQ=WEEKLY;BYDAY=FR;COUNT=12',
    },
    { id: 6, text: 'Lunch with Ana', startDate: day(3, 12, 30), endDate: day(3, 13, 30), color: '#2e7d32' },
  ]) as Booking[];
}
```

## Importing a file

`importICalendar(text)` reads the events and adds them in the same way as any new appointment: to the array, or through a data source's adapter.

```tsx
import { reactive } from '@motifx/core';
import { Button, Scheduler, Stack, TextArea } from '@motifx-community/ui';
import type { Booking } from './recurring-appointments';

const pad = (n: number) => String(n).padStart(2, '0');
const today = new Date();
const monday = new Date(today.getFullYear(), today.getMonth(), today.getDate() - ((today.getDay() + 6) % 7));
const date = (offset: number) => {
  const d = new Date(monday.getFullYear(), monday.getMonth(), monday.getDate() + offset);
  return `${d.getFullYear()}${pad(d.getMonth() + 1)}${pad(d.getDate())}`;
};

/** A typical calendar export: a zone with its Windows name and VTIMEZONE, a weekly series with one excluded day, an all-day event, and folded, escaped text. */
const FILE = [
  'BEGIN:VCALENDAR',
  'VERSION:2.0',
  'PRODID:-//Example//Calendar//EN',
  'BEGIN:VTIMEZONE',
  'TZID:W. Europe Standard Time',
  'BEGIN:STANDARD',
  'DTSTART:16010101T030000',
  'TZOFFSETFROM:+0200',
  'TZOFFSETTO:+0100',
  'RRULE:FREQ=YEARLY;BYDAY=-1SU;BYMONTH=10',
  'END:STANDARD',
  'BEGIN:DAYLIGHT',
  'DTSTART:16010101T020000',
  'TZOFFSETFROM:+0100',
  'TZOFFSETTO:+0200',
  'RRULE:FREQ=YEARLY;BYDAY=-1SU;BYMONTH=3',
  'END:DAYLIGHT',
  'END:VTIMEZONE',
  'BEGIN:VEVENT',
  'UID:sync-1@example.com',
  'DTSTAMP:20260101T000000Z',
  `DTSTART;TZID=W. Europe Standard Time:${date(0)}T100000`,
  `DTEND;TZID=W. Europe Standard Time:${date(0)}T110000`,
  'RRULE:FREQ=WEEKLY;BYDAY=MO,WE,FR;COUNT=12',
  `EXDATE;TZID=W. Europe Standard Time:${date(2)}T100000`,
  'SUMMARY:Sync with Berlin',
  'DESCRIPTION:Agenda:\n1. Status\, risks\n2. Next steps',
  'END:VEVENT',
  'BEGIN:VEVENT',
  'UID:offsite-1@example.com',
  'DTSTAMP:20260101T000000Z',
  `DTSTART;VALUE=DATE:${date(3)}`,
  `DTEND;VALUE=DATE:${date(5)}`,
  'SUMMARY:Team offsite',
  'END:VEVENT',
  'BEGIN:VEVENT',
  'UID:call-1@example.com',
  'DTSTAMP:20260101T000000Z',
  `DTSTART:${date(1)}T130000Z`,
  'DURATION:PT45M',
  'SUMMARY:Call with the customer about the long running rollout of the new pl',
  ' anning tool',
  'END:VEVENT',
  'END:VCALENDAR',
].join('\r\n');

/**
 * A file read in: each event is added through the data layer as any new appointment is (here an
 * array; a data source gets the same adds through its adapter), with `onAppointmentAdding` first.
 * Read it in again: an event whose UID is there already changes that appointment.
 */
export default function ImportCalendar() {
  const s = reactive({ text: FILE, said: '' });
  const scheduler = (<Scheduler<Booking> appointments={reactive([] as Booking[])} startDayHour={8} endDayHour={18} />) as Scheduler<Booking>;
  const read = async () => {
    const result = await scheduler.importICalendar(s.text);
    s.said = result ? `${result.added.length} added, ${result.updated.length} changed, ${result.failed.length} refused` : 'Not read in';
  };
  return (
    <div class="sched-demo">
      <TextArea label="iCalendar file" rows={8} spellcheck={false} wrap="off" x-model={() => s.text} />
      <Stack orientation="horizontal" wrap align="center">
        <Button text="Read in" tone="accent" onclick={() => void read()} />
        <output class="sched-log">{() => s.said}</output>
      </Stack>
      {scheduler}
    </div>
  );
}
```

## What is exported and imported

| iCalendar | The appointment |
| --- | --- |
| `UID` | The appointment's key. An individually edited occurrence uses the key of its series. On import, the UID becomes the new appointment's key (with a data source, the adapter assigns the key). |
| `DTSTART, DTEND (DURATION read too)` | In the appointment's own zone (`fields.startTimeZone`, `endTimeZone`), otherwise the scheduler's `timeZone`, otherwise the browser's, with `TZID`. All-day appointments are written as dates (`VALUE=DATE`), with the end on the following day. |
| `SUMMARY, DESCRIPTION` | The text and the description, escaped and folded at 75 octets as RFC 5545 requires. |
| `RRULE` | The series rule. An `UNTIL` in wall clock time is written in UTC, as the RFC requires for a rule with a time zone. |
| `EXDATE` | The times excluded from a series, in the same form as its start. |
| `RECURRENCE-ID` | An individually edited occurrence: the time in its series that it replaces (the excluded time closest to it). On import, the series excludes that time and the event references it (`fields.recurrenceId`). |
| `VTIMEZONE` | Written for every zone used, from the browser's own time zone data (with one rule per year when the changes follow a pattern). On import, a zone that is not an IANA name (such as `W. Europe Standard Time`) follows its VTIMEZONE. |
| `STATUS:CANCELLED` | On import, a canceled occurrence is excluded from its series, and a canceled event is not added. |

## Printing

When printing, every hour, row and column is rendered and visible (a large view is rendered in full for printing), nothing scrolls, colors are preserved, and the toolbar is omitted. A week of the month, a timeline row, a day of the agenda and an appointment are not split across pages.

## Styling

| Hook | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `scheduler.scheduler `print`, appointment `print`` | Unit states: the printed appearance, where a design language differs on paper (for example, no card frame). |
| `[data-printing]` | Set on the scheduler while printing. `print()` also marks the page so that only this scheduler prints. |

## API reference

### Methods

| Method | Returns | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `exportICalendar(options?)` | `string \| null` | `{ range: 'visible' (default) \| 'all' \| { start, end }, appointments, name }`. Returns the file's text, or `null` if `onICalendarExporting` canceled the export. |
| `importICalendar(text)` | `Promise<ICalendarImportResult \| null>` | `{ added, updated, failed }`. Each event is added through the data layer, with `onAppointmentAdding` first. An event whose UID matches an appointment's key updates that appointment. |
| `print()` | `Promise<boolean>` | Prints the scheduler alone. Returns `false` if `onPrinting` canceled it. |

### Events

| Event | Arguments | When |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `onICalendarExporting` | `{ appointments, range, cancel }` | Occurs before writing. Change `appointments` to export different ones. |
| `onICalendarExported` | `{ text, appointments }` | Occurs after writing. |
| `onICalendarImporting` | `{ text, appointments, cancel }` | Occurs before adding. `appointments` holds the values read, which you can change or filter. |
| `onICalendarImported` | `{ added, updated, failed }` | Occurs after adding. |
| `onPrinting` | `{ cancel }` | Occurs before the print dialog opens. |
| `onPrinted` | `{}` | Occurs when the print dialog closes, including after the browser's own print command. |

### The iCalendar utilities

The reader and writer have no DOM dependency and can be used without a scheduler.

| Function | Returns | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `parseICalendar(text)` | `ICalendar` | Returns the events, time zones and calendar name of a file. It handles folded lines, escaped text, multiple calendars and components inside events, and never throws. |
| `writeICalendar(options)` | `string` | `{ events, name, prodId, method, timeZones, stamp }`. |
| `timeZoneLines(zone, fromYear, toYear)` | `string[]` | Returns the VTIMEZONE of an IANA zone, using `Intl`. |
| `icalendarMoment(date, zones, fallback)` | `number` | Returns the moment a date in a file refers to: in UTC, an IANA zone, the file's VTIMEZONE, or otherwise `fallback`. |

## Example files

`ExportCalendar.tsx`

```tsx
import { reactive } from '@motifx/core';
import { Button, Scheduler, Stack, TextArea } from '@motifx-community/ui';
import { recurringAppointments, type Booking } from './recurring-appointments';

/**
 * The appointments as an iCalendar file (RFC 5545): the days shown or all of them. A series goes
 * whole with its rule, the times left out of it and the one moved apart (`RECURRENCE-ID`); every zone
 * used comes with its `VTIMEZONE`. Open the file in any calendar application.
 */
export default function ExportCalendar() {
  const s = reactive({ text: '', url: '' });
  const scheduler = (<Scheduler<Booking> appointments={recurringAppointments()} startDayHour={8} endDayHour={18} label="Team calendar" />) as Scheduler<Booking>;
  const write = (range: 'visible' | 'all') => {
    s.text = scheduler.exportICalendar({ range }) ?? '';
    if (s.url) URL.revokeObjectURL(s.url);
    s.url = URL.createObjectURL(new Blob([s.text], { type: 'text/calendar' }));
  };
  return (
    <div class="sched-demo">
      <Stack orientation="horizontal" wrap align="center">
        <Button text="Export the days shown" variant="outline" onclick={() => write('visible')} />
        <Button text="Export all" variant="outline" onclick={() => write('all')} />
        <a href={() => s.url || null} download="team-calendar.ics" x-display={() => !!s.url}>
          Download team-calendar.ics
        </a>
      </Stack>
      {scheduler}
      <TextArea label="The file" rows={10} readOnly spellcheck={false} wrap="off" x-model={() => s.text} />
    </div>
  );
}
```

`recurring-appointments.ts`

```tsx
import { reactive } from '@motifx/core';
import { formatRuleDate } from '@motifx-community/ui';

export interface Booking {
  id: number;
  text: string;
  startDate: Date;
  endDate: Date;
  allDay?: boolean;
  color?: string;
  recurrenceRule?: string;
  recurrenceException?: string;
  recurrenceId?: number;
  startDateTimeZone?: string;
  endDateTimeZone?: string;
}

/** Series around this week: a daily standup with one excluded day and one moved, a review every other week, a report on the last Friday, and an all-day Friday. */
export function recurringAppointments(): Booking[] {
  const today = new Date();
  const monday = new Date(today.getFullYear(), today.getMonth(), today.getDate() - ((today.getDay() + 6) % 7));
  const day = (offset: number, hour = 0, minute = 0) => new Date(monday.getFullYear(), monday.getMonth(), monday.getDate() + offset, hour, minute);
  return reactive([
    {
      id: 1,
      text: 'Team standup',
      startDate: day(-21, 9),
      endDate: day(-21, 9, 30),
      recurrenceRule: 'FREQ=WEEKLY;BYDAY=MO,TU,WE,TH,FR',
      // This Tuesday is excluded, and this Wednesday's occurrence is moved (appointment 2).
      recurrenceException: [day(1, 9), day(2, 9)].map((d) => formatRuleDate({ time: d.getTime(), utc: true, dateOnly: false })).join(','),
    },
    { id: 2, text: 'Team standup', startDate: day(2, 11), endDate: day(2, 11, 30), recurrenceId: 1 },
    {
      id: 3,
      text: 'Design review',
      startDate: day(-11, 14),
      endDate: day(-11, 15, 30),
      color: '#7c4dff',
      recurrenceRule: 'FREQ=WEEKLY;INTERVAL=2;BYDAY=TH',
    },
    {
      id: 4,
      text: 'Monthly report',
      startDate: day(-60, 16),
      endDate: day(-60, 17),
      color: '#c62828',
      recurrenceRule: 'FREQ=MONTHLY;BYDAY=-1FR',
    },
    {
      id: 5,
      text: 'Remote day',
      startDate: day(-3),
      endDate: day(-2),
      allDay: true,
      color: '#00838f',
      recurrenceRule: 'FREQ=WEEKLY;BYDAY=FR;COUNT=12',
    },
    { id: 6, text: 'Lunch with Ana', startDate: day(3, 12, 30), endDate: day(3, 13, 30), color: '#2e7d32' },
  ]) as Booking[];
}
```

```tsx
      appointments={sampleAppointments()}

    <div class="sched-demo">
      <Stack orientation="horizontal" wrap align="center">
        <Button text="Print" tone="accent" onclick={() => void scheduler.print()} />
        <output class="sched-log">{() => s.said}</output>
      </Stack>
      {scheduler}
    </div>
  );
}
```

# DataGrid

> DataGrid · @motifx-community/ui 0.1.0-beta.5

A grid for data entry and large data sets. Rows can be in memory or come from any data layer adapter, and can be displayed in a virtual list or in pages. It supports sorting, column layout, editing with kit editors, new rows with Tab navigation, three save modes, row actions, selection, filters, a search panel, grouping, summaries, a toolbar, lookup columns from other services, copy and paste, export, and a persistent layout. Every feature can be disabled for the grid or for a single column.

## Import

```tsx
import { DataGrid, type GridColumn } from '@motifx-community/ui';
import { data } from '@motifx-community/data';
```

## Declarative and programmatic

Pass in-memory rows with `rows` and their key with `rowKey`, and the grid places them in a `DataSource` over an `ArrayAdapter`. Every prop accepts a value or a function. A grid created with `new` is a regular object that you can add to the page, sort and query.

```tsx
/** An order, as stored by the sample server. */
export interface Order {
  id: number;
  customer: string;
  city: string;
  date: string;
  status: string;
  paid: boolean;
  amount: number;
  note: string;
}
```

## Virtual scrolling with server data

With a `DataSource` that loads by `blocks`, the scrollbar is sized from the total, and only the rows in the visible area are requested. A jump (Ctrl+End, or dragging the scrollbar) requests only the destination, and a block that is no longer needed while loading is aborted. A row that has not arrived yet appears as a placeholder. Above 10 million pixels of rows, the scrollbar is scaled.

```tsx
import { data } from '@motifx-community/data';

/** Rows in memory that answer a little later, the way a server does; for the examples. */
export class SlowAdapter<T extends object, K> extends data.ArrayAdapter<T, K> {
  constructor(
    options: data.ArrayAdapterOptions<T>,
    private readonly delayMs = 300,
  ) {
    super(options);
  }

  override async load(options: data.LoadOptions = {}): Promise<data.LoadResult<T>> {
    await new Promise((done) => setTimeout(done, this.delayMs));
    return super.load(options);
  }
}
```

## Paging

A `DataSource` that loads by `page` creates a paged grid. One page is requested at a time, and sorting returns to the first page. For in-memory rows, set `mode` to `paged`.

```tsx
import { data } from '@motifx-community/data';

/** Rows in memory that answer a little later, the way a server does; for the examples. */
export class SlowAdapter<T extends object, K> extends data.ArrayAdapter<T, K> {
  constructor(
    options: data.ArrayAdapterOptions<T>,
    private readonly delayMs = 300,
  ) {
    super(options);
  }

  override async load(options: data.LoadOptions = {}): Promise<data.LoadResult<T>> {
    await new Promise((done) => setTimeout(done, this.delayMs));
    return super.load(options);
  }
}
```

## Pager

The pager below the rows shows the page sizes (`pageSizeSelector`, with the sizes in `allowedPageSizes` and `all` for one page with every row), “Page 3 of 12 (250 items)” (`pagerInfo`, and `pagerInfoText` with `{0}`, `{1}`, `{2}`), the first, previous, next and last buttons (`pagerNavigation`), and the pages around the current one (`pagerNeighbors`). `pagerDisplayMode` sets its appearance: `full` shows page buttons and sizes as buttons, `compact` shows a page number box and a drop-down of sizes, and `adaptive` (the default) uses `full` while it fits within the grid's width. `pageSize(n)` also changes the rows per page programmatically. In either case, `onPageSizeChanging` can keep the old size, the grid returns to the first page, and with `layoutKey` the size is saved with the layout. PageUp and PageDown change the page (`pageKeys`).

```tsx
/** An order, as stored by the sample server. */
export interface Order {
  id: number;
  customer: string;
  city: string;
  date: string;
  status: string;
  paid: boolean;
  amount: number;
  note: string;
}
```

## Example files

`Programmatic.tsx`

```tsx
import { reactive } from '@motifx/core';
import { Button, DataGrid, Stack } from '@motifx-community/ui';
import type { Order } from './order';
import { columns, makeOrders, newOrder } from './orders';

/** Rows in memory given with `rows`, rows added programmatically, and a grid created with `new`. */
export default function Programmatic() {
  const s = reactive({ orders: makeOrders(40) });
  let grid: DataGrid<Order> | null = null;
  let host: Stack | null = null;

  // The grid reads the array as it is: after a push it loads it again.
  const pushOrder = () => {
    s.orders.push({ ...makeOrders(1)[0], id: s.orders.length + 1, customer: 'Pushed' });
    grid?.refresh();
  };

  const addGrid = () => {
    if (!host) return;
    host.controls.clear();
    const made = new DataGrid<Order>({ rows: makeOrders(8), rowKey: 'id', columns: columns.slice(0, 4), settings: { striped: true }, label: 'Created with new' });
    made.element.style.blockSize = '24rem';
    host.controls.add(made);
    made.sort = [{ field: 'customer', dir: 'asc' }];
  };

  return (
    <>
      <DataGrid
        class="dg-local"
        style="block-size: 30rem"
        rows={() => s.orders}
        rowKey="id"
        columns={columns}
        label="Orders"
        locale="en"
        settings={{ editable: true, addRows: true, striped: true }}
        newRow={{ create: newOrder }}
        ref={(g: DataGrid<Order>) => (grid = g)}
      />
      <Stack orientation="horizontal" wrap align="center">
        <Button text="Add a row programmatically" variant="outline" onclick={() => void grid?.addRow({ customer: 'Ada Lovelace' })} />
        <Button text="Push an order into the array" variant="outline" onclick={pushOrder} />
        <Button text="Add a grid programmatically" variant="outline" onclick={addGrid} />
        <output class="dg-local-count">{() => `${s.orders.length} orders in the array`}</output>
      </Stack>
      <Stack orientation="horizontal" wrap align="center" ref={(c: Stack) => (host = c)} />
    </>
  );
}
```

`orders.ts`

```tsx
import type { GridColumn } from '@motifx-community/ui';
import type { Order } from './order';

const CUSTOMERS = ['Ada Lovelace', 'Grace Hopper', 'Alan Turing', 'Cahit Arf', 'Katherine Johnson', 'Edsger Dijkstra', 'Barbara Liskov', 'Donald Knuth', 'İlhan Koman', 'Margaret Hamilton'];
const CITIES = ['Ankara', 'Antalya', 'Bursa', 'İstanbul', 'İzmir', 'Konya', 'Trabzon'];
const STATUSES = ['Draft', 'Approved', 'Shipped', 'Delivered', 'Cancelled'];
const NOTES = ['', 'Leave at the door', 'Call before delivery', 'Gift wrap, please, with a card that says happy birthday', '', 'Fragile'];

/** `n` sample orders, the same ones every time. */
export function makeOrders(n: number): Order[] {
  const day = Date.UTC(2026, 0, 1);
  return Array.from({ length: n }, (_, i) => ({
    id: i + 1,
    customer: CUSTOMERS[(i * 7) % CUSTOMERS.length],
    city: CITIES[(i * 3) % CITIES.length],
    date: new Date(day + ((i * 37) % 300) * 86_400_000).toISOString().slice(0, 10),
    status: STATUSES[i % STATUSES.length],
    paid: i % 3 === 0,
    amount: ((i * 7919) % 100_000) / 100,
    note: NOTES[i % NOTES.length],
  }));
}

const money = new Intl.NumberFormat('en', { minimumFractionDigits: 2, maximumFractionDigits: 2 });

/** The order columns: the number pinned to the start, the amount to the end. */
export const columns: GridColumn<Order>[] = [
  { field: 'id', title: 'No', type: 'number', width: 80, sticky: 'start', editable: false },
  { field: 'customer', title: 'Customer', width: 180, flex: 1, required: true },
  { field: 'city', title: 'City', type: 'list', width: 120, options: CITIES },
  { field: 'date', title: 'Date', type: 'date', width: 130, editable: false, creatable: true },
  { field: 'status', title: 'Status', type: 'list', width: 120, options: STATUSES, required: true },
  { field: 'paid', title: 'Paid', type: 'boolean', width: 80 },
  { field: 'note', title: 'Note', width: 200 },
  {
    field: 'amount',
    title: 'Amount',
    type: 'number',
    width: 120,
    sticky: 'end',
    required: true,
    validate: (v) => (typeof v === 'number' && v < 0 ? 'The amount cannot be negative.' : null),
    format: (v) => (typeof v === 'number' ? money.format(v) : ''),
  },
];

/** The same columns with a filter cell and a header filter on most of them. */
export const filterColumns: GridColumn<Order>[] = columns.map((c) => ({ ...c, filterRow: c.field !== 'note', headerFilter: c.field !== 'note' && c.field !== 'id' }));

const today = () => new Date().toISOString().slice(0, 10);

/** What a new order starts with. */
export const newOrder = () => ({ date: today(), status: 'Draft', paid: false });
```

`Virtual.tsx`

```tsx
import { reactive } from '@motifx/core';
import { data } from '@motifx-community/data';
import { Button, DataGrid, Stack } from '@motifx-community/ui';
import { SlowAdapter } from '../../../shared/slow-adapter';
import type { Order } from './order';
import { columns, makeOrders } from './orders';

/** 100,000 orders from a server, loaded by blocks only in the visible area. */
export default function Virtual() {
  const s = reactive({ loads: 0 });
  // Simulates a server. In an application, use new data.ODataAdapter({ url: '/odata/Orders', key: 'OrderID' }) here.
  const server = new SlowAdapter<Order, number>({ data: makeOrders(100_000), key: 'id' }, 300);
  server.onLoading(() => s.loads++);
  const orders = new data.DataSource<Order, number>({ adapter: server, loadMode: 'blocks', pageSize: 100 });
  let grid: DataGrid<Order> | null = null;

  return (
    <>
      <DataGrid class="dg-virtual" style="block-size: 32rem" dataSource={orders} columns={columns} label="100,000 orders" locale="en" ref={(g: DataGrid<Order>) => (grid = g)} />
      <Stack orientation="horizontal" wrap align="center">
        <Button text="Go to the end" variant="outline" onclick={() => grid?.scrollToIndex(grid.total - 1, 'end')} />
        <Button text="Back to the top" variant="outline" onclick={() => grid?.scrollToIndex(0)} />
        <Button text="Fit the columns" variant="outline" onclick={() => grid?.autoSizeColumns()} />
        <output class="dg-loads">{() => `${s.loads} loads for ${grid?.total ?? 0} rows`}</output>
      </Stack>
    </>
  );
}
```

`slow-adapter.ts`

```tsx
import { data } from '@motifx-community/data';

/** Rows in memory that answer a little later, the way a server does; for the examples. */
export class SlowAdapter<T extends object, K> extends data.ArrayAdapter<T, K> {
  constructor(
    options: data.ArrayAdapterOptions<T>,
    private readonly delayMs = 300,
  ) {
    super(options);
  }

  override async load(options: data.LoadOptions = {}): Promise<data.LoadResult<T>> {
    await new Promise((done) => setTimeout(done, this.delayMs));
    return super.load(options);
  }
}
```

`Pager.tsx`

```tsx
import { reactive } from '@motifx/core';
import { Button, DataGrid, Stack } from '@motifx-community/ui';
import type { Order } from './order';
import { columns, makeOrders } from './orders';

/** The page sizes, the information text, and the full, compact and adaptive pager layouts. */
export default function Pager() {
  const s = reactive({ look: 'adaptive' as 'adaptive' | 'compact' | 'full', told: '' });
  let grid: DataGrid<Order> | null = null;

  return (
    <>
      <Stack orientation="horizontal" wrap align="center">
        <Button text="Full" variant={() => (s.look === 'full' ? 'solid' : 'outline')} onclick={() => (s.look = 'full')} />
        <Button text="Compact" variant={() => (s.look === 'compact' ? 'solid' : 'outline')} onclick={() => (s.look = 'compact')} />
        <Button text="Adaptive" variant={() => (s.look === 'adaptive' ? 'solid' : 'outline')} onclick={() => (s.look = 'adaptive')} />
        <Button text="50 rows a page" variant="ghost" onclick={() => grid?.pageSize(50)} />
        <output class="dg-pager-state">{() => s.told}</output>
      </Stack>
      <DataGrid
        class="dg-pager"
        style="block-size: 30rem"
        rows={makeOrders(1000)}
        rowKey="id"
        mode="paged"
        pageSize={20}
        columns={columns}
        label="Orders in pages of a size you choose"
        locale="en"
        settings={{
          pageSizeSelector: true,
          allowedPageSizes: [10, 20, 50, 'all'],
          pagerDisplayMode: () => s.look,
        }}
        onPageSizeChanged={(e) => (s.told = `${e.pageSize || 'All'} rows a page (was ${e.previous || 'all'})`)}
        ref={(g: DataGrid<Order>) => (grid = g)}
      />
    </>
  );
}
```

---

# DataGrid: Editing

> DataGrid · @motifx-community/ui 0.1.0-beta.5

## Editing and save modes

Typing on a cell, pressing Enter or F2, or double-clicking opens its editor, and only the active cell has one. Entered values go into the row's draft in the grid's `ChangeTracker`, stored by key, and the row is saved when the user leaves it. `wait` sends the row and waits for the response, `background` sends it through a single queue and continues, and `batch` keeps everything until “Save changes”. A row with a validation message cannot be left, and Escape cancels the edit. The service in this example rejects a note that contains “error”.

```tsx
import { data } from '@motifx-community/data';

/** Rows in memory that answer a little later, the way a server does; for the examples. */
export class SlowAdapter<T extends object, K> extends data.ArrayAdapter<T, K> {
  constructor(
    options: data.ArrayAdapterOptions<T>,
    private readonly delayMs = 300,
  ) {
    super(options);
  }

  override async load(options: data.LoadOptions = {}): Promise<data.LoadResult<T>> {
    await new Promise((done) => setTimeout(done, this.delayMs));
    return super.load(options);
  }
}
```

## Saving all changes at once

With `saveMode: 'batch'`, every edit, new row and deletion waits for `saveChanges()`. Deletions, updates and new rows are then sent, each type in one call, and rows the server rejects keep their marks. This example uses a server that loads by page, so changes persist while the pages change, and the page's own buttons follow `hasChanges`.

```tsx
import { data } from '@motifx-community/data';

/** Rows in memory that answer a little later, the way a server does; for the examples. */
export class SlowAdapter<T extends object, K> extends data.ArrayAdapter<T, K> {
  constructor(
    options: data.ArrayAdapterOptions<T>,
    private readonly delayMs = 300,
  ) {
    super(options);
  }

  override async load(options: data.LoadOptions = {}): Promise<data.LoadResult<T>> {
    await new Promise((done) => setTimeout(done, this.delayMs));
    return super.load(options);
  }
}
```

## New rows

`addRow()` or the toolbar's “New row” opens a row at the bottom (the grid scrolls to the very end, and a virtual list loads only the last block) or at the top, with the first editable cell in edit mode. Tab on the last cell of a new row saves it and opens the next one, Escape discards it, and an untouched row is removed automatically.

```tsx
/** An order, as stored by the sample server. */
export interface Order {
  id: number;
  customer: string;
  city: string;
  date: string;
  status: string;
  paid: boolean;
  amount: number;
  note: string;
}
```

## Row actions

`actions` defines the buttons for each row, as a list or as a function of the row and its state (`isNew`, `isEditing`, `isDirty`, `isSaving`, `hasError`, `isRemoved`, `isSelected`). When a value read by the function changes, the row's buttons update. Built-in actions are referenced by name. Buttons that do not fit in the column move to the “more” menu, and those listed first stay visible. The column can be at the start or the end, pinned to its edge or scrolling with the rows.

```tsx
/** An order, as stored by the sample server. */
export interface Order {
  id: number;
  customer: string;
  city: string;
  date: string;
  status: string;
  paid: boolean;
  amount: number;
  note: string;
}
```

Actions can also appear in the toolbar (`actionsLocation: 'toolbar'`, with the `rowActions` item) or in the bottom bar (`'bottom'`) for the rows they apply to: the selected rows, or the active row when nothing is selected (`actionsTarget`). With no row, nothing appears. With one row, its own actions appear as the row would show them. With several rows, only the actions common to all of them appear, each with a row count (“Approve (3)”), and an action is disabled if it is disabled for any of the rows (`actionsMultipleEnabled: 'any'` runs it on the rows where it is enabled). An action's `location` takes precedence, so “Approve” can be in the toolbar while “Edit” stays in the row, and the column appears only when it contains an action. `onclickMany` runs once with every row. Without it, `onclick` runs row by row and waits for any promise, with progress and a Stop button over the rows, and the outcome is announced (“2 of 3 done, 1 failed”). The built-in `remove` action marks all the rows in batch mode, and in other modes sends them in one save (`ChangeTracker.removeRows`, which is one request when the adapter saves in batches, such as OData `$batch`, a REST batch endpoint or a SOAP `save`). An action's `tone` colors its button and menu items (`'danger'` for the built-in `remove`, and `'accent'` for `save`).

Every row's actions also appear in its context menu (right-click or Shift+F10), wherever they are displayed. Within a selection of several rows, the menu shows the actions common to all of them. With `actionsDisplay: 'menu'`, a row shows only its “more” button with every action in its menu, and the bars show one “Actions” menu button. An action's `menu` setting keeps it either always in the menu or always as a button.

After “select all” on a server, the rows are not loaded. Only actions with `onclickSelection` appear in that case, and they receive the selection in the form of `grid.selection` (`all`, `keys`, `except`, `filter`) to send to the server, so that every row does not have to be loaded.

```tsx
/** An order, as stored by the sample server. */
export interface Order {
  id: number;
  customer: string;
  city: string;
  date: string;
  status: string;
  paid: boolean;
  amount: number;
  note: string;
}
```

| Setting | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `actionsLocation` | `'row'` | Where the actions appear: `'row'`, `'toolbar'` (the `rowActions` toolbar item at the start, which can be placed through `toolbar.items` like other items) or `'bottom'` (the start of the bottom bar). |
| `actionsTarget` | `'auto'` | The rows the bars act on: `'selection'`, `'focused'` (the active row) or `'auto'` (the selected rows when selection is on, otherwise the active row). |
| `actionsDisplay` | `'auto'` | `'auto'` shows the buttons that fit, and the rest are in “more”. `'menu'` shows only the “more” button per row (the column is as wide as that button, or `actionsWidth` when an action is always a button) and one “Actions” menu button in the bars. The context menu always lists all of them. |
| `actionsMultipleEnabled` | `'all'` | Whether an action on several rows is available when it is enabled for all of them, or for any of them (`'any'` runs it on those rows). |
| `actionsShowCount` | `true` | Adds the row count after the text of an action that applies to several rows (“Approve (3)”). |
| `actionsStopOnError` | `false` | When running row by row, a failed row stops the remaining rows. |
| `actionsProgress, actionsStopButton` | `true`, `true` | The panel over the rows while an action runs on several rows (once one of them has returned a promise), and its Stop button. |
| `actionsContextMenu` | `true` | Includes a row's actions in its context menu. |

| Action field | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `id, text, icon, showText, hint` | The same as in the row. Rows share an action through its `id`. |
| `tone` | `'standard' \| 'accent' \| 'danger'`, default `'standard'`. The color of its button and of its item in the “more” menu, the context menu and the bars' “Actions” menu. |
| `visible, disabled` | `boolean` or `(row, state) => boolean`, evaluated for each row. With several rows, it must be visible for every row, and it is disabled as set by `actionsMultipleEnabled`. |
| `location` | `Bind<'row' \| 'toolbar' \| 'bottom'>`. Takes precedence over `actionsLocation`. |
| `menu` | `Bind<'auto' \| 'always' \| 'never'>`, default `'auto'`. Whether it moves to the “more” menu when it does not fit, is always there, or never is (a button even with the `'menu'` display). |
| `multiple` | `Bind<boolean>`, default `true` (`false` for the built-in `edit`). Whether it can run on several rows. |
| `multipleEnabled, stopOnError, showCount, contextMenu` | The action's own `actionsMultipleEnabled`, `actionsStopOnError`, `actionsShowCount` and `actionsContextMenu`, each of which takes precedence. |
| `beginGroup` | A separator before it in a menu. |
| `onclick(row, state)` | Runs for one row. On several rows, without `onclickMany`, it runs for each one in turn. A promise is awaited, and an exception, a rejection or a promise of `false` counts the row as failed. |
| `onclickMany(rows, e)` | Runs once for several rows, and for one row too if there is no `onclick`. `e` is `{ location, signal, progress(done, total?) }`, and Stop aborts `signal`. |
| `onclickSelection(selection, e)` | Runs for a selection whose rows are not loaded (“select all” on a server), with the selection state. Only these actions appear in that case. |

| Member | Parameters / return value | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `onActionRunning` | `{ action, rows, selection, location, cancel }` | Occurs before an action runs (in a row, a bar, a row's menu or programmatically). Set `cancel` to stop it. `rows` is empty for a selection that is not loaded. |
| `onActionRan` | `{ action, rows, location, done, failed, canceled, errors }` | Occurs after an action runs. Without a listener, exceptions from failed rows go to the console. |
| `runAction(id, rows?)` | `Promise<GridActionRanEventArgs \| null>` | Runs an action on `rows`, or on the rows the bars currently act on, where it is visible and enabled. Returns `null` when it is unavailable or was canceled. |
| `actionTargets` | `T[]`, reactive | The rows the bars currently act on. Empty for a selection that is not loaded. |
| `barActions` | `GridBarAction[]`, reactive | The actions the toolbar and the bottom bar currently show: `{ action, location, text, count, disabled, rows }`. |
| `stopAction()` | `void` | Stops the action running on several rows, as its Stop button does. |

## Example files

`SaveModes.tsx`

```tsx
import { reactive } from '@motifx/core';
import { data } from '@motifx-community/data';
import { Button, DataGrid, Stack } from '@motifx-community/ui';
import type { Order } from './order';
import { OrderService } from './order-service';
import { columns, makeOrders, newOrder } from './orders';

const MODES: data.SaveMode[] = ['wait', 'background', 'batch'];

/** Edits saved according to the save mode, to a server that rejects a note containing "error". */
export default function SaveModes() {
  const s = reactive({ saveMode: 'wait' as data.SaveMode });
  const service = new OrderService({ data: makeOrders(30), key: 'id', createKey: (_values, rows) => rows.length + 1 }, 300);
  const orders = new data.DataSource<Order, number>({ adapter: service, loadMode: 'all' });
  let grid: DataGrid<Order> | null = null;

  return (
    <>
      <Stack orientation="horizontal" wrap align="center" role="group" aria-label="Save mode">
        {MODES.map((mode) => (
          <Button key={mode} text={mode} size="sm" variant={() => (s.saveMode === mode ? 'solid' : 'ghost')} aria-pressed={() => s.saveMode === mode} onclick={() => (s.saveMode = mode)} />
        ))}
      </Stack>
      <DataGrid
        class="dg-editing"
        style="block-size: 32rem"
        dataSource={orders}
        columns={columns}
        label="Orders to edit"
        locale="en"
        saveMode={() => s.saveMode}
        settings={{ editable: true, addRows: true, striped: true }}
        newRow={{ create: newOrder }}
        validateRow={(row: Order) => (row.status === 'Cancelled' && row.paid ? { paid: 'A cancelled order is not paid.' } : null)}
        ref={(g: DataGrid<Order>) => (grid = g)}
      />
      <Stack orientation="horizontal" wrap align="center">
        <Button text="Delete the active row" variant="outline" onclick={() => void grid?.deleteRow()} />
        <Button text="Undo the deletion" variant="ghost" visible={() => s.saveMode === 'batch'} onclick={() => grid?.activeRow && grid.restoreRow(grid.activeRow)} />
        <output class="dg-changes">{() => `${grid?.changes.count ?? 0} unsaved, ${grid?.errorCount ?? 0} with errors`}</output>
      </Stack>
    </>
  );
}
```

`order-service.ts`

```tsx
import { data } from '@motifx-community/data';
import { SlowAdapter } from '../../../shared/slow-adapter';
import type { Order } from './order';

/** Orders in memory that answer like a server, and turn down a note with "error" in it. */
export class OrderService extends SlowAdapter<Order, number> {
  protected override updateRow(key: number, changes: Partial<Order>): Promise<Partial<Order>> {
    return this.later(changes, () => super.updateRow(key, changes));
  }

  protected override insertRow(values: Partial<Order>): Promise<Partial<Order>> {
    return this.later(values, () => super.insertRow(values));
  }

  private later(values: Partial<Order>, save: () => Promise<Partial<Order>>): Promise<Partial<Order>> {
    const message = 'The server does not take this note.';
    return new Promise((done, fail) =>
      setTimeout(() => {
        if (String(values.note ?? '').includes('error')) fail(data.DataError.create('MJD202', { operation: 'save', fields: { note: message } }, message));
        else save().then(done, fail);
      }, 300),
    );
  }
}
```

```tsx
import { data } from '@motifx-community/data';

/** Rows in memory that answer a little later, the way a server does; for the examples. */
export class SlowAdapter<T extends object, K> extends data.ArrayAdapter<T, K> {
  constructor(
    options: data.ArrayAdapterOptions<T>,
    private readonly delayMs = 300,
  ) {
    super(options);
  }

  override async load(options: data.LoadOptions = {}): Promise<data.LoadResult<T>> {
    await new Promise((done) => setTimeout(done, this.delayMs));
    return super.load(options);
  }
}
```

`BatchSave.tsx`

```tsx
import { reactive } from '@motifx/core';
import { data } from '@motifx-community/data';
import { Button, DataGrid, Stack } from '@motifx-community/ui';
import type { Order } from './order';
import { OrderService } from './order-service';
import { columns, makeOrders, newOrder } from './orders';

/** Every change kept until "Save changes", over a server that loads by page; the page's own buttons. */
export default function BatchSave() {
  const s = reactive({ note: '' });
  const service = new OrderService({ data: makeOrders(200), key: 'id', createKey: (_values, rows) => rows.length + 1 }, 250);
  const orders = new data.DataSource<Order, number>({ adapter: service, loadMode: 'page', pageSize: 15 });
  let grid: DataGrid<Order> | null = null;

  const save = async () => {
    const result = await grid?.saveChanges();
    if (result) s.note = `${result.saved} saved, ${result.failed} failed`;
  };

  return (
    <>
      <DataGrid
        class="dg-batch"
        style="block-size: 34rem"
        dataSource={orders}
        columns={columns}
        label="Orders saved together"
        locale="en"
        saveMode="batch"
        settings={{ editable: true, addRows: true, saveButtons: false, actionsWidth: 100 }}
        newRow={{ create: newOrder }}
        actions={(_row: Order, state) => (state.isRemoved ? ['restore'] : ['remove'])}
        ref={(g: DataGrid<Order>) => (grid = g)}
      />
      <Stack orientation="horizontal" wrap align="center">
        <Button text="Save changes" tone="accent" enabled={() => !!grid?.hasChanges} onclick={save} />
        <Button text="Discard" variant="outline" enabled={() => !!grid?.hasChanges} onclick={() => grid?.discardChanges()} />
        <output class="dg-batch-note">{() => `${grid?.changes.count ?? 0} unsaved${s.note ? ` · ${s.note}` : ''}`}</output>
      </Stack>
    </>
  );
}
```

`NewRows.tsx`

```tsx
import { reactive } from '@motifx/core';
import { Button, DataGrid, Stack } from '@motifx-community/ui';
import { columns, makeOrders, newOrder } from './orders';

const POSITIONS = ['bottom', 'top'] as const;

/** New rows open at the bottom or at the top; Tab on the last cell opens the next one. */
export default function NewRows() {

  return (
    <>
      <Stack orientation="horizontal" wrap align="center" role="group" aria-label="New rows">

        class="dg-new"
        style="block-size: 28rem"
        rows={makeOrders(12)}
        rowKey="id"
        columns={columns}

        locale="en"
        settings={{ editable: true, addRows: true }}
```

`RowActions.tsx`

```tsx
import { reactive } from '@motifx/core';
import { Button, CheckBox, DataGrid, Stack, type GridAction } from '@motifx-community/ui';
import type { Order } from './order';
import { columns, makeOrders } from './orders';

const PLACES = ['start', 'end'] as const;
const WIDTHS = [100, 140, 260];

/** Buttons per row from a function of the row and its state; the rest go into "more". */
export default function RowActions() {
  const s = reactive({ orders: makeOrders(30), at: 'end' as 'start' | 'end', sticky: true, width: 260, note: '' });
  let grid: DataGrid<Order> | null = null;

  const approve: GridAction<Order> = {
    id: 'approve',
    text: 'Approve',
    tone: 'accent',
    visible: (row) => row.status === 'Draft',
    onclick: (row) => {
      row.status = 'Approved';
      // The grid reads the row as it is: draw it again, its buttons with it.
      grid?.repaintRows([row.id]);
      s.note = `Order ${row.id} approved`;
    },
  };
  const print: GridAction<Order> = { id: 'print', text: 'Print', onclick: (row) => (s.note = `Order ${row.id} sent to the printer`) };
  const mail: GridAction<Order> = { id: 'mail', text: 'Mail the customer', disabled: (row) => !row.paid, onclick: (row) => (s.note = `Mail to ${row.customer}`) };

  return (
    <>
      <Stack orientation="horizontal" wrap align="center" role="group" aria-label="Actions column">
        {PLACES.map((at) => (
          <Button key={at} text={at} size="sm" variant={() => (s.at === at ? 'solid' : 'ghost')} aria-pressed={() => s.at === at} onclick={() => (s.at = at)} />
        ))}
        <CheckBox label="Pinned" x-model={() => s.sticky} />
        {WIDTHS.map((w) => (
          <Button key={`w${w}`} text={`${w}px`} size="sm" variant={() => (s.width === w ? 'solid' : 'ghost')} aria-pressed={() => s.width === w} onclick={() => (s.width = w)} />
        ))}
      </Stack>
      <DataGrid
        class="dg-actions"
        style="block-size: 30rem"
        rows={() => s.orders}
        rowKey="id"
        columns={columns}
        label="Orders with actions"
        locale="en"
        saveMode="batch"
        actions={(_row: Order, state) => (state.isRemoved ? ['restore'] : [approve, 'edit', 'remove', print, mail])}
        settings={{ editable: true, actionsPosition: () => s.at, actionsSticky: () => s.sticky, actionsWidth: () => s.width }}
        ref={(g: DataGrid<Order>) => (grid = g)}
      />
      <output class="dg-action-note">{() => s.note}</output>
    </>
  );
}
```

`BarActions.tsx`

```tsx
import { reactive } from '@motifx/core';
import { Button, CheckBox, DataGrid, Stack, type GridAction, type GridActionLocation } from '@motifx-community/ui';
import type { Order } from './order';
import { columns, makeOrders } from './orders';

const LOCATIONS: GridActionLocation[] = ['row', 'toolbar', 'bottom'];

const wait = (ms: number) => new Promise((resolve) => setTimeout(resolve, ms));

/** The actions of the selected rows in the toolbar or the bottom bar; several rows share the ones they all have. */
export default function BarActions() {
  const s = reactive({ orders: makeOrders(40), location: 'toolbar' as GridActionLocation, menu: false, note: '' });
  let grid: DataGrid<Order> | null = null;
  // The grid reads the rows as they are, so after a change in place it redraws them and re-reads their actions.
  const changed = (rows: readonly Order[]) => {
    grid?.repaintRows(rows.map((row) => row.id));
    grid?.refreshActions();
  };

  const approve: GridAction<Order> = {
    id: 'approve',
    text: 'Approve',
    tone: 'accent',
    visible: (row) => row.status === 'Draft',
    // Once for every selected row: one request to the server.
    onclickMany: async (rows) => {
      await wait(300);
      for (const row of rows) row.status = 'Approved';
      changed(rows);
      s.note = `${rows.length} orders approved`;
    },
    onclick: (row) => {
      row.status = 'Approved';
      changed([row]);
      s.note = `Order ${row.id} approved`;
    },
  };
  // Row by row: the grid shows the progress and a Stop button.
  const print: GridAction<Order> = {
    id: 'print',
    text: 'Print',
    onclick: async (row) => {
      await wait(400);
      s.note = `Order ${row.id} printed`;
    },
  };

  return (
    <>
      <Stack orientation="horizontal" wrap align="center" role="group" aria-label="Where the actions show">
        {LOCATIONS.map((at) => (
          <Button key={at} text={at} size="sm" variant={() => (s.location === at ? 'solid' : 'ghost')} aria-pressed={() => s.location === at} onclick={() => (s.location = at)} />
        ))}
        <CheckBox label="Menu only" x-model={() => s.menu} />
      </Stack>
      <DataGrid
        class="dg-bar-actions"
        style="block-size: 28rem"
        rows={() => s.orders}
        rowKey="id"
        columns={columns}
        label="Orders to approve"
        locale="en"
        saveMode="batch"
        actions={(_row: Order, state) => (state.isRemoved ? ['restore'] : [approve, print, 'remove'])}
        settings={{ selection: 'multiple', actionsLocation: () => s.location, actionsDisplay: () => (s.menu ? 'menu' : 'auto') }}
        onActionRan={(e) => {
          if (e.canceled) s.note = `${e.action.id}: stopped after ${e.done} rows`;
        }}
        ref={(g: DataGrid<Order>) => (grid = g)}
      />
      <output class="dg-bar-note">{() => s.note}</output>
    </>
  );
}
```


---

# DataGrid: Edit forms and popups

> DataGrid · @motifx-community/ui 0.1.0-beta.5

## Edit forms and popups

`settings.editMode` determines how a row is edited and when it is submitted for saving, and `saveMode` determines how a submitted row is sent: waiting for the response, in the background, or held for `saveChanges()`. In `form` mode, the row opens as a form in its place, using the kit's `FormLayout` with one field per column. Each field has the editor its cell would use, with a frame, a label and validation messages below it. The rows after it move down by its height, including in a virtual list. Save (or Enter in a field) saves the row according to the save mode, and Cancel or Escape discards the edit. Focus moves into the form and back to the row. In this example, the form has two groups, and the buttons switch the edit mode.

```tsx
import { data } from '@motifx-community/data';

/** Rows in memory that answer a little later, the way a server does; for the examples. */
export class SlowAdapter<T extends object, K> extends data.ArrayAdapter<T, K> {
  constructor(
    options: data.ArrayAdapterOptions<T>,
    private readonly delayMs = 300,
  ) {
    super(options);
  }

  override async load(options: data.LoadOptions = {}): Promise<data.LoadResult<T>> {
    await new Promise((done) => setTimeout(done, this.delayMs));
    return super.load(options);
  }
}
```

| editMode | Editing location | Submitted for saving | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `row` | In the cells, with one editor at a time | When leaving the row | The grid's default. With `saveMode: 'batch'`, it is the same as `batch`. |
| `cell` | In the cells | When leaving each cell (Enter, Tab, an arrow key or a click elsewhere), or for a new row, when leaving the row | A validation message keeps the cell open until it is fixed or Escape is pressed. |
| `batch` | In the cells | `saveChanges()` (“Save changes”) | Sets the save mode to `'batch'`, regardless of `saveMode`. |
| `form` | In a form that replaces the row, as wide as the grid | On Save (or Enter). Cancel and Escape discard the edit. | Typing on a cell does not open it. Use Enter, F2, the start-edit click, the `edit` action, `editRow()` or `addRow()`. |
| `popup` | In the same form, in a modal window | On Save (or Enter). Cancel, Escape and the close button discard the edit. | Focus stays in the window and returns to the row. |

In `popup` mode, the same form opens in the kit's `MxForm` as a modal window, for both existing and new rows (`addRow()`, “New row”). Focus stays in the window, Enter activates Save and Escape activates Cancel, and focus returns to the row when the window closes. `popup` sets the title and size, and `form` and the columns' `formItem` set the fields.

```tsx
/** An order, as stored by the sample server. */
export interface Order {
  id: number;
  customer: string;
  city: string;
  date: string;
  status: string;
  paid: boolean;
  amount: number;
  note: string;
}
```

| Setting | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `editMode` | `'row'` | How rows are edited and when a row is submitted for saving (see the table above). Changing to or from `batch` reloads the data, as with `saveMode`. |
| `confirmDelete` | `true` | Prompts before deleting a row (`deleteRow()`, `deleteRows()`, the `remove` action), once for all the rows an action deletes. This does not apply in batch mode, where a deletion is only marked and can be undone. Strings: `gridConfirmDelete`, `gridConfirmDeleteRows`, `gridConfirmDeleteTitle`. |
| `selectTextOnEditStart` | `true` | Selects the text of a cell or form field when its editor opens. When disabled, the caret moves to the end. |

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `form.items` | `Bind<(string \| FormItem)[]>` | Every column | The contents of the form, in order: a column by field name, or a kit `FormItem`. An item whose `field` matches a column uses that column's editor (by type, a lookup's, or the column's own `editor`), with the item's `label`, `colSpan`, `helpText`, `visible` and `editorProps`. Groups (`group`, `items`, `columns`), buttons and `template` items belong to the form. By default, the form includes every column, visible ones first, and a column the user cannot fill appears read-only. |
| `form.colCount` | `Bind<number>` | `2` | The number of columns in the form. |
| `form.minColWidth` | `Bind<string>` | — | Fits as many columns as possible, each at least this wide. `colCount` sets the maximum. |
| `form.labelMode` | `Bind<'top' \| 'side' \| 'floating' \| 'hidden'>` | `'top'` | Label placement. |
| `popup.title, popup.showTitle` | `Bind<string>`, `Bind<boolean>` | “Edit row” / “New row”, `true` | The window's title. When hidden, it still names the window for screen readers. |
| `popup.width, popup.height` | `Bind<number \| string>` | As the form requires | A CSS length, or pixels. |
| `popup.resizable, popup.movable` | `Bind<boolean>` | `true` | Whether it can be resized from its edges and moved by its title bar. |
| `popup.showCloseButton, popup.showMaximize, popup.fullScreen` | `Bind<boolean>` | `true`, `false`, `false` | The close button (which cancels), the maximize button, and opening maximized. |

| Column field | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `formItem.visible` | `Bind<boolean>` | Whether the column appears in the form. |
| `formItem.colSpan` | `number \| 'all'` | The number of form columns it spans. |
| `formItem.label, formItem.helpText` | `Bind<string>` | The label (by default, the title) and a line of text below the editor. |
| `formItem.editorOptions` | `Record<string, unknown>` | Props of its editor in the form only, which override the column's. |
| `formItem.order` | `number` | Its position in the form, with lower values first. |
| `validationRules` | `GridValidationRule[]` | The rules described below, checked after `required` and `validate`. |

## Validation rules

A column's `validationRules` are validated with the kit's validation rules as a value is entered, and again before its row is saved. `required` and `validate` still run before them. Rules run in order, and `async` rules run last, together. The row waits for their results, with its cell shown as busy in the meantime. A value is not validated twice: only `reevaluate` (on for `async`) and `compare` rules run on every validation of the row. `onRowValidating` occurs after the cells, for the row as a whole. Messages appear in the cells, the form and the window. In this example, the server rejects a customer whose name contains “test”.

```tsx
/** An order, as stored by the sample server. */
export interface Order {
  id: number;
  customer: string;
  city: string;
  date: string;
  status: string;
  paid: boolean;
  amount: number;
  note: string;
}
```

| Rule type | Options | Valid when |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `required` | `trim` (default `true`) | An empty value (spaces only, with `trim`) is invalid. |
| `numeric` | `ignoreEmptyValue` (`true`) | A number, or text that represents a number. |
| `range` | `min`, `max` (`Bind<number \| Date>`), `ignoreEmptyValue` (`true`), `reevaluate` | Between the bounds, for numbers or dates. |
| `stringLength` | `min`, `max`, `trim` (`true`), `ignoreEmptyValue` (`false`) | The length of the text. |
| `pattern` | `pattern` (`Bind<RegExp \| string>`), `ignoreEmptyValue` (`true`) | It matches. A string is found anywhere in the value, as with `new RegExp(pattern)`. |
| `email` | `ignoreEmptyValue` (`true`) | An email address. |
| `compare` | `comparisonTarget(row, context)` (`context.getValue('password')` returns the entered value, otherwise the row's), `comparisonType` (`'=='`, `'!='`, `'==='`, `'!=='`, `'<'`, `'<='`, `'>'`, `'>='`), `ignoreEmptyValue` (`false`) | Compares the value with what the function returns, such as another field of the row. Runs on every validation of the row. |
| `custom` | `validationCallback({ value, row, context, column, rule })` (`row` is the row itself, and `context` holds the entered values: `values`, `getValue(field)`), `ignoreEmptyValue` (`false`), `reevaluate` (`false`) | `true` is valid, `false` is invalid with `message`, and a string is invalid with that text. |
| `async` | `validationCallback(…)` returning a promise, `ignoreEmptyValue` (`false`), `reevaluate` (`true`) | The result: `true`, `false`, a message or `{ isValid, message }`. A rejection is invalid with its message. The row waits for the result before it is sent, and its cell appears busy. |

Every rule accepts a `message` (`Bind<string>`). Without it, the text comes from `uiLocale` (or the grid's `texts`): `required`, `gridInvalidNumber`, `tooShort` / `tooLong`, `outOfRange` / `tooSmall` / `tooLarge`, `invalidFormat`, `invalidEmail`, `noMatch`, `invalid`.

## Events and methods

| Event | Parameters | When |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `onEditingStart` | `{ field, row, values, getValue, rowIndex, isNew, cancel }` | Occurs before a cell editor or a row's form (`field` `''`) opens. Set `cancel` to leave the row unchanged. `row` is the row itself (a class instance stays one), `values` holds the entered, unsaved values, and `getValue(field)` returns the entered value, otherwise the row's. |
| `onEditorPreparing` | `{ field, row, values, getValue, isNew, options, cancel }` | Occurs before the editor of a cell or form field is created. Change its props, or set `cancel` to omit a field from the form. |
| `onEditorPrepared` | `{ field, row, values, getValue, isNew, editor, element, place: 'cell' \| 'form' }` | Occurs after an editor is created. |
| `onRowValidating` | `{ key, row, values, getValue, isNew, changed, errors, isValid, errorText, cancel }` | Occurs when a row is validated before saving, after its cells and their async rules. Add or remove messages in `errors` (by field, with `''` for the row), or set `isValid = false` with `errorText`. Occurs once per validation of the row. |
| `onInitNewRow, onSaving, onRowInserting, onRowUpdating, onEditCanceling …` | See [Events](datagrid-layout.md#events) | The same in every edit mode: Save in a form is a save, and Cancel is a cancel. |

| Member | Returns | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `editRow(i) / editRowByKey(key)` | `boolean` | Opens the first editor of a row, or its form (`form`, `popup`), by key while the row is loaded. |
| `addRow(values?)` | `Promise<boolean>` | Opens a new row: in its cells, in place as a form, or in the window. |
| `saveEditData()` | `Promise<boolean>` | Saves the current edit, as Save does: the form, otherwise the row being edited, and in batch mode every unsaved change. |
| `cancelEditData()` | `void` | Discards the current edit, as Cancel does, and in batch mode every unsaved change. |
| `closeEditCell()` | `boolean` | Keeps the open editor's value and closes it. In a form, it keeps every field's value. |
| `form, popup` | read/write, live | `grid.form.colCount = 3`, `grid.popup.width = '40rem'`. A function is tracked, and `onOptionChanged` reports `form.colCount`, `popup.width` and so on. |

## Example files

`FormMode.tsx`

```tsx
import { reactive } from '@motifx/core';
import { data } from '@motifx-community/data';
import { Button, DataGrid, Stack, type GridColumn, type GridSettings } from '@motifx-community/ui';
import type { Order } from './order';
import { OrderService } from './order-service';
import { columns, makeOrders, newOrder } from './orders';

const MODES: GridSettings['editMode'][] = ['row', 'cell', 'batch', 'form', 'popup'];

/** The note gets the whole width of the form and a line of help. */
const formColumns: GridColumn<Order>[] = columns.map((c) => (c.field === 'note' ? { ...c, formItem: { colSpan: 'all', helpText: 'Shown to the courier.' } } : c));

/** One grid in every edit mode; in 'form' the row opens as a form with two groups. */
export default function FormMode() {
  const s = reactive({ mode: 'form' as GridSettings['editMode'] });
  const service = new OrderService({ data: makeOrders(40), key: 'id', createKey: (_values, rows) => rows.length + 1 }, 300);
  const orders = new data.DataSource<Order, number>({ adapter: service, loadMode: 'all' });

  return (
    <>
      <Stack orientation="horizontal" wrap align="center" role="group" aria-label="Edit mode">
        {MODES.map((mode) => (
          <Button key={mode} text={mode} size="sm" variant={() => (s.mode === mode ? 'solid' : 'ghost')} aria-pressed={() => s.mode === mode} onclick={() => (s.mode = mode)} />
        ))}
      </Stack>
      <DataGrid
        class="dg-form"
        style="block-size: 30rem"
        dataSource={orders}
        columns={formColumns}
        label="Orders in an edit form"
        locale="en"
        settings={{ editable: true, addRows: true, editMode: () => s.mode }}
        newRow={{ create: newOrder }}
        actions={['edit', 'remove']}
        form={{
          colCount: 2,
          items: [
            { group: 'Order', items: [{ field: 'customer' }, { field: 'date' }, { field: 'status' }, { field: 'amount' }] },
            { group: 'Delivery', items: [{ field: 'city' }, { field: 'paid' }, { field: 'note' }] },
          ],
        }}
      />
    </>
  );
}
```

`order-service.ts`

```tsx
import { data } from '@motifx-community/data';
import { SlowAdapter } from '../../../shared/slow-adapter';
import type { Order } from './order';

/** Orders in memory that answer like a server, and turn down a note with "error" in it. */
export class OrderService extends SlowAdapter<Order, number> {
  protected override updateRow(key: number, changes: Partial<Order>): Promise<Partial<Order>> {
    return this.later(changes, () => super.updateRow(key, changes));
  }

  protected override insertRow(values: Partial<Order>): Promise<Partial<Order>> {
    return this.later(values, () => super.insertRow(values));
  }

  private later(values: Partial<Order>, save: () => Promise<Partial<Order>>): Promise<Partial<Order>> {
    const message = 'The server does not take this note.';
    return new Promise((done, fail) =>
      setTimeout(() => {
        if (String(values.note ?? '').includes('error')) fail(data.DataError.create('MJD202', { operation: 'save', fields: { note: message } }, message));
        else save().then(done, fail);
      }, 300),
    );
  }
}
```

`orders.ts`

```tsx
import type { GridColumn } from '@motifx-community/ui';
import type { Order } from './order';

const CUSTOMERS = ['Ada Lovelace', 'Grace Hopper', 'Alan Turing', 'Cahit Arf', 'Katherine Johnson', 'Edsger Dijkstra', 'Barbara Liskov', 'Donald Knuth', 'İlhan Koman', 'Margaret Hamilton'];
const CITIES = ['Ankara', 'Antalya', 'Bursa', 'İstanbul', 'İzmir', 'Konya', 'Trabzon'];
const STATUSES = ['Draft', 'Approved', 'Shipped', 'Delivered', 'Cancelled'];
const NOTES = ['', 'Leave at the door', 'Call before delivery', 'Gift wrap, please, with a card that says happy birthday', '', 'Fragile'];

/** `n` sample orders, the same ones every time. */
export function makeOrders(n: number): Order[] {
  const day = Date.UTC(2026, 0, 1);
  return Array.from({ length: n }, (_, i) => ({
    id: i + 1,
    customer: CUSTOMERS[(i * 7) % CUSTOMERS.length],
    city: CITIES[(i * 3) % CITIES.length],
    date: new Date(day + ((i * 37) % 300) * 86_400_000).toISOString().slice(0, 10),
    status: STATUSES[i % STATUSES.length],
    paid: i % 3 === 0,
    amount: ((i * 7919) % 100_000) / 100,
    note: NOTES[i % NOTES.length],
  }));
}

const money = new Intl.NumberFormat('en', { minimumFractionDigits: 2, maximumFractionDigits: 2 });

/** The order columns: the number pinned to the start, the amount to the end. */
export const columns: GridColumn<Order>[] = [
  { field: 'id', title: 'No', type: 'number', width: 80, sticky: 'start', editable: false },
  { field: 'customer', title: 'Customer', width: 180, flex: 1, required: true },
  { field: 'city', title: 'City', type: 'list', width: 120, options: CITIES },
  { field: 'date', title: 'Date', type: 'date', width: 130, editable: false, creatable: true },
  { field: 'status', title: 'Status', type: 'list', width: 120, options: STATUSES, required: true },
  { field: 'paid', title: 'Paid', type: 'boolean', width: 80 },
  { field: 'note', title: 'Note', width: 200 },
  {
    field: 'amount',
    title: 'Amount',
    type: 'number',
    width: 120,
    sticky: 'end',
    required: true,
    validate: (v) => (typeof v === 'number' && v < 0 ? 'The amount cannot be negative.' : null),
    format: (v) => (typeof v === 'number' ? money.format(v) : ''),
  },
];

/** The same columns with a filter cell and a header filter on most of them. */
export const filterColumns: GridColumn<Order>[] = columns.map((c) => ({ ...c, filterRow: c.field !== 'note', headerFilter: c.field !== 'note' && c.field !== 'id' }));

const today = () => new Date().toISOString().slice(0, 10);

/** What a new order starts with. */
export const newOrder = () => ({ date: today(), status: 'Draft', paid: false });
```

`ValidationRules.tsx`

```tsx
import { reactive } from '@motifx/core';
import { Button, DataGrid, Stack, type GridColumn, type GridSettings } from '@motifx-community/ui';
import type { Order } from './order';
import { columns, makeOrders, newOrder } from './orders';

const MODES: GridSettings['editMode'][] = ['row', 'form', 'popup'];

/** A pretend server: half a second to answer whether a customer may order. */
function customerAllowed(name: string): Promise<{ isValid: boolean; message?: string }> {
  return new Promise((done) => setTimeout(() => done(/test/i.test(name) ? { isValid: false, message: 'The server does not take test customers.' } : { isValid: true }), 500));
}

/** Validation rules on the columns, checked as values are entered and before a row is saved. */
const ruleColumns: GridColumn<Order>[] = columns.map((c) => {
  if (c.field === 'customer') {
    return {
      ...c,
      required: false,
      validationRules: [
        { type: 'required' },
        { type: 'stringLength', min: 3, max: 40 },
        { type: 'async', validationCallback: ({ value }) => customerAllowed(String(value)) },
      ],
    };
  }
  if (c.field === 'amount') return { ...c, validate: undefined, validationRules: [{ type: 'range', min: 1, max: 5000, message: 'An order is between 1 and 5,000.' }] };
  if (c.field === 'note') return { ...c, validationRules: [{ type: 'stringLength', max: 60 }, { type: 'pattern', pattern: /^[^<>]*$/, message: 'No angle brackets.' }] };
  return c;
});

/** Rules on the cells, a check of the whole row, and the messages in the cells, the form or the window. */
export default function ValidationRules() {
  const s = reactive({ mode: 'row' as GridSettings['editMode'] });
  return (
    <>
      <Stack orientation="horizontal" wrap align="center" role="group" aria-label="Edit mode">
        {MODES.map((mode) => (
          <Button key={mode} text={mode} size="sm" variant={() => (s.mode === mode ? 'solid' : 'ghost')} aria-pressed={() => s.mode === mode} onclick={() => (s.mode = mode)} />
        ))}
      </Stack>
      <DataGrid
        class="dg-rules"
        style="block-size: 28rem"
        rows={makeOrders(20)}
        rowKey="id"
        columns={ruleColumns}
        label="Orders with rules"
        locale="en"
        settings={{ editable: true, addRows: true, editMode: () => s.mode }}
        newRow={{ create: newOrder }}
        onRowValidating={(e) => {
          if (e.row.status === 'Cancelled' && e.row.paid) e.errors.paid = 'A cancelled order is not paid.';
        }}
      />
    </>
  );
}
```


---

# DataGrid: Filtering and search

> DataGrid · @motifx-community/ui 0.1.0-beta.5

## Filters

The filter row has one cell per column, with a condition chosen in the cell according to the column type (contains, starts with, =, <, between, empty …) and the kit field for the value. Typing applies the filter after a short pause. The header filter lists the column's values with their counts, taking the other filters into account. For in-memory rows, the grid does the counting. An adapter that supports grouping is queried with `group`, and any other server answers through `loadValues`. Both feed the data source's filter (`data.where`, `data.and`, `data.or`), combined with AND.

```tsx
/** An order, as stored by the sample server. */
export interface Order {
  id: number;
  customer: string;
  city: string;
  date: string;
  status: string;
  paid: boolean;
  amount: number;
  note: string;
}
```

## Filter panel and builder

`settings.filterPanel` adds a panel below the rows that shows the filter value as text, such as `[City] Equals 'Ankara' And [Amount] Is greater than '900.00'`, using column titles, formats and lookup text. Clicking it opens the kit's [FilterBuilder](filterbuilder.md) in a modal window with every column (`filterBuilder` disables it for a column), and with “is any of” and “is none of” for each one. OK applies the value as the filter value, and Cancel and Escape discard it. The check box turns the filter value off and on, and Clear removes it.

With `filterSyncEnabled` (on while the panel is visible), the filter row and header filters are part of the filter value. A condition set in the builder appears in the column's cell or value list if they can display it (one each), and what they set appears in the panel and opens in the builder. Conditions they cannot display, such as an OR group or a second condition on a column, stay only in the filter value. The filter goes to the data source like any other. This example uses 100,000 orders on a server, or 200 in memory. A layout saved with `layoutKey`, and `state()`, keep the filter value and the check box.

```tsx
import { data } from '@motifx-community/data';

/** Rows in memory that answer a little later, the way a server does; for the examples. */
export class SlowAdapter<T extends object, K> extends data.ArrayAdapter<T, K> {
  constructor(
    options: data.ArrayAdapterOptions<T>,
    private readonly delayMs = 300,
  ) {
    super(options);
  }

  override async load(options: data.LoadOptions = {}): Promise<data.LoadResult<T>> {
    await new Promise((done) => setTimeout(done, this.delayMs));
    return super.load(options);
  }
}
```

| Option | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `settings.filterPanel` | The panel below the rows: the check box, the filter as text (clicking it opens the builder), “Create Filter” when there is no filter, and “Clear”. `boolean`, default `false`. |
| `settings.filterSyncEnabled` | Makes the filter row and header filters part of the filter value, in both directions. `'auto'` applies while the panel is visible. `boolean \| 'auto'`, default `'auto'`. |
| `settings.filterBuilder, column `filterBuilder`` | Whether the column is a field in the builder. `boolean`, default `true`. |
| `filterValue` | The filter value. A function is tracked, and user changes arrive in `onFilterChanged` (`e.filterValue`). Also available as a property. `Bind<data.FilterExpression \| null>`, default `null`. |
| `filterEnabled` | Whether the filter value applies, which is the panel's check box. Also available as a property. `Bind<boolean>`, default `true`. |
| `filterPanelText` | Customizes the panel's text, starting from the default text. `({ text, filterValue }) => string`. |
| `filterBuilder` | Any prop of `FilterBuilder` except `value` and `fields` (`customOperations`, `maxGroupLevel`, `groupOperations`, its events …), also live as `grid.filterBuilder`. `GridFilterBuilderOptions`, default `{}`. |
| `filterBuilderPopup` | The window: `title`, `showTitle`, `width` (`'40rem'`), `height`, `resizable`, `movable`, `showCloseButton`, `showMaximize`, `fullScreen`. Also live as `grid.filterBuilderPopup`. `GridFilterBuilderPopup`, default `{}`. |
| `openFilterBuilder(), closeFilterBuilder(apply?), clearFilterValue()` | The panel's actions, available programmatically. `filterText` is the panel's text, and `filterBuilderInstance` is the open builder. |
| `onFilterBuilderOpening / Opened, onFilterBuilderClosing / Closed` | `e.cancel` keeps the builder closed or open, and `e.apply` and `e.applied` indicate whether OK was clicked. `onFilterChanging` (cancelable) and `onFilterChanged` also include `filterValue` and `filterEnabled`. |

## Ranges, dates and custom entries

A column's `headerFilterInterval` groups its header filter. A number column uses ranges of that size (“0 – 250”, “250 – 500”), and several sizes such as `[1000, 100]` create a tree. A date column uses a tree of years, months and days, down to the part it names (`'year'`, `'quarter'`, `'month'`, `'day'`, `'hour'`, `'minute'`, `'second'`), and `null` lists individual dates. Dates are a tree by default, down to the day (`headerFilterDateInterval`). The tree is the kit's `TreeView` with check boxes and “Select all”. A checked month is stored as `'2026/3'` and a year as `2026`, and each filters with `>=` its first moment and `<` the next one's, so a server can run it too. Counts are calculated in the browser from the column's distinct values, whether counted in memory, grouped by an adapter that supports grouping, or from `loadValues`.

`headerFilterItems` provides custom header filter entries, as `{ text, value }`, where a value is a value or a filter expression (`data.where('city', 'in', […])`). A function receives the other filters and `values()`, the entries it would list, so that you can add to them. `filterValues` and `filterType` (both can be tracked functions) set the contents of the header filter. `'exclude'` leaves those values out, so values added later appear. In the list, selecting every value and then deselecting some leaves those out in the same way.

```tsx
/** An order, as stored by the sample server. */
export interface Order {
  id: number;
  customer: string;
  city: string;
  date: string;
  status: string;
  paid: boolean;
  amount: number;
  note: string;
}
```

## Search panel

`searchPanel` adds a search box to the toolbar. Its text is searched in every searchable column at once, after a short typing pause. Each column interprets it according to its type: text columns contain it (case-insensitive and locale-aware), number, date and yes/no columns match when it can be read as one of their values, and list columns match their option text. The columns are joined with OR, and then with the filter row and header filter with AND. Text that no column can interpret returns no rows. The filter goes to the data source like any other (`data.where`, `data.or`), so a server can run it, and matches are highlighted in the cells. `searchText` binds the text in both directions with `onSearchTextChanged`, and `searchByText()` searches programmatically.

A lookup column is searched through its text. The lookup source (here, a customer service separate from the sales server) is queried for items whose text contains the search, up to `searchLimit`, and their keys go to the row server as `customerId in [...]`. A column with a `textFrom` field searches that field of the row instead.

```tsx
import { data } from '@motifx-community/data';

/** Rows in memory that answer a little later, the way a server does; for the examples. */
export class SlowAdapter<T extends object, K> extends data.ArrayAdapter<T, K> {
  constructor(
    options: data.ArrayAdapterOptions<T>,
    private readonly delayMs = 300,
  ) {
    super(options);
  }

  override async load(options: data.LoadOptions = {}): Promise<data.LoadResult<T>> {
    await new Promise((done) => setTimeout(done, this.delayMs));
    return super.load(options);
  }
}
```
