`Filters.tsx`

```tsx
import { Button, DataGrid, Stack } from '@motifx-community/ui';
import type { Order } from './order';
import { filterColumns, makeOrders } from './orders';

/** The filter row and the header filter, on rows in memory. */
export default function Filters() {
  let grid: DataGrid<Order> | null = null;

  const setFilters = () => {
    if (grid) grid.filters = { city: { values: ['Ankara', 'İzmir'] }, amount: { op: 'between', value: 100, value2: 500 } };
  };

  return (
    <>
      <DataGrid
        class="dg-filters"
        style="block-size: 30rem"
        rows={makeOrders(200)}
        rowKey="id"
        columns={filterColumns}
        label="Orders to filter"
        locale="en"
        settings={{ striped: true }}
        ref={(g: DataGrid<Order>) => (grid = g)}
      />
      <Stack orientation="horizontal" wrap align="center">
        <Button text="Ankara and İzmir, 100 to 500" variant="outline" onclick={setFilters} />
        <Button text="Clear the filters" variant="ghost" onclick={() => grid?.clearFilters()} />
        <output class="dg-filter-count">{() => `${grid?.total ?? 0} of 200 orders`}</output>
      </Stack>
    </>
  );
}
```

`orders.ts`

```tsx
import type { GridColumn } from '@motifx-community/ui';
import type { Order } from './order';

const CUSTOMERS = ['Ada Lovelace', 'Grace Hopper', 'Alan Turing', 'Cahit Arf', 'Katherine Johnson', 'Edsger Dijkstra', 'Barbara Liskov', 'Donald Knuth', 'İlhan Koman', 'Margaret Hamilton'];
const CITIES = ['Ankara', 'Antalya', 'Bursa', 'İstanbul', 'İzmir', 'Konya', 'Trabzon'];
const STATUSES = ['Draft', 'Approved', 'Shipped', 'Delivered', 'Cancelled'];
const NOTES = ['', 'Leave at the door', 'Call before delivery', 'Gift wrap, please, with a card that says happy birthday', '', 'Fragile'];

/** `n` sample orders, the same ones every time. */
export function makeOrders(n: number): Order[] {
  const day = Date.UTC(2026, 0, 1);
  return Array.from({ length: n }, (_, i) => ({
    id: i + 1,
    customer: CUSTOMERS[(i * 7) % CUSTOMERS.length],
    city: CITIES[(i * 3) % CITIES.length],
    date: new Date(day + ((i * 37) % 300) * 86_400_000).toISOString().slice(0, 10),
    status: STATUSES[i % STATUSES.length],
    paid: i % 3 === 0,
    amount: ((i * 7919) % 100_000) / 100,
    note: NOTES[i % NOTES.length],
  }));
}

const money = new Intl.NumberFormat('en', { minimumFractionDigits: 2, maximumFractionDigits: 2 });

/** The order columns: the number pinned to the start, the amount to the end. */
export const columns: GridColumn<Order>[] = [
  { field: 'id', title: 'No', type: 'number', width: 80, sticky: 'start', editable: false },
  { field: 'customer', title: 'Customer', width: 180, flex: 1, required: true },
  { field: 'city', title: 'City', type: 'list', width: 120, options: CITIES },
  { field: 'date', title: 'Date', type: 'date', width: 130, editable: false, creatable: true },
  { field: 'status', title: 'Status', type: 'list', width: 120, options: STATUSES, required: true },
  { field: 'paid', title: 'Paid', type: 'boolean', width: 80 },
  { field: 'note', title: 'Note', width: 200 },
  {
    field: 'amount',
    title: 'Amount',
    type: 'number',
    width: 120,
    sticky: 'end',
    required: true,
    validate: (v) => (typeof v === 'number' && v < 0 ? 'The amount cannot be negative.' : null),
    format: (v) => (typeof v === 'number' ? money.format(v) : ''),
  },
];

/** The same columns with a filter cell and a header filter on most of them. */
export const filterColumns: GridColumn<Order>[] = columns.map((c) => ({ ...c, filterRow: c.field !== 'note', headerFilter: c.field !== 'note' && c.field !== 'id' }));

const today = () => new Date().toISOString().slice(0, 10);

/** What a new order starts with. */
export const newOrder = () => ({ date: today(), status: 'Draft', paid: false });
```

`FilterPanel.tsx`

```tsx
import { reactive } from '@motifx/core';
import { data } from '@motifx-community/data';
import { Button, DataGrid, RadioGroup, Stack, Switch } from '@motifx-community/ui';
import { SlowAdapter } from '../../../shared/slow-adapter';
import type { Order } from './order';
import { filterColumns, makeOrders } from './orders';

/** The filter panel and its builder, on 100,000 orders of a server or 200 in memory, the filter row and header filters kept in step. */
export default function FilterPanel() {
  const orders = new data.DataSource<Order, number>({ adapter: new SlowAdapter<Order, number>({ data: makeOrders(100_000), key: 'id' }, 200), loadMode: 'blocks', pageSize: 100 });
  const rows = makeOrders(200);
  const s = reactive({ where: 'server', sync: true, filter: null as data.FilterExpression | null });
  let grid: DataGrid<Order> | null = null;

  return (
    <>
      <Stack orientation="horizontal" wrap align="center">
        <RadioGroup
          label="Rows"
          orientation="horizontal"
          items={[
            { value: 'server', text: '100,000 on a server' },
            { value: 'memory', text: '200 in memory' },
          ]}
          x-model={() => s.where}
        />
        <Switch label="filterSyncEnabled" x-model={() => s.sync} />
        <Button text="Open the builder" variant="outline" onclick={() => grid?.openFilterBuilder()} />
        <Button
          text="Paid, over 900"
          variant="ghost"
          onclick={() => (s.filter = data.and(data.where('paid', '=', true), data.where('amount', '>', 900)))}
        />
      </Stack>
      <DataGrid
        class="dg-server-filters"
        style="block-size: 30rem"
        dataSource={() => (s.where === 'server' ? orders : null)}
        rows={rows}
        rowKey="id"
        columns={filterColumns}
        label="Orders with a filter panel"
        locale="en"
        settings={{ filterPanel: true, filterSyncEnabled: () => s.sync }}
        filterValue={() => s.filter}
        filterBuilder={{ maxGroupLevel: 2 }}
        filterBuilderPopup={{ title: 'Filter the orders' }}
        onFilterChanged={(e) => (s.filter = e.filterValue)}
        ref={(g: DataGrid<Order>) => (grid = g)}
      />
      <output class="dg-server-filter">{() => `${(grid?.total ?? 0).toLocaleString('en')} orders · ${JSON.stringify(grid?.filter ?? null)}`}</output>
      <output class="dg-filter-value">{() => `filterValue: ${JSON.stringify(s.filter)}`}</output>
    </>
  );
}
```

`HeaderFilterIntervals.tsx`

```tsx
import { reactive } from '@motifx/core';
import { data } from '@motifx-community/data';
import { Button, DataGrid, Stack, type GridColumn } from '@motifx-community/ui';
import type { Order } from './order';
import { columns, makeOrders } from './orders';

const COAST = ['Antalya', 'İstanbul', 'İzmir', 'Trabzon'];

/** The order columns with header filters: amounts in ranges, dates in a tree, cities with custom entries, and excluded statuses. */
const intervalColumns: GridColumn<Order>[] = columns.map((c) => {
  switch (c.field) {
    case 'amount':
      // "0 – 250", "250 – 500" …
      return { ...c, headerFilter: true, headerFilterInterval: 250 };
    case 'date':
      // Year → month → day, by the grid's headerFilterDateInterval.
      return { ...c, headerFilter: true };
    case 'city':
      return {
        ...c,
        headerFilter: true,
        headerFilterItems: [
          { text: 'On the coast', value: data.where('city', 'in', COAST) },
          { text: 'Inland', value: data.not(data.where('city', 'in', COAST)) },
          { text: 'Ankara only', value: 'Ankara' },
        ],
      };
    case 'status':
      // Every status except Cancelled, so statuses added later also appear.
      return { ...c, headerFilter: true, filterValues: ['Cancelled'], filterType: 'exclude' };
    default:
      return c;
  }
});

/** The header filter with ranges of amounts, a tree of dates, custom entries and excluded values. */
export default function HeaderFilterIntervals() {
  const s = reactive({ months: false });
  let grid: DataGrid<Order> | null = null;

  return (
    <>
      <Stack orientation="horizontal" wrap align="center">
        <Button text={() => (s.months ? 'Dates down to the day' : 'Dates down to the month')} variant="outline" onclick={() => (s.months = !s.months)} />
        <Button text="Amounts in ranges of 1,000" variant="outline" onclick={() => grid?.columnOption('amount', 'headerFilterInterval', 1000)} />
        <Button text="Clear the filters" variant="ghost" onclick={() => grid?.clearFilters()} />
      </Stack>
      <DataGrid
        class="dg-intervals"
        style="block-size: 30rem"
        rows={makeOrders(300)}
        rowKey="id"
        columns={intervalColumns}
        label="Orders filtered by ranges and dates"
        locale="en"
        settings={{ headerFilterDateInterval: () => (s.months ? 'month' : 'day') }}
        ref={(g: DataGrid<Order>) => (grid = g)}
      />
      <output class="dg-intervals-filter">{() => `${grid?.total ?? 0} orders · ${JSON.stringify(grid?.filters ?? {})}`}</output>
    </>
  );
}
```

`Search.tsx`

```tsx
import { reactive } from '@motifx/core';
import { data } from '@motifx-community/data';
import { Button, CheckBox, DataGrid, Stack, type GridColumn } from '@motifx-community/ui';
import { SlowAdapter } from '../../../shared/slow-adapter';
import { makeCustomers, type Customer } from './customers';
import { columns, makeOrders } from './orders';

type Sale = { id: number; customerId: number; amount: number };

const money = new Intl.NumberFormat('en', { minimumFractionDigits: 2, maximumFractionDigits: 2 });

/** The search panel over rows in memory, and over a server whose customer names live on another service. */
export default function Search() {
  const s = reactive({ text: 'ankara', caseSensitive: false });

  // The sales and the customers are two services: the search asks the customers' service for the
  // names, then the sales' server only for keys.
  const customers = new data.DataSource<Customer, number>({ adapter: new SlowAdapter<Customer, number>({ data: makeCustomers(600), key: 'id' }, 300) });
  const salesServer = new SlowAdapter<Sale, number>({ data: Array.from({ length: 50_000 }, (_, i) => ({ id: i + 1, customerId: ((i * 37) % 600) + 1, amount: ((i * 7919) % 100_000) / 100 })), key: 'id' }, 250);
  const sales = new data.DataSource<Sale, number>({ adapter: salesServer, loadMode: 'blocks', pageSize: 100 });
  const saleColumns: GridColumn<Sale>[] = [
    { field: 'id', title: 'No', type: 'number', width: 90 },
    { field: 'customerId', title: 'Customer', flex: 1, width: 220, lookup: { dataSource: customers, valueField: 'id', textField: 'name' } },
    { field: 'amount', title: 'Amount', type: 'number', width: 120, format: (v) => (typeof v === 'number' ? money.format(v) : '') },
  ];
  let server: DataGrid<Sale> | null = null;

  return (
    <>
      <Stack orientation="horizontal" wrap align="center">
        <Button text="Search for “approved”" variant="outline" onclick={() => (s.text = 'approved')} />
        <CheckBox label="Mark only the same case" x-model={() => s.caseSensitive} />
      </Stack>
      <DataGrid
        class="dg-search"
        style="block-size: 30rem"
        rows={makeOrders(200)}
        rowKey="id"
        columns={columns}
        label="Orders to search"
        locale="en"
        searchText={() => s.text}
        onSearchTextChanged={(e) => (s.text = e.text)}
        settings={{ searchPanel: true, searchPanelWidth: 220, highlightCaseSensitive: () => s.caseSensitive }}
      />
      <output class="dg-search-text">{() => `Searching for “${s.text}”`}</output>
      <DataGrid
        class="dg-server-search"
        style="block-size: 30rem"
        dataSource={sales}
        columns={saleColumns}
        label="50,000 sales to search"
        locale="en"
        settings={{ searchPanel: true, searchPlaceholder: 'A customer, an amount…' }}
        ref={(g: DataGrid<Sale>) => (server = g)}
      />
      <output class="dg-server-search-filter">{() => `${(server?.total ?? 0).toLocaleString('en')} sales · ${JSON.stringify(server?.filter ?? null)}`}</output>
    </>
  );
}
```


# DataGrid: Lookup columns

> DataGrid · @motifx-community/ui 0.1.0-beta.5

## Lookup columns

A column with `lookup` holds a key, such as a customer ID, and displays the text of the matching item. Items can come from an array or from a `DataSource` of any adapter, including another service or a different protocol from the rows. Only the keys on screen are requested. Unknown keys at any given moment are sent together (`id in [...]`, up to `batchSize` each), or one at a time with `resolve: 'byKey'` for a service that returns one item by key. Texts are cached per source and shared by every column and grid that uses it. While a key loads, its cell is empty and busy. A key the source does not contain appears as it is, muted, and prevents its row from being saved.

```tsx
import { data } from '@motifx-community/data';

/** Rows in memory that answer a little later, the way a server does; for the examples. */
export class SlowAdapter<T extends object, K> extends data.ArrayAdapter<T, K> {
  constructor(
    options: data.ArrayAdapterOptions<T>,
    private readonly delayMs = 300,
  ) {
    super(options);
  }

  override async load(options: data.LoadOptions = {}): Promise<data.LoadResult<T>> {
    await new Promise((done) => setTimeout(done, this.delayMs));
    return super.load(options);
  }
}
```

Editing opens a `DropDown` with search (or `editor: 'combobox'`, or the kit's `Lookup` with columns) over its own data source on the same adapter, so its search never affects a source displayed on the page. Typing on the cell opens the list and searches the typed text, and the selected text appears immediately. `filter(row, context)` narrows the list for the row (through `context.getValue`, so a newly selected province is included), `setCellValue` writes other fields along with the value (in this example, a new province clears the district), and `onEditorPreparing` changes the editor's props, so the district waits for a province (`e.getValue('province')`).

```tsx
/** Provinces and their districts, for the cascading lists. */
export interface Province {
  code: string;
  name: string;
}

export interface District {
  id: number;
  name: string;
  province: string;
}

export const PROVINCES: Province[] = [
  { code: 'AN', name: 'Ankara' },
  { code: 'IS', name: 'İstanbul' },
  { code: 'IZ', name: 'İzmir' },
];

export const DISTRICTS: District[] = [
  { id: 1, name: 'Çankaya', province: 'AN' },
  { id: 2, name: 'Keçiören', province: 'AN' },
  { id: 3, name: 'Yenimahalle', province: 'AN' },
  { id: 4, name: 'Kadıköy', province: 'IS' },
  { id: 5, name: 'Beşiktaş', province: 'IS' },
  { id: 6, name: 'Üsküdar', province: 'IS' },
  { id: 7, name: 'Bornova', province: 'IZ' },
  { id: 8, name: 'Karşıyaka', province: 'IZ' },
  { id: 9, name: 'Konak', province: 'IZ' },
];
```

When the row already includes the text (OData `$expand`), `textFrom` reads it from the row, and the lookup source is used only for editing and lists. `sortField` sorts on the server by that field. Without them, a lookup column sorts by its key, and in-memory rows can sort by text with `sortBy: 'text'`. The filter row offers “(All)” and the texts (always `=`), and the header filter lists the texts with “(empty)” first. Both are searched by text and, with `syncLookupFilterValues`, contain only the keys of rows that match the other filters. Copy and export write the text (`raw` writes the key), and pasted text becomes the key of the single item that has it.

```tsx
import { data } from '@motifx-community/data';

/** Rows in memory that answer a little later, the way a server does; for the examples. */
export class SlowAdapter<T extends object, K> extends data.ArrayAdapter<T, K> {
  constructor(
    options: data.ArrayAdapterOptions<T>,
    private readonly delayMs = 300,
  ) {
    super(options);
  }

  override async load(options: data.LoadOptions = {}): Promise<data.LoadResult<T>> {
    await new Promise((done) => setTimeout(done, this.delayMs));
    return super.load(options);
  }
}
```

| Lookup field | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `dataSource` | `Bind<DataSource \| unknown[]>`. The items, searched and resolved on their own service, or an in-memory array. |
| `valueField, textField` | The field that matches the cell value (by default, the source's key, or the value itself in an array of plain values), and the displayed text as a field or `(item) => text` (by default, the value). |
| `searchFields` | The fields searched by the editor and text searches. By default, `textField` when it is a field. |
| `filter` | `(row, context) => FilterExpression`. Narrows the items for a row (for cascading lists, `context.getValue('province')` returns the entered value, otherwise the row's). `row` is `null` for filter lists. |
| `allowClearing` | `Bind<boolean>`. Adds a clear button to the editor. The default is `false`. |
| `resolve, batchSize` | `'batch'` (the default: keys in one request, `batchSize` 100 each) or `'byKey'` (one request per key). |
| `sortBy` | `Bind<'key' \| 'text'>`. Sorts in-memory rows by key (the default) or by displayed text. |
| `editor, editorOptions` | `'dropdown'` (the default), `'combobox'` or `'lookup'`, and props for it (such as a `Lookup`'s `columns`). A column's own `editor` still takes precedence and receives the lookup in its context. |
| `searchLimit` | The maximum number of items containing the search panel's text that the search converts to keys. The default is 100. |
| `filterSearchLimit` | The same for the header filter's search box. The default is 1000. |
| `pageSize` | The number of items the editor's list loads per request while scrolling (with a data source). The default is 50. |
| `parallelRequests` | With `'byKey'`, the number of simultaneous requests. The default is 6. |
| `pasteSearchLimit` | The number of items searched for pasted text. The default is 50. |

`Lookups.tsx`

```tsx
import { reactive } from '@motifx/core';
import { data } from '@motifx-community/data';
import { Button, DataGrid, Stack, type GridColumn } from '@motifx-community/ui';
import { SlowAdapter } from '../../../shared/slow-adapter';
import { makeCustomers, type Customer } from './customers';

type Sale = { id: number; customerId: number | null; amount: number };

const money = new Intl.NumberFormat('en', { minimumFractionDigits: 2, maximumFractionDigits: 2 });

/** In-memory sales whose customer comes from another service: only the customers on screen are requested, several in one request. */
export default function Lookups() {
  const s = reactive({ requests: 0, keys: 0 });
  // Simulates another service. In an application, use new data.RestAdapter({ url: '/api/customers', key: 'id' }) here.
  const service = new SlowAdapter<Customer, number>({ data: makeCustomers(600), key: 'id' }, 400);
  // Counts the requests that turn keys into names; the editor's own list loads are not among them.
  service.onLoading((e) => {
    const asked = e.options.filter as data.FilterCondition | undefined;
    if (asked?.op !== 'in' || !Array.isArray(asked.value)) return;
    s.requests++;
    s.keys = asked.value.length;
  });
  const customers = new data.DataSource<Customer, number>({ adapter: service });
  const sales: Sale[] = Array.from({ length: 300 }, (_, i) => ({ id: i + 1, customerId: i === 4 ? 9999 : ((i * 37) % 600) + 1, amount: ((i * 7919) % 100_000) / 100 }));
  const columns: GridColumn<Sale>[] = [
    { field: 'id', title: 'No', type: 'number', width: 80, editable: false },
    {
      field: 'customerId',
      title: 'Customer',
      width: 220,
      flex: 1,
      required: true,
      filterRow: true,
      headerFilter: true,
      lookup: {
        dataSource: customers,
        valueField: 'id',
        textField: 'name',
        editor: 'lookup',
        editorOptions: { columns: [{ field: 'name', caption: 'Name' }, { field: 'city', caption: 'City', width: '7rem' }] },
      },
    },
    { field: 'amount', title: 'Amount', type: 'number', width: 120, filterRow: true, format: (v) => (typeof v === 'number' ? money.format(v) : '') },
  ];
  let grid: DataGrid<Sale> | null = null;

  return (
    <>
      <DataGrid
        class="dg-lookups"
        style="block-size: 30rem"
        rows={sales}
        rowKey="id"
        columns={columns}
        label="Sales with customers from another service"
        locale="en"
        saveMode="batch"
        settings={{ editable: true, filterDelay: 200 }}
        ref={(g: DataGrid<Sale>) => (grid = g)}
      />
      <Stack orientation="horizontal" wrap align="center">
        <Button text="Read the names again" variant="outline" onclick={() => grid?.refreshLookups()} />
        <output class="dg-lookup-requests">{() => `${s.requests} requests for names to the customers service, the last for ${s.keys} customers`}</output>
      </Stack>
    </>
  );
}
```

```tsx
import { DISTRICTS, PROVINCES } from './places';

type Branch = { id: number; name: string; province: string | null; district: number | null };

  { id: 1, name: 'Head office', province: 'AN', district: 1 },
  { id: 2, name: 'Harbour', province: 'IZ', district: 9 },

      style="block-size: 24rem"
      rows={branches}

      columns={columns}
      label="Branches"
      locale="en"
      settings={{ editable: true, addRows: true, filterRow: true, headerFilter: true }}
      newRow={{ create: () => ({ id: Math.max(0, ...branches.map((b) => b.id)) + 1, province: null, district: null }) }}
      onEditorPreparing={(e) => {
        if (e.field === 'district') e.options.enabled = e.getValue('province') !== null;
      }}
    />
  );
}
```

`TextFrom.tsx`

```tsx
import { reactive } from '@motifx/core';
import { data } from '@motifx-community/data';
import { DataGrid, type GridColumn } from '@motifx-community/ui';
import { SlowAdapter } from '../../../shared/slow-adapter';
import { makeCustomers, type Customer } from './customers';

/** An invoice as its service returns it, with the customer included (OData `$expand=customer`). */
type Invoice = { id: number; customerId: number; customer: { name: string }; total: number };

const money = new Intl.NumberFormat('en', { minimumFractionDigits: 2, maximumFractionDigits: 2 });

/** The name is read from the row itself, and the customer service is used only for editing. */
export default function TextFrom() {
  const s = reactive({ requests: 0 });
  const people = makeCustomers(600);
  const invoices: Invoice[] = Array.from({ length: 5_000 }, (_, i) => {
    const customer = people[(i * 53) % people.length];
    return { id: i + 1, customerId: customer.id, customer: { name: customer.name }, total: ((i * 4337) % 50_000) / 10 };
  });
  // Simulate two services: new data.ODataAdapter({ url: '/odata/Invoices', key: 'id' }) with expand: ['customer'], and the customer service.
  const invoiceSource = new data.DataSource<Invoice, number>({ adapter: new SlowAdapter<Invoice, number>({ data: invoices, key: 'id' }, 250), loadMode: 'blocks', pageSize: 100 });
  const customerService = new SlowAdapter<Customer, number>({ data: people, key: 'id' }, 400);
  customerService.onLoading(() => s.requests++);
  const columns: GridColumn<Invoice>[] = [
    { field: 'id', title: 'Invoice', type: 'number', width: 100, editable: false },
    {
      field: 'customerId',
      title: 'Customer',
      width: 220,
      flex: 1,
      textFrom: 'customer.name',
      sortField: 'customer.name',
      lookup: { dataSource: new data.DataSource<Customer, number>({ adapter: customerService }), valueField: 'id', textField: 'name' },
    },
    { field: 'total', title: 'Total', type: 'number', width: 120, editable: false, format: (v) => (typeof v === 'number' ? money.format(v) : '') },
  ];

  return (
    <>
      <DataGrid class="dg-text-from" style="block-size: 28rem" dataSource={invoiceSource} columns={columns} label="Invoices" locale="en" saveMode="batch" settings={{ editable: true }} />
      <output class="dg-text-from-requests">{() => `${s.requests} requests to the customers service`}</output>
    </>
  );
}
```

# DataGrid: Grouping and summaries

> DataGrid · @motifx-community/ui 0.1.0-beta.5

## Grouping

Rows can be grouped by one or more columns. Each group has a row showing “Column: value (count)”, using the text of a lookup column or the column's format for in-memory rows, with an arrow that expands and collapses it and with lower-level groups indented. Grouped columns are removed from the columns area unless `showWhenGrouped` is set. `groupIndex` on columns sets the initial grouping, and `groupPanel` adds a panel at the start of the toolbar where dropping a header groups by its column. Clicking a chip reverses the order of its groups, and a chip can move along the panel or be dragged back onto the headers to ungroup the column at that position. The column menu provides the same actions from the keyboard. Sorting applies to the rows inside the groups, and the header of a grouped column, like its chip, sorts its groups. `calculateGroupValue` groups by a computed value. In paged mode, pages count both group rows and data rows, and a collapsed group counts as one row.

```tsx
/** An order, as stored by the sample server. */
export interface Order {
  id: number;
  customer: string;
  city: string;
  date: string;
  status: string;
  paid: boolean;
  amount: number;
  note: string;
}
```

On a server, a `DataSource` that loads by `blocks` over an adapter that supports grouping is asked only for the groups and their counts (`loadGroups`, `group` with `groupsOnly`). Rows arrive in group order, in blocks, only for expanded groups in the visible area. In this example, the groups start collapsed (`autoExpandGroup: false`). An adapter that cannot group (OData, REST), a source that loads by page, or a `calculateGroupValue` function loads every matching row and groups them in the browser. Filters, search and selection work with groups, and “select all” still means every row of the filter. CSV export writes a “Column: value” line before each group, and `group` is saved with the layout.

```tsx
import { data } from '@motifx-community/data';

/** Rows in memory that answer a little later, the way a server does; for the examples. */
export class SlowAdapter<T extends object, K> extends data.ArrayAdapter<T, K> {
  constructor(
    options: data.ArrayAdapterOptions<T>,
    private readonly delayMs = 300,
  ) {
    super(options);
  }

  override async load(options: data.LoadOptions = {}): Promise<data.LoadResult<T>> {
    await new Promise((done) => setTimeout(done, this.delayMs));
    return super.load(options);
  }
}
```

## Summaries

`summary` calculates values for the rows that match the filter and search. `totalItems` appear in a totals row below the rows, which stays at the bottom while the rows scroll and moves sideways with the columns. `groupItems` appear for each group: after the group row's count, under their column in the group row (`alignByColumn`), or in a footer row after the group's rows (`showInGroupFooter`). An item aggregates a `column` (and its `value` reader) with a `summaryType` of `sum`, `min`, `max`, `avg`, `count` or `custom`, and appears under `showInColumn` (otherwise its own column), with several items in one column stacked. Its text is `displayFormat` (`{0}` for the value and `{1}` for the column), or a string from `summary.texts` and `uiLocale`, formatted by `valueFormat` (`Intl` options or a function, otherwise the column's format), or `customizeText`. A `custom` item uses `calculateCustomSummary` in three stages: `start`, `calculate` per row, and `finalize`. Empty values are excluded (`skipEmptyValues`, and `count` counts every row). Unsaved edits count once saved, or as they are made with `recalculateWhileEditing`. `getTotalSummaryValue(name)` and `getGroupSummaryValue(key, name)` read the values, `onSummaryChanged` reports recalculation, and CSV and `exportRows()` write the footers and totals.

```tsx
/** An order, as stored by the sample server. */
export interface Order {
  id: number;
  customer: string;
  city: string;
  date: string;
  status: string;
  paid: boolean;
  amount: number;
  note: string;
}
```

On a server, a source that loads pages or blocks requests the totals of the query from its adapter when the adapter has the `summary` capability (`remoteSummary`, `DataSource.loadSummary`), and requests group summaries with the groups when it groups (`loadGroups` with `groupSummary`). The sample server in this example does both, using one request for totals and one for groups, regardless of what the list shows. An adapter without this capability, a `custom` item or a computed column loads every matching row once per row set (`groupLoadPageSize` per request), and the values are calculated in the browser. If only the browser can calculate the group summaries, the rows are grouped in the browser as well.

```tsx
import { data } from '@motifx-community/data';

/** Rows in memory that answer a little later, the way a server does; for the examples. */
export class SlowAdapter<T extends object, K> extends data.ArrayAdapter<T, K> {
  constructor(
    options: data.ArrayAdapterOptions<T>,
    private readonly delayMs = 300,
  ) {
    super(options);
  }

  override async load(options: data.LoadOptions = {}): Promise<data.LoadResult<T>> {
    await new Promise((done) => setTimeout(done, this.delayMs));
    return super.load(options);
  }
}
```

| Field | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `totalItems, groupItems` | The items of the totals row and of each group. A function is tracked. Items are read as provided, so after changing them in place, call `grid.refreshSummary()`. |
| `calculateCustomSummary` | `(e) => void` with `{ name, summaryProcess, value, totalValue, groupIndex, component }`. One function for every `custom` item. Set `e.totalValue` at `start`, combine `e.value` (the column's value, or the row when there is no column) into it at each `calculate`, and adjust it at `finalize`. |
| `recalculateWhileEditing` | With `false`, the values reflect unsaved edits, new rows and rows marked for deletion. When enabled, they change once the changes are saved. |
| `skipEmptyValues` | With `true`, empty values (`null`, `undefined`, `''`) are excluded from browser calculations. When disabled, `sum` and `avg` count them as 0. An item can set its own value. |
| `texts` | The item strings by type: `sum`, `sumOtherColumn`, `min`, `minOtherColumn`, `max`, `maxOtherColumn`, `avg`, `avgOtherColumn` and `count`. They override the `gridSummary…` strings of `uiLocale` and the grid's `texts`. |

| Item field | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `column` | The column to aggregate. Without one, `count` counts rows and `custom` receives the rows themselves. |
| `summaryType` | `'sum' \| 'min' \| 'max' \| 'avg' \| 'count' \| 'custom'`, default `'count'`. |
| `name` | Names the item for `getTotalSummaryValue` and `calculateCustomSummary`. |
| `showInColumn` | The column the item appears under (by default, `column`). When it appears under a different column, the text names its column (“Sum of Amount: …”). |
| `valueFormat` | `Intl.NumberFormatOptions`, `Intl.DateTimeFormatOptions` or `(value) => string`. By default, the column's format (or a plain number for `count`). |
| `displayFormat, customizeText` | The text, where `{0}` is the formatted value and `{1}` is the column's title. `({ value, valueText }) => string` takes precedence. |
| `alignment, cssClass` | `'start' \| 'center' \| 'end'` (by default, the column's), and a custom class on the item. |
| `skipEmptyValues` | Excludes empty values for this item. The default is `summary.skipEmptyValues`. |
| `visible` | Whether the item appears. The default is the `totalSummary` (`groupSummary`) setting. |
| `showInGroupFooter, alignByColumn` | For group items: places them in the group footer, or under their column in the group row, except under the first column, which holds the text. |

`Grouping.tsx`

```tsx
import { reactive } from '@motifx/core';
import { Button, CheckBox, DataGrid, Stack } from '@motifx-community/ui';
import type { Order } from './order';
import { columns, makeOrders } from './orders';

/** Orders in memory grouped by city, then by status; the group panel and the switches change it. */
export default function Grouping() {
  const s = reactive({ panel: true, dragging: true, open: true, collapsing: true, rowClick: false, showCity: false });
  let grid: DataGrid<Order> | null = null;
  const grouped = columns.map((c) => (c.field === 'city' ? { ...c, groupIndex: 0, showWhenGrouped: () => s.showCity } : c.field === 'status' ? { ...c, groupIndex: 1 } : c));

  return (
    <>
      <Stack orientation="horizontal" wrap align="center">
        <CheckBox label="Group panel" x-model={() => s.panel} />
        <CheckBox label="Drag to group" x-model={() => s.dragging} />
        <CheckBox label="Groups start open" x-model={() => s.open} />
        <CheckBox label="The user can open and close" x-model={() => s.collapsing} />
        <CheckBox label="A click on the row opens" x-model={() => s.rowClick} />
        <CheckBox label="City stays a column" x-model={() => s.showCity} />
      </Stack>
      <DataGrid
        class="dg-grouping"
        style="block-size: 34rem"
        rows={makeOrders(500)}
        rowKey="id"
        columns={grouped}
        label="Orders by city and status"
        locale="en"
        settings={{
          groupPanel: () => s.panel,
          groupPanelDragging: () => s.dragging,
          autoExpandAll: () => s.open,
          allowCollapsing: () => s.collapsing,
          groupExpandMode: () => (s.rowClick ? 'rowClick' : 'button'),
          selection: 'multiple',
        }}
        ref={(g: DataGrid<Order>) => (grid = g)}
      />
      <Stack orientation="horizontal" wrap align="center">
        <Button text="Open all" variant="outline" onclick={() => grid?.expandAll()} />
        <Button text="Close all" variant="outline" onclick={() => grid?.collapseAll()} />
        <Button text="Open only the cities" variant="outline" onclick={() => (grid?.expandAll(0), grid?.collapseAll(1))} />
        <Button text="Ungroup" variant="outline" onclick={() => grid?.clearGrouping()} />
        <output class="dg-grouping-state">{() => `Grouped by ${grid?.group.map((g) => `${g.field} ${g.dir}`).join(', ') || 'nothing'}`}</output>
      </Stack>
    </>
  );
}
```

`orders.ts`

```tsx
import type { GridColumn } from '@motifx-community/ui';
import type { Order } from './order';

const CUSTOMERS = ['Ada Lovelace', 'Grace Hopper', 'Alan Turing', 'Cahit Arf', 'Katherine Johnson', 'Edsger Dijkstra', 'Barbara Liskov', 'Donald Knuth', 'İlhan Koman', 'Margaret Hamilton'];
const CITIES = ['Ankara', 'Antalya', 'Bursa', 'İstanbul', 'İzmir', 'Konya', 'Trabzon'];
const STATUSES = ['Draft', 'Approved', 'Shipped', 'Delivered', 'Cancelled'];
const NOTES = ['', 'Leave at the door', 'Call before delivery', 'Gift wrap, please, with a card that says happy birthday', '', 'Fragile'];

/** `n` sample orders, the same ones every time. */
export function makeOrders(n: number): Order[] {
  const day = Date.UTC(2026, 0, 1);
  return Array.from({ length: n }, (_, i) => ({
    id: i + 1,
    customer: CUSTOMERS[(i * 7) % CUSTOMERS.length],
    city: CITIES[(i * 3) % CITIES.length],
    date: new Date(day + ((i * 37) % 300) * 86_400_000).toISOString().slice(0, 10),
    status: STATUSES[i % STATUSES.length],
    paid: i % 3 === 0,
    amount: ((i * 7919) % 100_000) / 100,
    note: NOTES[i % NOTES.length],
  }));
}

const money = new Intl.NumberFormat('en', { minimumFractionDigits: 2, maximumFractionDigits: 2 });

/** The order columns: the number pinned to the start, the amount to the end. */
export const columns: GridColumn<Order>[] = [
  { field: 'id', title: 'No', type: 'number', width: 80, sticky: 'start', editable: false },
  { field: 'customer', title: 'Customer', width: 180, flex: 1, required: true },
  { field: 'city', title: 'City', type: 'list', width: 120, options: CITIES },
  { field: 'date', title: 'Date', type: 'date', width: 130, editable: false, creatable: true },
  { field: 'status', title: 'Status', type: 'list', width: 120, options: STATUSES, required: true },
  { field: 'paid', title: 'Paid', type: 'boolean', width: 80 },
  { field: 'note', title: 'Note', width: 200 },
  {
    field: 'amount',
    title: 'Amount',
    type: 'number',
    width: 120,
    sticky: 'end',
    required: true,
    validate: (v) => (typeof v === 'number' && v < 0 ? 'The amount cannot be negative.' : null),
    format: (v) => (typeof v === 'number' ? money.format(v) : ''),
  },
];

/** The same columns with a filter cell and a header filter on most of them. */
export const filterColumns: GridColumn<Order>[] = columns.map((c) => ({ ...c, filterRow: c.field !== 'note', headerFilter: c.field !== 'note' && c.field !== 'id' }));

const today = () => new Date().toISOString().slice(0, 10);

/** What a new order starts with. */
export const newOrder = () => ({ date: today(), status: 'Draft', paid: false });
```

`GroupingServer.tsx`

```tsx
import { reactive } from '@motifx/core';
import { data } from '@motifx-community/data';
import { Button, DataGrid, Stack } from '@motifx-community/ui';
import { SlowAdapter } from '../../../shared/slow-adapter';
import type { Order } from './order';
import { columns, makeOrders } from './orders';

/** 100,000 orders grouped on the server: the groups arrive with their counts, and rows load only in the visible area. */
export default function GroupingServer() {
  const s = reactive({ loads: 0 });
  // An adapter that groups (here rows in memory acting as a server) answers `group` itself; one
  // that cannot (OData, REST) gets every matching row grouped in the browser instead.
  const server = new SlowAdapter<Order, number>({ data: makeOrders(100_000), key: 'id' }, 300);
  server.onLoading(() => s.loads++);
  const orders = new data.DataSource<Order, number>({ adapter: server, loadMode: 'blocks', pageSize: 100 });
  const grouped = columns.map((c) => (c.field === 'status' ? { ...c, groupIndex: 0, autoExpandGroup: false } : c));
  let grid: DataGrid<Order> | null = null;

  return (
    <>
      <DataGrid
        class="dg-grouping-server"
        style="block-size: 32rem"
        dataSource={orders}
        columns={grouped}
        label="100,000 orders by status"
        locale="en"
        settings={{ groupPanel: true }}
        ref={(g: DataGrid<Order>) => (grid = g)}
      />
      <Stack orientation="horizontal" wrap align="center">
        <Button text="Open “Shipped”" variant="outline" onclick={() => grid?.expandGroup(['Shipped'])} />
        <Button text="Open all" variant="outline" onclick={() => grid?.expandAll()} />
        <Button text="Close all" variant="outline" onclick={() => grid?.collapseAll()} />
        <output class="dg-grouping-loads">{() => `${s.loads} loads for ${grid?.total ?? 0} rows`}</output>
      </Stack>
    </>
  );
}
```

`slow-adapter.ts`

```tsx
import { data } from '@motifx-community/data';

/** Rows in memory that answer a little later, the way a server does; for the examples. */
export class SlowAdapter<T extends object, K> extends data.ArrayAdapter<T, K> {
  constructor(
    options: data.ArrayAdapterOptions<T>,
    private readonly delayMs = 300,
  ) {
    super(options);
  }

  override async load(options: data.LoadOptions = {}): Promise<data.LoadResult<T>> {
    await new Promise((done) => setTimeout(done, this.delayMs));
    return super.load(options);
  }
}
```

`Summaries.tsx`

```tsx
import { reactive } from '@motifx/core';
import { CheckBox, DataGrid, Stack, type GridCustomSummaryInfo, type GridSummary } from '@motifx-community/ui';
import type { Order } from './order';
import { columns, makeOrders } from './orders';

/** Totals under the rows, group summaries in the group rows and footers, and a custom one: paid orders. */
export default function Summaries() {
  const s = reactive({ grouped: true, footers: true, aligned: true, live: false });
  let grid: DataGrid<Order> | null = null;
  // The amount gets room for its totals.
  const byCity = columns.map((c) => (c.field === 'city' ? { ...c, groupIndex: () => (s.grouped ? 0 : undefined) } : c.field === 'amount' ? { ...c, width: 170 } : c));

  // Counts the paid orders: start, then each row, then the result.
  const calculateCustomSummary = (e: GridCustomSummaryInfo<Order>) => {
    if (e.summaryProcess === 'start') e.totalValue = 0;
    else if (e.summaryProcess === 'calculate' && (e.value as Order).paid) e.totalValue = (e.totalValue as number) + 1;
  };

  const summary: GridSummary<Order> = {
    recalculateWhileEditing: () => s.live,
    totalItems: [
      { column: 'id', summaryType: 'count', showInColumn: 'customer' },
      { name: 'paid', summaryType: 'custom', showInColumn: 'paid', displayFormat: '{0} paid' },
      { column: 'date', summaryType: 'max', displayFormat: 'Last: {0}' },
      { name: 'total', column: 'amount', summaryType: 'sum' },
      { column: 'amount', summaryType: 'avg', valueFormat: { maximumFractionDigits: 0 } },
    ],
    groupItems: [
      { column: 'amount', summaryType: 'sum', alignByColumn: () => s.aligned },
      { column: 'amount', summaryType: 'max', showInGroupFooter: true, visible: () => s.footers },
      { name: 'paid', summaryType: 'custom', showInColumn: 'paid', showInGroupFooter: true, displayFormat: '{0} paid', visible: () => s.footers },
    ],
    calculateCustomSummary,
  };

  return (
    <>
      <Stack orientation="horizontal" wrap align="center">
        <CheckBox label="Group by city" x-model={() => s.grouped} />
        <CheckBox label="Group footers" x-model={() => s.footers} />
        <CheckBox label="Sum under its column in the group row" x-model={() => s.aligned} />
        <CheckBox label="Follow unsaved edits" x-model={() => s.live} />
      </Stack>
      <DataGrid
        class="dg-summaries"
        style="block-size: 34rem"
        rows={makeOrders(300)}
        rowKey="id"
        columns={byCity}
        label="Orders with totals"
        locale="en"
        saveMode="batch"
        summary={summary}
        settings={{ editable: true, filterRow: true }}
        ref={(g: DataGrid<Order>) => (grid = g)}
      />
      <output class="dg-summaries-total">{() => `The amounts add up to ${Number(grid?.getTotalSummaryValue('total') ?? 0).toLocaleString('en', { maximumFractionDigits: 2 })}`}</output>
    </>
  );
}
```

`SummariesServer.tsx`

```tsx
import { reactive } from '@motifx/core';
import { data } from '@motifx-community/data';
import { Button, DataGrid, Stack } from '@motifx-community/ui';
import { SlowAdapter } from '../../../shared/slow-adapter';
import type { Order } from './order';
import { columns, makeOrders } from './orders';

/** 100,000 orders on a server that calculates the totals and returns the group summaries with the groups. */
export default function SummariesServer() {
  const s = reactive({ asked: 0 });
  // An adapter with the `summary` capability is asked for the values (`remoteSummary: 'auto'`). Without it,
  // every matching row is loaded once and the values are calculated in the browser.
  const server = new SlowAdapter<Order, number>({ data: makeOrders(100_000), key: 'id' }, 300);
  server.onLoading((e) => {
    if (e.options.summary || e.options.groupSummary) s.asked++;
  });
  const orders = new data.DataSource<Order, number>({ adapter: server, loadMode: 'blocks', pageSize: 100 });
  const byStatus = columns.map((c) => (c.field === 'status' ? { ...c, groupIndex: 0, autoExpandGroup: false } : { ...c, filterRow: c.field === 'city' || c.field === 'amount', width: c.field === 'amount' ? 170 : c.width }));
  let grid: DataGrid<Order> | null = null;

  return (
    <>
      <DataGrid
        class="dg-summaries-server"
        style="block-size: 32rem"
        dataSource={orders}
        columns={byStatus}
        label="100,000 orders with server totals"
        locale="en"
        settings={{ groupPanel: true }}
        summary={{
          totalItems: [
            { column: 'id', summaryType: 'count', showInColumn: 'customer' },
            { name: 'total', column: 'amount', summaryType: 'sum' },
            { column: 'amount', summaryType: 'max' },
          ],
          groupItems: [
            { column: 'amount', summaryType: 'sum' },
            { column: 'amount', summaryType: 'avg', showInGroupFooter: true, valueFormat: { maximumFractionDigits: 2 } },
            { column: 'id', summaryType: 'count', showInColumn: 'customer', showInGroupFooter: true },
          ],
        }}
        ref={(g: DataGrid<Order>) => (grid = g)}
      />
      <Stack orientation="horizontal" wrap align="center">
        <Button text="Open all" variant="outline" onclick={() => grid?.expandAll()} />
        <Button text="Close all" variant="outline" onclick={() => grid?.collapseAll()} />
        <output class="dg-summaries-server-state">{() => `${s.asked} summary requests · totals ${grid?.summaryStatus ?? 'loading'}`}</output>
      </Stack>
    </>
  );
}
```


---

# DataGrid: Master-detail

> DataGrid · @motifx-community/ui 0.1.0-beta.5

## Master-detail

`masterDetail` gives every row its own details. The expand column opens a row to display the output of `template` (in this example, another grid over its own data source, filtered by the customer's key) in a row spanning the grid, which stays in place while the columns scroll sideways. Details are created the first time they are shown and kept while the row is open, and they are removed when the row leaves the data or when the grid is disposed. The list stays virtual: each detail is measured as it renders (and again when its content changes size), so the scrollbar, the following rows and navigation to a row stay accurate, and the rows themselves remain a small pool.

```tsx
/** A customer, as stored by a second sample service. */
export interface Customer {
  id: number;
  name: string;
  city: string;
}

const FIRST = ['Ada', 'Grace', 'Alan', 'Cahit', 'Katherine', 'Edsger', 'Barbara', 'Donald', 'İlhan', 'Margaret', 'Feza', 'Ali Nesin'];
const LAST = ['Lovelace', 'Hopper', 'Turing', 'Arf', 'Johnson', 'Dijkstra', 'Liskov', 'Knuth', 'Koman', 'Hamilton', 'Gürsey', 'Yılmaz'];
const CITIES = ['Ankara', 'Antalya', 'Bursa', 'İstanbul', 'İzmir', 'Konya', 'Trabzon'];

/** `n` sample customers, the same ones every time. */
export function makeCustomers(n: number): Customer[] {
  return Array.from({ length: n }, (_, i) => ({
    id: i + 1,
    name: `${FIRST[i % FIRST.length]} ${LAST[Math.floor(i / FIRST.length) % LAST.length]} ${Math.floor(i / (FIRST.length * LAST.length)) + 1}`,
    city: CITIES[(i * 5) % CITIES.length],
  }));
}
```

| Option | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `masterDetail.enabled` | `Bind<boolean>` | `false` | The expand column, after the status and check box columns and pinned with them, lets the user open and close details. When disabled, they can be opened only programmatically. |
| `masterDetail.template` | `(ctx: DetailContext<T>) => unknown` | — | The content of a row's details: a component (another `DataGrid`, a `FormLayout`, `Tabs` …), an element or text. It is created the first time the details are shown. `ctx` provides `row` (the row itself) and `rowIndex`, both getters that are read again when the row shows another one and on `grid.repaint()` or `grid.repaintRows(keys)`, plus `key`, `grid` and `collapse()`. |
| `masterDetail.autoExpandAll` | `Bind<boolean>` | `false` | Every row starts open. Changing this setting, `enabled` or `template` opens or closes every row again. |
| `masterDetail.canExpand` | `Bind<boolean> \| (row) => boolean` | `true` | Whether a row has details. A row without details has no arrow, and `expandRow` leaves it closed. Unsaved new rows have no details. |
| `masterDetail.keepDetails` | `Bind<boolean>` | `true` | A closed row keeps the content of its details and shows it unchanged when it reopens. When disabled, closing disposes the content. |
| `masterDetail.keepAcrossPages` | `Bind<boolean>` | `false` | In a paged grid, the details of the previous page keep their content while the user changes pages (up to `keepLimit`). When disabled, changing the page or page size disposes them, and they are recreated when their page appears. A row stays open in either case. |
| `masterDetail.keepLimit` | `Bind<number>` | `100` | The number of details out of view that keep their content (open ones, and closed ones with `keepDetails`). Past this limit, the least recently seen are disposed and recreated when they appear. |
| `masterDetail.height` | `Bind<number> \| (row) => number` | The content's height | A fixed height in pixels, with the content scrolling inside. A function sets a height per row. |
| `masterDetail.estimatedHeight` | `Bind<number>` | `200` | The estimated height of details before they are rendered and measured, used until the first measurement, after which the measured average applies. Only the scrollbar uses it. |
| `masterDetail.columnWidth` | `Bind<number>` | `36` | The width of the expand column, in pixels. |
| `masterDetail.toggleKeys` | `Bind<string[]>` | `['Enter', ' ']` | The keys on the expand cell that open and close the details. |
| `masterDetail.arrowKeys` | `Bind<boolean>` | `true` | Right on the expand cell of a closed row opens it, and Left on an open row closes it. Otherwise, they move as on any cell. |

Open rows are tracked by key, so sorting, filtering, searching, grouping and paging leave them open, and a row that returns after a filter opens again. Selection and editing work as usual, and a row edited in the edit form keeps its details below the form. Copy and export omit the details, and the saved layout does not include which rows are open.

## Tabs and forms in the details

Details can contain any component. In this example, they are tabs with a read-only `FormLayout` for the customer and a list of its orders that is created when the tab is first shown. The row adjusts its height, and the following rows move. `canExpand` hides the arrow for customers without orders, `ctx.collapse()` closes a row from inside its details, and the buttons call `expandAllRows()` and `collapseAllRows()`.

```tsx
/** A customer, as stored by a second sample service. */
export interface Customer {
  id: number;
  name: string;
  city: string;
}

const FIRST = ['Ada', 'Grace', 'Alan', 'Cahit', 'Katherine', 'Edsger', 'Barbara', 'Donald', 'İlhan', 'Margaret', 'Feza', 'Ali Nesin'];
const LAST = ['Lovelace', 'Hopper', 'Turing', 'Arf', 'Johnson', 'Dijkstra', 'Liskov', 'Knuth', 'Koman', 'Hamilton', 'Gürsey', 'Yılmaz'];
const CITIES = ['Ankara', 'Antalya', 'Bursa', 'İstanbul', 'İzmir', 'Konya', 'Trabzon'];

/** `n` sample customers, the same ones every time. */
export function makeCustomers(n: number): Customer[] {
  return Array.from({ length: n }, (_, i) => ({
    id: i + 1,
    name: `${FIRST[i % FIRST.length]} ${LAST[Math.floor(i / FIRST.length) % LAST.length]} ${Math.floor(i / (FIRST.length * LAST.length)) + 1}`,
    city: CITIES[(i * 5) % CITIES.length],
  }));
}
```

## Keyboard and accessibility

The arrow is a button with `aria-expanded` and `aria-controls`, and the row also has `aria-expanded`. A row's details are a separate row in the grid's reading order (`aria-owns`), directly after it and counted in `aria-rowindex` and `aria-rowcount`, with one cell across the columns named “Details of row 3” (`gridDetailsOf`, and `gridDetails` for the arrow and its column, both in `uiLocale` and the grid's `texts`).

| Key | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `Enter, Space (`toggleKeys`)` | On the expand cell, opens or closes the row's details. |
| `Right / Left (`arrowKeys`)` | On the expand cell, Right opens a closed row and Left closes an open one. Then they move to the next cell. Mirrored on right-to-left pages. |
| `Up / Down, Page Up / Page Down` | Moves between rows, skipping a row's details. |
| `Tab` | On a row whose details are visible, moves into the details, to their first stop. With details on screen, Tab otherwise leaves the grid, as Shift+Tab does from a row. |
| `Tab in the details` | Moves through their content. From the last stop, it leaves the grid. |
| `Escape, Shift+Tab on the first stop` | Returns to the row the details belong to, when the content does not use Escape itself. |
| `Enter on the details’ own cell` | Moves into the content, to its first stop. |

## Events and methods

| Event | Parameters | When |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `onRowExpanding / onRowCollapsing` | `{ kind: 'detail', key, row, cancel }` | Occurs before a row's details open or close, from the user or programmatically. Set `cancel` to keep them as they are. These are the same events as for groups (`kind: 'group'`). |
| `onRowExpanded / onRowCollapsed` | `{ kind: 'detail', key, row }` | Occurs after they open or close. |
| `onRowPrepared` | `{ rowType: 'detail', row, rowIndex, element }` | Occurs when a row's details have been rendered for a row. |
| `onOptionChanged` | `{ name: 'masterDetail.enabled', value, previous }` | Occurs when a `masterDetail` option is assigned through `grid.masterDetail`. |

| Member | Returns | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `expandRow(key) / collapseRow(key)` | `boolean` | Opens or closes a row's details by key, as the arrow does (the events run, and `cancel` applies). It has no effect on a row that is not loaded or has no details. |
| `isRowExpanded(key)` | `boolean` | Indicates whether a row's details are open. Reactive. |
| `expandAllRows() / collapseAllRows()` | `void` | Opens or closes every row's details at once, without row events (as `expandAll()` does for groups). |
| `masterDetail` | read/write, live | `grid.masterDetail.enabled = true`. A function is tracked reactively. |
| `getVisibleRows()` | `GridVisibleRow[]` | A row's details are listed directly after it, with `rowType: 'detail'` and with its index and key. |

## Example files

`MasterDetail.tsx`

```tsx
import { data } from '@motifx-community/data';
import { DataGrid, type GridColumn } from '@motifx-community/ui';
import type { CustomerOrder } from './customer-order';
import { makeCustomerOrders, orderColumns } from './customer-orders';
import { makeCustomers, type Customer } from './customers';

const customers = makeCustomers(2000);
const orders = new data.ArrayAdapter<CustomerOrder, number>({ data: makeCustomerOrders(customers), key: 'id' });

const columns: GridColumn<Customer>[] = [
  { field: 'id', title: 'No', type: 'number', width: 80 },
  { field: 'name', title: 'Customer', width: 220, flex: 1 },
  { field: 'city', title: 'City', width: 140 },
];

/** A customer's orders: a grid over a source of its own, filtered by the customer's key, disposed with the details. */
function Orders(props: { customerId: unknown; name: string }) {
  const source = new data.DataSource<CustomerOrder, number>({ adapter: orders, loadMode: 'all', filter: data.where('customerId', '=', props.customerId) });
  return (
    <DataGrid
      class="dg-orders"
      style="block-size: 14rem"
      dataSource={source}
      columns={orderColumns}
      label={`Orders of ${props.name}`}
      locale="en"
      settings={{ rowCount: true }}
      onDisposing={() => source.dispose()}
    />
  );
}

/** Two thousand customers in a virtual list; each opens to a grid of its own orders. */
export default function MasterDetail() {
  return (
    <DataGrid
      class="dg-master"
      style="block-size: 30rem"
      rows={customers}
      rowKey="id"
      columns={columns}
      label="Customers and their orders"
      locale="en"
      masterDetail={{ enabled: true, template: (ctx) => <Orders customerId={ctx.key} name={ctx.row.name} /> }}
    />
  );
}
```

`customer-orders.ts`

```tsx
import type { GridColumn } from '@motifx-community/ui';
import type { Customer } from './customers';
import type { CustomerOrder } from './customer-order';

const ITEMS = ['Notebook', 'Pencil set', 'Desk lamp', 'Chair', 'Monitor', 'Keyboard', 'Coffee beans', 'Tea', 'Backpack', 'Umbrella'];
const money = new Intl.NumberFormat('en', { minimumFractionDigits: 2, maximumFractionDigits: 2 });

/** A few orders of every customer (none for every seventh), the same ones every time. */
export function makeCustomerOrders(customers: Customer[]): CustomerOrder[] {
  const day = Date.UTC(2026, 0, 1);
  const out: CustomerOrder[] = [];
  for (const c of customers) {
    const count = c.id % 7 === 0 ? 0 : 2 + (c.id % 5);
    for (let k = 0; k < count; k++) {
      const n = out.length + 1;
      out.push({
        id: n,
        customerId: c.id,
        date: new Date(day + ((n * 37) % 300) * 86_400_000).toISOString().slice(0, 10),
        item: ITEMS[(n * 3) % ITEMS.length],
        quantity: 1 + (n % 4),
        amount: ((n * 7919) % 50_000) / 100,
      });
    }
  }
  return out;
}

/** The columns of a customer's orders. */
export const orderColumns: GridColumn<CustomerOrder>[] = [
  { field: 'id', title: 'No', type: 'number', width: 80 },
  { field: 'date', title: 'Date', type: 'date', width: 130 },
  { field: 'item', title: 'Item', width: 180, flex: 1 },
  { field: 'quantity', title: 'Qty', type: 'number', width: 80 },
  { field: 'amount', title: 'Amount', type: 'number', width: 120, format: (v) => (typeof v === 'number' ? money.format(v) : '') },
];
```

`customers.ts`

```tsx
/** A customer, as stored by a second sample service. */
export interface Customer {
  id: number;
  name: string;
  city: string;
}

const FIRST = ['Ada', 'Grace', 'Alan', 'Cahit', 'Katherine', 'Edsger', 'Barbara', 'Donald', 'İlhan', 'Margaret', 'Feza', 'Ali Nesin'];
const LAST = ['Lovelace', 'Hopper', 'Turing', 'Arf', 'Johnson', 'Dijkstra', 'Liskov', 'Knuth', 'Koman', 'Hamilton', 'Gürsey', 'Yılmaz'];
const CITIES = ['Ankara', 'Antalya', 'Bursa', 'İstanbul', 'İzmir', 'Konya', 'Trabzon'];

/** `n` sample customers, the same ones every time. */
export function makeCustomers(n: number): Customer[] {
  return Array.from({ length: n }, (_, i) => ({
    id: i + 1,
    name: `${FIRST[i % FIRST.length]} ${LAST[Math.floor(i / FIRST.length) % LAST.length]} ${Math.floor(i / (FIRST.length * LAST.length)) + 1}`,
    city: CITIES[(i * 5) % CITIES.length],
  }));
}
```

`DetailTabs.tsx`

```tsx
import { reactive } from '@motifx/core';
import { Button, DataGrid, FormLayout, Stack, Tab, Tabs, type DetailContext, type FormItem, type GridColumn } from '@motifx-community/ui';
import { makeCustomerOrders } from './customer-orders';
import { makeCustomers, type Customer } from './customers';

const customers = makeCustomers(60);
const orders = makeCustomerOrders(customers);
const money = new Intl.NumberFormat('en', { style: 'currency', currency: 'EUR' });

/** The details of a customer: its fields and the total of its orders. */
interface Profile extends Customer {
  orders: number;
  total: string;
  since: string;
}

const profiles: Profile[] = customers.map((c) => {
  const own = orders.filter((o) => o.customerId === c.id);
  return { ...c, orders: own.length, total: money.format(own.reduce((sum, o) => sum + o.amount, 0)), since: own[0]?.date ?? '' };
});

const columns: GridColumn<Profile>[] = [
  { field: 'id', title: 'No', type: 'number', width: 80 },
  { field: 'name', title: 'Customer', width: 220, flex: 1 },
  { field: 'city', title: 'City', width: 140 },
  { field: 'orders', title: 'Orders', type: 'number', width: 100 },
];

const items: FormItem[] = [
  { field: 'name', label: 'Name' },
  { field: 'city', label: 'City' },
  { field: 'since', label: 'First order' },
  { field: 'total', label: 'Orders total' },
];

/** A customer's details: tabs, the first with a read-only form. The other tab is created when first shown, and the row grows with it. */
function CustomerTabs(props: { ctx: DetailContext<Profile> }) {
  const profile = reactive({ ...props.ctx.row });
  return (
    <Tabs label={`About ${profile.name}`} size="sm">
      <Tab title="Profile">
        <FormLayout data={profile} items={items} columns={2} readOnly />
      </Tab>
      <Tab title="Orders">
        <ul class="dg-detail-list">
          {orders
            .filter((o) => o.customerId === profile.id)
            .map((o) => (
              <li key={String(o.id)}>{`${o.date} · ${o.item} × ${o.quantity} · ${money.format(o.amount)}`}</li>
            ))}
        </ul>
        <Button text="Close" size="sm" variant="outline" onclick={() => props.ctx.collapse()} />
      </Tab>
    </Tabs>
  );
}

/** Customers with tabs in their details; those without orders have none. The buttons open and close every row. */
export default function DetailTabs() {
  const s = reactive({ log: '' });
  let grid: DataGrid<Profile> | null = null;
  return (
    <>
      <Stack orientation="horizontal" wrap align="center" role="group" aria-label="Details">
        <Button text="Open all" size="sm" variant="outline" onclick={() => grid?.expandAllRows()} />
        <Button text="Close all" size="sm" variant="outline" onclick={() => grid?.collapseAllRows()} />
        <output class="dg-detail-log">{() => s.log}</output>
      </Stack>
      <DataGrid
        class="dg-detail-tabs"
        style="block-size: 30rem"
        ref={(g: DataGrid<Profile>) => (grid = g)}
        rows={profiles}
        rowKey="id"
        columns={columns}
        label="Customers with their details"
        locale="en"
        settings={{ selection: 'single' }}
        masterDetail={{ enabled: true, canExpand: (row: Profile) => row.orders > 0, template: (ctx) => <CustomerTabs ctx={ctx} /> }}
        onRowExpanded={(e) => e.kind === 'detail' && (s.log = `Opened ${(e.row as Profile).name}`)}
        onRowCollapsed={(e) => e.kind === 'detail' && (s.log = `Closed ${(e.row as Profile).name}`)}
      />
    </>
  );
}
```

# DataGrid: Bands and adaptive columns

> DataGrid · @motifx-community/ui 0.1.0-beta.5

## Band headers

A band is a header that spans several columns. Give it a `title` and the `columns` under it, which can be columns or other bands to any depth. The header gains one row per band level above the column titles, with each band spanning its columns. A column can be dragged only within its band, and dragging a band moves its columns with it. A band is pinned, hidden and moved as a whole, from its own menu (its header button or Alt+Down) or with `columnOption` by its `name`. In this example, “Payment” spans three columns, and “Order” spans two columns and the “Delivery” band.

```tsx
/** An order, as stored by the sample server. */
export interface Order {
  id: number;
  customer: string;
  city: string;
  date: string;
  status: string;
  paid: boolean;
  amount: number;
  note: string;
}
```

| Band field | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `title, columns` | `Bind<string>`, `(GridColumn \| GridBand)[]` | — | The band's caption and its contents: columns and bands, to any depth. A band holds no data. |
| `name` | `string` | `band-` and its position | Its identity in the layout, `columnOption`, `columnSettings` and the events (`band-1`, or `band-1-2` when nested, if none is given). |
| `isBand, ownerBand` | `boolean`, `string \| number` | — | Bands specified as a flat list: a band with `isBand`, and columns or bands that reference it in `ownerBand`, by `name` or by its position in `columns`. |
| `align` | `Bind<'start' \| 'center' \| 'end'>` | The `bandAlign` setting | The position of the caption above its columns. |
| `sticky, hidden` | `'start' \| 'end'`, `boolean` | — | Pins or hides the band with all its columns. A column inside a band uses its band's side, and pinning it pins the band. |
| `movable, hideable, pinnable, menu` | `Bind<boolean>` | The grid's settings | What the user can do with the band: drag it among its neighbors, hide it, pin it and open its menu. |
| `headerCell` | `(ctx) => unknown` | — | Custom content in the band's header, created once. Provides `ctx.band` and `ctx.title`. |
| `settings.bandAlign` | `Bind<'start' \| 'center' \| 'end'>` | `'center'` | The position of captions when a band does not specify one. |

| Topic | Band behavior |
| --- | --- |
| `Moving` | A column moves only among the columns and bands of its own band, and a band among those beside it, both within their pinned zone and not across an item that cannot move (`movable: false`). They move by dragging the header, with “Move” in the menu and the arrow keys, or with `columnOption(name, 'visibleIndex', n)`. |
| `Sizing` | Columns resize as usual (drag the edge of a column's header, or double-click to fit), and a band follows its columns. |
| `Sorting and filters` | A band's header does not sort and has no filter, but its columns work as usual. |
| `Hiding` | Hiding every column of a band hides the band, and hiding a band (from its menu or with `columnOption(name, 'visible', false)`) hides its columns. The last visible column stays. |
| `Column chooser` | With bands, the column list is a tree with check boxes, with bands above their columns. A band's check box shows or hides all of them. |
| `Layout` | `grid.layout` keeps the column order, widths and hidden state, plus `bands` with each band's hidden state and side. A band's position comes from its columns. A layout that splits a band reassembles it at its first column. `layoutKey` saves all of this. |
| `Export` | CSV writes one line per band level above the titles, with each band's title over its first column. `exportSheet()` adds header rows, and `merges` lists the cells a band (and a column spanning the band rows) covers, for the writer to merge. |
| `Rows` | Only the header changes. The rows, the virtual list and paging work as usual. |

Band rows are `row` elements of `columnheader` cells in the header's row group. A band's header has the `aria-colindex` of its first column and an `aria-colspan` of its columns, the columns keep their own index, and band rows count in `aria-rowindex` and `aria-rowcount`. Above a pinned column with no band, an empty piece stays with the column so that the band rows scroll under it.

## Adaptive columns

With `settings.columnHidingEnabled`, the grid hides columns while it is narrower than they are, starting from the last. With `hidingPriority` on some columns, only those hide, lowest first. A “…” column then opens a row's adaptive detail below it, showing the titles and values of the hidden columns (with editors where the row can be edited), one row at a time. This is calculated from the column widths and the grid's width (through a `ResizeObserver`), never from the rendered output, and recalculated whenever either changes. Drag the splitter to see it. Hidden columns still count as visible, so the column chooser, `getVisibleColumns()`, export and copying include them.

```tsx
/** An order, as stored by the sample server. */
export interface Order {
  id: number;
  customer: string;
  city: string;
  date: string;
  status: string;
  paid: boolean;
  amount: number;
  note: string;
}
```

| Option | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `settings.columnHidingEnabled` | `Bind<boolean>` | `false` | Hides columns while the grid is narrower than they are, starting from the last, and shows them in the row's adaptive detail. |
| `column.hidingPriority` | `Bind<number>` | — | When set on any column, only columns with a priority hide (even without `columnHidingEnabled`), lowest first. Pinned and grouped columns never hide. |
| `adaptiveDetail.colCount, minColWidth, labelMode` | `Bind<number>`, `Bind<string>`, `Bind<'top' \| 'side' \| 'floating' \| 'hidden'>` | `2`, —, `'side'` | The form layout of the detail (the kit's `FormLayout`). |
| `adaptiveDetail.editors` | `Bind<boolean>` | `true` | Uses editors instead of text for cells the user can fill, in the `row`, `cell` and `batch` edit modes. They write into the row's draft, as its cells do. |
| `adaptiveDetail.expandOnEdit` | `Bind<boolean>` | `true` | Editing a row with hidden columns it can fill opens its detail, and leaving the row closes it (the `row` edit mode). |
| `adaptiveDetail.columnWidth, toggleKeys` | `Bind<number>`, `Bind<string[]>` | `36`, `['Enter', ' ']` | The width of the “…” column, and the keys on its cell that open and close the detail. |

The detail is a separate row directly after its row, before the row's master-detail when both are open. It is measured as it renders, is in the reading order (`aria-owns`), counts in `aria-rowindex`, and has one cell named “Hidden columns of row 3” (`gridAdaptiveOf`, with `gridAdaptive` naming the “…” and its column). Grouped rows, paging and the virtual list keep it below its row, and a wider grid with nothing hidden closes it.

## Keyboard

| Key | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `Up on a column’s header` | Moves to its band's header, and again to the band above. |
| `Down on a band’s header` | Moves to the first column or band under it. |
| `Left / Right, Home / End on a band’s header` | Moves along the bands of its row. |
| `Alt+Down, the context menu key on a band’s header` | Opens its menu: pin, move, hide the band, the column chooser and reset. |
| `Enter, Space on the “…” cell (`toggleKeys`)` | Opens or closes the row's adaptive detail. |
| `Tab on a row whose detail shows` | Moves into the detail. From its last stop, it moves into the row's master-detail or, while the row is being edited, on to the next row's cells. |
| `Tab on the last cell editor of a row` | Moves into the editors of its open adaptive detail. |
| `Escape, Shift+Tab on the detail’s first stop` | Returns to the row. |

## Events and methods

| Member | Parameters or return value | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `onAdaptiveDetailRowPreparing` | `{ row, key, rowIndex, editors, formOptions }` | Occurs before a row's detail lays out its form, when it opens and again when other columns hide or show. Change `formOptions` (`items`, which are the hidden fields or kit form items, plus `colCount`, `minColWidth` and `labelMode`). |
| `onAdaptiveDetailRowExpanding / onAdaptiveDetailRowCollapsing` | `{ row, key, rowIndex, cancel }` | Occurs before a row's detail opens or closes, from its “…”, its keys or code. Set `cancel` to keep it as it is. |
| `onAdaptiveDetailRowExpanded / onAdaptiveDetailRowCollapsed` | `{ row, key, rowIndex }` | Occurs after it opens or closes. |
| `expandAdaptiveDetailRow(key) / collapseAdaptiveDetailRow()` | `boolean` | Opens a row's detail by key (any open detail closes first), or closes the open one. |
| `isAdaptiveDetailRowExpanded(key)` | `boolean` | Indicates whether that row's detail is open. Reactive. |
| `adaptiveHiddenColumns` | `string[]`, reactive | The columns currently hidden by width, in display order. |
| `adaptiveDetail` | read/write, live | `grid.adaptiveDetail.colCount = 1`. `onOptionChanged` reports `adaptiveDetail.colCount`. |
| `getVisibleRows()` | `GridVisibleRow[]` | The open detail directly after its row, with `rowType: 'detailAdaptive'`, before the row's master-detail. |

```tsx
import type { GridColumn } from '@motifx-community/ui';
import type { Order } from './order';

const CUSTOMERS = ['Ada Lovelace', 'Grace Hopper', 'Alan Turing', 'Cahit Arf', 'Katherine Johnson', 'Edsger Dijkstra', 'Barbara Liskov', 'Donald Knuth', 'İlhan Koman', 'Margaret Hamilton'];
const CITIES = ['Ankara', 'Antalya', 'Bursa', 'İstanbul', 'İzmir', 'Konya', 'Trabzon'];
const STATUSES = ['Draft', 'Approved', 'Shipped', 'Delivered', 'Cancelled'];
const NOTES = ['', 'Leave at the door', 'Call before delivery', 'Gift wrap, please, with a card that says happy birthday', '', 'Fragile'];

/** `n` sample orders, the same ones every time. */
export function makeOrders(n: number): Order[] {
  const day = Date.UTC(2026, 0, 1);
  return Array.from({ length: n }, (_, i) => ({
    id: i + 1,
    customer: CUSTOMERS[(i * 7) % CUSTOMERS.length],
    city: CITIES[(i * 3) % CITIES.length],
    date: new Date(day + ((i * 37) % 300) * 86_400_000).toISOString().slice(0, 10),
    status: STATUSES[i % STATUSES.length],
    paid: i % 3 === 0,
    amount: ((i * 7919) % 100_000) / 100,
    note: NOTES[i % NOTES.length],
  }));
}

const money = new Intl.NumberFormat('en', { minimumFractionDigits: 2, maximumFractionDigits: 2 });

/** The order columns: the number pinned to the start, the amount to the end. */
export const columns: GridColumn<Order>[] = [
  { field: 'id', title: 'No', type: 'number', width: 80, sticky: 'start', editable: false },
  { field: 'customer', title: 'Customer', width: 180, flex: 1, required: true },
  { field: 'city', title: 'City', type: 'list', width: 120, options: CITIES },
  { field: 'date', title: 'Date', type: 'date', width: 130, editable: false, creatable: true },
  { field: 'status', title: 'Status', type: 'list', width: 120, options: STATUSES, required: true },
  { field: 'paid', title: 'Paid', type: 'boolean', width: 80 },
  { field: 'note', title: 'Note', width: 200 },
  {
    field: 'amount',
    title: 'Amount',
    type: 'number',
    width: 120,
    sticky: 'end',
    required: true,
    validate: (v) => (typeof v === 'number' && v < 0 ? 'The amount cannot be negative.' : null),
    format: (v) => (typeof v === 'number' ? money.format(v) : ''),
  },
];

/** The same columns with a filter cell and a header filter on most of them. */
export const filterColumns: GridColumn<Order>[] = columns.map((c) => ({ ...c, filterRow: c.field !== 'note', headerFilter: c.field !== 'note' && c.field !== 'id' }));

const today = () => new Date().toISOString().slice(0, 10);

/** What a new order starts with. */
export const newOrder = () => ({ date: today(), status: 'Draft', paid: false });
```
