# DataGrid: Selection and export

> DataGrid · @motifx-community/ui 0.1.0-beta.5

## Selection

`selection` is `single`, where the selection follows the active row, or `multiple`, with a check box column. Clicking selects a row, Ctrl adds or removes one, and Shift selects a range. Shift+Space, Shift+arrow keys and Ctrl+A do the same from the keyboard. The header check box selects every row of the filter, including on a server, where the grid keeps a state of “all except these keys” instead of the rows. `selection` provides that state, and `selectionFilter` provides the same thing as a filter for the server. Selected rows use the selection appearance of the design language, as its lists and trees do, with its fill and text color and any frame, raised effect or start bar it defines. The hover and active row tints sit above it, with the keyboard focus ring on top, and a selected row stays one row high.

```tsx
import { data } from '@motifx-community/data';

/** Rows in memory that answer a little later, the way a server does; for the examples. */
export class SlowAdapter<T extends object, K> extends data.ArrayAdapter<T, K> {
  constructor(
    options: data.ArrayAdapterOptions<T>,
    private readonly delayMs = 300,
  ) {
    super(options);
  }

  override async load(options: data.LoadOptions = {}): Promise<data.LoadResult<T>> {
    await new Promise((done) => setTimeout(done, this.delayMs));
    return super.load(options);
  }
}
```

## Copy and paste

Ctrl+C copies the selected rows, or the active cell, as tab-separated text and an HTML table, so a spreadsheet or document receives it as a table. Ctrl+V on a cell writes tab-separated text, from a spreadsheet or copied from the grid, into the editable cells to the right of and below that cell. Each value is interpreted by column type (numbers and dates by locale, yes or no, and a list option by its text) and goes into the row's draft with validation, as if typed. Cells that cannot be edited keep their values. Rows below the active row are saved according to the save mode.

```tsx
/** An order, as stored by the sample server. */
export interface Order {
  id: number;
  customer: string;
  city: string;
  date: string;
  status: string;
  paid: boolean;
  amount: number;
  note: string;
}
```

## Export

`exportCsv()` saves the rows of the filter, in sort order, with the visible columns in their order, as a CSV file that a spreadsheet can open directly. The file is UTF-8 with a byte order mark and uses the locale's separator (`;` where decimals use a comma), with column titles first, and text that a spreadsheet would run as a formula is neutralized. `exportRows()` returns the same rows as objects. In-memory rows are used as they are, and server rows are requested in parts through the data source, so its filter, search and sort apply and nothing on screen changes. `exportButton` adds an “Export” button to the toolbar, and `exportable` excludes a column.

```tsx
import { data } from '@motifx-community/data';

/** Rows in memory that answer a little later, the way a server does; for the examples. */
export class SlowAdapter<T extends object, K> extends data.ArrayAdapter<T, K> {
  constructor(
    options: data.ArrayAdapterOptions<T>,
    private readonly delayMs = 300,
  ) {
    super(options);
  }

  override async load(options: data.LoadOptions = {}): Promise<data.LoadResult<T>> {
    await new Promise((done) => setTimeout(done, this.delayMs));
    return super.load(options);
  }
}
```

## Export to Excel

The grid does not include an xlsx writer. The application provides ExcelJS (`npm i exceljs`, an optional peer dependency) and calls `exportDataGrid({ component, worksheet })` from `@motifx-community/ui/excel`, a separate entry point that applications without Excel export never load. With `export: { formats: ['xlsx', 'csv'] }`, the toolbar's export button becomes a menu (“Export all data to Excel”, and “Export selected rows to Excel” with `allowExportSelectedData`). The Excel commands raise `onExporting` with `format: 'xlsx'` and `selectedRowsOnly`, and the handler writes and saves the workbook. In this example, it is a Blob download, with ExcelJS loaded on the first export.

```tsx
/** An order, as stored by the sample server. */
export interface Order {
  id: number;
  customer: string;
  city: string;
  date: string;
  status: string;
  paid: boolean;
  amount: number;
  note: string;
}
```

The sheet contains the frozen header row and the rows in grid order with the filter, search and grouping applied. Every matching row is included, and server rows load in parts while a panel over the rows shows the progress and a Stop button. It also includes group rows (“Column: value” with their summary items, with aligned items under their columns) with Excel outline levels, group footers and totals. Numbers stay numbers, with a number format derived from the column's `Intl` format, and dates stay dates. Yes/no cells are Excel's `TRUE` and `FALSE` (`booleanText` writes the grid's text), lookup and list cells contain their text, a column with a `format` function contains its text, and widths follow the grid. `customizeCell({ gridCell, excelCell })` changes any cell, and `gridCell` provides `rowType`, `column`, `data`, `value`, `groupIndex`, `groupSummaryItems` and `totalSummaryItemName`. The promise resolves with the cells written, `{ from, to }`.

| exportDataGrid option | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `component, worksheet` | — | The grid, and the ExcelJS worksheet to write to (`workbook.addWorksheet('Orders')`). |
| `topLeftCell` | `{ row: 1, column: 1 }` | The position of the first cell: `{ row, column }` or a reference such as `'B2'`. |
| `customizeCell` | — | `({ gridCell, excelCell }) => void` for every cell, after its value and style are set. |
| `autoFilterEnabled` | `false` | Adds Excel filter buttons to the header row. |
| `keepColumnWidths` | `true` | Makes columns as wide as in the grid. |
| `selectedRowsOnly` | The toolbar command, otherwise `false` | Exports only the selected rows, without group rows or summaries, as with CSV. |
| `loadPanel` | On | The panel over the rows while they load: `true` / `false`, or `{ enabled, text, showProgress, cancelButton }`. |
| `encodeExecutableContent` | `false` | Prefixes text that a spreadsheet would run as a formula with `'`. |
| `headers, frozenHeader` | `true` | The row of column titles, which stays in view while the sheet scrolls. |
| `groups, outline, summaries` | `true` | Group rows, outline levels by group (up to 7), group summary items, footers and totals. |
| `numberFormats, booleanText` | `true`, `false` | Excel number formats from the columns' `Intl` formats, and the grid's yes/no text instead of `TRUE` and `FALSE`. |
| `pageSize, onProgress, signal` | The `exportPageSize` setting | The rows per request to a server, a callback after each part, and a signal that stops the export (the promise rejects with an `AbortError`). |

## Export to PDF

PDF export works the same way. The application provides jsPDF (`npm i jspdf`, an optional peer dependency) and calls `exportDataGrid({ jsPDFDocument, component })` from `@motifx-community/ui/pdf`, a separate entry point. Add `'pdf'` to `export.formats`, and the toolbar menu offers “Export all data to PDF” (and the selected rows). The command raises `onExporting` with `format: 'pdf'`, and the handler creates the document, draws the grid on it and saves it. The table is drawn with jsPDF's own calls and no table plugin. It includes the header rows with bands merged over their columns, the rows in grid order with the filter, search, grouping, text and alignment of the grid, the group rows across the row, the group footers and the totals. Columns use the grid's widths, narrowed to fit the page, and rows that do not fit continue on the next page below repeated header rows. In right-to-left layouts, the columns run from the right edge.

```tsx
/** An order, as stored by the sample server. */
export interface Order {
  id: number;
  customer: string;
  city: string;
  date: string;
  status: string;
  paid: boolean;
  amount: number;
  note: string;
}
```

The built-in jsPDF fonts (Helvetica, Times, Courier) support Latin-1 only. Turkish letters such as İ, ş and ğ, and Cyrillic, Greek or Arabic text, require a TrueType font that contains them, added to the document before export (`doc.addFileToVFS`, `doc.addFont`, `doc.setFont`). A bold style is also needed, because group rows and totals use it. This example fetches Noto Sans on the first export, and keeps the jsPDF font if the fetch fails. The promise resolves with the end of the table (`{ page, y }`), so that you can continue writing below it.

| exportDataGrid option | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `jsPDFDocument, component` | — | The jsPDF document to draw on (`new jsPDF()`, with the table starting on its current page), and the grid. |
| `topLeft` | `{ x: 0, y: 0 }` | The position where the table starts on its first page, measured from the top left margin. |
| `margin` | 40 points on each side | The space kept free at the page edges: a number, or `{ top, right, bottom, left }`. |
| `columnWidths` | The grid's widths, scaled to fit | The width of each column, in order. An omitted column uses the grid's width. |
| `fitColumns` | `'shrink'` | Without `columnWidths`: narrows the grid's widths when wider than the page (`'shrink'`), always makes them as wide as the page (`'fill'`), or leaves them as they are (`'none'`). |
| `repeatHeaders` | `true` | Repeats the header rows, including bands, at the top of every page. |
| `indent` | `0` | The indent of a group's rows from its group row, per level. |
| `customizeCell` | — | `({ gridCell, pdfCell }) => void` for every cell, before the rows are measured: `text`, `font` (`size`, `name`, `style`), `textColor`, `backgroundColor`, `borderColor`, `borderWidth`, the four `draw…Border` options, `horizontalAlign`, `verticalAlign`, `padding` and `wordWrapEnabled`. |
| `customDrawCell` | — | `({ doc, rect, gridCell, pdfCell, cancel }) => void` before a cell is drawn. Draw it yourself, such as an image or a bar, and set `cancel` (the borders are still drawn). |
| `onRowExporting` | — | `({ rowCells, rowHeight }) => void` before a row is placed. Set a taller `rowHeight` (never less than its text requires). |
| `wordWrapEnabled, fontSize` | `false`, `10` | Wraps long text onto more lines (otherwise, a line that does not fit ends in “…”), and sets the cell font size in points. |
| `selectedRowsOnly` | The toolbar command, otherwise `false` | Exports only the selected rows, without group rows or summaries, as with CSV and Excel. |
| `loadPanel` | On | The panel over the rows while they load, with the progress and a Stop button: `true` / `false`, or `{ enabled, text, showProgress, cancelButton }`. |
| `headers, groups, summaries` | `true` | The header rows, one row per group, group summary items, footers and totals. |
| `pageSize, onProgress, signal` | The `exportPageSize` setting | The rows per request to a server, a callback after each part, and a signal that stops the export (the promise rejects with an `AbortError`, and nothing is drawn). |

`Selection.tsx`

```tsx
import { reactive } from '@motifx/core';
import { data } from '@motifx-community/data';
import { Button, DataGrid, Stack, type GridAction, type GridSelection } from '@motifx-community/ui';
import { SlowAdapter } from '../../../shared/slow-adapter';
import type { Order } from './order';
import { columns, makeOrders } from './orders';

const MODES = ['none', 'single', 'multiple'] as const;

const describe = (sel: GridSelection | undefined) =>
  !sel ? '' : sel.all ? `all but ${sel.except.length} (${sel.except.slice(0, 5).join(', ')})` : `${sel.keys.length} picked (${sel.keys.slice(0, 5).join(', ')})`;

/** Single and multiple selection; over 100,000 rows on a server "all" is a state, never the rows. */
export default function Selection() {
  const s = reactive({ mode: 'multiple' as 'none' | 'single' | 'multiple', selection: undefined as GridSelection | undefined, note: '' });
  // The server groups, so "all except these keys" is sent to it as a filter.
  const orders = new data.DataSource<Order, number>({ adapter: new SlowAdapter<Order, number>({ data: makeOrders(100_000), key: 'id' }, 200), loadMode: 'blocks', pageSize: 100 });
  let grid: DataGrid<Order> | null = null;
  let server: DataGrid<Order> | null = null;

  const print: GridAction<Order> = { id: 'print', text: 'Print', onclick: (row) => (s.note = `Order ${row.id} sent to the printer`) };
  const mail: GridAction<Order> = { id: 'mail', text: 'Mail the customer', disabled: (row) => !row.paid, onclick: (row) => (s.note = `Mail to ${row.customer}`) };

  return (
    <>
      <Stack orientation="horizontal" wrap align="center" role="group" aria-label="Selection mode">
        {MODES.map((mode) => (
          <Button key={mode} text={mode} size="sm" variant={() => (s.mode === mode ? 'solid' : 'ghost')} aria-pressed={() => s.mode === mode} onclick={() => (s.mode = mode)} />
        ))}
      </Stack>
      <DataGrid
        class="dg-selection"
        style="block-size: 28rem"
        rows={makeOrders(40)}
        rowKey="id"
        columns={columns}
        label="Orders to select"
        locale="en"
        settings={{ selection: () => s.mode }}
        onSelectionChanged={(e) => (s.selection = e.selection)}
        ref={(g: DataGrid<Order>) => (grid = g)}
      />
      <output class="dg-selection-state">{() => `${(grid?.selectedCount ?? 0).toLocaleString('en')} selected: ${describe(s.selection)}`}</output>
      <DataGrid
        class="dg-server-selection"
        style="block-size: 28rem"
        dataSource={orders}
        columns={columns}
        label="100,000 orders to select"
        locale="en"
        settings={{ selection: 'multiple' }}
        actions={[print, mail]}
        ref={(g: DataGrid<Order>) => (server = g)}
      />
      <output class="dg-server-selection-state">{() => `${(server?.selectedCount ?? 0).toLocaleString('en')} selected: ${describe(server?.selection)}`}</output>
      <output>{() => s.note}</output>
    </>
  );
}
```

`orders.ts`

```tsx
import type { GridColumn } from '@motifx-community/ui';
import type { Order } from './order';

const CUSTOMERS = ['Ada Lovelace', 'Grace Hopper', 'Alan Turing', 'Cahit Arf', 'Katherine Johnson', 'Edsger Dijkstra', 'Barbara Liskov', 'Donald Knuth', 'İlhan Koman', 'Margaret Hamilton'];
const CITIES = ['Ankara', 'Antalya', 'Bursa', 'İstanbul', 'İzmir', 'Konya', 'Trabzon'];
const STATUSES = ['Draft', 'Approved', 'Shipped', 'Delivered', 'Cancelled'];
const NOTES = ['', 'Leave at the door', 'Call before delivery', 'Gift wrap, please, with a card that says happy birthday', '', 'Fragile'];

/** `n` sample orders, the same ones every time. */
export function makeOrders(n: number): Order[] {
  const day = Date.UTC(2026, 0, 1);
  return Array.from({ length: n }, (_, i) => ({
    id: i + 1,
    customer: CUSTOMERS[(i * 7) % CUSTOMERS.length],
    city: CITIES[(i * 3) % CITIES.length],
    date: new Date(day + ((i * 37) % 300) * 86_400_000).toISOString().slice(0, 10),
    status: STATUSES[i % STATUSES.length],
    paid: i % 3 === 0,
    amount: ((i * 7919) % 100_000) / 100,
    note: NOTES[i % NOTES.length],
  }));
}

const money = new Intl.NumberFormat('en', { minimumFractionDigits: 2, maximumFractionDigits: 2 });

/** The order columns: the number pinned to the start, the amount to the end. */
export const columns: GridColumn<Order>[] = [
  { field: 'id', title: 'No', type: 'number', width: 80, sticky: 'start', editable: false },
  { field: 'customer', title: 'Customer', width: 180, flex: 1, required: true },
  { field: 'city', title: 'City', type: 'list', width: 120, options: CITIES },
  { field: 'date', title: 'Date', type: 'date', width: 130, editable: false, creatable: true },
  { field: 'status', title: 'Status', type: 'list', width: 120, options: STATUSES, required: true },
  { field: 'paid', title: 'Paid', type: 'boolean', width: 80 },
  { field: 'note', title: 'Note', width: 200 },
  {
    field: 'amount',
    title: 'Amount',
    type: 'number',
    width: 120,
    sticky: 'end',
    required: true,
    validate: (v) => (typeof v === 'number' && v < 0 ? 'The amount cannot be negative.' : null),
    format: (v) => (typeof v === 'number' ? money.format(v) : ''),
  },
];

/** The same columns with a filter cell and a header filter on most of them. */
export const filterColumns: GridColumn<Order>[] = columns.map((c) => ({ ...c, filterRow: c.field !== 'note', headerFilter: c.field !== 'note' && c.field !== 'id' }));

const today = () => new Date().toISOString().slice(0, 10);

/** What a new order starts with. */
export const newOrder = () => ({ date: today(), status: 'Draft', paid: false });
```

`slow-adapter.ts`

```tsx
import { data } from '@motifx-community/data';

/** Rows in memory that answer a little later, the way a server does; for the examples. */
export class SlowAdapter<T extends object, K> extends data.ArrayAdapter<T, K> {
  constructor(
    options: data.ArrayAdapterOptions<T>,
    private readonly delayMs = 300,
  ) {
    super(options);
  }

  override async load(options: data.LoadOptions = {}): Promise<data.LoadResult<T>> {
    await new Promise((done) => setTimeout(done, this.delayMs));
    return super.load(options);
  }
```
```tsx
}
```

`Export.tsx`

```tsx
import { reactive } from '@motifx/core';
import { Button, DataGrid, Stack } from '@motifx-community/ui';
import type { Order } from './order';
import { columns, filterColumns, makeOrders } from './orders';
import { pagedOrders } from './paged-orders';

/** The bar's "Export" button, rows as objects, and 100,000 rows of a server saved in parts. */
export default function Export() {
  const s = reactive({ exported: '', progress: '' });
  let grid: DataGrid<Order> | null = null;

  const firstTwo = async () => {
    const rows = (await grid?.exportRows({ values: 'raw' })) ?? [];
    s.exported = JSON.stringify(rows.slice(0, 2));
  };

  // A grid created with `new` can export without being shown. This one reads the orders of the paged grid.
  const exportServer = async () => {
    const server = new DataGrid<Order>({ dataSource: pagedOrders, columns, label: 'Orders by page', locale: 'en' });
    s.progress = 'starting…';
    try {
      await server.exportCsv({ pageSize: 10_000, fileName: 'orders', onProgress: (n, total) => (s.progress = `${n.toLocaleString('en')} of ${total.toLocaleString('en')}`) });
      s.progress += ' — saved';
    } catch {
      s.progress = 'failed';
    } finally {
      server.dispose();
    }
  };

  return (
    <>
      <DataGrid
        class="dg-export"
        style="block-size: 28rem"
        rows={makeOrders(60)}
        rowKey="id"
        columns={filterColumns}
        label="Orders to export"
        locale="en"
        settings={{ exportButton: true, filterRow: true }}
        ref={(g: DataGrid<Order>) => (grid = g)}
      />
      <Stack orientation="horizontal" wrap align="center">
        <Button text="The first two rows as objects" variant="outline" onclick={firstTwo} />
        <Button text="Export the 100,000 orders by page" variant="outline" onclick={() => void exportServer()} />
      </Stack>
      <output class="dg-exported">{() => s.exported}</output>
      <output class="dg-export-progress">{() => (s.progress ? `Server export: ${s.progress}` : '')}</output>
    </>
  );
}
```

`ExcelExport.tsx`

```tsx
import { reactive } from '@motifx/core';
import { DataGrid, type GridExportingEventArgs, type GridSummary } from '@motifx-community/ui';
import { exportDataGrid } from '@motifx-community/ui/excel';
import type { Order } from './order';
import { columns, makeOrders } from './orders';

/** Saves a file through a link the browser downloads. */
function saveFile(blob: Blob, name: string) {
  const url = URL.createObjectURL(blob);
  const link = document.createElement('a');
  link.href = url;
  link.download = name;
  link.click();
  setTimeout(() => URL.revokeObjectURL(url), 1000);
}

/** The toolbar's export menu: Excel through ExcelJS and `exportDataGrid`, CSV by the grid itself. */
export default function ExcelExport() {
  const s = reactive({ saved: '' });
  // Grouped by city; the amount in `Intl` options, which become its Excel number format.
  const byCity = columns.map((c) =>
    c.field === 'city' ? { ...c, groupIndex: 0 } : c.field === 'amount' ? { ...c, width: 150, format: { minimumFractionDigits: 2, maximumFractionDigits: 2 } } : c,
  );
  const summary: GridSummary<Order> = {
    totalItems: [
      { column: 'id', summaryType: 'count', showInColumn: 'customer' },
      { column: 'amount', summaryType: 'sum' },
    ],
    groupItems: [
      { column: 'amount', summaryType: 'sum', alignByColumn: true },
      { column: 'amount', summaryType: 'max', showInGroupFooter: true },
    ],
  };

  // The grid raises onExporting for 'xlsx'; the file is written here. ExcelJS
  // loads the first time, so the page does not carry it until someone exports.
  const onExporting = async (e: GridExportingEventArgs) => {
    if (e.format !== 'xlsx') return;
    const { default: ExcelJS } = await import('exceljs');
    const workbook = new ExcelJS.Workbook();
    const worksheet = workbook.addWorksheet('Orders');
    const range = await exportDataGrid({
      component: e.component,
      worksheet,
      selectedRowsOnly: e.selectedRowsOnly,
      autoFilterEnabled: true,
      customizeCell: ({ gridCell, excelCell }) => {
        if (gridCell.rowType === 'data' && gridCell.column?.field === 'status' && gridCell.value === 'Cancelled') excelCell.font = { color: { argb: 'FFB42318' } };
      },
    });
    const buffer = await workbook.xlsx.writeBuffer();
    saveFile(new Blob([buffer], { type: 'application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.spreadsheetml.sheet' }), 'Orders.xlsx');
    s.saved = `Orders.xlsx: rows ${range.from.row}–${range.to.row}, columns ${range.from.column}–${range.to.column}`;
  };

  return (
    <>
      <DataGrid
        class="dg-excel"
        style="block-size: 32rem"
        rows={makeOrders(200)}
        rowKey="id"
        columns={byCity}
        label="Orders for Excel"
        locale="en"
        summary={summary}
        settings={{ exportButton: true, selection: 'multiple' }}
        export={{ formats: ['xlsx', 'csv'], allowExportSelectedData: true }}
        onExporting={onExporting}
      />
      <output class="dg-excel-saved">{() => s.saved}</output>
    </>
  );
}
```

`PdfExport.tsx`

```tsx
import { reactive } from '@motifx/core';
import { DataGrid, type GridExportingEventArgs, type GridSummary } from '@motifx-community/ui';
import { exportDataGrid } from '@motifx-community/ui/pdf';
import type { jsPDF } from 'jspdf';
import type { Order } from './order';
import { columns, makeOrders } from './orders';

// jsPDF's own fonts write Latin-1 only: "İzmir" and "İlhan Koman" need a font that has their letters.
const FONT = 'https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/@expo-google-fonts/noto-sans@0.2.3/';
let font: Promise<{ regular: string; bold: string }> | null = null;

async function base64(url: string): Promise<string> {
  const bytes = new Uint8Array(await (await fetch(url)).arrayBuffer());
  let text = '';
  for (let i = 0; i < bytes.length; i += 0x8000) text += String.fromCharCode(...bytes.subarray(i, i + 0x8000));
  return btoa(text);
}

/** Noto Sans in the document, fetched once; without the network the document keeps jsPDF's own font. */
async function useNotoSans(doc: jsPDF) {
  font ??= Promise.all([base64(`${FONT}NotoSans_400Regular.ttf`), base64(`${FONT}NotoSans_700Bold.ttf`)]).then(([regular, bold]) => ({ regular, bold }));
  try {
    const { regular, bold } = await font;
    doc.addFileToVFS('NotoSans-Regular.ttf', regular);
    doc.addFont('NotoSans-Regular.ttf', 'NotoSans', 'normal');
    doc.addFileToVFS('NotoSans-Bold.ttf', bold);
    doc.addFont('NotoSans-Bold.ttf', 'NotoSans', 'bold');
    doc.setFont('NotoSans', 'normal');
  } catch {
    font = null;
  }
}

/** The toolbar's export menu with PDF: `onExporting` draws the grid on a jsPDF document and saves it. */
export default function PdfExport() {
  const s = reactive({ saved: '' });
  const byCity = columns.map((c) => (c.field === 'city' ? { ...c, groupIndex: 0 } : c));
  const summary: GridSummary<Order> = {
    totalItems: [{ column: 'amount', summaryType: 'sum' }],
    groupItems: [
      { column: 'id', summaryType: 'count' },
      { column: 'amount', summaryType: 'sum', showInGroupFooter: true },
    ],
  };

  // The grid raises onExporting for 'pdf', and the file is written here. jsPDF loads
  // the first time someone exports.
  const onExporting = async (e: GridExportingEventArgs) => {
    if (e.format !== 'pdf') return;
    const { jsPDF } = await import('jspdf');
    const doc = new jsPDF({ orientation: 'landscape' });
    await useNotoSans(doc);
    doc.setFontSize(14);
    doc.text('Orders by city', 14, 14);
    const end = await exportDataGrid({
      jsPDFDocument: doc,
      component: e.component,
      selectedRowsOnly: e.selectedRowsOnly,
      topLeft: { y: 6 },
      margin: 14,
      indent: 4,
      customizeCell: ({ gridCell, pdfCell }) => {
        if (gridCell.rowType === 'group') pdfCell.backgroundColor = '#EEF2F8';
        if (gridCell.rowType === 'data' && gridCell.column?.field === 'status' && gridCell.value === 'Cancelled') pdfCell.textColor = '#B42318';
      },
    });
    doc.save('Orders.pdf');
    s.saved = `Orders.pdf: ${doc.getNumberOfPages()} pages, the table ends on page ${end.page}`;
  };

  return (
    <>
      <DataGrid
        class="dg-pdf"
        style="block-size: 28rem"
        rows={makeOrders(120)}
        rowKey="id"
        columns={byCity}
        label="Orders for PDF"
        locale="en"
        summary={summary}
        settings={{ exportButton: true, selection: 'multiple' }}
        export={{ formats: ['pdf', 'csv'], allowExportSelectedData: true }}
        onExporting={onExporting}
      />
      <output class="dg-pdf-saved">{() => s.saved}</output>
    </>
  );
}
```

# DataGrid: Row drag and drop

> DataGrid · @motifx-community/ui 0.1.0-beta.5

## Reorder rows

With `rowDragging: { allowReordering: true }`, a column of drag icons appears at the start. Drag a row by its icon, and a copy of the row follows the pointer while a line shows the drop position. With `dropFeedbackMode: 'push'`, the rows move aside to make room instead. Near the top or bottom edge, the rows scroll. On drop, `onReorder` reports the new position. The grid does not move the data itself, so the handler must do it. In this example, the rows are in memory, so the handler removes the row and inserts it at the position of `toItemData` (the row at `toIndex`). Ctrl+Shift+Up and Down move the active row the same way.

```tsx
/** A task of the drag and drop examples. */
export interface Task {
  id: number;
  title: string;
  owner: string;
  priority: string;
  /** Its place in the list, as a server keeps it. */
  order: number;
}
```

## Reorder rows on a server

On a server, the order is a field the rows are sorted by. The handler asks the server to move the row to the position of `toItemData`, and gives the promise to the grid (`e.promise`). The line stays until the response arrives, and then `refresh()` loads the rows in their new order. This example has 10,000 rows, and the virtual list loads blocks as it scrolls.

```tsx
import { data } from '@motifx-community/data';

/** Rows in memory that answer a little later, the way a server does; for the examples. */
export class SlowAdapter<T extends object, K> extends data.ArrayAdapter<T, K> {
  constructor(
    options: data.ArrayAdapterOptions<T>,
    private readonly delayMs = 300,
  ) {
    super(options);
  }

  override async load(options: data.LoadOptions = {}): Promise<data.LoadResult<T>> {
    await new Promise((done) => setTimeout(done, this.delayMs));
    return super.load(options);
  }
}
```

## Drag rows between grids

Grids with the same `group` accept each other's rows. When a row is dropped on the other grid, `onRemove` occurs on the source grid and `onAdd` on the target grid, with `toIndex` and `toItemData` giving the position. Both grids in this example also push rows aside and support reordering.

```tsx
/** A task of the drag and drop examples. */
export interface Task {
  id: number;
  title: string;
  owner: string;
  priority: string;
  /** Its place in the list, as a server keeps it. */
  order: number;
}
```

## Options

| rowDragging | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `allowReordering` | `Bind<boolean>` | `false` | Allows rows to move within the grid. |
| `allowDropInsideItem` | `Bind<boolean>` | `false` | Allows a row to be dropped onto another (the middle half of a row), reported as `dropInsideItem` in the events. This is useful for trees and details. |
| `dropFeedbackMode` | `Bind<'indicate' \| 'push'>` | `'indicate'` | How the drop position appears: a line between the rows, or the rows moving aside to make room (not with `allowDropInsideItem`). |
| `showDragIcons` | `Bind<boolean>` | `true` | A column of drag icons pinned to the start. When disabled, the whole row is draggable (a click still selects and edits). |
| `handle` | `Bind<string>` | `''` | A CSS selector for the part of a row used for dragging, instead of the icon or the whole row. |
| `group, data` | `Bind<string>`, `Bind<unknown>` | — | Grids in the same group accept each other's rows. `data` is passed to the events as `fromData` and `toData`. |
| `dragDirection` | `Bind<'both' \| 'vertical' \| 'horizontal'>` | `'both'` | Where the copy of the row can go. |
| `boundary, container` | `Bind<string \| HTMLElement>` | None, and the grid | The element the dragged row stays inside, and the element that displays its copy. |
| `cursorOffset` | `Bind<{ x, y } \| string>` | Where the row was grabbed | The offset of the copy from the pointer. |
| `dragTemplate` | `({ itemData, itemElement }) => unknown` | A copy of the row | Custom content under the pointer: a component, an element or text. |
| `autoScroll, scrollSpeed, scrollSensitivity` | `Bind<boolean>`, `Bind<number>`, `Bind<number>` | `true`, `30`, `60` | The rows scroll while the pointer is near their top or bottom edge: the speed in pixels per frame at the edge, and the distance at which it starts. |
| `keyboard, moveUpKeys, moveDownKeys` | `Bind<boolean>`, `Bind<string[]>` | `true`, `['Ctrl+Shift+ArrowUp']`, `['Ctrl+Shift+ArrowDown']` | Moves the active row one position up or down with these keys (any combination, such as `Mod+Alt+Up`), with the same events as a drop. The move is announced. |
| `columnWidth` | `Bind<number>` | `36` | The width of the drag icon column, in pixels. |
| `settings.dragThreshold, settings.dragGhost` | `Bind<number>`, `Bind<boolean>` | `5`, `true` | The distance the pointer moves before a drag starts, and whether a copy follows it. These are the same as for headers. |

| Topic | Dragging behavior |
| --- | --- |
| `The data` | The grid does not move anything itself. `onReorder` and `onAdd` / `onRemove` move the row in your array or notify the server. The grid reads your rows as they are, plain or reactive, so after the move, call `e.component.refresh()` (for both in-memory rows and a server). |
| `Sorted, filtered, grouped` | Rows can be dragged in their displayed order, and the indexes are the displayed ones. A manually ordered list usually disables `sortable`. While grouped, the keys move a row within its group, and only data rows can be dragged (not group rows, new rows or rows still loading). |
| `Virtual and paged` | The rows under the pointer are the pooled rows currently rendered, and near the edges, the rows scroll and new ones receive the marks. In paged mode, a row moves within its page, and the indexes count across pages. |
| `Screen readers` | The drag icon cell is named “Drag to move the row”, with the keys in `aria-keyshortcuts`. Drops and key moves are announced politely. |

## Events and methods

| rowDragging handler | When |
| --- | --- |
| `onDragStart` | Occurs before a row is dragged, by pointer or keys. Set `cancel` to keep it in place. |
| `onDragMove` | Occurs when the row moves under the pointer. Set `cancel` to refuse a drop there. |
| `onDragChange` | Occurs when the drop position changes (another index, another grid, or onto a row). Set `cancel` to refuse a drop there. |
| `onDragEnd` | Occurs before the row is dropped (`toIndex` is -1 when it is not over a grid that accepts it). Set `cancel` to drop nothing. |
| `onReorder` | Occurs on a drop elsewhere in this grid, where you move the row in the data. With `promise`, the grid waits for it while keeping the marks visible. |
| `onRemove / onAdd` | Occurs on a drop on another grid of the group: `onRemove` on the source grid and `onAdd` on the target grid. |

| Event field | Value |
| --- | --- |
| `component, fromComponent, toComponent` | The grid raising the event, the grid the row comes from, and the grid under the pointer (the same while reordering, or `null` when over none). |
| `itemData, itemKey, itemElement` | The dragged row, its key and its element. |
| `fromIndex, toIndex` | The grid's row indexes (as counted by `focusedRowIndex` and `getVisibleRows()`, also across pages): the current position, and the position after the drop. |
| `toItemData` | The row at `toIndex` before the drop, which is where to insert the row. It is `undefined` at the end of the other grid or on a group row. |
| `dropInsideItem, fromData, toData, event` | Whether it was dropped onto the row at `toIndex`, the grids' `rowDragging.data`, and the pointer or key event. |
| `cancel / promise` | The four drag events can be canceled, and the three drop events accept a promise. |

| Member | Parameters or return value | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `rowDragging` | read/write, live | `grid.rowDragging.allowReordering = true`, and handlers too. `onOptionChanged` reports `rowDragging.allowReordering`. |
| `moveRow(fromIndex, toIndex)` | `Promise<boolean>` | Moves a row as a drop there would: `onDragStart`, `onDragChange` and `onDragEnd` (any of which can cancel), then `onReorder`. Returns whether the event was raised. |

## Keyboard

| Key | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `Ctrl+Shift+Up / Ctrl+Shift+Down on a row (`moveUpKeys`, `moveDownKeys`)` | Moves the active row one position up or down (`allowReordering`). The row stays active, and the move is announced (“Row moved to position 3 of 20”). |
| `Escape while dragging` | Cancels the drag, and nothing is dropped. |

## Example files

`RowReorder.tsx`

```tsx
import { reactive } from '@motifx/core';
import { CheckBox, DataGrid, Stack } from '@motifx-community/ui';
import type { Task } from './task';
import { makeTasks, taskColumns } from './tasks';

/** Rows in memory reordered by dragging (or Ctrl+Shift+Up / Down): `onReorder` moves the row in the array. */
export default function RowReorder() {
  const s = reactive({ rows: makeTasks(500), push: true, icons: true });

  return (
    <>
      <Stack orientation="horizontal" wrap align="center">
        <CheckBox label="The rows make room (push)" x-model={() => s.push} />
        <CheckBox label="Drag icons (off: drag the whole row)" x-model={() => s.icons} />
      </Stack>
      <DataGrid
        class="dg-reorder"
        style="block-size: 28rem"
        rows={() => s.rows}
        rowKey="id"
        columns={taskColumns}
        label="Tasks to reorder"
        locale="en"
        settings={{ sortable: false }}
        rowDragging={{
          allowReordering: true,
          dropFeedbackMode: () => (s.push ? 'push' : 'indicate'),
          showDragIcons: () => s.icons,
          onReorder: (e) => {
            // The grid does not move the data: take the row out and put it where the row at `toIndex` is.
            const from = s.rows.indexOf(e.itemData);
            const to = s.rows.indexOf(e.toItemData as Task);
            s.rows.splice(from, 1);
            s.rows.splice(to, 0, e.itemData);
            e.component.refresh();
          },
        }}
      />
    </>
  );
}
```

`tasks.ts`

```tsx
import type { GridColumn } from '@motifx-community/ui';
import type { Task } from './task';

const TITLES = ['Write the release notes', 'Fix the login page', 'Review the pull request', 'Plan the sprint', 'Update the docs', 'Call the customer', 'Test on mobile', 'Clean up the backlog'];
const OWNERS = ['Ada', 'Grace', 'Alan', 'Cahit', 'Katherine', 'Edsger'];
const PRIORITIES = ['Low', 'Normal', 'High'];

/** `n` sample tasks from id `from`, in order. */
export function makeTasks(n: number, from = 1): Task[] {
  return Array.from({ length: n }, (_, i) => ({
    id: from + i,
    title: `${TITLES[(from + i) % TITLES.length]} #${from + i}`,
    owner: OWNERS[(from + i) % OWNERS.length],
    priority: PRIORITIES[(from + i) % PRIORITIES.length],
    order: i,
  }));
}

export const taskColumns: GridColumn<Task>[] = [
  { field: 'id', title: 'No', type: 'number', width: 70 },
  { field: 'title', title: 'Task', width: 240, flex: 1 },
  { field: 'owner', title: 'Owner', width: 110 },
  { field: 'priority', title: 'Priority', width: 100 },
];
```

`task.ts`

```tsx
/** A task of the drag and drop examples. */
export interface Task {
  id: number;
  title: string;
  owner: string;
  priority: string;
  /** Its place in the list, as a server keeps it. */
  order: number;
}
```

`RowReorderServer.tsx`

```tsx
import { reactive } from '@motifx/core';
import { data } from '@motifx-community/data';
import { DataGrid } from '@motifx-community/ui';
import { SlowAdapter } from '../../../shared/slow-adapter';
import type { Task } from './task';
import { makeTasks, taskColumns } from './tasks';

const tasks = makeTasks(10_000);
const server = new SlowAdapter<Task, number>({ data: tasks, key: 'id' }, 200);
const source = new data.DataSource<Task, number>({ adapter: server, loadMode: 'blocks', pageSize: 100 });

/** What the server does when a task moves to place `order`: the tasks in between move one place. */
async function moveTask(id: number, order: number) {
  await new Promise((done) => setTimeout(done, 200));
  const task = tasks.find((t) => t.id === id)!;
  const from = task.order;
  for (const t of tasks) {
    if (from < order && t.order > from && t.order <= order) t.order--;
    else if (from > order && t.order >= order && t.order < from) t.order++;
  }
  task.order = order;
}

/** 10,000 tasks on a server, sorted by their `order` field. A drop notifies the server and reloads. */
export default function RowReorderServer() {
  const s = reactive({ saved: '' });
  return (
    <>
      <DataGrid
        class="dg-reorder-server"
        style="block-size: 28rem"
        dataSource={source}
        columns={[...taskColumns, { field: 'order', title: 'Order', type: 'number', width: 90 }]}
        sort={[{ field: 'order', dir: 'asc' }]}
        label="Tasks on a server"
        locale="en"
        settings={{ sortable: false }}
        rowDragging={{
          allowReordering: true,
          onReorder: (e) => {
            // The row at `toIndex` gives the position. The grid waits for the promise while the line stays visible.
            const order = (e.toItemData as Task).order;
            e.promise = moveTask(e.itemData.id, order).then(() => {
              s.saved = `Task ${e.itemData.id} moved to order ${order}`;
              return e.component.refresh();
            });
          },
        }}
      />
      <output class="dg-reorder-saved">{() => s.saved}</output>
    </>
  );
}
```

```tsx
    options: data.ArrayAdapterOptions<T>,
    private readonly delayMs = 300,
  ) {
    super(options);
  }

  override async load(options: data.LoadOptions = {}): Promise<data.LoadResult<T>> {
```

`RowDragBetween.tsx`

```tsx
import { reactive } from '@motifx/core';
import { DataGrid, Stack } from '@motifx-community/ui';
import type { GridRowDropEventArgs } from '@motifx-community/ui';
import type { Task } from './task';
import { makeTasks, taskColumns } from './tasks';

/** Two grids in one `group`: a row dropped on the other grid raises `onRemove` here and `onAdd` there. */
export default function RowDragBetween() {
  const s = reactive({ todo: makeTasks(12), done: makeTasks(4, 101) });
  const columns = taskColumns.filter((c) => c.field !== 'priority');
  const grid = (list: 'todo' | 'done', label: string) => {
    const rows = () => s[list];
    const add = (e: GridRowDropEventArgs<Task>) => {
      const at = e.toItemData ? rows().indexOf(e.toItemData) : rows().length;
      rows().splice(at, 0, e.itemData);
      e.component.refresh();
    };
    // The grids read the arrays as they are: each loads its own again after the change.
    const remove = (e: GridRowDropEventArgs<Task>) => {
      rows().splice(rows().indexOf(e.itemData), 1);
      e.component.refresh();
    };
    const reorder = (e: GridRowDropEventArgs<Task>) => {
      const from = rows().indexOf(e.itemData);
      const to = rows().indexOf(e.toItemData as Task);
      rows().splice(from, 1);
      rows().splice(to, 0, e.itemData);
      e.component.refresh();
    };
    return (
      <DataGrid
        class={`dg-board dg-board-${list}`}
        style="block-size: 28rem; flex: 1 1 18rem"
        rows={rows}
        rowKey="id"
        columns={columns}
        label={label}
        locale="en"
        settings={{ sortable: false }}
        rowDragging={{ group: 'board', allowReordering: true, dropFeedbackMode: 'push', onAdd: add, onRemove: remove, onReorder: reorder }}
      />
    );
  };
  return (
    <Stack orientation="horizontal" wrap align="start">
      {grid('todo', 'To do')}
      {grid('done', 'Done')}
    </Stack>
  );
}
```

# DataGrid: Selecting by dragging

> DataGrid · @motifx-community/ui 0.1.0-beta.5

## Rows

With `selection: 'multiple'`, press on a row and drag over others to select the rows in between, with a frame around them during the drag. A plain drag replaces the selection, Ctrl (⌘ on Apple platforms) adds to it, and Shift extends from the anchor. Over the check boxes, all rows passed take the state of the first one. Near the top or bottom edge, the rows scroll (300 rows in this example), and when grouped, group rows are skipped. `onSelectionChanged` occurs once per row reached, with `e.byDrag`.

```tsx
/** An order, as stored by the sample server. */
export interface Order {
  id: number;
  customer: string;
  city: string;
  date: string;
  status: string;
  paid: boolean;
  amount: number;
  note: string;
}
```

## Cell ranges

`cellSelection` draws rectangles of cells as in a spreadsheet. Press on a cell and drag. Ctrl or ⌘ starts another range (`'multiple'`), Shift+click extends the last one from its anchor, and a plain click starts over. Shift and the arrow keys do the same from the keyboard. Ctrl+C copies the ranges as tab-separated text, Ctrl+V pastes into them (one value fills them all), Delete clears them through the normal edit path, and the status bar sums the numbers. The Note column is excluded until you include it.

```tsx
/** An order, as stored by the sample server. */
export interface Order {
  id: number;
  customer: string;
  city: string;
  date: string;
  status: string;
  paid: boolean;
  amount: number;
  note: string;
}
```

## Over 100,000 rows

Ranges are marks on the currently rendered cells: the pooled rows and, with virtual columns, the visible columns. Drawing a range over 100,000 rows × 60 columns keeps the frame rate, and a range change writes only the marks that changed, never a cell's text. The buttons set ranges by key programmatically.

```tsx
import { reactive } from '@motifx/core';
import { Button, DataGrid, Stack, type GridColumnItem } from '@motifx-community/ui';

type Reading = { id: number };

const SENSORS = 60;

const columns: GridColumnItem<Reading>[] = [
  { field: 'id', title: 'Hour', type: 'number', width: 90, sticky: 'start' },
  ...Array.from({ length: SENSORS }, (_, n) => ({ field: `s${n}`, title: `S${n + 1}`, type: 'number' as const, width: 90, value: (r: Reading) => ((r.id * (n + 7)) % 1000) / 10 })),
];

const rows: Reading[] = Array.from({ length: 100_000 }, (_, i) => ({ id: i + 1 }));

/** 100,000 rows × 60 virtual columns: a range is drawn over pooled rows, only the drawn cells carry its marks. */
export default function CellRangesVirtual() {
  const s = reactive({ told: '' });
  let grid: DataGrid<Reading> | null = null;
  const show = () => {
    const sum = grid?.cellSelectionSummary;
    s.told = sum ? `${sum.cells.toLocaleString('en')} cells, sum ${sum.sum.toLocaleString('en')}` : '';
  };

  return (
    <>
      <Stack orientation="horizontal" wrap align="center">
        <Button text="Hours 10–20, S1–S5" size="sm" variant="outline" onclick={() => grid?.selectCells({ key: 10, field: 's0' }, { key: 20, field: 's4' }) && show()} />
        <Button text="Add hour 50, S10–S12" size="sm" variant="outline" onclick={() => grid?.selectCells({ key: 50, field: 's9' }, { key: 50, field: 's11' }, true) && show()} />
        <Button text="Clear" size="sm" variant="ghost" onclick={() => grid?.clearCellSelection()} />
      </Stack>
      <DataGrid
        class="dg-range-virtual"
        style="block-size: 30rem"
        rows={rows}
        rowKey="id"
        columns={columns}
        label="Sensor readings as a sheet"
        locale="en"
        settings={{ cellSelection: 'multiple', columnRenderingMode: 'virtual' }}
        onCellSelectionChanged={show}
        ref={(g: DataGrid<Reading>) => (grid = g)}
      />
      <output class="dg-range-virtual-state">{() => s.told}</output>
    </>
  );
}
```

## Options

| settings | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `rowDragSelection` | `Bind<boolean>` | `true` | With `selection: 'multiple'`, pressing on a row and dragging selects the rows passed. |
| `cellSelection` | `Bind<'none' \| 'single' \| 'multiple'>` | `'none'` | Allows rectangles of cells: one at a time, or more with Ctrl or ⌘. While enabled, clicking cells draws ranges, and rows are selected from the check box column. |
| `cellDragSelection` | `Bind<boolean>` | `true` | Allows ranges to be drawn by dragging. When disabled, Shift+click and the keys still draw them. |
| `cellSelectable (column too)` | `Bind<boolean>` | `true` | Whether the column's cells can be in a range. The column's own value takes precedence. A range excludes such a column, and pressing there draws nothing. |
| `dragSelectionThreshold` | `Bind<number>` | `5` | The distance in pixels the pointer moves after a press before a drag starts. A shorter movement is a click, which selects, or starts editing with `startEditAction: 'click'`. |
| `dragSelectionAutoScroll, dragSelectionScrollSpeed, dragSelectionScrollSensitivity` | `Bind<boolean>`, `Bind<number>`, `Bind<number>` | `true`, `30`, `60` | The rows scroll while the pointer is near or past an edge, vertically and (for ranges) horizontally: the speed in pixels per frame at the edge, and the distance at which it starts. |
| `dragSelectionTouch, dragSelectionLongPress` | `Bind<'scroll' \| 'longPress'>`, `Bind<number>` | `'scroll'`, `500` | On a touch screen, a drag scrolls, and a press held for this many milliseconds starts a drag selection. |
| `dragSelectionOnEditableCells` | `Bind<boolean>` | `true` | Allows a drag to start on a cell the user can edit. When disabled, presses there are only clicks. |
| `selectAllCellsKeys, clearCellSelectionKeys` | `Bind<string[]>` | `['Mod+A']`, `['Escape']` | The keys that select every cell and clear the ranges (any combination, such as `Ctrl+Shift+A`). |
| `extendCellsKeys` | `Bind<GridCellExtendKeys>` | `{ up: ['Shift+ArrowUp'], down, left, right, pageUp, pageDown, home, end` with Shift; `top, bottom, leftmost, rightmost` with `Mod+Shift+Arrow…`; `first: ['Mod+Shift+Home'], last: ['Mod+Shift+End'] }` | The keys that move the far corner of the last range, by destination: a cell, a screen of rows, the first or last cell of the row, the first or last row, the leftmost or rightmost cell, or the very first or last cell. Each is a list of key combinations. Assign a new object to change some of them. |
| `toggleRowSelectionKeys` | `Bind<string[]>` | `['Shift+Space']` | The keys that select or deselect the active row. Space alone still does so on the check box column and on cells that cannot be edited. |
| `extendRowSelectionKeys` | `Bind<GridRowExtendKeys>` | `{ up: ['Shift+ArrowUp'], down: ['Shift+ArrowDown'], pageUp: ['Shift+PageUp'], pageDown: ['Shift+PageDown'] }` | For multiple selection, the keys that move the active row and extend the selection from the anchor (while cells are selected, from the check box column). |
| `cellSummary, cellSummaryItems` | `Bind<boolean>`, `Bind<('count' \| 'sum' \| 'average' \| 'min' \| 'max')[]>` | `true`, `['average', 'count', 'sum']` | The summary of selected cells in the bottom bar, shown while more than one cell is selected. |

| Change | Effect on ranges |
| --- | --- |
| `Sorting, filtering, searching, grouping` | The rows between the corners would change, so the ranges are cleared (without raising `onCellSelectionChanging`). Expanding or collapsing a group does the same. |
| `Paging` | A range belongs to the page it was drawn on, so changing the page clears it. Shift+PageUp and PageDown extend within the page. |
| `Rows added, loaded again, edited` | Corners keep their row by key (a new row by its ID), so a range follows its rows when new rows open above them, the data reloads or a value changes. A row that was loading when the corner was set is the row at that position once it arrives. |
| `Columns` | A range keeps its columns by field. When moved, they stay selected in their new position. When hidden, by the user or by width, they are excluded until they appear again. Pinned columns, band headers and virtual columns work as usual, and a column with `cellSelectable: false` breaks the frame. |
| `Virtual and infinite rows` | Ranges are drawn only on the pooled rows, cell by cell, and never redraw a cell's text. Rows that load while the rows scroll under a drag are included as they arrive. Copying requires every row of the ranges to be loaded (otherwise, use Export). |
| `Group rows, details` | Group rows, group footers, details and adaptive details are never selected. Dragging over a group row selects the visible rows on each side of it, and the rows of a collapsed group stay unchanged. |
| `Selected rows and ranges` | Both can be enabled. Over a selected row, a range is drawn in full with its own text color, so the text keeps its contrast. |

| Feature | How it shares the pointer |
| --- | --- |
| `Row drag and drop` | The drag icon (or `handle`) moves the row. Without icons, the whole row moves it, and rows are not selected by dragging. |
| `Editors and clicks` | The threshold separates a click from a drag. A click selects, opens a cell with `startEditAction: 'click'`, and a double-click edits. The click after a drag is ignored. |
| `Headers, filter row, group panel, totals` | Presses there belong to them: sort, resize, move, filter and group. |
| `Buttons, links, fields, toggles` | Presses on action buttons, master-detail and “…” toggles, links, buttons and fields inside cells belong to them. |
| `Text` | While a drag selects, the browser does not select text. Alt+drag is left to the browser, for selecting text in cells. |

## Events and methods

| Member | Parameters or return value | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `cellRanges` | `GridCellRange[]`, read/write, reactive | `{ from, to, fields }`: the cell the range started on, its far corner (`{ field, key, rowIndex }`) and its columns. Assign by key or grid index, and `[]` clears. |
| `selectCells(from, to?, add?)` | `boolean` | Selects a range from cell to cell (one cell without `to`), alone or after the others (`add`, with `'multiple'`). Returns whether it is displayed. |
| `clearCellSelection()` | `void` | Clears all ranges. |
| `getSelectedCellValues()` | `GridCellValue<T>[]` | The selected cells of the loaded rows, each once, row by row: `{ rowIndex, key, field, value, row }`, including unsaved edits. |
| `cellSelectionSummary` | `GridCellSummary`, reactive | `{ cells, count, numbers, sum, average, min, max }`, as in a spreadsheet status bar. |
| `onCellSelectionChanging` | `{ ranges, previous, byDrag, cancel }` | Occurs before every change, by the user or code. Set `cancel` to keep the ranges (while drawing, the last step). |
| `onCellSelectionChanged` | `{ ranges, byDrag }` | Occurs after every change: once per cell the pointer reaches while drawing. |
| `onSelectionChanging / onSelectionChanged` | `{ …, byDrag }` | The row selection events, raised once per row a drag reaches. `byDrag` identifies them. |
| `onCopying` | `{ text, html, rows, ranges, cancel }` | Occurs before a copy. `ranges` holds the ranges being copied. |

## Keyboard and screen readers

| Key | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `Shift+Arrows, Shift+Home / End, Shift+PageUp / PageDown (`extendCellsKeys`)` | Extends the last range from its far corner (with no range, from the active cell), and focus moves with the corner. Ctrl+Shift (⌘+Shift) with the arrow keys, Home and End moves to the edge. |
| `Ctrl+A (`selectAllCellsKeys`)` | Selects every cell of the rows the user can reach. |
| `Escape (`clearCellSelectionKeys`)` | Clears the ranges. While drawing, it cancels the drag, and for rows, restores the previous selection. |
| `Arrows, Home, End, PageUp / PageDown` | Moves the active cell and clears the ranges, as in a spreadsheet. |
| `Ctrl+C / Ctrl+V / Delete` | Copies the ranges, pastes into them (one value fills them all, and a block starts at the first cell), or clears their editable cells, saved according to the save mode. |
| `Shift+Space (`toggleRowSelectionKeys`), Shift+Up / Down and PageUp / PageDown (`extendRowSelectionKeys`)` | Selects rows as usual. While cells are selected, this works from the check box column. |

With `cellSelection` on, the grid is `aria-multiselectable` and every selectable cell has `aria-selected`. A selection by drag or key is announced politely: “4 rows selected”, “3 × 5 cells selected”, “12 cells selected in 2 ranges” (`gridRowsSelected`, `gridCellsSelected`, `gridCellRangesSelected`, in English and Turkish).

## Tokens

| Token | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `datagrid.range-fill, range-fill-opacity` | The fill of the cells of a range, over the row's own appearance at that opacity, and in full over a selected row. |
| `datagrid.cell (`range-selected`, `range-anchor`)` | The text of a range over a selected row, and of the anchor cell. |
| `datagrid.range-border-color, range-border-width` | The frame around a range. |
| `datagrid.range-anchor-fill` | The cell the last range started on (the design language's surface). |
| `datagrid.row-run-border-color, row-run-border-width` | The frame around the rows a drag selects, shown during the drag. |

```tsx
import { columns, makeOrders } from './orders';

/** Rows selected by dragging over them: live, with Ctrl to add, Shift from the anchor, over the check boxes too. */
export default function DragSelectRows() {
  const s = reactive({ drag: true, scroll: true, grouped: false, last: '' });
```

`CellRanges.tsx`

```tsx
import { reactive } from '@motifx/core';
import { Button, CheckBox, DataGrid, Stack, type GridCellSelectionChangedEventArgs } from '@motifx-community/ui';
import { columns, makeOrders } from './orders';

const MODES = ['none', 'single', 'multiple'] as const;

/** Ranges of cells as in a spreadsheet: drawn, extended, copied, filled and emptied; the bar sums them up. */
export default function CellRanges() {
  const s = reactive({ mode: 'multiple' as (typeof MODES)[number], drag: true, summary: true, touch: false, note: false, last: '' });
  const told = (e: GridCellSelectionChangedEventArgs) =>
    (s.last = e.ranges.map((r) => `${r.from.key ?? r.from.rowIndex}.${r.from.field} → ${r.to.key ?? r.to.rowIndex}.${r.to.field}`).join(', ') + (e.byDrag ? ' (drawing)' : ''));

  return (
    <>
      <Stack orientation="horizontal" wrap align="center" role="group" aria-label="Cell selection">
        {MODES.map((mode) => (
          <Button key={mode} text={mode} size="sm" variant={() => (s.mode === mode ? 'solid' : 'ghost')} aria-pressed={() => s.mode === mode} onclick={() => (s.mode = mode)} />
        ))}
        <CheckBox label="Draw by dragging" x-model={() => s.drag} />
        <CheckBox label="Summary in the bar" x-model={() => s.summary} />
        <CheckBox label="Long press on touch" x-model={() => s.touch} />
        <CheckBox label="Note can be selected" x-model={() => s.note} />
      </Stack>
      <DataGrid
        class="dg-cell-ranges"
        style="block-size: 28rem"
        rows={makeOrders(60)}
        rowKey="id"
        columns={columns.map((c) => (c.field === 'note' ? { ...c, cellSelectable: () => s.note } : c))}
        label="Orders as a sheet"
        locale="en"
        settings={{
          editable: true,
          cellSelection: () => s.mode,
          cellDragSelection: () => s.drag,
          cellSummary: () => s.summary,
          dragSelectionTouch: () => (s.touch ? 'longPress' : 'scroll'),
        }}
        onCellSelectionChanged={told}
      />
      <output class="dg-cell-ranges-state">{() => s.last}</output>
    </>
  );
}
```


---

# DataGrid: Scrolling

> DataGrid · @motifx-community/ui 0.1.0-beta.5

## Scrolling modes

The `mode` prop determines how rows are reached. Every mode renders only the visible rows from a small pool, so the page never holds one element per row.

| Mode | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `'virtual' (default)` | A single long list. The scrollbar is as long as every row, blocks load at the visible position (with a source using `loadMode: 'blocks'`), and rows in between are never requested. |
| `'paged'` | Pages with a pager. A source that loads by page is always paged. |
| `'infinite'` | Rows appear page by page, `pageSize` at a time. The next page loads as the view nears the end, and the scrollbar grows with the loaded rows. No total is required. In-memory rows, groups and summaries appear page by page the same way. |

## Infinite scrolling

With `mode: 'infinite'`, the grid shows 50 orders, and when the last of them comes into view, it requests the next 50 from the server, with “Loading more rows…” at the bottom while they arrive. This server cannot provide a count (`count: false`), so the grid finds the end when a page comes back short. Turn on “The next page fails” and scroll down, and the indicator offers Retry. Sorting, filtering or searching starts again from the first page.

```tsx
import { data } from '@motifx-community/data';

/** Rows in memory that answer a little later, the way a server does; for the examples. */
export class SlowAdapter<T extends object, K> extends data.ArrayAdapter<T, K> {
  constructor(
    options: data.ArrayAdapterOptions<T>,
    private readonly delayMs = 300,
  ) {
    super(options);
  }

  override async load(options: data.LoadOptions = {}): Promise<data.LoadResult<T>> {
    await new Promise((done) => setTimeout(done, this.delayMs));
    return super.load(options);
  }
}
```

| Option | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `mode` | `Bind<'virtual' \| 'paged' \| 'infinite'>` | `'virtual'` | How rows are displayed. Changing the mode reloads the data. |
| `pageSize` | `Bind<number>` | `100` | The rows per page for in-memory rows (0 shows every row at once). A source that loads by blocks uses its own block size. |
| `settings.loadMoreDistance` | `Bind<number>` | `0` | The number of rows left below the view when the next page starts to load. 0 waits for the last row to come into view. |
| `settings.preloadEnabled` | `Bind<boolean>` | `false` | Loads the next page one page earlier (in virtual mode, one page on each side of the view), so that scrolling rarely has to wait. |
| `settings.loadMoreIndicator` | `Bind<boolean>` | `true` | The “Loading more rows…” indicator over the last rows while a page loads, with Retry if it fails. |
| `DataSource count` | `boolean` | `true` | When disabled, no page asks the server for a total. A page shorter than the block size ends the rows, as does an empty page after a full one. |

| Member | Parameters or return value | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `onMoreRowsLoading` | `{ skip, take, cancel }` | Occurs before the next page loads (the view is near the end, `loadMore()`, or Ctrl+End). Set `cancel` to keep the rows as they are. |
| `onMoreRowsLoaded` | `{ skip, count, ended }` | Occurs when a page arrives: `count` rows from `skip`, and `ended` once every row is displayed. |
| `loadMore()` | `boolean` | Loads the next page, after `onMoreRowsLoading`. Returns `false` while rows are loading, when a page is loading or has failed, or when every row is displayed. |
| `loadingMore, endReached` | `boolean`, reactive | Indicates whether a page is loading, and whether every row is displayed (always true outside infinite mode). |
| `retry()` | — | Reloads a page that failed, as the indicator's Retry does. |
| `pageIndex(), pageIndex(n), page` | `number` | The last displayed page. With a number, loads the pages up to that one and scrolls to its first row. |
| `pageCount` | `number`, reactive | The number of pages of all rows once the count is known, otherwise the displayed pages. |
| `total, totalCount()` | `number` | `total` is the number of rows displayed so far. `totalCount()` is every matching row once known (counted, or when the last page arrived), and −1 until then. |
| `refresh()` | — | Reloads the displayed rows and keeps the position. |

| Topic | Infinite mode behavior |
| --- | --- |
| `The end` | With a count, the end is known from the first page. Without one (`count: false`), a page that comes back short is the last. Scrolling at the end requests nothing further. |
| `Failing parts` | A page that fails shows Retry in the indicator (or in the bottom bar with `loadMoreIndicator` off), and scrolling does not request it again until Retry. The displayed rows stay, and a failure of the first page shows the grid's own error. |
| `Sort, filter, search` | Starts again from the first page, at the top. |
| `Grouping` | Group rows and data rows appear page by page together. Groups from a server load only the rows of the displayed page, and in memory, every row is already available. |
| `Selection, export` | “Select all” and Ctrl+A select every matching row, loaded or not, and export writes every row, including pages not yet loaded. |
| `Editing, details` | The row being edited, the focused row, its details and the selection stay as pages arrive, and new rows open after the displayed rows. |
| `Pager` | Hidden. Rows are reached by scrolling. |
| `Assistive technology` | `aria-rowcount` is −1 until the last page arrives, and each row keeps its `aria-rowindex`. |

## In-memory rows, grouped

In-memory rows also appear page by page, here 100 places at a time, grouped by city. Group rows and data rows both count, so the next city's group appears with its page. Details, selection and group summaries work as in the other modes.

```tsx
/** An order, as stored by the sample server. */
export interface Order {
  id: number;
  customer: string;
  city: string;
  date: string;
  status: string;
  paid: boolean;
  amount: number;
  note: string;
}
```

## Virtual columns

With `settings.columnRenderingMode: 'virtual'`, only the visible scrolling columns and `extraColumns` on each side have cells. The other columns keep their position in the layout and receive cells as they come into view. This example shows 100,000 hours of 200 sensors, in bands of 20, with the hour and the sum pinned. Turn off “Virtual columns” to see the same grid with every column rendered.

```tsx
import { reactive } from '@motifx/core';
import { CheckBox, DataGrid, NumberBox, Stack } from '@motifx-community/ui';
import type { GridColumnItem } from '@motifx-community/ui';

type Reading = { id: number };

const SENSORS = 200;

/** 200 sensors in bands of 20, with each reading calculated from the row, so no row holds 200 values. */
const columns: GridColumnItem<Reading>[] = [
  { field: 'id', title: 'Hour', type: 'number', width: 90, sticky: 'start' },
  ...Array.from({ length: SENSORS / 20 }, (_, b) => ({
    title: `Sensors ${b * 20 + 1}–${b * 20 + 20}`,
    columns: Array.from({ length: 20 }, (_, k) => {
      const n = b * 20 + k;
      return { field: `s${n}`, title: `S${n + 1}`, type: 'number' as const, width: 90, value: (r: Reading) => ((r.id * (n + 7)) % 1000) / 10 };
    }),
  })),
  { field: 'total', title: 'Sum', type: 'number', width: 100, sticky: 'end', value: (r: Reading) => (r.id * 31) % 100_000 },
];

const rows: Reading[] = Array.from({ length: 100_000 }, (_, i) => ({ id: i + 1 }));

/** 100,000 rows × 200 columns: only the columns in view (and two on each side) get cells. */
export default function VirtualColumns() {
  const s = reactive({ virtual: true, extra: 2 });

  return (
    <>
      <Stack orientation="horizontal" wrap align="center">
        <CheckBox label="Virtual columns" x-model={() => s.virtual} />
        <NumberBox label="Extra columns" labelMode="side" min={0} max={20} x-model={() => s.extra} />
      </Stack>
      <DataGrid
        class="dg-columns"
        style="block-size: 30rem"
        rows={rows}
        rowKey="id"
        columns={columns}
        label="Sensor readings"
        locale="en"
        settings={{ columnRenderingMode: () => (s.virtual ? 'virtual' : 'standard'), extraColumns: () => s.extra ?? 0, filterRow: true }}
      />
    </>
  );
}
```

| Option | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `settings.columnRenderingMode` | `Bind<'standard' \| 'virtual'>` | `'standard'` | With `'virtual'`, only the visible scrolling columns and `extraColumns` on each side have cells. Pinned columns always have them. |
| `column.columnRenderingMode` | `Bind<'standard' \| 'virtual'>` | The grid's value | A column's own setting. `'standard'` keeps its cells while it is out of view (for cell content with its own state), and `'virtual'` releases only that column. |
| `settings.extraColumns` | `Bind<number>` | `2` | The columns rendered beyond the visible ones on each side, so that a quick sideways scroll shows no gap. |
| `settings.renderAsync` | `Bind<boolean \| 'auto'>` | `'auto'` | Whether columns coming into view are rendered during scrolling (`false`), once scrolling stops (`true`), or once it stops when rendering takes longer than the threshold. |
| `settings.columnRenderingThreshold` | `Bind<number>` | `300` | How long rendering new columns can take, in milliseconds, before they wait for scrolling to stop (`renderAsync: 'auto'`). |
| `settings.columnRenderingDelay` | `Bind<number>` | `300` | How long, in milliseconds, there must be no sideways scrolling before waiting columns are rendered. |

| Topic | Virtual column behavior |
| --- | --- |
| `Rows of every kind` | The header, the filter row, the rows, group row items under their columns, the group footers and the totals all follow, and the row being edited keeps its editor's column. |
| `Pinned columns and bands` | Pinned columns are always rendered. A band header spans only its rendered columns and goes with the last of them, and its `aria-colindex` and `aria-colspan` stay those of all its columns. |
| `Keyboard` | The active column is always rendered. Tab, the arrow keys, Home and End can move into a column without cells, which receives them and scrolls into view. |
| `Layout` | Resizing, moving (including dragging a header past columns without cells), pinning and hiding work as usual, and “Fit all columns” renders every column while measuring them. |
| `Assistive technology` | Cells keep their `aria-colindex` and the grid its `aria-colcount`, so a screen reader still announces column 120 of 202. |
| `Export, copy` | CSV, Excel and PDF write every column, including those without cells, and copying reads the values rather than the cells. |
| `Events` | `onCellPrepared` and `onRowPrepared` run as cells are created, so they run again after a sideways scroll. |

## Keyboard

| Key | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `Ctrl+End` | In infinite mode, moves to the last displayed row, and the next page loads. |
| `Down, Page Down on the last rows` | In infinite mode, the view nears the end and the next page loads. |
| `Home, End, Tab, Left / Right` | With virtual columns, moves into a column without cells, which is rendered and scrolled into view. |

## Example files

`InfiniteScroll.tsx`

```tsx
import { reactive } from '@motifx/core';
import { data } from '@motifx-community/data';
import { Button, CheckBox, DataGrid, Stack } from '@motifx-community/ui';
import { SlowAdapter } from '../../../shared/slow-adapter';
import type { Order } from './order';
import { columns, makeOrders } from './orders';

/** A server that cannot count, and fails on purpose while `failing` is on. */
class OrderServer extends SlowAdapter<Order, number> {
  failing = false;

  override async load(options: data.LoadOptions = {}): Promise<data.LoadResult<Order>> {
    const result = await super.load(options);
    if (this.failing && (options.skip ?? 0) > 0) throw new Error('The server did not answer.');
    return result;
  }
}

/** 1,030 orders from a slow server without a count, loaded 50 at a time as the list nears its end. */
export default function InfiniteScroll() {
  const s = reactive({ loads: 0, parts: 0, preload: false, failing: false });
  // Simulates a server. In an application, use new data.RestAdapter({ url: '/api/orders', key: 'id' }) here.
  const server = new OrderServer({ data: makeOrders(1_030), key: 'id', capabilities: { count: false } }, 600);
  server.onLoading(() => s.loads++);
  // `count: false`: no page requests a total, and a page shorter than 50 rows is the last one.
  const orders = new data.DataSource<Order, number>({ adapter: server, loadMode: 'blocks', pageSize: 50, count: false });
  let grid: DataGrid<Order> | null = null;

  return (
    <>
      <Stack orientation="horizontal" wrap align="center">
        <CheckBox label="Load a part ahead" x-model={() => s.preload} />
        <CheckBox label="The next page fails" x-model={() => s.failing} onValueChanged={(e) => (server.failing = !!e.value)} />
        <Button text="Load more" variant="outline" onclick={() => grid?.loadMore()} />
        <Button text="To the last row" variant="outline" onclick={() => grid?.scrollToIndex(grid.total - 1, 'end')} />
        <output class="dg-infinite-state">{() => `${s.loads} loads, ${s.parts} parts came${grid?.endReached ? ', every row is here' : ''}`}</output>
      </Stack>
      <DataGrid
        class="dg-infinite"
        style="block-size: 30rem"
        mode="infinite"
        dataSource={orders}
        columns={columns}
        label="Orders, part by part"
        locale="en"
        settings={{ preloadEnabled: () => s.preload, selection: 'multiple', filterRow: true }}
        onMoreRowsLoaded={() => s.parts++}
        ref={(g: DataGrid<Order>) => (grid = g)}
      />
    </>
  );
}
```
